| **true** | The list was read in full, holds **no** password method, the account is a cloud-only member account (not synchronised from Active Directory, not a guest / `#EXT#` account), and it holds at least one method Microsoft documents as a way to sign in without a password: FIDO2 security key / passkey (`fido2`), Windows Hello for Business, Microsoft Authenticator, platform credential (macOS), certificate-based authentication (`x509Certificate`), Temporary Access Pass, SMS sign-in (`phone`), QR code (`qrCodePin`). |
| **unknown** | Everything else: the read was refused (the permission is not granted or consented yet), Microsoft throttled it and the user was not read in the run's retries, the list came back paged (not read in full), the user was not read, a synchronised or guest account without a cloud password method (its password lives in Active Directory or its home tenant, which this read cannot see), or a list with no password and no way to sign in. |

**What the API cannot tell.** Graph lists the password as a method when it exists; it cannot say that an existing
password is blocked from use (by Conditional Access, an authentication strength or a sign-in policy). SecurityInsight
uses the strictest correct reading: **a password that exists counts as usable** (false). Unknown is never false -- a
report reads unknown as "may use a password".

**Completeness.** Each user carries whether *its* list was read in full (`ENTRA_AuthMethodsReadComplete`) next to the
verdict (`ENTRA_PasswordlessOnly`, `$null` unless read in full); the Entra record's `authenticationMethods` part is
written only for a user read in full, and the field mapping fills `si_passwordless_only` from it. Throttling is
normal: a 429 is retried with the server's Retry-After (the whole request's and each throttled user's), and the users
still throttled after the last round stay unknown -- the run says so in one information line, never a warning or a
failed run. A refused read stops at once (the permission is tenant-wide) and the run says in one plain warning which
permission to grant. Existing installs get the permission the next time their permission setup runs
(`setup\Grant-SIIdentity.ps1 -Apply`, `-AppId <client id>` for an app registration, or the guided install), which needs an
administrator's consent; until then the field stays unknown.

**PIM-for-Groups expansion** — `IdentityRoleFetcher.ps1` also pulls `identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/eligibilitySchedules` + `assignmentSchedules`. Recursive walker (`Get-SIRolesViaPimGroupChain`) handles nested chains: `User → PIM Group A (eligible) → PIM Group B (eligible) → Role`. Eligible roles inherited via PIM-for-Groups now flow into `EntraRoles_Eligible`.

**Per-source verdict split** — Catalog matching produces SEPARATE `EntraRolesPermanentVerdict_*` and `EntraRolesEligibleVerdict_*` flat columns. Was previously combined (and Eligible hardcoded to 0).

#### Endpoint engine

**MDE pass-through fix** — MDE Discovery emits `MDE_*`-prefixed keys (was unprefixed). Stage Collect has an explicit `elseif ($a.MDE_DeviceId)` branch BEFORE the Entra-device fallback. Without this, MDE-discovered devices fell into the wrong branch and `Hostname` / `OsPlatform` / `OsVersion` / `MachineGroup` / `LastSeen` etc. all landed empty.

**Asset-class catalog** (`endpoint-tiering.json`) — **RETIRED as a tier source.** The file still ships and is still read for its version stamp, but its 128 class definitions no longer influence any tier: endpoint tiers come from the **`AssetProfileBy*` rule set** (MIN across matched rules), which covers the same ground. The per-device matcher that walked its four detection channels was removed, and with it the customer override file — an override of a catalog nothing consults could only ever look like it worked.

**Server-application catalog** (`server-applications.json`) — 500 entries (T0=89, T1=186, T2=212, T3=13), vendor + name pairs. Stage Enrich does ONE bulk `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` query per run (NOT per posture rule), populates `$asset.Metadata.TvmSoftware`, then in-process matches against the 500-entry catalog. ~99% reduction in Defender hunting calls vs naive one-rule-per-product.

**Cross-engine user-based tier** — per device, find top-5 most-frequent logon users (3-day window via `DeviceLogonEvents`) → look up their tier in `SI_Identity_Profile_CL` → MIN tier across them = `MostFrequentUserTier`. Three new flat columns: `MostFrequentUserTier`, `MostFrequentUsers`, `MostFrequentUsersCount`. Aggregator contributor `endpoint_user_based_tier` weight 0.9.

KQL example — devices used by Tier-0 admins:
```kql
SI_Endpoint_Profile_CL
| where MostFrequentUserTier == 0
| project Hostname, MostFrequentUserTier, MostFrequentUsers, OsPlatform, MachineGroup
```

### Run-integrity guards — making absence loud

A Risk Analysis run that produces *less* data than yesterday still exits 0, still writes a workbook and
still looks successful. Absence reads as good news. Two guards run at the end of every run and compare
this run against the previous one for the same report template. **Both WARN; neither ever fails a run** —
a customer who genuinely remediates everything should reach zero, and a guard that cries wolf on success
gets switched off.

| Guard | Question it answers | State file |
|---|---|---|
| **Row-count guard** | did a report stop returning rows? | `OUTPUT/RowCountHistory.json` |
| **Column-fill guard** | did the rows stay while their *content* drained? | `OUTPUT/ColumnFillHistory.json` |

Both are keyed **template → report** (the same report legitimately returns different counts under a
Summary vs a Detailed template, so keying by report alone would corrupt both baselines). The column
guard adds a third level, **→ column**, storing the populated-row count per column plus `__rows` as the
denominator.

**Row-count guard** reports `WENT-TO-ZERO` (produced rows before, none now) and `LARGE-DROP` (fell by
more than 80%).

**Column-fill guard** reports, in descending severity:

| Finding | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `COLUMN-VANISHED` | the column was populated before and is no longer in the schema at all |
| `COLUMN-EMPTIED` | the column still ships and is blank on every row |
| `FILL-DROP` | still populated, but its fill rate fell by more than 80% |

Two properties are worth knowing when reading the output:

- **Comparison is on fill *fraction*, not raw filled count.** Row counts move between runs for ordinary
  reasons. A column that stays fully populated while its report legitimately halves is not a loss, and
  is reported as nothing.
- **A report that produced no rows is skipped by the column guard**, which defers to the row-count
  guard. Every column in an empty report is trivially empty; reporting each one would bury the single
  accurate message under dozens of derived ones.

Both guards are advisory signals for the operator, not gates. A finding means *investigate before
trusting this export* — most often an upstream property was renamed or reshaped, or an enrichment
source stopped supplying data, neither of which produces an error anywhere else.

### The CI build in SQL (v3, #477 / #501)

> Operator 2026-10-09: *"we dont support la for correlation, sql only"*, *"la is troubleshooting and kusto"*, *"we need
> correlated data in kusto right in la"*, *"performance and cost must be optimed"*.

**Where the data lives.** The provider records live in the install's database only (`sidata.CiRecord` + its strong
identifiers in `sidata.RecordIdentifier`, `engine/data-model/SI-RecordSql.ps1`). Nothing in correlation, the CI build or
the data sync reads Log Analytics. Log Analytics keeps what Risk Analysis's Kusto reads (the profile tables, `SI_CI_CL`,
Risk Analysis's output) and the troubleshooting data (run health, guard events, ingest diagnostics), unchanged.
`SI_LaExport = records` (off by default; it costs ingestion) adds a one-way copy of the records to `SI_Record_CL` /
`SI_RecordRaw_CL` for Azure Monitor or workbooks — nothing reads it back (guard test).

**The build** (`Invoke-SICiBuild`, `SI-CiBuildRun.ps1` + `SI-CiBuildSql.ps1`; free code, both editions):

| Phase | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| group | SQL | connected components by **label propagation** over `sidata.RecordIdentifier`: every record starts with its own key as label; each round a record takes the smallest label of the records it shares an identifier with, until no label moves (binary collation, so "smallest" is ordinal on every host; a chain longer than the round limit throws). Result: `sidata.CiGroupMember` (record → group, batch number), batches of ~2,000 CIs. Records of the last `SI_ActiveStaleDays` (30) days; CMDB records and records without a strong identifier are left out. |
| feeds | SQL | per provider + record type, the newest collection and whether it was complete (the link states) |
| batch | SQL → PowerShell | one batch's records (JSON + the per-run columns), the groups in ordinal order — the same core as the in-memory build (`Invoke-SICiCore`: identity, links, fields, enrichment rules). A group is a whole CI, so a batch decides exactly what a whole run would. |
| ledger | SQL | only the batch's identifiers and every row of the ids they point at (`Get-SIObjectLedgerSubset`; the ledger can be another database, so no cross-database join); the batch's changes in one statement (`Save-SIObjectLedgerSet`). A blob ledger is read once and written once. |
| write | SQL | `sidata.Ci` / `CiLink` / `CiDaily` and the records' `CiId` — **only CIs whose content hash changed** are rewritten (an unchanged CI gets only its last seen); the finding totals are the data sync's and never overwritten |
| post | Log Analytics | `SI_CI_CL` after **every** build: a slim **seen** row for every CI (id, collection time, content hash, last seen) and a **full** row (the columns Risk Analysis reads and the CI's own facts a person filters on in Kusto -- operating system, addresses, onboarding and hardening, mail and title, the Azure network and access settings, lifecycle, first seen, purpose, category, the CMDB match; V3-DATA-MODEL 2.21. Every CI field of the field catalog is either posted or named as database-only -- the lists, ids and summaries the web app and the exports read from the database -- so no column exists that no row fills) when the CI's posted hash changed — plus a full refresh of every CI when the last one (`sidata.CiBuildState`) is older than 7 days |

**One CI id, one asset (#642).** A name is never an identifier: the Exposure Graph enrichment of an identity or an Azure
resource that matched a node only by its name (a name only one node has -- a name two nodes share is no key) takes the
node's values but never its node id (`Find-SIIdentityEgHit` / `Get-SIIdentityEgFields`, `Invoke-Collect.ps1`). A name
match that did hand on the node id is what put 11 same-named Defender service principals (one per subscription) under one
ledger id at a ring 1 install. Such a wrong merge already in a ledger is split by `Resolve-SIObjectIdentity` (the CI
build's and the correlation engine's one identity step) when it is PROVEN: for two or more identifier types an object
holds once (object id, app id, Azure resource id, Exposure Graph node, AD object guid), the id holds another value written
in the same run as the group's own (`Test-SILedgerWrongMerge`). The object the id was minted from keeps it (else the oldest
anchor -- decided from the ledger alone, so every batch agrees); the other gets the v5 id of its own birth anchor and its
anchors are re-pointed, so it is split once and never again. Ids that rotate (a Defender device id, an Entra device id) or
values written in different runs never prove two objects -- those stay on the id and are reported. Groups of a batch that
still share an id are built as ONE CI from all their records -- never the first group kept and the others dropped -- and
counted. Both are said in one WARN line each and kept in `sidata.CiBuildState` (`WrongMergesSplit` / `WrongMergesSplitIds`,
`SharedIdGroups` / `SharedIds`). Existing installs are repaired by the update: build version 8 rebuilds every CI once.
**A cloud resource's last seen** is the newest time its source listed it (Resource Graph has no last seen of its own;
`si_field_sources.si_last_seen.from = listed_by_source`) -- only for cloud resources: an identity or a device keeps its
source's own last seen, or an account that never signs in would look active.

Memory is one batch at any tenant size. Every phase logs its count and seconds, and the run ends with the rows written to
SQL and the rows + approximate KB posted. **No database configured, or one that cannot be reached, is a plain failure with
its reason** — never a Log Analytics fallback.

**Changed-only.** Records and CIs carry a SHA-256 content hash of their JSON with the per-run fields left out (collection
time, completeness, source last seen, run id; for a CI also its days inactive, action, last seen, field sources). A
record whose hash is unchanged keeps its JSON and identifiers — only its per-run columns are set, and the build reads
those columns over the stored JSON. A second build of unchanged data writes ~0 SQL rows and posts no full row.

**A list stays a list (#690 (35)).** A list field reaches `SI_CI_CL` as a JSON list even with one item: the field mapper's
`parse_json` keeps a text that is not JSON as the value (the identity profile writes a one-item list as the bare item --
"Global Administrator", not `["Global Administrator"]`), and the post (`ConvertTo-SILogValue`) never unrolls a one-item
array into its item (an empty list stays empty). Before, every identity with exactly one role, permission or group had the
field empty or scalar, and every report reading it as a list (`array_length`, `set_has_element`, `mv-expand`) lost it --
internal 2026-10-15: 3 of 6 Global Administrators. A service principal's `si_created` comes from its profile row, else its
own Graph object (`sp.createdDateTime`), so one without a profile row still has a creation date. `SIv3-NoLostRows`.

**Why one table with a row kind, not a second "seen" table.** `si_row_kind = seen | full` in `SI_CI_CL`: no new table or
DCR, the same ingestion path, and a seen row is five columns — the cost is the bytes posted, which is the same either way.

**Readers** (`Get-RACiIndexKql`): the SET of CIs = the rows of the newest build (`si_collection_time == max`; a full row
counts as seen; rows from before the row kinds count as both); each CI's PROPERTIES = its latest full row within
`SI_ActiveStaleDays` (default 30) — a device off for a week keeps its properties. **The workspace retention of `SI_CI_CL`
must be at least 31 days** (the installer checks or sets it). The data sync no longer reads `SI_CI_CL` / `SI_Record_CL`:
what is left of it for the CI tables is the findings per CI (`SI_Finding_CL` → `sidata.CiFinding`) and the CIs' finding
totals, set-based in SQL.

### Risk Analysis writes its result to SQL, a query slice at a time (v3, #638 / #641)

**The model (owner, 2026-10-13).** Per bucket: the report's Kusto query (unchanged), the rows scored, WRITTEN to the Pro
database, then the next bucket -- nothing of the result is gathered in memory across buckets. Everything that needs the whole
picture is read back from SQL afterwards. SQL is what the web app and everything after Risk Analysis read; Log Analytics
still gets every row (read back from SQL in pages, posted in chunks).

**When.** `Test-RAStreamWanted`: the Pro database is configured (`SI_ProSqlServer` / `SI_ProSqlDatabase`) and
`SI_RA_ResultInSql` is not off; `New-RAStream` checks that the database carries the tables (`sql/si-data-schema.sql`, the
updater's step -- the engine runs no DDL). Otherwise, or in a dry run, the result is kept in memory as before, and that is
said. Both paths run the SAME per-report code (`Invoke-RAReportRows`: filters, exemptions, tiers, CI context, scoring,
trace identity, columns) -- per bucket when streaming, once per report otherwise.

**A bucket** (`_shared/RA-SqlStream.ps1`, `Write-RAStreamRows`): its scored rows go into `sidata.Finding` (Detailed run) or
`sidata.SummaryRow` + `sidata.SummaryAsset` (Summary run) through the DATA SYNC'S mapping (`ConvertTo-SIDataFindingJson`,
`ConvertTo-SIDataSummaryItems`; one mapping, never a second), the whole row as `DetailJson` / `RowJson` (null, '' and empty
lists left out, as Log Analytics' `pack_all(true)`), plus Risk Analysis' own columns: `RaReport` (report order), `RaBucket`
(`3/16`, `late:3/16`, `sub:<index>/<count>`, `whole`, `page:N`), `RaSeq` (write order), `RaDedup`, `RaSort` (the weighted
score), `RaInView` (the workbook / mail view: exemptions + output scope, decided per row as before), the trace parts,
`RaFindingKey` (SI_Finding_CL), `RaAssetId` / `RaAssetTier` (for the data sync). Written in chunks of OPENJSON (the data
sync's `Write-SIDataJsonRows`, chunk size from the measured time) -- not SqlBulkCopy, because the mapping is the data sync's.
**A retried bucket never doubles**: its rows are deleted by bucket, then inserted. A report that runs again with more buckets
(escalation), a bucket that returned the complete result (#401), a report that cannot be sent or fails: the report's rows are
removed (`Clear-RAStreamReport`). A passing SQL failure is retried (3 attempts); a write that keeps failing fails the report.

**How a slice's rows are scored and written -- per row, on several cores (#666).** A Detailed slice is tens of thousands of
rows, and every per-row step costs PowerShell interpreter time, so the steps are written for that: the advanced-hunting answer
is converted into rows with a list (never an array grown by `+=`, which copies the whole array per row) and plain values taken
over without a call per cell; the CI and Defender context work out what depends only on the CI once per CI; scoring
(`Calculate-RiskScore`) works out what is the same for every row once per call (the factor catalog plan, the rating bands,
compiled patterns, the report's finding texts) and what repeats across rows once per distinct value set (the risk-index bases,
the finding factors -- keyed on the fields their conditions read --, the factor sums, the classification of the finding's
fields -- keyed on the fields its rows read --, the MITRE / compliance references), and walks a row's columns once for its
links. Then the work is split over the processor cores (`_shared/RA-ParallelScore.ps1`): for a report that is not a Summary
report each row's scored output depends only on that row, so the de-duplicated rows are scored in contiguous parts, each by
the same function in its own runspace (the engine's files dot-sourced, the run's global variables handed over, a risk-index
memo of its own), and put back in order before the one final sort; the rows' stored form (`ConvertTo-RAStreamRowItems`: the
JSON item, the dedup / trace / finding keys, the write order) is made the same way, each part from its own place in the write
order. The result is the result of one pass over all the rows -- the same rows, values and order (tested against the code as
it was, `SIv3-RaRowPerformance`; one core vs four on 16,000 rows in en-US and da-DK, `SIv3-RaParallelScoring`).
`SI_RA_ScoringThreads` (default: ON, the cores the process has -- a 4-CPU job scores on 4; `1` / `off` = one core; a number
= that many, never more than the cores; the environment variable `SI_RA_SCORINGTHREADS` is read when the setting is not
set) and `SI_RA_ParallelMinRows` (default 2,000) set it; if the workers fail, that is said and the step runs on one core.
Every slice says `risk scores of N row(s) worked out on K processor cores in S s` (one core: and why). A worker is never
handed a script block or delegate from the run's globals (it would run against the main runspace's variables from the
worker's thread) and works in the main thread's culture. Summary reports are scored on one core (their impacted-asset
lists are report-wide). (Off by default 2026-10-14 to -16 after a live run was reported hung; the run log showed the
silence was the Defender catalogue read before scoring, #666 -- on again with #716.)

**How a CVE finding gets its Defender context -- from the report's own query (#666).** `Device_Missing_CVEs_Detailed` is
an advanced-hunting query against Defender XDR, and the query itself fills the CVE context columns: **exposed devices**
(`si_exposed_devices`) -- the number of devices of the tenant that vulnerability management lists for the CVE, each
device once, excluded devices left out, counted over the whole tenant (not only the query slice); **EPSS, CVSS vector,
published date** (`si_epss`, `si_cvss_vector`, `si_published`) -- from the vulnerability knowledge base; **verified
exploit, exploit kit** (`si_exploit_verified`, `si_in_exploit_kit`) -- from the Exposure Graph's CVE node. A finding the
graph does not carry (added from vulnerability management) leaves verified exploit and exploit kit **unknown (empty),
never false**, and the exploit types (`si_exploit_types`) are not available in advanced hunting, so they stay unknown.
No call to the Defender vulnerability API is made in a default run. Measured live before this change: reading that API's
whole catalogue (about 351,000 CVEs, paged by position) took 27-71 minutes of a 35-78 minute report, to keep the few
thousand CVEs that concern the tenant.

**The vulnerability API, opt-in** (`SI_RA_DefenderCveApi = on`, default off; `_shared/RA-DefenderCveContext.ps1`): it
adds the API's verified exploit, exploit kit, exploit types and exposed devices to the CVE rows (it wins over the
query's values; the query's EPSS / vector / published date win where the row has them). It reads **only the CVEs of the
rows being enriched**, never one twice in a run: the distinct CVE ids of a slice are asked for with OData filters -- `$filter=id in ('...','...')`, and when the service refuses that form on the run's first request,
`$filter=id eq '...' or id eq '...'` (the form learnt is kept for the run) --, as many ids per request as keep the address under `SI_RA_DefenderCveFilterUrlMax`
(default 6,000 characters; a request the service says is too long is split and sent again, and the limit learnt is kept),
the service's next links followed, one request after another (the API's rate limit makes parallel requests pointless). A
later slice asks only for the ids not asked yet; the answers join one index per run. Kept, as in the whole-list read: the
CVEs that expose at least one device. A CVE the service does not return is unknown, never false / 0. **Never fewer:** when
the service refuses the filter on the run's first request (400 / 405 / 501, "not supported") or answers with CVEs it was not
asked for, the whole list is read once for the run as before, said once in plain words (`SI_RA_DefenderCveRead = full`
forces that). A request that fails after the pager's retries makes the read not complete: said once, the rows go on
unchanged. One start line and one end line per slice (how many vulnerabilities, how many requests, how long); each
request's timing and retries are verbose-only lines.

**Cross-bucket work, the SQL way** (`Complete-RAStreamReport`, at the end of each report):
* de-duplication: the key `Calculate-RiskScore` de-duplicates on (`Get-RARowDedupKey`, 128-bit hash) -- a finding two buckets
  both returned is kept ONCE, the first written (the whole-report pass kept the first too); within a bucket the scoring itself.
  The key is the finding's dimensions + its asset (name and id) + its TARGET when the row carries one (`TargetAssetId` --
  the target's CI id, else its graph node id, on the attack paths; `LinkedAzureResourceId` on the identity-on-resource report; #690): one identity's role
  on 19 exposed resources is 19 findings, an exact copy (the same target too) is still one. A row without a target column
  keeps exactly the key it had, so no other report changes which rows it keeps;
* a missing tier stays missing (#690): `CriticalityTier` null, `CriticalityTierLevel` blank (kept by the scope filter, then
  given a tier by the tier rules, else Unclassified), never "Low - tier 3" / tier 2 / 3. The risk index has no base for a
  missing tier, so that side's base is 0 (the row is scored, ranked low, never dropped);
* every finding has a severity, one of the five SI values (Very High, High, Medium-High, Medium, Low -- never "Unknown",
  never empty). The SEVERITY MODEL (`data-model/severity-model.locked.json`) is the one place that says how: per report an
  ORDERED list of metric kinds -- the provider's own severity (a word map), an impact score (CVSS, EPSS, secure-score impact,
  attack-path priority: bands), the asset tier (a map) -- and owner_defined last (the report's own severity, the owner
  validates it), so every row ends with a value. Loaded and validated with the data model (`Get-SISeverityModel`,
  `Resolve-SISeverity`, `Test-SISeverityModel`; Pro overrides one report like any data-model item). The reports' queries
  still carry their own case() today -- each produces only the five (pinned by `SIv3-SeverityModel`); the generated severity
  block that reads the model is the next step;
* trace ids: `Set-RATraceIdentity` per bucket; then the rows whose trace name another asset of the same report shares in
  ANOTHER bucket get the asset id at the end (`RaTraceHash` / `RaTraceKey`, one update of only those rows);
* Summary groups that span buckets: the raw rows are staged per bucket (`sidata.RaStage`, with their group = the query's final
  summarize-by values, `Get-RASummaryGroupKey`); at the end they are read back a page of WHOLE groups at a time (in the order the
  groups were first seen), combined by `Merge-RASummaryBucketRows` (the same rules), scored and written;
* columns: the union per report, in first-seen order, kept in memory (names, not rows) -- read-back rows get every column of
  their report (absent = `$null`) and their date columns back as `[datetime]`;
* row counts and column fill for the run-to-run guards: added up per bucket.

**The CI context of a bucket** (`Get-RAStreamCiIndex`): the bucket's ids (with and without SI's id prefixes) and names looked
up in `sidata.Ci` / `sidata.CiLink`; a name only when ONE current CI in the whole tenant has it. Where Risk Analysis builds the
CIs itself (Community) they are built once at the start, into the database.

**After the reports** (every step reads pages, `New-RARowPager`, in the final order: `RaSort` desc, then `RaSeq`):
the workbook (up to its 1,000,000-row ceiling, the highest-risk rows; above it an **'Extract' sheet says so** -- the large-size
form is the owner's open question), the JSON file, Log Analytics (one pass for the schema sample, the companions and the key
check, a second to post; every page chunked; rows posted counted against the rows in SQL), the AI rollup (the Detailed
(asset × finding) collapse while streaming: the first row seen per pair is its highest-weighted one), the KPI (a running sum),
the executive view (also written straight into `sidata.RiskExecView`), the trend (the Summary run's rollup computed in SQL,
`Get-RAStreamTrendRollup`, handed to the trend engine) and SI_Finding_CL (rows grouped by finding key; a finding's rows never
split over two posts). **What is held:** one bucket's rows while it is scored; one page (32 MB of stored JSON) after; names
and counts per report; the AI rollup's aggregates (one entry per asset and per finding, and the (asset, finding) pairs seen);
the workbook up to its ceiling (Excel's limit).

**The end.** Only when every bucket of every report is in and Log Analytics took the result is the run's collection marked
(`Complete-RAStream`: `RaCompletedAt` on a Detailed collection, `Complete` on a Summary one, only when the row count matches).
A run that fails before leaves it `Loading`: nothing reads it. **The data sync** never loads a Risk Analysis-written collection
from Log Analytics (`Get-SIDataLoadPlan`: Skip, "written by Risk Analysis itself"); it completes it from SQL
(`Invoke-SIDataAdoptRaCollection`): each finding's CI key (#297/#298), the CIs and identifiers, the correlation evidence, the
recommendations, the daily aggregates, a partial run marked partial, then `Complete`. Its other work is unchanged.

**#641 -- no data may be lost.** Per report, every run: a count of the unbucketed query (`| count`; a count fits where the rows
do not) against the rows the buckets returned (the combined groups for a Summary report). Equal = `Complete`; different =
`NotComplete` (a failed report: the run is partial, nothing downstream closes on it, the run record names it); no count (the
query too large to run whole, or `SI_RA_CompletenessCheck` off) = `Unverified`, said. **A short answer is caught**: every bucket is checked against the source's own count of the same query (`Test-RABucketRowCount`, `SI_RA_BucketCountCheck`); short = asked again once, still short = a recorded bucket loss (the report is partial). A Log Analytics answer that carries its partial-error object (HTTP 200, rows cut at a limit) and an advanced-hunting answer AT its 100,000-row limit (`SI_RA_HuntingRowCap`; the API says nothing when it cuts) are refused as too large, so the slice is made smaller. A template report with no verdict at the
end (failed, not found, could not be sent) is `NotComplete`. Stored per run and report in `sidata.RaReportStatus` (expected,
retrieved, stored, state, reason). **The bucket proof** (on demand, `SI_RA_BucketProof = on`): for a report of at most
`SI_RA_BucketProofMaxRows` (20,000) rows the buckets' rows are compared row by row with the unbucketed query's -- the verdict in
the reason. `diagnostics/Compare-SIRiskAnalysisRuns.ps1` compares an old-path run with a new-path run on an install (rows per
report, a row-level diff, Summary groups, KPI and top 50, trend, Log Analytics, the verdicts).
**Since #753 a part's own count is asked only for a part whose rows reach half the source's row limit**
(`Test-RABucketCountWanted`; `SI_RA_BucketCountCheck = all` = every part, `off` = none): an answer AT the limit is refused and
the part made smaller, a part well below it was not cut, and the report's own count above still checks every report once.

**#753 -- several parts of a report at a time, the same result.** While the engine processes a part, the advanced-hunting
requests of the next parts are already on their way (`RA-PartsInParallel.ps1`; the transport's ask-ahead store in
`engine/_shared/SI-GraphRest.ps1`). After a part's answer the main loop builds the next parts' queries exactly as their own
runs will (`Invoke-GraphHuntingQuery`, slice coordinates set) with the store in "ask ahead" mode: the transport sends the
request and stops; every engine variable the build touched is put back and nothing it said is printed. When a part's turn
comes, its own request finds the answer by its exact body; a request that came out different is sent as before and the
answer asked ahead is dropped. The parts are processed one by one, in order, on the engine's thread -- only HttpClient runs
in the background, so no engine state is shared between threads and the stored rows and their order are those of one part
at a time. Only advanced-hunting requests are asked ahead (the lake and Log Analytics routes are refused in the hunting
layer); the late retry and the split parts run one at a time. How many at a time adapts: 2 to start, one more after a round
of quick answers the engine had to wait for, half on 429 / 503 / 504 with nothing asked ahead until Retry-After has passed;
`SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max` (default 6, at most 4 per core; 1 = one at a time).

**#674 -- a lookup a report needs that cannot be read: that report is NOT COMPLETE (fail closed).** A report that joins
SI's own Log Analytics tables (SI_*_CL) with the Exposure Graph gets those lookups read from Log Analytics and sent with the
query. A failed read used to fall through two fallbacks ("[scope] failed; let-blocks left for table-shadow fallback", then
"[shadow] failed; routing query as-is") to Microsoft Defender, which does not have SI's tables, where `union isfuzzy` turned
the lookup EMPTY -- Complete, with duplicates (an empty hand-off list) or without the CI / CMDB values (an empty
enrichment). Now (`Invoke-RAResolveLookups`, RA-GraphHunting.ps1; the 2-phase enrichment in `Invoke-ProfileAugment`) a
failed read throws the "lookup unavailable" error (`New-RALookupUnavailableError`): the bucket loop ends the report in one
decision, as for a request that can never fit (`Test-RAReportCannotRunError`), the report is a failed report ("it was not
run: a lookup this report needs could not be read ..."), the run goes on. A table that does not exist in Log Analytics
keeps the existing "no data source in this tenant" rule (`Test-RANoDataSource`), unchanged. **A hand-off list that reads
EMPTY** (`Assert-RAHandoffLookupReadable`, before the route is chosen, so the three set-ups decide alike) is checked once
per table and run with a count over 90 days (`SI_RA_HandoffSourceLookbackDays`): the table does not exist = no list was
ever written (kept, said); only older lists = no current list (kept, said); the table exists but none of its rows can be
read (a new table in Log Analytics takes up to about 45 minutes -- an install's first run) or the count fails = NOT
complete. And when the RECEIVING report (Azure_DefenderRecommendations_*) then finds rows in the same run although the
giver's list read empty, the giver is marked not complete (`Get-RAHandoffContradiction`). An intentionally empty hand-off
(#278: the receiving report is not in the run, the block is emptied) is not looked at.

**#673 -- plan B for the Azure recommendation reports: the Defender de-duplication in the engine, against a list in SQL
(SI_RA_DefenderFilterInEngine ON by default since rc2 -- owner 2026-10-16 "we need all out now", not set = on, 'off' = off; SI_RA_DefenderFilterCompare OFF by default; REMOVE-ME once plan B has held live).** Azure_Recommendations_*
drop every (resource, recommendation) the Defender recommendation reports carry with three `join kind=leftanti (_dfcPairs)` on
three pair keys (name, resource id, assessment). _dfcPairs has no key the query slices are cut on, so it travels with every
request and grows with the Defender list. Between those anti-joins and the final summarize / project every step is a per-row
extend / where / mv-apply or a leftouter join on a unique key (_subTierG, one row per subscription) -- held by a guard test
on the shipped queries -- so removing the rows at the END is removing them where they are. The YAML keeps the anti-joins
between `//__SI_DFC_ANTIJOIN_BEGIN__` / `_END__` (pasted into Log Analytics it still de-duplicates). With
`SI_RA_DefenderFilterInEngine = on` (RA-DefenderFilter.ps1, decided first in `Invoke-GraphHuntingQuery`, before any route, so
the three set-ups -- Defender XDR only, + Sentinel, + Sentinel data lake -- are the same): the anti-join blocks are cut out,
the hand-off lookup is emptied (nothing of the list travels), and the three keys are added to the final project (Summary: also
to the final summarize-by, with the asset `_dfcPart = tostring(DeviceKey)`, so a partial group never spans two slices); a
completeness count appended to the query keeps its place. **The list lives in SQL**: `sidata.RaDefenderKey (RunKey, K BIGINT)`
-- the first 8 bytes of `hash_sha256(<pair text>)`, see the keys below -- loaded once per run from SI's own workspace over the Log Analytics API,
counted first and read in parts of at most 200,000 keys cut on the key itself (a range of its first 4 hex digits), no `make_set` (it stops at
1,048,576 values), and the stored count checked against the count (short = nothing kept, the report not complete). An empty
list follows #674: no table / only older lists = nothing to filter; a table whose rows cannot be read yet or a count that
fails = not complete. **Every answer is filtered in SQL**: its distinct keys go in (in chunks of 20,000), the listed ones come
back; a row goes when ANY key is listed, counted under the first kind that matched (name, resource id, assessment -- the
query's order); the keys are taken off; a Summary answer's partial groups are combined with the existing merge
(`Merge-RASummaryBucketRows`, plan built from the ORIGINAL query text), and then across slices exactly as before.
**Completeness**: the source is asked the query without the anti-joins, so every check compares with the rows retrieved
BEFORE the filter (per slice `Get-RADfcCountedRows`; per report the `Pre` total, and a Summary report counted in its split
groups); the rows the filter removed are a named category, "N handed to the Defender recommendation report (by name a, by
resource id b, by assessment c)", so a normal run stays Complete (`Get-RAStoredVerdict -Handed`). The list is removed at the
end of the run; one a failed run leaves behind is removed by the next load after two days. Without the result in SQL the
query stays as it is (said once). **`SI_RA_DefenderFilterCompare = on`** runs BOTH paths for every answer and compares them
(Detailed rows exactly; Summary groups with lists compared as sets; the handed rows per kind), says a differing answer at once
and writes `staging/risk-analysis/ra-defender-handoff-compare-<time>.json` at the end of the run; the run's result is the query
path's unless in-engine is also on. Cost: a Summary answer is per (group, asset) instead of per group -- about the size of the
Detailed answer -- so its slices may need to be more; the request no longer carries the list.
**The keys (fixed 2026-10-16 after build 1938 stored 865 Detailed / 439 Summary rows on internal where plan A stores 51 / 29):**
plan A compares `hash(<text>)` of a row with `hash(<text>)` of the list INSIDE ONE QUERY; the first plan B kept `hash()` numbers
of a separate Log Analytics query and compared them with the hunting query's -- and KQL `hash()` is guaranteed the same only
within one query (its documentation: use `hash_sha256()` for values kept outside it). Now the cut query's three key columns are
`"x" + tolower(substring(hash_sha256(<the text plan A hashes>), 0, 16))` (`ConvertTo-RADfcShaKeyQuery` rewrites only the three
`extend _dfc*Key` expressions; the text inside is the YAML's, character for character; a query whose three keys cannot all be
rewritten is not cut), the list's query keys the YAML's `_dfcPairs` texts the same way, and both read as one signed 64-bit
number -- so a row and a list entry match exactly when their texts are equal, plan A's rule, whatever engine computes each side
(SHA-256 is a defined algorithm; the slicing already relies on KQL and .NET agreeing on it). Same texts, same normalisation
(lower-cased in KQL on both sides), same direction (a row goes when any of its three keys is listed). A key in another form
refuses the answer as not complete -- never a silent "no match".

**#675 -- a subscription-level Azure recommendation takes the tier of the WHOLE subscription, also in a sliced run.** The
Azure recommendation reports give a subscription-level row no CI links the tier of the subscription's most critical CI
(`_subTierG`, #192). It was computed from `_ciLink`, which the hybrid path cuts per query slice on `_ciKey`: a slice held only
the CIs whose keys hash into it, so the minimum was taken over a share of the subscription's CIs -- proved with the engine's
own inlining (a tier-0 VM in another slice: the subscription row got tier 3). `_subTierG` is now its own canonical CI block
(`Get-RACiKqlBlock -Kind subtier`, markers `//__SI_CI_SUBTIER_BEGIN__` / `_END__`, regenerated with the install's stale days
like the others): the same CI set, link keys and one-CI-per-key rule as `_ciLink`, the keys under `/subscriptions/`, then the
most critical tier per subscription -- read once per run from Log Analytics and, with no key the slices are cut on, inlined
WHOLE into every slice (one row per subscription; allowed whole by the lookup guard). Unsliced and data-lake runs give the
same tier as before.

**#677 -- a row's OTHER asset keeps its CI context in a sliced run (`_ciPeer`).** `_ciLink` is cut per slice on `_ciKey`, so a
join against it is complete only on the key the row itself was sliced on. Verified over every sliced report (2026-10-15): the
96 `_ciAsset` reports are answered by Log Analytics (nothing inlined); of the 32 that go to advanced hunting, the 12 Device_* /
Azure_Recommendations_* reports and the vulnerable-device attack-path Summary join `_ciLink` only on their slice key
(`_subTierG`, `_dfcPairs`, `_dfcRecByKey` travel whole or reduced); the other 19 do not, in four shapes, all proved with the
engine's own inlining (`SIv3-OtherSideCiSliced`):
- S1 the 8 `Identity_*LogonTo_*Device_*` reports, sliced on the USER, joined the DEVICE's CI on `DeviceCiKey` -- a device lost
  its CI id and factors, InternetExposedDevice dropped the finding (its filter reads the factor), LowTierDevice listed a tier-0
  device as low tier (its tier read null). FIXED.
- S2 `Attack_Paths_Detailed_Device_with_high_severity_..._Azure`, sliced on the entry device, joined the Azure TARGET's CI
  (`_TargetCi = _ciLink`) on its node id -- the target fell to tier 3 with no CMDB values. FIXED.
- S3 `Attack_Paths_*_Credential_Based_Lateral_Movement` cut their rows on the credential edges' `SourceNodeId` (a graph node
  id: the edges carry no DeviceKey), and every CI join was on a CI key. FIXED (second round).
- S4 the other 8 `Attack_Paths_*` reports (Github_to_Azure, Public_IP_to_VM, Identity_Group_Membership, Data_Sensitivity) cut
  only their Nodes catalog; the paths LEFT-join it, so every slice emits every path, with the source's context only in the
  source's slice and the target's only in the target's -- the tier escalation never saw both. FIXED (second round).

The fix (S1, S2): a fourth canonical CI block, `_ciPeer` (`Get-RACiKqlBlock -Kind peer`, markers `//__SI_CI_PEER_BEGIN__` /
`_END__`): the same CI set, link keys and one-CI-per-key rule as `_ciLink`, a lean projection under names the slice cut does not
key on (`_peerKey`, `peer_ci_id`, `peer_tier`, `peer_cmdb_*`, `peer_rf_p`, `peer_rf_names`, `peer_in_scope`). The report joins it
AFTER the slice filter at `//__SI_LOOKUP_KEYS_HERE__`, on the other asset's own key, and declares it under `LookupNeededKeys`
(the key lines are the query's own). So it travels whole while the part no slice count shrinks fits the planned request size,
and once it does not, each slice first asks which of its keys it can match and carries only those rows -- the same engine
reduction `_dfcPairs` uses (#674). One row per needed key (about 170 bytes a row inlined with two factors; the test holds it under 400), so a slice's share is
bounded by its own rows, never by the tenant; nothing is copied whole above the budget. In S1 `_ciLink` is narrowed to
`identity` (the user side only), which makes every slice smaller; the CI-dependent device filters (internet exposure, tier)
moved with the join to after the slice filter -- the same rows survive. In S2 the target's CI is read only from cloud
resources. Unsliced and data-lake runs give the same values as before.

**#697 -- a part is not asked for its keys when the answer is already known** (`Invoke-RALookupKeyDiscovery`). The key query
of a part is the report's own text up to the cut point, with that part's slice filter and its other lookups inlined, so the
same text is the same question. The answer to the text asked just before is used again, and any other text is asked. Only
the last text is remembered, so nothing grows. The repeats this removes, measured on a live estate: each part was asked once
for its rows and again for its own `| count` check (whose text before the cut point is identical), and the probe's part was
asked again as part 1. That was 33 asks (331 s) on one report of 25 rows. A part that came back short and is asked again
gets a fresh answer (`Clear-RALookupKeyAnswerMemo`, called by the bucket loop), and every report starts with nothing
remembered. A declared lookup that has **no rows at all** is never asked about: the part is sent with it empty (its columns
kept) at once. The line "N of its rows can match this part" is said only for a part that is sent. It is no longer said
while the key query itself is built, where the lookup is empty on purpose and the line read as "0 rows can match".

The fix (S3, S4 -- the 10 attack-path reports): the slice filter moved onto the edge set that gives each path its FINAL TARGET,
keyed on the target's node id (`| extend DeviceKey = <target node id>` right before the filter): Credential_Based on the Hop 2
edges (`TargetNodeId`), Github_to_Azure on its Hop 2 edges, Public_IP_to_VM on `PublicIPConnections` (`ExposedResourceNodeId`),
Identity_Group_Membership on `GroupAccessToTargets` (`FinalTargetId`), Data_Sensitivity on `SensitiveDataLocations` (the data
location). Every path's grain (its `summarize ... by`) includes its target, and every input that feeds one path is either
unsliced or cut on that same target, so a path is built in exactly one slice from the same rows as unsliced -- no path twice,
none lost -- and a Summary's `dcount` of its target (`AssetCount`) adds up over the slices, which is what the bucket merge does
(`FinalTargetId` / the target column is an asset-identity column there). The hop bounds (#56 semi-joins) stay; a hop
bounded by the sliced set shrinks with it. The Nodes catalog is no longer sliced and reads no CI (its tier is the SI tier TAG); the CI of
both ends (tier, CMDB, factors, in-scope) is read after the cut point from `_ciPeer` on `SourceCiKey` / `TargetCiKey` -- the
same values unsliced (`coalesce(CI tier, tag, 3)` as before, since an end found in Nodes has `<End>CiKey = NodeCiKey`).
`_ciLink` is gone from these reports. Intermediate nodes (credential, intermediate identity) carry no CI tier: no report shows
it. The cut point now sits inside a let in the Summary reports (their rows are built in a let and end in a summary); the key
query closes that let and makes it the result (`Get-RALookupKeyQuery` / `Get-RALookupCutLetName`).

**Request size per slice (S1-S4).** Fixed part: the query text plus whatever travels whole -- `_ciPeer` only while that whole
part is under the planning budget (75% of the 1 MB body); above it, `_ciPeer` is cut to the slice's own end keys. Worst case
per slice = query text + `_ciLink`'s share where a report still has it (cut with the rows, shrinks with more slices) + one
`_ciPeer` row (about 170 bytes) per distinct end key of the slice's rows. More slices shrink every part but one: the paths of
ONE target (or one user's devices, S1) are always in one slice, so a target reached by P paths from S distinct sources costs at
least (S + 1) x ~170 bytes in its slice -- about 4,000 sources before that alone passes the budget. Beyond that the engine's
size verdicts (#674) fail the report plainly, never silently. Graph work per slice: the hops up to the target edge set are
computed whole in each slice (they were before too); the Nodes catalog is now read whole in each slice (it was 1/N).

**Guard.** `SIv3-SliceKeyJoinGuard` (whole catalog, every advanced-hunting report): every join against a lookup the engine
cuts per slice (a column `Get-SICLBucketKey` keys on -- `_ciLink`), directly or through a let over it, renames followed, has
`DeviceKey` -- or the one column the report sets DeviceKey to -- as its left key and the lookup's cut column as its right key.
It fails on each shape #677 found.

**Forcing N slices for the live check (internal, after the merge).** Two settings for that run: `AutoBucketCount = false`
(no adaptive escalation, no cached count) and `SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed = N` -- every Detailed report then runs in exactly
N slices; a Summary report runs in 2 (the engine's starting count) unless its template carries `BucketCount` (the two
vulnerable-device attack paths: 8). Add `SI_RA_BucketProof = on`: for every report of at most `SI_RA_BucketProofMaxRows`
(20,000) rows the sliced rows are compared row by row with the unsliced query's, and the verdict is stored with the report's
completeness -- the live counterpart of `SIv3-OtherSideCiSliced`. Put the settings back afterwards.

**Where the new path's output can differ from the old.** (1) Order among rows of EQUAL score: old = the whole report sorted
(Sort-Object, not guaranteed stable), new = report order, then bucket, then the per-bucket sort -- deterministic. (2) The row
kept of two duplicates in different buckets is the first BUCKET's, not the first in the concatenated list (identical values but
for the bucket key). (3) A Summary report larger than one page (64 MB of stored rows): `Calculate-RiskScore`'s report-wide
fallbacks (`UniqueIssues` when the query gives none, the name -> id map for a name without an id in its own row) are page-wide.
(4) The JSON file shows `null` where a value was `''` or an empty list (the stored row leaves them out, as Log Analytics does).
(5) The trend's distinct assets are counted in SQL (case-insensitive collation; the in-memory set was ordinal case-insensitive).
(6) `DetailJson` of a Risk Analysis-written finding lacks the columns Log Analytics adds (`TimeGenerated`, `_ItemId`, ...).

**One incomplete report does not hold a whole run -- per-report loading.** A run in which one report could not be completed
is loaded as soon as it is in; every report that IS complete is current. Per report that is not:
- *Risk Analysis, at its end*: every report it judged incomplete (its query failed, its count did not match, the row-count
  guard flagged it, a query slice of it was lost) has the verdict `NotComplete` in `sidata.RaReportStatus`, and the run records
  what its incompleteness covers on its Detailed collection (`sidata.Collection.RaPartialScope`): `reports` when every cause is
  a named report, `run` when anything else made it partial (a Log Analytics post that failed, a profile it was built on that
  was partial). Unknown is `run`.
- *The data sync* (`Invoke-SIDataCarryReports`, before the collection is marked `Complete`): the rows this run stored for the
  report are kept; the rows of the report's LAST COMPLETE collection that this run did not return are carried in, each marked
  with that collection's time (`sidata.Finding.CarriedFrom`) -- the same finding (report, asset, finding id) is never there
  twice, and the earlier collection is never touched. A carried result has no age limit: a report that could not be
  completed always carries its last complete result, however old, and says from when it is. With no complete earlier
  result at all, this run's rows are
  shown, marked as not complete -- and nothing of the report is closed either way. What was done is kept per collection and report (`sidata.CollectionReportCarry`: from which collection, rows
  carried, rows this run stored, the reason). With scope `reports` the collection is marked `per report` and the web app says
  which reports show their last complete result ("from <date> -- this run's report could not be completed"; badge "some
  reports earlier"); with any other scope it is marked partial as a whole, as before. The data sync's run carries a warning
  per such collection -- never a hold. A database the updater has not updated yet is said once and marked as a whole.
- *The closes*: the vulnerability close-loop and the finding lifecycle read the verdicts of the collection
  (`Resolve-SIReportScopedComplete`). A run that ended `success-partial` with scope `reports` is complete for every other
  report: what is gone from them closes as usual. An open record or finding that an incomplete report found -- or that names
  no report -- is frozen (never counted absent, never closed). Scope `run`, no scope, no verdicts, a failed run or a database
  that cannot be read: nothing closes, as before.
- *Data out*: the findings of an incomplete report that this run does not have stay as last sent (never "no longer sent"),
  and a file keeps their last row; the summary keeps that report's groups.
- *What still holds a whole collection*: a run that failed, a source that dropped out, rows without their key columns, a run
  that was partial for a reason that is not one report -- the hold and its release as before. Summary rows Risk Analysis
  writes itself are not carried (they are complete as written).
### The SI baseline dataset (v3, #455)

**The field catalog is the baseline.** `data-model/field-catalog.locked.json` defines every SI field once (name, classes,
type, group, level, join, resolution, pii, description). The baseline is its `record` / `both` fields that are not
computed (~150): what a provider record carries after its mapping, and what the CI resolves.

**Who fills a field is never a second list.** `Get-SIFieldProviders` (`engine/data-model/SI-FieldBaseline.ps1`) derives
it from the provider mappings (`data-model/mappings/<provider>.locked.json`): per field the providers, record types and
source paths. An `authority` field's order must have a place for every provider that fills it (a CMDB provider's place is
the `cmdb_owner` token) -- `Test-SIDataModel` refuses a mapping that has none, because such a value would only ever win
when nothing else is there.

**Complete for Risk Analysis.** `Get-SIFieldBaseline` reads every report of `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml` that reads
a v2 profile table, collects the profile columns it names, and checks each against the column map of
`risk-analysis-detection/ra-ci-migration.locked.json` (the #505 work: an SI field, an expression over SI fields,
`provider` when the report keeps reading that column from a provider table, or dropped with its reason); every SI field
the map names must be in the catalog. The identity profiler's look-ups no provider object carries (role and permission
look-ups, privilege tiers, break-glass, credential expiry, shadow admin, service account ...) reach the Entra record of
the same object as its `profile` part (`Add-SIRecordPartsFromProfileRows`), so the mapping fills them like any provider
field. Gaps are reported, never fatal: `ra-column-unmapped`, `ra-field-missing`, `no-provider`, and
`authority-no-mapping` (an authority order that names a provider with no mapping for the field -- informational).

**Raw data** stays outside the baseline: `SI_RawData` (off by default) keeps a provider's whole object as
`properties_<provider>_raw` in `SI_RecordRaw_CL` (with `SI_LaExport = records`).

### Mapping templates through the template channel (v3, #456)

**Used at collection.** Every provider object a profiler reads becomes a record through its provider's mapping (`SI field
<- source path(s) + normalisation`, `engine/data-model/SI-FieldMapper.ps1`, closed operation set); the record writer
(`Publish-SIRecords`), the CI build and the outputs load the model with `Get-SIDataModel`, which reads the folder
`Get-SIDataModelRoot` names.

**Community** (files): `data-model/<template>.locked.json` shipped, `<template>.custom.json` beside it holding only the
items that differ (per item: override, `remove`, own item; `baseHash` -> UpgradeAvailable). A container gets the custom
files through the install's overlay (`sioverlay`, `^data-model/(mappings/|outputs/)?<name>.custom.json$`).

**Pro** (SQL): the data model is the template kind **`datamodel`** (`engine/pro-settings/SI-DataModelTemplateRows.ps1`),
one `cfg.Template` row per item -- a field, a mapping, a value-map document, a factor, a list, a trust entry, a coverage
check, an output column -- plus one header row per template file (the document without its items):

| item key | what |
|---|---|
| `field-catalog` / `mappings/mde` | the template's header (kind, version, objects ...) |
| `field-catalog:si_os_version` | one field |
| `mappings/mde:si_asset_name\|device\|` | one mapping (the file merge's own key; a repeat `#2`; a key over 128 characters keeps its first part + `~<12 hex>`) |
| `outputs/servicenow-ci:u_tier` | one output column |

The customer overrides, disables or adds ONE item (`cfg.ItemOverride`) on Template conformance; an item's body must give
back the key it is stored under. At run start the settings layer merges templates and overrides per item and
**materialises** `<run>\data-model\<template>.locked.json` (shipped order, own items after; a template file with no rows
is copied from the installation), validates the whole model (`Test-SIDataModel` -- an override that breaks it stops the
run with the reason, like every refused item) and sets `$global:SI_DataModelRoot`; the engines' own loaders read it.
**Classification `fix`**: installed with the code by setup and by every update (`Publish-SITemplates`, the split
install), never held -- so an existing install converges on its next update (framework §12.16); an override is never
changed: when the shipped item moves under it the conformance view says UpgradeAvailable with both diffs. Detection
method per template file: `datamodel/field-catalog`, `datamodel/mappings-mde`, ... (engine and web app, same rule).

### Source of truth on the CI, with conflicts (v3, #459)

Each SI field on a CI is resolved from its linked records by the field's catalog policy (`Resolve-SICiField`): only
**fresh** candidates count -- the record's provider timestamp (`si_source_last_seen`, from the mapping object's
`timestamp`: MDE heartbeat, Entra device sign-in, Intune sync, EG last seen, AD `lastLogonTimestamp`, ...; none = the
collection time) within the field's `staleDays` (7 / 30 / 90) -- and the first provider of the field's `authority` order
wins; with nothing fresh the newest value is kept and marked stale. Risk booleans resolve any-true, lists union, first /
last seen min / max. `si_field_sources` records the winner (provider, record, observed at, stale) and, for an authority
field, the **conflicts**: other fresh providers holding a different value (`SI-FieldResolution.ps1`, at most 5) -- shown
on the CI page as "Other sources say", never deciding, outside the CI's content hash (a conflict alone does not rewrite a
CI).
### Enrichment on the CI — one generic rule model (v3 P3, #462)

Results live **on the CI** (never on a linked object). `Invoke-SICiEnrichment` (`engine/data-model/SI-CiEnrich.ps1`) runs
per CI, in this order: rules → manual overrides → the owning CMDB's record → criticality → risk factors.

- **Two rule sources, one CI-rule shape.** (1) The `AssetProfileBy*` rule files (DeviceType, IPSubnet, LogonUser,
  ApplicationServiceDetection, ExtensionAttributes, GroupMembership, Tags, CmdbTag …) are converted once per run onto SI
  fields (`ConvertTo-SICiRules`; a kind is a condition over SI fields, never a provider column). (2) **Native rule
  packs** in the design's own shape (`data-model/rules/<Pack>.locked.yaml`, customer `*.custom.yaml` beside it or under
  `<SI_DataModelOverlayRoot>/rules/`; `SI-CiRules.ps1`): `id, stage, priority, applies_to, mechanism, when, set`, a
  condition is `<si field>: { <op>: <value> }` over the closed operation set; a provider column or an unknown operation
  is refused; the override grain is one rule. A **pack** (the file / the `AssetProfileBy*` family) is a grouping and a
  label, not an engine path; every claim carries it.
- **AssetTagging in the model.** `data-model/rules/AssetTagging.locked.yaml` states the tagging engine's auto-exclusion
  tags over `si_onboarding_status` / `si_asset_name`; its `AutoExcludeRules.*` switches and `DeviceNamePatterns`
  (`config/asset-tagging.config.json`) apply. The engine still writes the tags to Defender (a writer, unchanged); the CI
  carries the same decision. **An exclusion is the customer's choice, never a default (#643):** every tag of the pack is an
  exclusion (`<bucket>--Excluded--SI`, which every report honours through the data-model list `excluded_asset_tags`), so a
  rule runs ONLY when its switch is `true` -- no file, no switch, false or a non-boolean = the rule is `not_used`. That is
  how the tagging engine (`Test-TaggingConfigFlag`), the Pro GUI (`GatesFormModel.Flag`) and the shipped sample (every
  switch false) always read it; the CI side read "no file = on" until 2026-10-13, so from the 10-12 CI build 774 of 1,890
  device CIs at a large install (704 of them onboarded in Defender) carried `Auto-CanBeOnboarded--Excluded--SI` and left
  every report although nobody had chosen it. The check side (`si_tags_ has_any ("--excluded--si")`) was right and is
  unchanged. CI build version 8 rebuilds every CI once, so the tags come off at the next build.
- **Asset tagging is OFF by default -- one customer setting governs it (#643, owner 2026-10-13: "tagging must be disabled by
  default. customer must enable it in settings"; "switch off in code").** `SI_AssetTagging_Enabled` ("Asset tagging",
  card Asset tagging, both editions; only a real true is on, missing = off). **Off:** every rule of the AssetTagging pack
  is `not_used` whatever its `AutoExcludeRules.*` switch says and carries `strip_tags`, so the CI build also takes the tags
  those rules name off a CI when a provider brings them back (a tag an earlier tagging run wrote to Defender) -- no report
  treats a device as excluded because of a tagging rule; the Pro tagging job is not started (dispatch Skip); the
  Community/server engine never writes (`Resolve-SIAssetTaggingRunMode` -> report only, Source `tagging-off`, even with
  `-Apply` or `SI_AssetTagging_Apply`). A customer's own exclusion tags (any other name ending in `--Excluded--SI`) keep
  working. **On:** the rules apply inside SecurityInsight per their switches; WRITING to Defender / Azure / Entra stays the
  separate opt-in (`SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply`, `SI_AssetTagging_Apply` / `-Apply`). Existing installs reach the new
  default with the release itself: the setting is new, so no install holds a value and the code default (off) applies;
  CI build version 8 rebuilds every CI once, which takes the stored rule tags off. Not covered: the attack-path reports read
  Exposure Graph node tags directly (`EgNodeTags` against the exclusion list), so a tag an earlier tagging run WROTE to
  Defender still excludes there -- such a tag exists only where a customer had switched both a rule and writing on.
- **Two truth stages.** `stage: production | testing | not_used` on a rule file (read by `Get-SIRuleSet` since #462 — it
  was dropped before) or a native rule. A claim decides only when its stage is production and its mechanism is trusted
  and fresh (the trust list, 2.19.2); otherwise it is recorded with the reason and **its effect is a proposal**
  (`si_rule_proposals`: rule, stage, reason, field, current, proposed — "testing rule X would set Tier 1").
- **Conflict resolution.** Tier: `MIN` over the deciding claims (the default-tier rule only when none decided). Other
  single values (purpose, category, CMDB id/name/criticality/sensitivity): the **highest-priority** deciding rule
  (`priority`, default 100); equal priorities keep the order before #462 (the winning tier claim, then trust position,
  then rule order). Tags: union, each with its source.
- **Precedence 1 — manual overrides.** `sidata.CiOverride` (CiId, Field, Value, **Reason**, SetBy, SetAt, **ExpiresAt**,
  Removed): the build reads every override in force once per run (a database without the table has none) and applies it
  over the rules — `si_tier_set_by = override`, the reason in `si_tier_reason`, the rules' value kept in `si_overrides`
  and in `si_tier_claims`. Overridable: tier, purpose, category, department, `si_cmdb_*`; never the lifecycle.
- **Tier trace** (`si_tier_claims`): rule, name, stage, mechanism, tier, admissible, reason, winner, evidence (fields) +
  `priority`, `pack`, `evidence_detail` (field, value, provider from `si_field_sources`) and, for a claim that did not
  decide, `would_set`. Since #579 also `label` (the purpose it sets, else the rule name's first line), `kind`
  (rule | tag | default) and `matched` (the VALUES that made the claim true, in words: "Defender tag PAWDevices--tier0--SI",
  "installed software microsoft/sql_server", "name dc1" -- `Get-SICiConditionMatches` + `ConvertTo-SICiEvidenceText`).
- **Who decided the tier (#579).** `si_tier_set_by`: `rule` (an observed SI rule), `tag` (the operator's tier tag -- an
  asserted claim, it decides only when no observed rule claims a tier and always beats the default), `default` (nothing
  claims), `override` (a manual override, precedence 1). A claim's **mechanism is the evidence that matched**: for an
  any-rule the best-placed of its matching detections in the trust list, never the rule's first detection kind.
  **A bare tier pattern is no evidence of a role**: a machine-tag pattern that says only a tier (`(?i)tier.?0`) matches
  every operator tier tag, so it is not in the shipped rule files and the converter ignores it in a custom rule
  (`Test-SIBareTierTagPattern`; the profile's `RuleEval` does the same). Root of the 2026-10-11 defect: 183 detections
  carried one, so a PAW tagged `PAWDevices--tier0--SI` claimed "Domain Controller" and "AD CS Server" as observed rules,
  and -- ranked as installed software by its first kind -- beat the real PAW rule at the same tier.
- **The tier in one sentence (#579, `si_tier_explanation`, `Get-SICiTierExplanation`, PURE).** Built from what the build
  decided (si_tier, si_tier_set_by, si_tier_claims, si_overrides) in the customer's words, no internal ids:
  `Tier <n> -- <who>. Also claimed: <claim> (<why it lost>); ...` where who is `SI rule <label> (<matched>)`, `your tag
  <tag>`, `manual override by <who>: <reason> (until <date> | no expiry)` or `the default tier (no SI rule or tag claims
  one)`; each other claim on the tier says why it lost: a higher tier number (the lowest wins), the same tier (another
  claim decided first), a tag counts only when no SI rule decides, the default applies only when nothing claims, the
  manual override decides, or it is not used (testing / untrusted / stale). Lowest tier first, then rule / tag / default;
  at most four, then "and N more". Re-built after an override. Posted to SI_CI_CL with a SLIM `si_tier_claims` (the claims
  on the tier: rule, label, kind, tier, admissible, winner, reason, matched -- the evidence detail stays in sidata.Ci).
  Web app: a default column of the CIs (whole, never cut), a filter "Tier decided by" (`tiersetby`), and on the CI page
  the sentence in full with the claims on the tier as a small table. *Before #579 si_tier_claims was in SI_CI_CL only
  until the column contract (2026-10-09): it was never in `$script:SICiPostFields`.*
- **The rule behind a claim (`rule_key`).** Every claim of `si_tier_claims` carries the key of the rule that made it:
  `<engine>/<rule id>`, the engine being the folder the rule file lies in (endpoint, identity, azure or shared) and the
  id the rule's own id (`Get-SICiRuleKey`, set when the rules are converted for the CI build). It is the key a rule
  change names -- turn the rule off, move it to another tier, put it back -- so the tier board offers those as buttons on
  the claim itself and nobody types a key. The key is empty for a claim no such rule made: the operator's tier tag, a pin
  set for one asset, a rule of a rule pack. It is data for the buttons only: the tier explanation and the tier reason do
  not carry it, and it is kept in the CI document, not in the slim claims posted to SI_CI_CL. A CI document written
  before the claims carried a key gets one when the CI is next built (the rules are part of the build fingerprint, so
  that is the first run after the update).

- **One CMDB owner (#463).** `SIWeb_CmdbSource` (`Get-SICmdbOwner`: cmdb | servicenow) is the tenant's one CMDB truth.
  The catalog's `cmdb_owner` authority resolves to it and a `si_cmdb_*` field takes values from the owner's records only
  (`Resolve-SICiField -CmdbOwner`). The CMDB join (`Set-SICiCmdb`) uses the owner's index (`Get-SICiCmdbIndexForOwner`):
  SI's CMDB cache, or the external owner's `cmdb_ci` records in `sidata.CiRecord` (`New-SICiCmdbIndexFromRecords`) — SI's
  own CMDB is then not read. The CI gets name, class, criticality, data sensitivity, environment, owner, owner department,
  service, support group, `si_cmdb_source`, match rule + confidence; a rule's value still wins (precedence 2).

- **The work per CI, and the threads (#739, 2026-10-17).** A rebuild of every CI is almost all in-memory work per CI --
  assembling the fields from the records, the rules, the risk factors, the classification -- so that work is kept small
  without changing a single CI: no pipeline in a per-CI step; two texts are compared in place (trimmed, without case --
  what the value comparison does); a classification row, a factor leaf or an entry of a conditions list that reads a field
  the CI does not carry is decided without evaluating it (it can only be false); the factor catalog is read once per set of
  CIs. The same CIs come out, CI for CI (proven against the released build). On a PowerShell 7 job with more than one CPU
  the CIs of a batch are enriched on several threads (`SI_CiParallel`, default the job's CPUs); the threads read the same
  rule and catalog objects, and PowerShell builds an object's property list the first time it is read -- read for the first
  time on two threads at once, it can come back empty and the batch failed ("CI enrichment failed on 1 of 8 chunk(s)").
  `Initialize-SICiSharedObjects` therefore reads every shared object's property list once, on one thread, before the threads
  start.

### Findings and history per CI (v3, #464)

- **Findings, de-duplicated.** Risk Analysis's Detailed rows → one finding per `(si_ci_id, finding key)` (`RA-Findings.ps1`
  → `SI_Finding_CL` → `sidata.CiFinding`); every report that found it in `si_detected_by`; the highest severity, and
  `si_severity_sources` (report → severity) when the reports disagree.
- **"Copy findings per CI to Log Analytics (SI_Finding_CL)" is an optional output, OFF by default (#829).** Setting
  `SI_RA_Findings` (catalog type bool, default off, every edition; shipped `$false` in the shared defaults; on only for an
  explicit `$true` / `on` / `true` / `1` / `yes` -- `Test-SIFindingsCopyOn` in `RA-Findings.ps1`, the one rule Risk Analysis
  and the data sync both use; not set, `off`, `false`, `0` and anything else are off). Risk Analysis Detailed itself, its
  result in the database (`sidata.Finding`, keyed by `RaFindingKey` = the finding's `<CI or asset:<id>>|<key>`) and the
  report rows (`SendToLogAnalytics` → `SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL`) are not changed by it -- they are their own optional output (#830, below).
  - **Off (the default):** nothing is posted to `SI_Finding_CL`; the run log says so in one INFO line. The data sync makes
    the findings per CI from the newest complete Detailed result in the database (`Get-SIDataCiFindingFromDbSql`, set-based,
    the same semantics as the copy) -- the normal path, one plain OK line, Log Analytics not read. Only a database that has
    no keyed result yet (not updated, or no Detailed run yet) reads `SI_Finding_CL` as before.
  - **On:** the copy runs at the end of the Detailed run, **before** the run's run-health END record, so a run that has
    ended is a copy that has ended. The data sync reads `SI_Finding_CL` only when its newest collection is not older than
    the database's newest result, and only when it is settled (`Test-SIDataCiFindingCopySettled`, checked before a page is
    read): a Risk Analysis END record covers the collection time AND its newest row arrived at least 10 minutes ago
    (`LastIngest = max(ingestion_time())` in the count query). Not shown = the findings per CI are made from the database
    at once (one INFO line), never a read that is refused hours later; with no result in the database either, the stored
    findings are kept as they are (one WARNING, nothing closed).
  - **Shown as a writer:** the Pro web app lists it under **Connectors > Setup → Optional outputs to Log Analytics** with
    its state and a link to change it on the Settings page (Settings: Data & retention → "Where collected data goes").
  - **Every reader has its SQL source:** the data sync is the only reader of `SI_Finding_CL`; the finding lifecycle, the
    CI totals, the daily trend detail, the views and data out read `sidata.CiFinding` / `sidata.CiFindingState`, which the
    data sync fills from either source. The web app, the trend row, the close-loop and the workbooks never read it. Existing installs reach the new-install state without an update step:
    not set = off; a value an install set itself is kept.
- **Pro reads Risk Analysis Detailed from the database only; "Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics
  (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL)" is an optional output, OFF by default (#830).** Risk Analysis Detailed writes its result to
  the database itself (`sidata.Collection` + `sidata.Finding`; each row's `DetailJson` is the very row a Log Analytics copy
  would carry). Every SecurityInsight reader of that result reads it there:
  - **The vulnerability connectors** (`Invoke-SIVulnLoop.ps1`, `SI-VulnDesired.ps1` `Read-SIVulnSnapshotSql`): the newest
    Detailed collection of this edition in the look-back whose Risk Analysis result is complete (`Status = 'Complete'`, or
    completed by Risk Analysis and waiting for the data sync), never one the retention removed -- anchored on the newest
    one with a CVE finding, else the newest with any finding, exactly as the Log Analytics query anchored its snapshot. Its
    rows are read a page at a time on the table's own key (`FindingId`), each value from the row as Risk Analysis wrote it
    (the Log Analytics column names), and grouped per (asset, finding key) as the query's `summarize` grouped them
    (`Add-SIVulnSnapshotRows`: the first severity / name / title, the highest risk score, the lowest tier, the distinct
    non-blank values of every set and every output-scope field); every row with an asset id also counts for the
    snapshot's assets. Rows the data sync carried in from an earlier collection were never in Log Analytics and are left
    out. A resend of a collection the retention removed is refused in plain words (only the newest complete collections
    keep their rows). Without a Pro database the connector reads Log Analytics as before.
  - **The data sync** (`SI-DataSync.ps1`): the Detailed collections Risk Analysis wrote are completed from the database;
    `SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL` (its listing and its rows without a collection time) is read only while the copy is on --
    the fallback for a run whose result could not go to the database. Off: one plain line, Log Analytics not read for them.
  - **Data quality** (`SI-DataQuality.ps1` `Get-SIDataQualityReportSql`): the Detailed rows per report and the fill of the
    key columns (`RiskFactor_*_Detailed`, `CriticalityTier`, `si_component`) from the newest complete Detailed collection --
    the same numbers the Log Analytics query counted.
  - **The trend:** the day totals the data sync writes (`sidata.FindingDaily` / `AssetDaily` and their counted twins) are
    the trend; the web app's risk trend (average risk score per finding, findings, Very High / High findings, tier-0 assets
    with findings) and domain trend read them (`EstateQueries.RiskTrendAsync` / `DomainTrendAsync` over
    `ProDataSql.Trend`). The day's trend row in `SI_Trend_CL` is part of the optional copy: Risk Analysis writes it only
    with the copy on (`Test-SIRaTrendAtEnd -Copy`), and the trend job run by hand does nothing with the copy off.
  - **The web app's asset lookup** (the estate tools): the asset itself from the identity map (the profile tables, which
    Risk Analysis's own queries read in Log Analytics too -- a prerequisite), its top findings from `sidata.Finding` of the
    newest complete collection under every id of the asset (its CI key or the id Risk Analysis gave the row).
  - **Left in Log Analytics:** what Risk Analysis's own queries read there (`SI_CI_CL`, `SI_ObjectMap_CL`,
    `SI_AssetProperties_CL`, `SI_CIRelation_CL`, the `SI_*_Profile_CL` tables, `SI_AzureRecommendation_CL`) -- prerequisites;
    the run-health records; the top-risks tool over the Summary rows (the Summary report is optional and off by default).
    The Azure workbook in `preview/AzureWorkbook` is the customer's own use of the copy: it needs the copy on.
  - **The setting** `SendToLogAnalytics` ("Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL)",
    a bool, default off in every edition and every shipped place: the defaults file, the samples, the generated config
    file, the container's fallback, the guided install no longer makes the jobs with the copy on). One rule for its value
    (`Test-SIRaReportCopyOn` in `RA-Findings.ps1`: on only for an explicit `$true` / `on` / `true` / `1` / `yes`, so a text
    `false` is off). On: after every run, once its result is complete in the database, its report rows go to
    `SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL` (`SI_RiskAnalysis_Summary_CL` for the Summary report) and the trend row to `SI_Trend_CL`.
    Off: nothing is copied; the Excel reports, the mail and everything SecurityInsight shows are unchanged. The findings
    copy (`SI_RA_Findings`) follows the delivery from the database, whatever this copy is. Without a database (a run whose
    result could not go there) and the copy off, the run says in one warning that its result is kept only in its files and
    mail. Listed under **Connectors > Setup → Optional outputs to Log Analytics** with the findings copy.
  - **The values read on every finding are typed columns (#830 / #834).** The connectors' snapshot and data quality read
    some of a row's fields on every finding of a collection (876,000 at a large install). They are stored once, in the
    pass the derive already makes over the collection (`Get-SIDataDeriveFindingSql -RowColumns`, the row parsed ONCE per
    finding with `OPENJSON ... WITH`): `RaRowAssetId`, `RaRowSolutionVersion`, `RaRowCriticalityTier`, `RaRowSiComponent`;
    one column per output-scope field, already coalesced over its source fields in the readers' order (`RaScopeRiskRating`,
    `RaScopeCategory`, `RaScopeSubcategory`, `RaScopeClass`, `RaScopeComponent`, `RaScopePatchCycle`, `RaScopeOsFamily`,
    `RaScopeSubCi`, `RaScopeAffectedProduct`); and data quality's two fill flags (`RaFillRiskFactorProbability`,
    `RaFillRiskFactorConsequence`). Each holds exactly what the reader took from the JSON before (a list or an object as
    its JSON text, NULL past 4,000 characters or for a row that is not JSON). The rest the readers need is already typed
    on the finding (asset name, finding id, title, severity, domain, report, risk score). `sidata.Collection.RaRowsAt`
    marks a collection whose rows carry them; `IX_Finding_RaRows` (CollectionId, FindingId with every column read) serves
    a page or a per-report count without the wide rows. A collection derived before the columns existed, and a scope field
    no typed column holds, are read from the JSON as before. The schema change is additive; the index is built online
    after the schema file on a large table.
  - **Existing installs** reach the new-install state once (the update's step "report row copy",
    `setup/_shared/SI-ReportCopyDefault.ps1`, marker `cfg.InstallState 'ReportRowCopyDefault'`; a new install writes the
    marker itself): until now every guided install carried the copy on without anyone choosing it (the generated config
    file's `$true`, imported into the settings database as "<who> (import)"; the jobs' `SI_RA_SEND_TO_LOG_ANALYTICS=1`; the
    defaults file). A stored value that is on and was written by an import, setup or an update is set off, with its
    change-log row; a value a person set on the Settings page is kept (one line says so); with no stored value the
