    solution-wide value off is written, which the jobs read after their environment, so nothing on the jobs changes. A
    value someone once typed into the config file looks exactly like the shipped line and is turned off too -- the line
    says where to turn it on again.- **Two findings linked into one (#693)**, `data-model/recommendation-equivalence` (`SI-RecommendationEquivalence.ps1`),
  one group per id, `match`: **key** (the same recommendation under each provider's id or exact title, any CI);
  **link** (an operator's link on ONE CI: `owner`, the member keys -- any provider or report --, `canonicalId` = the
  finding that stays, `linkedBy` / `reason` / `linkedAt`; unlink = stage `not_used`, so the record stays and the change is
  reversible); **fold** (a meaning rule over the generic SI finding fields after mapping and normalisation -- lower case,
  spaces / underscores made one -- never a provider column: `evidence` and `canonical` conditions `{ field, pattern |
  equals }`, `on` pairs of an SI field or a named capture against an SI field). key and link resolve per row, so the
  database's finding key, the pager and the lifecycle see them unchanged; a fold applies to the CI's findings (the
  publish keeps a CI's rows in one batch while a fold is on): a finding meeting the evidence side that meets a canonical
  finding of the same CI is evidence on every such finding (report, key, title, severity, rule), its reports join their
  `si_detected_by`, and its key is an alias of the first (its history carries over) -- it is not a finding of its own.
  With nothing to fold into, it stays a finding. The canonical keeps its key, title, severity and exemption, so the data
  out (ServiceNow, SQL hand-off, Excel) emits it once with the same key. The report rows are never changed. Only
  production groups apply; the shipped fold rule (Defender for Cloud "Update <software>" onto Defender for Endpoint's
  CVEs of that software on the same CI) ships at `testing`.
  - **The manual link screen (Pro, Admin only).** *Link as one* on the shared action bar (`Actions/LinkFindingsAction.cs`):
    two or more findings of ONE CI (the owner Risk Analysis keyed each on -- the part of `sidata.Finding.RaFindingKey`
    before the first `|`), the finding that stays (default the most severe), a reason -> one item
    `recommendation-equivalence:link-<16 hex of SHA-256(owner + sorted keys)>` written by the one writer of
    `cfg.ItemOverride` (`Changes/FindingLinks.cs` -> `ItemOverrideRepository.WriteAsync`: one transaction with its
    `cfg.ChangeLog` row; audit `finding.link.create`). The finding page lists its links (members, which stays, who / when /
    why) and an Admin's *Unlink* (stage `not_used` + `unlinkedBy` / `unlinkReason` / `unlinkedAt`; audit
    `finding.link.remove`). The link is in force from the next Risk Analysis run, like every data-model change.
  - **The close-loop sends a linked finding once.** It reads Risk Analysis' report rows, not the findings, so
    `SI-VulnLinked.ps1` (`Merge-SIVulnDesiredLinked`) applies the same template with the same functions to its desired set
    (key / link: one entry under the canonical key -- the most severe severity, the highest score, the canonical member's
    report; fold: the evidence entry dropped while a canonical entry of the CI matches, on the title, the finding type and
    `si_affected_product`, which the snapshot carries while a fold rule is in production). A member's open record closes as
    `Linked` (`New-SIVulnSyncPlan -Linked`): at once, never as fixed, outside the close ceiling and the collapse floor.
  - **Promotion = one data change.** A fold rule goes live by its `stage` alone: Risk factors > *Make live* stages the rule's
    body with `stage: production` (Review & commit, `datamodel.item.stage`); Community sets the same in
    `recommendation-equivalence.custom.json`. Before that, `setup/Get-SIFindingFoldPreview.ps1` (read-only, Support session)
    shows on an install what the rule would fold, with the engine's own `Merge-SIFindingFolds` over `sidata.CiFinding`.
- **Lifecycle** (`SI-DataCiLifecycle.ps1`, after the data sync stored the newest findings): `sidata.CiFindingState`, one
  row per (owner = CI or `asset:<id>`, finding key): first detected, last seen, `open | reopened | closed`, close reason
  `remediated | asset_retired | no_longer_monitored | rekeyed | report changed`. A close needs absence in `SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns` (2)
  **complete** Risk Analysis runs (`Test-SIVulnSnapshotComplete` over the run-health heartbeats; unknown is never
  complete); an incomplete run changes nothing; a collection is processed once (`sidata.CiBuildState`
  `FindingStateSnapshot`). One set-based statement.
  **2026-10-25 an empty CI id is no CI id; a change of key is not a fix.** A finding no CI holds carries NO CI id (never
  `''`, which matched no CI and closed it as `no_longer_monitored`) -- in both staging paths and in the statement. An
  absent finding under an asset key that the collection reports under a CI instead (the CI's stored finding in
  `sidata.CiFinding` names the same asset id and finding key, and that CI's finding is in this collection) closes, after the
  usual absences, as `rekeyed` (after the CI's own reasons, before `report changed`); nothing else is called that. While a
  source is on its last good collection (`Get-SISourceDropoutOwners`), an open asset-key owner is unfrozen ONLY when its
  asset is proven to belong to exactly one CI (a stored finding or the CI link) and every source of that CI is current;
  everything unproven stays frozen and is counted (`Unlinked`, said in the data sync's log). One-time repair (REMOVE-ME):
  `SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair` off (default) / count (read only, per bucket) / apply (once, after a complete
  collection: an empty CI id becomes none; an asset-key row open under its CI too closes as `rekeyed`; nothing deleted).
  **#690 (34) a report that changed is not a fix.** Risk Analysis stores with every report verdict the fingerprint of what
  the report asks (`sidata.RaReportStatus.QueryHash`, additive nullable column; `Get-RAReportQueryFingerprint`: SHA-256 of
  its query as authored -- before the run's substitutions -- white space made one, plus its tier / severity scope). An
  absent finding closes as `report changed` (after the asset's own reasons, before `remediated`) when a report in its
  `DetectedBy` has, at this collection, a different fingerprint from the one at the latest collection up to the finding's
  `LastSeen` -- or is not in this collection at all while it recorded fingerprints (the report was removed). No fingerprint
  on either side = unknown = the reason is as before. The vulnerability close-loop applies the same rule per record
  (`Read-SIReportQueryHistory`, indexed once per plan by `New-SIReportChangeIndex`, + `Test-SIReportChangedSince`): close reason `Report changed`, never `Remediated`, never
  corroborated; a connector's close-code map leaves it as it is (only `Remediated` may map to a fix), the data out sends
  `si_close_reason` as it is, the finding model's `fixed` stays `remediated` only. Seen again, it reopens like any close; the
  one-time freeze repair treats it like `remediated`.
- **History** (`Get-SICiWriteSql`): before a changed CI is rewritten, `sidata.CiChange` gets one row per changed tracked
  field — tier (source = set-by, reason = tier reason), tier set-by, lifecycle, internet exposure, risk factors, the CMDB
  owner's values — per link added / removed, and per new CI, with the run id. Unchanged CIs write nothing. A database
  without the table skips it. `sidata.CiDaily` gains `OpenCritical/High/Medium/Low` and `FactorCount` (data sync).
- **Retention** (data sync): `SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays` 730, `SI_Pro_CiDailyRetentionDays` 400,
  `SI_Pro_FindingStateRetentionDays` 365 (closed rows).

**Not built here:** the Pro GUI for overrides and for staging / importing Invardia rule packs (the packs are files; the
existing template-pack mechanism does not carry `data-model/rules` yet); the P3a identities → P3b devices order inside
the CI build (the logon-user tier is still the endpoint profiler's derived field `si_frequent_user_tier`, a P1 derived
field as 2.8 allows).

### Every view honours the CI lifecycle -- active by default (v3, #855)

Owner 2026-10-21: *"we need to be able to trust all data"* / *"default filter is active, so it should be active only"*. Risk
Analysis keeps producing findings for CIs that are not seen or retired; what a view COUNTS is decided by the CI's lifecycle
(`sidata.Ci.Lifecycle`, the CI build's, from the install's windows -- never a day count of the view's own, #859).

- **The stamp (W10, the root).** The data sync stamps `sidata.Finding.CiLifecycle` from the finding's CI -- the CI id =
  AssetKey, else the CI that carries it as a linked object (`CiLink.NativeId`, primary and newest first; the key figures'
  resolution) -- in FindingId ranges sized from their measured time, BEFORE the collection is marked complete and before any
  aggregate is built (`Invoke-SIDataCiLifecycleStamp`, `engine/_shared/data-sql/SI-DataSql.ps1`). A finding no CI carries stays
  NULL; NULL counts as **active** everywhere (its asset is not known to be gone). `Collection.CiLifecycleAt` marks a stamped
  collection. Collections stored before the stamp count every finding as active (their trend days stay what they were); the
  newest and the published one are stamped ONCE by the next data sync (`Invoke-SIDataCiLifecycleRestamp`, step 4 (y)) and
  marked to be derived again (`DerivedAt` / `ResolvedVersion` NULL) -- the run's own steps then rebuild every aggregate,
  the context, the summaries, the remediations and the key figures of that collection. Bounded to those two collections.
- **The derived tables, per table (the smallest correct change).** A KEY (an asset has exactly one lifecycle, so the
  distinct-asset counts of two lifecycles add up): `FindingDaily` / `AssetDaily` (+ counted; `GROUP BY lifecycle, CUBE(...)`),
  `FindingPivotCell` (+ counted), `PivotCell`, `CiFindingSummary` (from the CI; NULL = built before, rebuilt once). A
  COLUMN per CI: `AssetRiskSummary` (+ counted, also its `Unclassified` findings for the Tier board's line), `Tier0Asset`
  (+ counted). BUILT OVER ACTIVE CIs ONLY -- their primary key `(CollectionId, Facet, Value)` / `(..., DepartmentId,
  Severity, Tier)` / `(CollectionId, Cve)` cannot take a fourth column in an additive schema, the Summary groupings' keys are
  the shared definition's own, and the remediations are a to-do list: `FindingFacet`, `DepartmentFacet`, `CveSummary` (+ the
  counted twins), `SummaryGroup` (+ counted; the DB statement only -- the Risk Analysis row path is unchanged), `Remediation`
  / `RemediationAsset`. Those pages offer no choice and say "active CIs only"; the findings browser and the CI list show the
  others. Unchanged (not asset counts or not in the sweep): What changed, the report previews, the service aggregates, the
  prepared context, the Domain -> Category pairs.
- **What is open, what is fixed.** A retired CI and a closed finding (`CiFindingState.State = closed`) never count as open
  on the CI (`Ci.OpenFindings / RiskScore / WeightedRiskScore`, today's `CiDaily`, and so what goes to ServiceNow -- W6 / W7).
  A close is FIXED only with reason Remediated: `VulnLifecycleDaily.ClosedFixed / ClosedRetired / ClosedOther` (W9), the
  department report's fixed count, the key figures (rc17 hotfix, W1).
- **Risk Analysis' stale flag** (`si_stale_` -> `si_ci_stale`) is the lifecycle's not seen (`RA-SqlStream.ps1`,
  `RA-CiContext.ps1`); `SI_ActiveStaleDays` only decides for a CI without a lifecycle. The KQL CI blocks of the locked report
  queries keep their own day window (a report-scope option, default off) -- regenerating the locked queries is a separate
  change.
- **The views.** ONE filter type in the web app, `LifecycleFilter` (`SI.Management.Core/ProData/LifecycleFilter.cs`): the
  address parameter `lifecycle` (the CI list's), default Active, `not_seen` / `retired` / `all`; its SQL predicate is written
  from the fixed state names only (NULL = active); its words with the numbers in force come from `CiLifecycleRules`. Every
  page that lets a person choose shows the shared control `Pages/Shared/_LifecycleChoice.cshtml` next to its "What you're
  looking at" line. The mails (department report, governance) read active CIs only (`Get-SIActiveCiAnd`).
- **The guard.** `tests/pester/SIv3-LifecycleReaderGuard.Tests.ps1`: a statement in the web app or the Pro engine's readers
  that reads the CIs or a finding-derived table without naming the lifecycle fails the build, unless
  `tests/lifecycle-readers.allow.json` names it (file, table, count) with its reason.

### The CI graph -- relations, service ownership, one finding model, history (v3, #493 / #494 / #495 / #496)

`engine/data-model/SI-CiGraph.ps1`, wired into the CI build (`SI-CiBuildRun.ps1`) and the data sync's finding lifecycle
(`SI-DataCiLifecycle.ps1`). Both editions (SQL in every install); the CMDB page's links exist in Pro only. It writes only
SecurityInsight's own database and its own Log Analytics table -- no system outside SecurityInsight.

- **Services own CIs** (`Set-SICiServices`, in the enrichment after the CMDB join, before the criticality). A CI belongs to
  a service by a link on the CMDB page (`cfg.vCmdbAssetService`, the authoritative CMDB's links -- the existing audited
  customer path), by a binding rule of the service model (`config/service-model.locked.json`, first match wins; Pro: the
  servicemodel template), and by its own CMDB record (`si_cmdb_id` / `si_cmdb_service`) -- in that order, one membership
  per service. The service's values come from the catalog (`cfg.vCmdbService`), a service model service, else the CI's own
  CMDB values. The CI inherits the STRICTEST: criticality and data sensitivity by the criticality mapping's factor
  (`Get-SICiCriticalityEntry`: the CMDB owner's vocabulary first), environment by the list `service_environment_order`,
  owner and department of the most critical service. Fields `si_services`, `si_service_keys`, `si_service_count`,
  `si_service_orphan`, `si_service_owner`, `si_service_criticality(_level)`, `si_service_data_sensitivity`,
  `si_service_environment`, `si_service_department`; the inherited ones are in `SI_CI_CL`. `Set-SICiCriticality` takes the
  inherited criticality / sensitivity when stricter than the CI's own (`si_criticality_source.inherited_from = service`), so
  the CI's findings are weighted by it. A changed CMDB link or service dirties only the CIs that used it: the service keys
  (`bsvc|<service>`, `bsvclink|<CI>`, `bsvcext|<old id>`, `bsvcname|<name>`, `Get-SICiServiceKeyHashes`) ride the CMDB key
  mechanism (`sidata.CiCmdbKey` / `CiCmdbRef`, #534) and a CI writes the keys it used with its CMDB refs
  (`Get-SICiServiceRefKeys`); the service model's binding rules can place any CI, so they are in the build fingerprint with
  the CI rules. The CIs with services are CI build version 2: the first build after the update rebuilds every CI once.
- **Relations are data** (`data-model/relations.locked.json`, template kind `relation`; `Test-SIDataModel` validates field,
  classes, target, idType / nodeType, reverse, confidence, stage). Per CI the build makes claims (`Get-SICiRelationClaims`:
  identifiers and nodes lower case, a resource group qualified with its subscription, no self relation); per batch ONE
  statement (`Get-SICiGraphWriteSql`) replaces the services (`sidata.CiService`) and claims (`sidata.CiRelationClaim`) of
  the CIs it rebuilt -- a full build every CI, an incremental build the CIs whose content changed (services and claims are
  derived from the CI's content, so an unchanged CI's are what they were). After the batches ONE statement
  (`Get-SICiRelationResolveSql`) resolves every claim into `sidata.CiRelation` (key = SHA-256 of from | kind | to type | to
  value): `ci` = that CI; an identifier = the CI that carries it (`sidata.RecordIdentifier` -> `sidata.CiRecord.CiId`), else
  the identifier itself; a still-claimed relation is refreshed at most once in 20 hours; one no claim holds is GONE (never
  deleted). `SI_CIRelation_CL` gets the changes, and every active relation with the weekly full SI_CI_CL refresh or after a
  post that did not land (`RelationFullPostDue`).
- **History** (`sidata.CiChange`): the CI write tracks owner, owner CI, exposure level, service keys and the inherited
  values, and software per package; the graph write records memberships added / removed; the relation statement
  `relation` / `relation_in` rows; the lifecycle statement every finding opened / reopened / closed. The first build of the
  graph records no membership or relation history (`sidata.CiBuildState GraphSeeded`). The daily row gains lifecycle,
  exposure, services, inherited criticality, relations, overdue and exempted findings.
- **One finding model** (`Get-SIDataFindingModelSql`, after the lifecycle): `sidata.CiFindingState` gets type, title, owner
  (service owner, else CMDB owner, else the CI's owner), services, SLA days and due date by severity
  (`SI_Pro_FindingSla_<Critical|High|Medium|Low>Days`, 15 / 30 / 90 / 180, 0 = none; from the first detection or the last
  reopen), exemption reason / expiry (`cfg.Exemption`), the close-loop ticket's state (`vuln.VulnerabilityItem`) and
  `Excluded` (#533). Read: `sidata.vCiFindingModel` (status open / reopened / exempted / fixed / closed; overdue never for an
  excluded or exempted finding), `sidata.vServiceFinding`, `sidata.vServiceCi`, `sidata.vCiUnowned`, `sidata.vCiRelation`.
- **Web app** (`CiGraphViews.cs`, read-only): the CI page shows Business services, Relations (to / from, ended ones kept),
  Findings and their lifecycle, What changed; the CMDB service page lists the CIs the service owns with their open /
  overdue findings; the CI grid filters unowned CIs (`si_service_orphan`).

### More sources in the model -- on-premises AD, Intune, the Defender inventory, AWS / GCP (v3, #497 / #498 / #499 / #500)

Every one is the ordinary path: a collector hands provider objects to the record capture (`Add-SIRecordPart`), the
mapping in `data-model/mappings/<provider>.locked.json` turns them into SI fields, and the CI build groups records into CIs
by their strong identifiers (`Get-SICiLedgerTypeMap`). Read only, REST only, streamed (each answer becomes record parts and
is let go), one code path for every tenant size. A source the tenant does not have is said in one plain line ("the source
is not present") -- nothing is read, nothing removed, never a failure. A read that does not finish marks its provider's
pull not complete, so nothing is read as gone (absence is not remediation).

**On-premises Active Directory, from the cloud signals first** (the decided order):
- **Entra's sync attributes, at every level.** The user read asks `onPremisesSecurityIdentifier`, `onPremisesImmutableId`,
  `onPremisesSamAccountName`, `onPremisesDistinguishedName`, `onPremisesDomainName`; the device read asks
  `onPremisesSecurityIdentifier` and `onPremisesSyncEnabled` (the same reads, the same permissions). They map to `ad_sid`,
  `ad_object_guid` (strong: they join), `si_sam_account_name`, `si_ad_distinguished_name` (the OU placement) and
  `si_ad_domain` -- a hybrid user and its AD account, a hybrid-joined device and its AD computer, are one CI.
- **Defender for Identity** (`IdentityInfo`, the read the identity profiler already makes) adds the distinguished name.
- **The Exposure Graph's AD computer accounts** (`Get-SIEgAdComputers.ps1`, a records-only source of the endpoint
  discover): the `computer-account` nodes, counted first, then read in hash buckets of at most 5,000 nodes
  (`SI_EgAdComputerPageRows`) -- the number of buckets follows the count. Each node is an Exposure Graph device record with
  its AD ids resolved from EntityIds or rawData (`node.SIEntityIds`: the SID, the object GUID). It joins the hybrid Entra
  device (`ad_sid`) and the Defender device when the graph names it; an AD computer no other source knows is its own device
  CI (the rule of the AD-only identity: an asset, not noise). AD identities (users, groups) already come from the Exposure
  Graph identity read (V3-DATA-MODEL 2.4.1).
- **The hybrid collector -- the later phase (CONTRACT ONLY, not built).** What the cloud does not see (the full OU tree,
  GPO links, full group nesting, computers no cloud service knows) comes from an OPTIONAL on-premises collector, the one
  on-premises component of v3 (an exception to containers-only for this collector alone):
  - *Runs* on a domain-joined host the customer chooses (Azure Arc machine / hybrid worker), PowerShell 7, LDAP through
    .NET `System.DirectoryServices` (no ActiveDirectory module), READ ONLY, with a read-only domain account or the
    machine's own identity; no write to AD, ever.
  - *Emits* provider `ad` records exactly as `mappings/ad.locked.json` describes (parts `computer` and `user`, keyed by
    `objectGUID`; plus parts `ou` and `gpo` and a `group` record type when built), paged (LDAP paged search) and streamed.
  - *Delivers* the records to the install as the other collectors do (the run's record hand-over through the install's
    storage, the identity the install grants), never to Log Analytics only; one run record per run (complete / partial /
    failed) so absence is read only from a complete run.
  - *Is a listed source* (the data-quality providers list already names Active Directory), with its own settings switch,
    off until installed; the cloud signals above keep working without it.
  - Joins by `ad_object_guid` / `ad_sid` -- the identifiers the cloud signals already carry -- so its records land on the
    same CIs.

**Intune devices** (`Get-SIIntuneContext.ps1`): `GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices` (compliance state, OS, primary user,
encryption, enrolment, owner type) plus the compliance policies the device does not meet and its Windows update rings, as
parts `device` / `compliance` / `updateRings` of an Intune device record, joined into the device CI by `intune_device_id`
and `entra_device_id` (Intune carries the Entra device id). Permission `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` (and
`DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` for the policies), read only: in the permission catalog, granted by setup, and an
update tells an existing install that has not granted it yet (the permission note). A refused read is "not permitted"
(the source is not present), never a failed collection; a tenant without the licence is said on every Entra device.

**Defender inventory on the CI** (`Get-SIDefenderFindingSummary.ps1`): per device, the vulnerabilities and the secure
configuration assessments are summarised into parts `vulnerabilities` / `configurations` (counts per severity, the top
items, the oldest / newest), and the SOFTWARE INVENTORY into part `softwareInventory` -- its own advanced hunting query per
page of 500 devices (`Add-SIDefenderSoftwareInventoryParts`; a device's product list is long), always read: `Installed`,
every product (`vendor/product` -> `si_installed_software`), and the products past or near their end of support
(`si_software_eos_count`, `si_software_eos`: "vendor/product version (status, date)"). A device without inventory rows gets
no part (unknown, never "no software"). The FINDINGS -- one per device and CVE, one per device and security setting --
arrive through Risk Analysis (the Defender vulnerability and recommendation reports) and become findings on the CI with
their lifecycle (`sidata.CiFindingState`).

**Resources in AWS and GCP** (`Get-SIMulticloudResources.ps1`, in the Azure discover after the Defender for Cloud
assessment summary): first Defender for Cloud's multicloud connectors (Resource Graph `microsoft.security/securityconnectors`,
environment AWS / GCP) -- none: the source is not present. Then ONE paged Resource Graph query over the assessments whose
resource is in AWS / GCP, summarised per resource: native id (AWS ARN / GCP resource name), cloud, name, type, region,
account / project, connector, and the assessment summary. Each resource is a Defender for Cloud record of type
`multicloud_resource` (class `cloud_resource`), keyed by Defender for Cloud's own id of the resource -- the id its
recommendations carry, so the Defender for Cloud recommendation report attaches each recommendation to the resource's CI
(a recommendation on such a resource is no longer rolled up to its connector). `mdc_native_resource_id` is a strong
identifier (ledger type `CloudNativeResourceId`), so the same resource seen by another source joins. Fields
`si_cloud_provider`, `si_cloud_resource_type`, `si_cloud_region`, `si_cloud_account_id`, `si_cloud_connector`,
`si_mdc_*`. Exposure Graph cloud nodes of AWS / GCP are a later source (their node labels are to be confirmed on a tenant
with a connector).

**Where they show.** Each provider is in the data-quality providers list and continuous discovery ("Records per source"),
and every run records its pull (complete / not complete) on the provider's collection. The heartbeat's `Sources` list is
the closed list of technical sources agreed with the update platform (Defender, Graph, Azure, Exposure Graph, Log
Analytics): Intune and the Entra AD attributes are Graph, the AD computer accounts are the Exposure Graph, AWS / GCP are
Azure (Resource Graph).

## Provider plugin contract

> A provider is a self-contained plugin folder under `v2.2/asset-profiling-providers/<name>/`. The engine talks to providers via 4 well-known PowerShell functions. Adding a new data source = new folder; no engine code changes.

### Folder layout

```
v2.2/asset-profiling-providers/<name>/
  manifest.locked.json         Required. Conforms to _manifest.schema.locked.json.
  Test-Connection.ps1          Required. Exports Test-<Name>ProviderConnection.
  Read.ps1                     Required when manifest.kind includes 'in'.
                               Exports Read-<Name>ProviderData -Engine X.
  Write.ps1                    Required when manifest.kind includes 'out'.
                               Exports Write-<Name>ProviderData -Engine X -Rows.
  Connect.ps1                  Optional helper exposing connection setup.
  schema-fragment.json         Optional. Provider-specific schema additions.
  sample/                      Optional. Sample data for offline testing.
```

A worked layout for a read+write provider:

```
asset-profiling-providers/
  _manifest.schema.locked.json                provider-manifest JSON-Schema
  entra/
    manifest.locked.json
    Read.ps1                                  bulk pull
    Test-Connection.ps1
  generic-cmdb/
    manifest.locked.json
    Refresh-CmdbCache.ps1                     daily cache refresh
    CMDB.csv                                  customer drop-in (gitignored)
    sample/
      CMDB.csv                                shipped sample
```

### manifest.locked.json

One per provider — never `manifest.json`. Conforms to `_manifest.schema.locked.json`.

| Field          | Type    | Required | Notes                                                                  |
|----------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `id`           | string  | yes      | Lowercase, dash-separated. Matches the folder name.                    |
| `kind`         | string  | yes      | `in` (read-only data source), `out` (sink), or `both` (read + write).  |
| `engines`      | array   | yes      | Engines this provider serves (`identity`, `endpoint`, `azure`, `publicip`). |
| `auth`         | object  | yes      | `{ type: spn|umi|api-key|none, scopes: [...] }`                         |
| `bulk`         | bool    | yes      | `true` when `Read-...` returns all assets in N pages (no per-asset calls). |
| `rateLimit`    | object  | optional | `{ calls: N, per: '60s' }` for hint-only client throttle.              |
| `description`  | string  | optional | One-line summary.                                                      |

Example:

```jsonc
{
  "id":        "entra",
  "kind":      "in",                 // in | out | both
  "engines":   ["identity"],
  "auth":      { "type": "spn", "scopes": ["Directory.Read.All"] },
  "bulk":      true,
  "rateLimit": { "calls": 1000, "per": "60s" }
}
```

### Required functions

Every provider MUST export these (regardless of `kind`):

```powershell
function Get-<Name>ProviderManifest { <# returns manifest.json content as a hashtable #> }

function Test-<Name>ProviderConnection {
    <# Returns @{ Ok=<bool>; Error=<string?>; Detail=<string?> }.
       Must NOT throw on transport errors -- swallow + report via Ok=false.
       Should make ONE lightweight call (e.g. /me, $top=1, count=...).
    #>
}
```

When `kind` includes `in`:

```powershell
function Read-<Name>ProviderData {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Engine,
        [Parameter()]$RunContext
    )
    <# Returns array of [hashtable] / [pscustomobject] asset rows for $Engine.
       Use the engine's profile schema (profiles/<engine>.schema.json) field
       names. Bulk-fetch in pages; do NOT loop per-asset.
    #>
}
```

When `kind` includes `out`:

```powershell
function Write-<Name>ProviderData {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Engine,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][object[]]$Rows,
        [Parameter()]$RunContext
    )
    <# Pushes $Rows to the destination. Idempotent (same rows twice = same
       end state). Returns @{ Sent=<int>; Failed=<int>; Errors=[...] }.
    #>
}
```

The contract restated in table form — the engine only ever calls these four functions:

| Function                              | Required when         |
|---------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `Get-ProviderManifest`                | always                |
| `Test-ProviderConnection`             | always                |
| `Read-ProviderData -Engine X`         | `kind` includes `in`  |
| `Write-ProviderData -Engine X -Rows`  | `kind` includes `out` |

Adding a new provider is a new folder; no engine code changes.

### Engine integration

Stage Profile (and the Reconcile phase) discovers providers by scanning `providers/*/manifest.json`. For each manifest:

1. Filters by `engines` matching the current engine.
2. Calls `Test-<Name>ProviderConnection` (skips on Ok=false).
3. For `kind` in (`in`, `both`): calls `Read-<Name>ProviderData -Engine X`.
4. For `kind` in (`out`, `both`): calls `Write-<Name>ProviderData -Engine X -Rows $finalRows`.

The schema declares which providers each engine USES via `providers.in[]` / `providers.out[]`. Engine refuses to run if a declared provider is missing.

A folder-level lint rule enforces that no file under `engine/` references a path under `asset-profiling-providers/<x>/` directly — all access goes through `Invoke-Provider <id>`.

### Provider list at v2.2

| Provider          | Kind | Engines                        | Notes                         |
|-------------------|------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| `entra`           | in   | identity                       | Graph                         |
| `mde`             | in   | endpoint                       | Defender XDR Hunting          |
| `mde-identity`    | in   | identity                       | IdentityInfo + LogonEvents    |
| `azure-arg`       | in   | azure, public-ip               | Resource Graph                |
| `exposure-graph`  | in   | identity, endpoint, azure      | XDR ExposureGraph*            |
| `shodan`          | in   | public-ip                      | External REST + cache         |
| `loganalytics`    | out  | all                            | DCR via SI's REST ingest      |
| `generic-cmdb` | both | endpoint, identity, azure      | CMDB read (CSV) + write-back  |
| `local-files`     | out  | all                            | JSON / CSV / XLSX dump        |

**Which data collection endpoint a post uses.** An endpoint name alone is ambiguous (the ingestion module SecurityInsight used before 3.0 looked endpoints up by name only), so a tenant with several endpoints of the same name (in different subscriptions or resource groups) could have rules created on, and posts sent to, the wrong one -- and ingestion accepts a post only through the endpoint the rule is bound to. Every engine that publishes therefore chooses the endpoint itself, before the rule is created or updated and again right before the post: a rule that already exists posts through the endpoint it is bound to; a new rule is created on this install's endpoint (`SI_AzSubscriptionId` + `SI_DceResourceGroup` + `SI_DceName`). A single endpoint of that name anywhere is used as it is; several, with none in this install's resource group, stop the post with a message naming `SI_DceResourceGroup`. Rules are never moved between endpoints at run time -- a moved rule keeps refusing posts for a while.

### Reference implementation

See `providers/entra/` for a working example. It wraps the existing `discovery/Get-DiscoveryFromEntra*.ps1` functions in the provider contract.

## Asset-profiling data model & schema

> Consolidated from the machine-generated per-engine column reference (`docs/asset-profiling-schema.md`, generated by `asset-profiling-schema/tools/Build-SchemaDoc.ps1`) and the JSON authoring/loader reference (`SCHEMA-REFERENCE.md`). The single source of truth for the per-engine schema files is `engine/asset-profiling/shared/Get-SISchemaWithCustomMerge.ps1` — if a key isn't read there, the engine doesn't read it. Validated against `Get-SISchemaWithCustomMerge.ps1` (loader+merger, lines 86-170), `Build-EndpointProfileRow.ps1` (consumer, lines 699-810), `Test-SISchemaCompliance.ps1` (linter), and `SCHEMA.locked.json` (meta-schema). When code disagrees with this doc, code wins.

### Overview

SecurityInsight runs **four asset-profiling engines** (endpoint, identity, azure, publicip), each emitting one **flat-column table** in Log Analytics. Every customer KQL goes against one of these tables (or joins across them). Cross-engine joins use `PrimaryEntityId` (the first member of `EntityIds[]`).

| Engine | LA table | DCR | Field count | Schema version | Last modified |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| endpoint | `SI_Endpoint_Profile_CL` | `dcr-si-endpoint-profile` | 160 | 2.3.6 | 2026-04-29 |
| identity | `SI_Identity_Profile_CL` | `dcr-si-identity-profile` | 154 | 2.3.6 | 2026-04-29 |
| azure | `SI_Azure_Profile_CL` | `dcr-si-azure-profile` | 314 | 2.3.6 | 2026-04-29 |
| publicip | `SI_PublicIP_Profile_CL` | (publicip DCR) | — | 2.3.6 | — |

### Source legend

Every field carries a `source` telling you where the value comes from:

| Source | Description |
|---|---|
| `azure` | Azure Resource Graph + Az resource APIs — one row per Azure resource |
| `cmdb` | Customer CMDB (generic-cmdb provider, default-disabled). Folded onto `Properties.collect.cmdb` at Reconcile. |
| `derived` | Computed in the engine — Profile stage (drift hashes, IsEnabledActive, IsStaleAsset, AssetName, etc.) or Collect stage (PrimaryEntityId from EntityIds[0]) |
| `entra` | Microsoft Entra ID (Graph users + servicePrincipals + groups + signInActivity) |
| `exposureGraph` | Microsoft Defender Exposure Graph (ExposureGraphNodes + ExposureGraphEdges) — the v2.2 master discovery + property source |
| `mde` | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (advanced hunting / DeviceInfo) — machine-as-asset |
| `mdi` | Microsoft Defender for Identity (on-prem AD signal — investigation priority + sensitive group membership) |
| `signInLogs` | Entra sign-in logs |
| `shodan` | Shodan REST (publicip engine) |
| `ad` | On-prem Active Directory |

### Stage legend

Each field has a `stage` block: which pipeline phase WROTE the column (always exactly one) and which phases later READ it.

- **collect** — Stage 2 (Discover + Collect), pulls raw data from each provider and lands the row.
- **enrich** — Stage 3, joins cross-source signal (EG edges, Entra group membership).
- **profile** — Stage 5, derives flat-column verdicts (IsEnabledActive, UnsupportedOSDetected, IsStaleAsset, AssetName, …).
- **classify** — Stage 4, AI tier verdict + `Properties.classify.*` sub-tree.
- **reconcile** — Stage 7, folds CMDB matches + cross-engine references.
- **posture_analyze** — evaluates posture rules against the profiled row, emits `Properties.posture.findings[]`.
- **dashboard / sentinel** — consumed only by KQL queries and the Workbook (not written by the engine).

### Schema file pairs

| File pattern | Purpose | Edited by |
|---|---|---|
| `<engine>.schema.locked.json` | Shipped baseline column inventory for `SI_<Engine>_Profile_CL` | Maintainer |
| `<engine>.schema.custom.json` | Customer overlay (gitignored) | Customer |
| `SCHEMA.locked.json` | Meta-schema — vocabularies, DAG rules, contract for the per-engine files | Maintainer |
| `tools/Dedup-SchemaFields.ps1` | Linter / cleanup helper | Maintainer |

`<engine>` = `endpoint` / `identity` / `azure` / `publicip`.

### Top-level structure of a per-engine schema file

Each per-engine schema file is one JSON object:

```json
{
  "$schema":         "...",
  "engine":          "endpoint",
  "table":           "SI_Endpoint_Profile_CL",
  "dcrName":         "<dcr-name>",
  "extends":         "SCHEMA.locked.json",
  "sourcesConsumed": ["mde","entra","exposureGraph","cmdb","ad"],
  "entityIds":       { "primaryPriority": [...], "expectedTypes": [...], "hubJoin": "..." },
  "hashes":          { "CollectHash": {...}, "ProfileHash": {...}, ... },
  "rawPayload":      { "storageColumn": "...", "sources": {...} },
  "fields":          [ ... ],
  "aggregator":      { "contributors": [...] }
}
```

| Top-level key | Type | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | string | recommended | JSON-Schema draft URL. Documentation-only; loader doesn't validate. |
| `engine` | string | yes | One of `endpoint` / `identity` / `azure` / `publicip`. Used by the loader to key its cache. |
| `table` | string | yes | Target LA table (e.g. `SI_Endpoint_Profile_CL`). Read by `Invoke-Output.ps1` to route DCR ingest. |
| `dcrName` | string | yes | DCR name. Read by `Invoke-Output.ps1`. |
| `extends` | string | yes | Reference to `SCHEMA.locked.json`. Documentation-only — loader doesn't auto-load the meta-schema. |
| `sourcesConsumed` | `[string,...]` | yes | Discovery providers this engine pulls from. Lints against the source vocabulary in `SCHEMA.locked.json`. |
| `entityIds` | object | yes | Cross-engine join keys. `primaryPriority` = order tried when joining; `expectedTypes` lints incoming asset types; `hubJoin` = canonical id used in cross-engine lookups. |
| `hashes` | object | yes | Per-stage content hashes for cache invalidation. Engine doesn't write these; they're generated. |
| `rawPayload` | object | yes | Where source JSON blobs land. `storageColumn` = LA column; `sources.<src>.includePaths` = JSON-pointer list of fields kept in the blob; truncation strategy if the blob exceeds the LA cell limit. |
| **`fields`** | `[object,...]` | yes | **The big one.** One entry per LA column. See "Per-field shape". |
| `aggregator` | object | optional | Tier-roll-up rules: `contributors[]` lists the inputs the engine reduces over (one entry per AssetProfileBy* rule family + per CMDB source). |

### `fields[]` — per-field shape

Every column the engine ever emits to LA appears here exactly once.

| Key | Type | Required | Code (consumer) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | `Build-EndpointProfileRow.ps1:709` | LA column name. PascalCase, no `SI_` prefix. |
| `type` | string | yes | `:709` | LA type: `string` / `int` / `bool` / `datetime` / `real` / `dynamic`. |
| `purpose` | string | yes | `:701` (filter) | Semantic role — one of `identity`, `correlation`, `risk`, `posture`, `lifecycle`, `freshness`, `pivot`, `kpi`, `compliance`, `attribution`, `policy`, `enrichment`, `forensic`, `raw`. Drives which RA reports auto-include the column. |
| `source` | string | yes | `:704` | Origin: `mde`, `entra`, `azure`, `exposureGraph`, `derived`, `cmdb`, `signInLogs`, `shodan`, `ad`. Routes value resolution to `Resolve-SISourceValue` (or `Get-SIDerivedValue` for `derived`). |
| `sourcePath` | string | optional | docs only | Human-readable pointer into the source blob (e.g. `mde.machine.id`). Surfaces in `docs/asset-profiling-schema.md`. |
| `stage` | object `{writtenBy, readBy[]}` | yes | `:783-786` (hash bucketing); `SCHEMA.locked.json:111-119` (DAG validation) | `writtenBy` = single phase that emits the value (`collect`, `enrich`, `posture_analyze`, `classify`, `profile`, `reconcile`). `readBy` = list of consumers (`classify`, `dashboard`, `risk-analysis`). |
| `default` | any | optional | `:709` (implicit when source returns null) | Fallback. Type must match `type`. |
| `addedIn` | string | optional | docs only | Semantic version when the field landed (e.g. `2.2.0`). |
| `description` | string | optional | docs only | One-liner of what the column means. |
| `derivation` | object | required when `source: derived` | `:705` (dispatcher) | `algorithm` (e.g. `min_tier_over_catalog_match`, `pass_through`, `coalesce_then_default`); optional `inputs[]` listing field names the derivation consumes (DAG-validated — inputs MUST be `writtenBy` an earlier stage). |
| `emit` | bool | optional, default `true` | `:700` | When `false`, the field is computed but NOT written to LA. Internal-only artifacts. |
| `usedBy` | `[string,...]` | optional | linter | Which posture rules / aggregator contributors reference this field. Helps detect orphans. |
| `algorithm` | string | optional (in `aggregator.contributors[]`) | `SCHEMA.locked.json:203-222` | Tier-reduction algorithm for an aggregator contributor (e.g. `min_tier_over_catalog_match`). |
| `required` | bool | optional | not consumed | LA enforces nullability client-side; the engine does not. |

### Custom-overlay merge semantics

The engine loads BOTH `<engine>.schema.locked.json` AND `<engine>.schema.custom.json` (when present) and merges them via `Get-SISchemaWithCustomMerge.ps1` lines 86-170. The merged result is cached in `$script:_SISchemaMergeCache[$Engine]`.

| Section | Merge rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `fields[]` | by `name`: same name → custom **REPLACES** locked; new name → **APPENDED** | Override `OsPlatform.default`, or add a brand-new `MyCustomTag`. |
| `aggregator.contributors[]` | by `id`: same id → **REPLACES**; new id → **APPENDED** | Bump weight on an existing contributor or add a new tier-source rule family. |
| `rawPayload.sources.<src>.includePaths[]` | **UNION** (locked first, then custom additions, deduped) | Add extra MDE `DeviceInfo` fields without removing locked ones. |
| `rawPayload.sources.<new-src>` | new source bucket → **ADDED** | Add a custom source bucket like `tanium`, with its own `includePaths`. |
| `hashes`, `entityIds`, engine metadata, `extends`, `aiEligibility` | **NOT mergeable** — engine invariants | If you set them in custom, the loader ignores them. |

### Adding a new column / overriding an existing column

Add a column by creating `<engine>.schema.custom.json` with a new `fields[]` entry, then implement the value computation in the matching stage (e.g. `Invoke-Enrich.ps1`, routed via `Get-SIDerivedValue` because `source: derived`). The DCR needs an explicit update for the new column to flow into LA — the engine logs `SchemaDiff` each run (`Invoke-SchemaDiff.ps1`).

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "MyCustomTag",
      "type": "string",
      "purpose": "enrichment",
      "source": "derived",
      "stage": { "writtenBy": "enrich", "readBy": ["classify", "dashboard"] },
      "default": "",
      "description": "Tenant-custom tag injected via overlay for segmentation.",
      "addedIn": "2.2.0"
    }
  ]
}
```

To override an existing column, repeat the locked entry's `name` in the custom file. The custom entry FULLY REPLACES the locked entry — copy the locked block, edit, paste (e.g. change `OsPlatform.default` from `""` to `"Unknown"`).

### Engine consumers (where the schema is read)

| File | Lines | What it reads |
|---|---|---|
| `Get-SISchemaWithCustomMerge.ps1` | 34-180 | Loads + merges + caches |
| `Build-EndpointProfileRow.ps1` | 699-810 | `fields[*]` (name, type, source, purpose, stage, emit, derivation) — emits flat columns + the Properties JSON blob |
| `Build-IdentityProfileRow.ps1` | similar pattern | Identity row builder |
| `Build-AzureProfileRow.ps1` | similar pattern | Azure row builder |
| `Build-PublicIpProfileRow.ps1` | similar pattern | PublicIP row builder |
| `Invoke-Output.ps1` | output stage | `table`, `dcrName` — routes the row batch to the right LA table / DCR |
| `Test-SISchemaCompliance.ps1` | rule + schema lint | Lints the rule tree (`*.locked.yaml` / `*.custom.yaml`) and checks no `fields[].name` in a profile schema carries an `SI_` prefix. Run it directly: `.\Test-SISchemaCompliance.ps1` (add `-CustomOnly` for just your own rules, `-CI` for an exit code) |
| `Invoke-SchemaDiff.ps1` | DAG analysis | Compares schema between runs to detect breaking column changes |
| `tools/Dedup-SchemaFields.ps1` | maintainer-only | Detects duplicate `name` entries inside one file |

### Defender for Cloud recommendations — `SI_AzureRecommendation_CL`

Written by the **azure** engine's last stage (`Recommendations`), after the profile rows have landed. It reads
**every unhealthy Defender for Cloud (Secure Score) recommendation** from Azure Resource Graph (`securityresources`,
`microsoft.security/assessments`) across every subscription the engine identity can read — the same list a customer
sees in the portal. The Exposure Graph is not involved: a resource the graph does not know still gets its
recommendations.

- **One row per resource × recommendation.** Subscription-level recommendations are their own rows.
- **Sub-entities are rolled up, not dropped.** Container-image findings (one per package per image) roll up to the
  **registry** × recommendation, and cloud-posture identity findings roll up to the **subscription** × recommendation;
  `AffectedEntityCount` counts them and `AffectedEntities` lists every one. The highest severity and CVSS in the group
  are kept.
- **Never a partial list.** The read is paged to the end with a stable sort and retries throttling. If it still cannot
  be completed, nothing is published and the previous complete snapshot stays the latest — a shorter list would read
  as recommendations that were fixed.
- Columns: `ResourceId` / `ResourceIdLower`, `ResourceName`, `ResourceType`, `SubscriptionId`, `ResourceGroup`,
  `RowKind` (`Resource` / `Subscription` / `RolledUpEntities`), `Recommendation`, `AssessmentKey`, `Severity`,
  `RecommendationCategory`, `SecurityIssue`, `Categories`, `Tactics`, `Threats`, `Description`, `Remediation`,
  `ImplementationEffort`, `UserImpact`, `PortalLink`, `RiskLevel`, `RiskFactors`, `FirstEvaluated`, `StatusChanged`,
  `MaxCvssScore`, `AffectedEntityKind`, `AffectedEntityCount`, `AffectedEntities`, `PrimaryEntityId`, `CollectionTime`,
  `RunId`, `SubFindingCount`, `SubFindingMaxSeverity`, `SubFindings`. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.
- **The findings behind a recommendation are listed on it.** Where Defender reports a recommendation's detail as
  sub-assessments (for example a VM's individual vulnerabilities or a SQL database's vulnerability-assessment
  rules), every unhealthy one is read. They are attached to the recommendation's own row: `SubFindingCount` holds
  the exact count, `SubFindingMaxSeverity` the highest severity, and `SubFindings` lists each as
  "name [id] (severity)". A recommendation is therefore never counted twice. A finding whose recommendation is not
  in the list gets a row of its own. Very long lists stop short of the workbook's cell limit and say how many
  entries were not printed. Tenants on Defender's newer model expose this detail as the entity findings described
  above instead.
- Turn off with `$global:SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations = $false`.

The **Azure_DefenderRecommendations_Summary / _Detailed** reports read this table as their base and take tier, CMDB
values and tag exclusion from `SI_Azure_Profile_CL` by ARM id (a virtual machine is named by the machine it is -- its endpoint name -- as in every other report), and internet exposure from the same profile. Both carry
the remediation steps as `RecommendedAction`; the Detailed report also carries the description as
`ConfigurationDescription`. The **Azure_Recommendations_*** reports (Exposure Graph based) keep everything the graph
knows beyond Defender — for example per-setting machine baseline findings — and leave out only the resource ×
recommendation pairs the Defender reports already carry, so no recommendation is listed twice. That list of pairs is
read from Log Analytics before the Exposure Graph query runs and passed into it as one key column. A pair is matched by the resource's ARM id as well as by its name: the graph names a virtual machine by the machine (its device name) and Defender by its Azure resource name, so a name-only match would list every recommendation on a VM twice. A pair is also matched by the Defender
**assessment** itself -- the resource's ARM id and the assessment key, which the graph's recommendation edge names in
`rawData.recommendationAzureResourceId` (`<resource>/providers/Microsoft.Security/assessments/<key>`) -- so a
recommendation the two sources spell differently (a SQL database the graph names `db (server/db)`) is still listed
once. When the table is empty (collection turned off, or not yet run), nothing is left out.

**A recommendation whose graph node is missing is still reported (#349).** The Exposure Graph keeps "affecting" edges
after the recommendation's own node has gone from `ExposureGraphNodes` (measured on ring 1, 2026-10-05: 3,891 edges
from 81 recommendations, among them "Public network access on Azure SQL Database should be disabled" and "Audit flow
logs configuration for every virtual network", all still Unhealthy in Defender for Cloud). Joining each edge to its
recommendation node dropped them, and for a resource outside the subscriptions the install reads the graph is the
only source -- an open finding disappeared from every report. Such an edge is now reported from the edge itself: the
name, label and categories it carries for its source, and the assessment key from the assessment id it names.
Severity and security issue come from Defender for Cloud by that key (`SI_AzureRecommendation_CL`, the newest row per
key on any resource the install reads -- a recommendation's severity is the same on every resource); where Defender
has no row for the key (a per-setting machine baseline, or a recommendation seen only outside the install's reach)
the risk level the graph puts on the edge stands in. An edge whose ASSET node is missing has nothing to report on and
stays out. The rebuilt rows go through the same hand-off, exclusions, tier and scoring as every other row, so a
recommendation Defender already reports is still listed once, in the Defender report. Measured read-only on ring 1:
Azure_Recommendations_Detailed 426 -> 588 rows (Summary 296 -> 430); the SQL server and virtual network rows came
back; two database rows the Defender report already carried under another name left (they had been listed twice).
From the run in which the install's identity reads every subscription (ring 1 has Reader at the tenant root), the
Defender report carries these resources itself and the graph report hands them over as usual.

The **Device_Missing_CVEs_*** reports likewise combine the Exposure Graph's CVE findings with every CVE Defender
Vulnerability Management reports for a device (`DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`), so a device or CVE the graph has
not picked up is still reported. The optional CVE content filters (`SI_CVE_MinSeverity`, `SI_CVE_MinCvssScore`,
`SI_CVE_RequireExploit`, `SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays`) apply to both.

## Privilege-tier catalog

> Source of truth: `privilege-tier-catalog/privilege-tier-catalog.locked.json` — the AI-classified inventory of every AD group, Entra role, Graph API permission, and Azure RBAC role, scored on the attacker-centric Tier 0..3 scale. Validated against `engine/privilege-tier-classifier/Invoke-PrivilegeTierClassifier.ps1` (producer) and `engine/asset-profiling/shared/IdentityCatalogTierComputer.ps1` (consumer, lines 84-496). When code disagrees with this doc, code wins.

### File pair

| File | Purpose | Edited by |
|---|---|---|
| `privilege-tier-catalog/privilege-tier-catalog.locked.json` | Shipped baseline (AI-classified, reviewed) — every release can update it | shipped; never written on a customer install |
| `privilege-tier-catalog/privilege-tier-catalog.custom.json` (optional) | Your tenant's catalog: the classifier's output, including your custom AD groups and Entra / Azure custom roles. Laid over the baseline — same key = this file wins, keys only in the baseline still apply | `Invoke-PrivilegeTierClassifier.ps1` **rewrites it on every run** — do not edit it by hand |

`Initialize-SIIdentityCatalog` (`IdentityCatalogTierComputer.ps1`) reads the baseline and, when present, the
`.custom.json` beside it; absence is silent. In a container, a newer copy shared through the storage account is
taken first. **No other overlay file is read.** In particular `asset-profiling-enrichment/identity/PrivilegeTierClassifier.json`
(named by older versions of this document) has not been read since 2.2.25.

### Tier scale (attacker-centric)

| Tier | Means | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | One-step compromise of the identity plane / tenant | Domain Admins; Global Administrator; Privileged Role Administrator; Directory.ReadWrite.All |
| **1** | Privilege-escalation path (multi-step) | Backup Operators; Server Operators; Helpdesk Administrator; Owner (subscription) |
| **2** | Workload / data impact, no direct identity-plane path | Hyper-V Administrators; DnsAdmins; Reports Reader; Contributor on a single resource |
| **3** | Standard accounts — no escalation path | Users; Authenticated Users; Domain Users; Reader |

`Get-SIMinTier` (consumer lines 489-496) reduces over all signal sources for one identity and returns the **lowest tier number** (= highest privilege). When all sources return `$null`, default is **Tier 3**.

### Top-level structure

```json
{
  "Metadata": { ... },
  "AD_BuiltInPermissionGroups_Tier0":  [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "AD_CustomGroups_Tier0":             [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "EntraID_BuiltInRoles_Tier0":        [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "EntraID_CustomRoles_Tier0":         [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "EntraID_APIPermissions_Tier0":      [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "Azure_BuiltInRoles_Tier0":          [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...],
  "Azure_CustomRoles_Tier0":           [ ... ],   "...Tier1": [...], "...Tier2": [...], "...Tier3": [...]
}
```

### `Metadata` envelope

| Field | Type | Required | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GeneratedAt` | string (ISO 8601) | yes | `IdentityCatalogTierComputer.ps1:55` (freshness check) |
| `GeneratedBy` | string | yes | docs only |
| `TenantId` | string (GUID) | yes | docs only — sanitize to `<tenant-id>` in shared docs |
| `TieringModel` | string | yes | docs only |
| `AICallsUsed` | int | yes | docs only — one Azure OpenAI batch per provider category (typically 4) |

### Per-entry shape (per section)

Different sections use different key fields; the locked+custom merge uses these keys (case-insensitive).

**AD groups (`AD_*Groups_Tier*`)** — `Name` (string, required, **merge key**, lowercased lookup at `IdentityCatalogTierComputer.ps1:248,354`), `Tier` (int 0..3, required, line 356), `Reason` (string, required, shown in audit logs line 427).

**Entra roles (`EntraID_*Roles_Tier*`)** — `DisplayName` (string, required, **merge key**, line 177), `Tier` (int 0..3, required, line 379), `Description` (optional, AI classifier context).

**API permissions (`EntraID_APIPermissions_Tier*`)** — `Value` (string, required, **merge key**, HashSet O(1) lookup lines 203,341), `Tier` (int 0..3, required, line 341), `Description` (optional). Example `Value`s: `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, `Mail.Send`, `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory`.

**Azure roles (`Azure_*Roles_Tier*`)** — `Name` (string, required, **merge key**, line 282), `Tier` (int 0..3, required, line 407), `Description` (optional).

### Default tier behaviour (no-match)

| Provider | Lookup miss with non-empty input | Lookup miss with empty input |
|---|---|---|
| Entra roles | **Tier 2** (line 335) | `$null` |
| API permissions | **Tier 2** (line 345) | `$null` |
| AD groups | `$null` (line 369) | `$null` |
| Azure roles | **Tier 2** (line 369) | `$null` |

`Get-SIMinTier` (lines 489-496): excludes `$null` and `-1`; returns the smallest remaining number; if every signal is `$null`, returns **3** (safest fallback).

### Tier resolution and the default tier rule

An asset's tier is the MOST CRITICAL (lowest) tier any tier source claims for it: the tier rules, the privilege-tier catalog, logons, the owner of a public IP, a pin set on the Tier board. When nothing claims a tier, the **default tier rule** decides -- it is a rule, not a number in the code:

- `asset-profiling-enrichment/shared/AssetProfileByDefaultTier.locked.yaml` -- `fallback: true`, one detection per asset kind (`kind: assetKind`, `kinds: [endpoint]` / `[identity]` / `[azure]` / `[publicip]`), each **Tier 3** as shipped.
- A fallback rule never votes in the MIN: the rule loader returns it only when asked for the fallback (`Get-SIRuleSet -Fallback`), and `engine/asset-profiling/shared/Resolve-SIDefaultTier.ps1` applies it only to an asset nothing else gave a tier. The profile row then records `SI_TierSetBy = default` ("set by default" on the Tier board).
- Change it like any rule: a custom copy (`AssetProfileByDefaultTier.custom.yaml` in the shared folder or the operator overlay), the Pro Rules page, or a whole-rule move on the Tier board. Turned off (`mode: disable`), an asset nothing else classifies stays **Unclassified**. A SecurityInsight Pro install whose rule templates predate the rule uses the shipped file until its templates carry it.

**Findings on assets no profiler has seen.** Risk Analysis reports on what the Exposure Graph sees, which can be more than the profilers read (for example Azure resources outside the subscriptions the Azure profiler reads, or a subscription itself). For such a finding (a Detailed row without a tier) Risk Analysis resolves the tier from the same rule set, using what the finding knows -- its asset kind (from the asset type, an Azure resource id, or the report's domain) and its name: first the rules a name decides (name patterns, and every pin from the Tier board), else the default tier rule. Attack-path rows (their tier is the path's target), Summary rows and rows whose asset kind cannot be told are left as they are.

**Unclassified** means one thing everywhere: the tier is not 0-3. A finding's tier is its asset's tier -- the Pro data load gives a finding that arrived without a tier the tier of its asset. Every Unclassified count and label in the web app links to the Tier board filtered to the assets with no tier (or to the asset there), where an Admin gives the asset a tier: open its row and use *Pin to a tier* (staged, reviewed, committed and audited like every tier change). The *No tier* tile also says how many of the newest run's Unclassified findings are on an asset and how many name no asset at all (those cannot be listed).

### Your tenant's custom groups and roles

Your Entra and Azure custom roles reach the catalog by running the classifier
(`launcher\privilege-tier-classifier\launcher.community-vm.ps1`): it enumerates the AD built-in groups, the Entra
roles and API permissions and the Azure roles of your tenant (built-in and custom), tiers them and writes
`privilege-tier-catalog.custom.json` in the shape above. **Merge:** same merge key in the same section → the
`.custom.json` entry **replaces** the baseline's; a new key is **appended**; sections it does not carry are
untouched. A tier the AI could not evaluate in a run keeps the tier it had in the previous catalog.

Because the classifier rewrites that file on every run, a hand edit there does not last, and it does not enumerate
your own (non-built-in) AD groups. To decide the tier of the members of a group yourself, use a tier rule — for
example a group-membership rule (`asset-profiling-enrichment/identity/AssetProfileByGroupMembership.custom.sample.yaml`
→ copy to `AssetProfileByGroupMembership.custom.yaml` in the same folder and edit), or in SecurityInsight Pro a rule
on the Tier board.

### How the catalog is generated

`engine/privilege-tier-classifier/Invoke-PrivilegeTierClassifier.ps1` outputs `privilege-tier-catalog/privilege-tier-catalog.locked.json`. Runs in 4 stages, one batched Azure OpenAI call per stage:

1. **Stage A** — enumerate AD built-in groups (no member collection).
2. **Stage B** — enumerate Entra role definitions (built-in + custom).
3. **Stage C** — enumerate Microsoft Graph API permissions from well-known service principals.
4. **Stage D** — enumerate Azure RBAC role definitions (built-in + custom).

Each stage POSTs name + description to Azure OpenAI with the attacker-centric framework prompt; the classifier returns `Tier` (0..3) and an optional `Reasoning`, written into the appropriate `*_Tier{0..3}` arrays. Re-run when: a new custom AD group / Entra role / Azure RBAC role is created; new tenant onboarding; Microsoft adds new built-in roles. Requires Azure OpenAI credentials — defaults `AI_ChunkSize=50`, `AI_MaxRetries=5`, `AI_MaxTokens=16384` (set silently at script top). A throttled request waits as long as the service asks (`Retry-After`), otherwise backs off 5 → 10 → 20 → 40 seconds.

**A known tier is never lost to a bad AI run.** Items the AI could not evaluate this run — retries exhausted, OpenAI not configured, or AI turned off with `$global:SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI = $false` — keep the tier they had in the previous catalog, and their reason says so. Only a role or permission that has never been tiered stays at 99 (manual review). With AI turned off, nothing is sent to Azure OpenAI; the catalog still refreshes the role and permission inventory.

### Engine consumers

| File | Lines | Reads |
|---|---|---|
| `IdentityCatalogTierComputer.ps1` | 84-496 | All sections; computes per-identity `Get-SITierFromEntraRoles`, `Get-SITierFromEntraAPIPerms`, `Get-SITierFromADGroups`, `Get-SITierFromAzureRoles`; reduces via `Get-SIMinTier` |
| `Build-IdentityProfileRow.ps1` | per-identity emit | Reads computed tier + writes `Tier` column |

Endpoints don't read this catalog directly — they use a separate `EndpointCatalogTierComputer.ps1` keyed on machine roles. The `Tier` column lives in `SI_Identity_Profile_CL` per `identity.schema.locked.json`.

## Enrichment / detection rule model

> Source of truth for the `*.locked.yaml` / `*.custom.yaml` rule grammar used by the asset-profiling engines (Identity, Endpoint, Azure, PublicIP). Generated from `engine/asset-profiling/shared/RuleEval.ps1` (the kind handlers) and `Get-SIRuleSet.ps1` (the loader). Annotated canonical example: `_TEMPLATE.custom.sample.yaml`. If this doc disagrees with the code, the code wins.

### File-level fields

| Field | Required | Allowed values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string (PascalCase, no spaces) | Rule identity. **Must equal the file basename** (stripped of `.locked` / `.custom`). Engine deduplicates rules by `id` — a `*.custom.yaml` with the same `id` as a `*.locked.yaml` overrides it. |
| `appliesTo` | yes | `endpoint` / `identity` / `azure` / `publicip` / a list | Engine(s) that evaluate this rule. Cross-engine rules live under `shared/`. |
| `mode` | no (default `locked`) | `locked` / `disable` | `locked` = rule loads normally. `disable` = engine skips entirely (`Invoke-SIRuleEval` returns `$null` immediately). Any other value treated as `locked`. |
| `purpose` | recommended | string | Free-text description; surfaces in run logs. |
| `category` | recommended | string | Grouping label (`Server Roles`, `CMDB Mapping`, `Group Membership`, …); surfaces in `SIRules` array on each profile row. |
| `description` | recommended | YAML literal block (`|`) | Multi-line operator notes. |
| `detections` | yes | list of detection blocks | One or more detect→set blocks, walked in array order; the **first** detection whose `detect` matches wins (per-rule first-match). |

**Override semantics for custom files**: a `*.custom.yaml` always wins the dedup pass against its `*.locked.yaml` sibling with the same `id:`, and is then combined with it by its `mode` — `overwrite` (default) / `append` / `merge` / `disable`, as in *Custom override* above (#470).

### Detection-block fields (one per `detections:` item)

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Detection identity, globally unique within the rule. Surfaces as `DetectionId` in `SIRules[]`. |
| `detect` | yes | The match condition (see detect kinds). |
| `set` | yes | What to stamp on the row when `detect` is true. |
| `excludeAssets` | no | List of asset names / `-like` wildcards. When the asset's `Name` matches any entry (CI), this detection is SKIPPED even if `detect` would fire — evaluation continues with the next detection. Alias `excludeNames`. Use to exempt one legacy box from a single detection (e.g. compat-blocking software you can't remove). |

```yaml
id:        MicrosoftSystemCenter
appliesTo: endpoint
mode:      locked
detections:
  - id: MicrosoftSystemCenter
    detect:
      any:
        - kind: hasSoftwareInstalled
          tvmSoftwareNames:
            - 'microsoft/system_center'
    excludeAssets:
      - 'oldlegacybox01'            # exact name match (CI)
      - 'finance-svr-*'             # wildcard match (CI)
    set:
      Tier:     0
      Purpose:  'System Center role (excluded boxes get default tier)'
      Category: 'Application Service'
```

### `detect` — combine semantics

```yaml
detect:
  any:                  # OR -- fires if ANY child kind matches
    - kind: ...
  # OR
  all:                  # AND -- fires only if EVERY child kind matches
    - kind: ...
```

- `any:` = "match if asset shows EITHER fingerprint A OR B". `all:` = "match only if BOTH A AND B".
- An unknown `kind:` inside `all:` fails the whole `all:` block (AND-failure); inside `any:` that arm is skipped and the other arms still decide.
- **It is no longer silent.** `Get-SIRuleSet` reports every unknown kind once per run, with the number of detections affected — a typo in a `kind:` used to cost the detection an arm with no visible symptom at all. (Audit #35: an unregistered `nameMatches` did exactly that to 95 detections for the whole v2.2 lifetime.) The loader also names any rule that loads with **zero detections** (audit #36) and any rule file that fails to parse (audit #29). `mode: disable` is excluded from the zero-detection report — suppressing a locked rule is the one legitimate empty case.

### Detect kinds — exhaustive registry (12 total)

Straight from `RuleEval.ps1` `$script:SIKindRegistry`. These are the **only** kinds the engine knows; anything else in YAML is silently ignored.

1. **`nameMatches`** *(all engines)* — regex against display-name fields. `namePatterns:` `[regex,...]` (required; aliased `patterns:`). Fields scanned (first non-empty wins per pattern): `Name`, `Hostname`, `DisplayName`, `Fqdn`, `MDE_DeviceName`, `ENTRA_DisplayName`, `AZ_Name`.
2. **`osPlatform`** *(endpoint)* — regex against OS-platform fields. `osPatterns:` `[regex,...]` (aliased `patterns:`). Fields scanned: `MDE_OSPlatform`, `ENTRA_OS`, `EG_OS`.
3. **`hasMdeMachineGroupTag`** *(endpoint)* — regex against MDE machine-group string. `machineTagPatterns:` `[regex,...]` (aliased `patterns:`). Field scanned: `MDE_MachineGroup` (single string; can be comma/semicolon-separated when multi-group — regex sees the joined string).
4. **`egDetectedRoles`** *(endpoint, identity)* — `egSignals:` `[string,...]` (aliased `roles:`). Two match modes: (1) substring against joined `EG_DetectedRoles` (sourced from EG `confidenceHigh`/`confidenceLow` arrays); (2) boolean property against `EG_RawData` (e.g. `egSignals: ['isDomainController']` matches when `EG_RawData.isDomainController: true`).
5. **`hasEntraExtensionAttributeTag`** *(identity)* — `attribute:` (e.g. `extensionAttribute6`), `value:`, `match:` (`exact` default = case-sensitive full match `-ceq`; anything else = case-insensitive substring `-like '*value*'`). Reads in order: top-level `ENTRA_<attribute>`, then nested `ENTRA_ExtensionAttributes.<attribute>`, `ExtensionAttributes.<attribute>`, `extensionAttributes.<attribute>`.
6. **`hasSoftwareInstalled`** *(endpoint)* — `tvmSoftwareNames:` `[glob,...]` (PowerShell `-like`; shape `vendor/name` OR `*/name`, e.g. `microsoft/windows server 2019`, `*/sql server*`, `apache/tomcat*`). Requires the `tvmSoftware` bulk index (built once per run by `Build-SIRuleIndexes`); without it the kind silently returns `$false`.
7. **`groupMembership`** *(identity)* — `group:` (single name; no list — repeat under `any:` for OR-of-groups). Exact CI match against Entra direct+transitive memberships from `ENTRA_Groups`. Short-circuits to `false` for non-user assets (SP/MI). Requires the `GroupMembership` bulk index.
8. **`hasAzureTagDirectOrParent`** *(azure; also endpoint when EndpointAzureCorrelation has linked the row)* — `tag:` (KEY, exact CI), `value:` (string/list; omit = presence-only), `match:` (default `equal`). Walks parent chain: resource → RG → subscription → MG; matches if any level carries the tag. Requires the `parentChain` bulk index; looks up id from `AZ_ResourceId` (or `PrimaryEntityId` fallback).
9. **`egKustoQuery`** *(endpoint, identity, azure — escape hatch)* — `kql:` (raw KQL run against the EG endpoint; must return a column of asset IDs: NodeId/DeviceId/AccountObjectId). The engine submits the KQL once at run start and caches the resulting node IDs into `$script:SIRuleIndexes.kustoSets[<RuleId>]`; per-asset evaluation does NOT submit KQL — it's a hashtable lookup against `PrimaryEntityId`/`EG_NodeId`/`MDE_DeviceId`/`AccountObjectId`. Cost paid once per rule per run.
10. **`mostFrequentUserTier`** *(endpoint)* — `tierValues:` `[int,...]`. Endpoint inherits its tier verdict from the most-frequent interactive user (logon-graph inheritance). Reads `Metadata.MostFrequentUserTier` (stamped by `Get-SIBulkDeviceUserCorrelation` at Enrich, sourced from logon graph + `SI_Identity_Profile_CL`). Matches if device's most-frequent user tier is in the list.
11. **`ipInRange`** *(endpoint, azure)* — `cidrs:` `[CIDR,...]` (IPv4/IPv6, aliased `cidr:`), `fields:` (optional; restrict which Metadata fields to scan, default = all known carriers). Default fields: `MDE_EffectiveIpAddresses`, `MDE_PublicIp`, `MDE_LastIpAddress`, `EG_PublicIp`, `EG_PrivateIp`, `EG_LastIpAddress`, `EG_InternalIpAddresses`, `ENTRA_PrivateIp`, `ENTRA_PublicIp`, `ENTRA_IpAddress`, `AZ_PrivateIp`, `AZ_PrivateIpAddresses`, `AZ_PublicIp`, `AD_IpAddress`, `AD_IpAddresses`, `CMDB_PrivateIp`, `CMDB_IpAddresses`, `CMDB_ip`, `CMDB_private_ip`. Also parses `AZ_PropertiesJson` for `ipAddress` / `ipConfigurations[*].properties.privateIPAddress`.
12. **`hasTag`** *(endpoint, identity, azure — cross-source convenience)* — `tag:` (KEY, exact CI), `value:` (string/list), `match:` (default `equal`), `sources:` (restrict to `mde`/`eg`/`entra`/`arm`/`cmdb`/`ad`, default all). At least one of `tag:`/`value:` required. Three modes: **Mode 1 key presence** (`tag:` only — any source has that key with non-empty value); **Mode 2 value presence** (`value:` only, requires `match: in`/`regex`/`like`/`has` — plain `equal` value-only is REFUSED to prevent over-broad matches); **Mode 3 exact pair** (`tag:`+`value:` — also matches literal `key:value`/`key=value` strings inside value-only carriers like MDE machineTags).

   **Carriers walked**: `mde` (value-only list, `MDE_MachineTags`); `eg` (value-only + key:value, `EG_RawData.deviceDynamicTags`/`deviceManualTags`/`tags`); `entra` (key:value, `ENTRA_ExtensionAttribute1..15` + `ENTRA_OnPremisesExtensionAttributes`); `arm` (key:value, `AZ_TagsJson` direct + parent-chain inheritance RG/sub/MG); `cmdb` (key:value, `Metadata.CMDB_<col>` folded by Reconcile from CMDB.csv columns); `ad` (value-only list, `AD_GroupMemberships` placeholder).

### `match:` operators (used by `hasTag`, `hasAzureTagDirectOrParent`)

All operator names case-insensitive on name AND value; comparisons case-insensitive throughout.

| Operator | Behavior | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `equal` (default) | Exact string match (`-ieq`) | `value: 'production'` matches `'PRODUCTION'` |
| `like` | PowerShell `-ilike` wildcards | `value: '*-prod-*'` matches `'app-prod-01'` |
| `has` | Substring presence (regex-escaped) | `value: 'finance'` matches `'finance-2026'` |
| `regex` | .NET regex (`-imatch`) | `value: '(?i)^prod[-_]'` |
| `matches` | Alias for `regex` | (same) |
| `in` | Value appears in a list | `value: ['prod','prd']` |
| `startswith` | Prefix match | `value: 'prod'` matches `'prod-app-01'` |
| `endswith` | Suffix match | `value: '-prod'` matches `'app-prod'` |

### `set` — what to stamp on the row

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Tier` | int 0..3 | Engine's tier verdict. **0=Critical, 1=High, 2=Medium, 3=Low**. Engine reduces `min(Tier)` across all matching rules. |
| `Purpose` | string | Human-readable role label (e.g. `'Domain Controller'`). Surfaces on the profile row. |
| `Category` | string | Grouping label (e.g. `'Server Roles'`, `'CMDB Mapping'`). |
| `Tags` | list of strings | Free-form tags, aggregated across rule matches. |
| `cmdbId` | string | **OPTIONAL.** Foreign key into `asset-profiling-providers/generic-cmdb/CMDB.csv`. When set, the engine looks up `cmdbId` in the CSV at Reconcile and **auto-stamps** `cmdbName` + `cmdbCriticality` + `cmdbDataSensitivity` from the CSV row. |
| `cmdbName` / `cmdbCriticality` / `cmdbDataSensitivity` | string | **OPTIONAL override.** Set only when the matched assets differ from the CMDB record: the rule's value **wins** over the CMDB record for that field, and the row records `Cmdb<Field>Source = rule:<RuleId>`. |

> **Set `cmdbName`/`cmdbCriticality`/`cmdbDataSensitivity` inline only as a deliberate override.** Left out, they come from the CMDB record via the `cmdbId` lookup; set, they win over it for the matched assets, field by field (see *Rule overrides win over the CMDB record*). `cmdbId` and the overrides are silently ignored when CMDB is not configured (gated on `$global:SI_EnableCmdbProvider`), so community customers can leave cmdb fields inert in custom rules and flip the global to activate them.

### Locked vs. custom — naming + override

| File suffix | Purpose | Edited by | Survives release upgrade? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<RuleId>.locked.yaml` | Shipped baseline (universal logic) | Maintainer | No — overwritten on update |
| `<RuleId>.custom.sample.yaml` | Shipped starter template | Maintainer | No — overwritten |
| `<RuleId>.custom.yaml` | Customer override | Customer | **Yes** — gitignored, never overwritten |

**Override workflow**: copy `.locked.yaml` to `.custom.yaml`, keep the same `id:`, edit the `set:` block (and optionally `detections:`). Engine deduplicates by `id`; the `.custom.yaml` wins. When **only** the `.custom.yaml` exists (typical for inherently tenant-specific rules like `AssetProfileByCmdbTag`, `AssetProfileByIPSubnet`, `AssetProfileByExtensionAttributes`, `AssetProfileByGroupMembership`) the rule loads fine — nothing to override.

Worked example (keep shipped `ADDomainController` detection but stamp your own `cmdbId` + add a CAB tag): copy `ADDomainController.locked.yaml` → `ADDomainController.custom.yaml`, keep the exact same `id:`, paste the full rule body, then set:

```yaml
set:
  Tier:     0
  Purpose:  'Domain Controller'
  Category: 'Server Roles'
  Tags:     [ 'cab:domain-controllers' ]
  cmdbId:   'SVC-AD-PROD'           # your CMDB foreign key
```

Result on the next run: the locked rule is suppressed, the custom rule fires for the same DCs, the asset gets `Tier=0` + the tag + `cmdbId`, and Reconcile auto-stamps `cmdbName`/`cmdbCriticality`/`cmdbDataSensitivity` from the CSV (any of them the rule sets itself is kept: the rule's override wins). The `.custom.yaml` is gitignored so the override survives every release upgrade.

### Loading order + dedup

1. Engine scans every `*.yaml` under `asset-profiling-enrichment/<engine>/` (recursively).
2. Files ending in `.sample.yaml` are **skipped** (documentation only).
3. Each remaining file is parsed; rules are tagged with their source folder (`locked` / `custom`).
4. Dedup pass — rules with the same `id:` collapse; `custom` wins over `locked`.
5. Rules with `mode: disable` are dropped.
6. Final ruleset is evaluated against every asset; **first-match-wins per rule**; every matching rule contributes one entry to `SIRules[]` on the profile row.

Engine code: `RuleEval.ps1` (per-detection evaluator / every kind handler), `Get-SIRuleSet.ps1` (loader), `RuleIndexes.ps1` (bulk-index builders for kinds that need pre-fetched data). The `aggregator.contributors[]` in the schema reference the same AssetProfileBy* rule families.
