## Risk-score model

> Source of truth for `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.json` and its `.sample` companion. Grounded in `engine/risk-analysis/Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` — `Get-WeightedFactorsConfig` (loads the JSON), `Build-WeightedFactorsKql` (emits the per-field `case()` + `RiskScore_Weight_Factor` + `RiskScore_Weight_Detailed` columns), and the Layer-3 application loop (multiplies `RiskScoreTotal` by `RiskFactor_Weight`). When code disagrees with this doc, code wins.
>
> **v2.2.228 loader behaviour**: `Get-WeightedFactorsConfig` no longer requires `$global:SettingsPath`. It walks up from the engine's `$PSScriptRoot` looking for a `risk-analysis-detection/` sibling at every level (depth cap 6). Per-report `<ReportName>.weighted.custom.json` overrides the solution-wide `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.json`. Each successful load emits `[INFO] [weight] <Report> (engine=<x>): N field(s), source=<path>`; a miss emits a `[WARN]` naming the searched dirs.

### File pair

| File | Purpose | Edited by |
|---|---|---|
| `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.json` | Active config consumed by every report | Customer (or maintainer pre-shipped) |
| `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.sample.json` | Annotated starter copy | Maintainer |

There is no `.locked.json`. The custom file IS the source of truth — no merge.

### Three-layer risk model

The engine computes a single `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted` per row in three stages. Every section in this JSON tunes one stage.

| Layer | Formula | What this JSON tunes |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Base** (#559) | `AssetBase = lookup(finding x asset class x si_tier)` and `VulnerabilityBase = lookup(finding type / category / subcategory / si_severity)` from your `riskscore.index.custom.csv` rows, then the shipped `riskscore.index.locked.csv` -- keyed by the SI generic fields | `impactNormalizer`, `severityMapper`, `tierMapper` (label translation that drives the lookup) |
| **2. Additive adjustment** (#559) | asset side `RiskConsequenceScore = AssetBase + SUM(enabled asset factors' impacts)`; vulnerability side `RiskProbabilityScore = VulnerabilityBase + SUM(enabled finding factors' impacts)`; no cap; `RiskScoreTotal = asset side x vulnerability side` | the risk-factor catalog (impact 1-5, state), not this JSON |
| **3. Multiplicative business multiplier** | `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted = floor(RiskScoreTotal * RiskFactor_Weight / 100.0)` | `weightedRiskFactors` (the big one) |

### Risk factor model v2 -- the score (#559, owner 2026-10-10)

*"Everything will be risk factors ... each of the risk factors will be linked to an risk score impact value (1-5) ...
(5+5) x (5+4) = 90"*, *"Sum, no cap"*, *"base values come from the risk index. that is the magic"*.

```
asset side         = AssetBase          (risk index: finding x asset class x tier)                  + SUM(impact of every enabled ASSET factor the row has)
vulnerability side = VulnerabilityBase  (risk index: finding type / category / subcategory / severity) + SUM(impact of every enabled FINDING factor)
RiskScoreTotal     = asset side x vulnerability side        no cap
example            = (Tier 0 base 5 + PortOpenInternet 5) x (very high 5 + ExploitKit 4) = 90
```

- **Columns.** `RiskConsequenceScore` = the asset side, `RiskProbabilityScore` = the vulnerability side (the owner's words:
  consequence = asset, probability = vulnerability). `RiskFactor_Consequence_Detailed` lists the asset factors' **short
  names**, `RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed` the vulnerability factors'; `RiskFactor_Consequence` / `RiskFactor_Probability`
  are their **impact sums** (a number a report sets is scaffolding). `RiskFactorIds` keeps the ids (the report's own, else the
  catalog ids that counted).
- **Each factor once, on its own side** (`Measure-RARowFactors`, `_shared/RA-FactorKeys.ps1`): a token that names a catalog
  factor (id, short name, legacy token, description) counts that factor's impact on ITS side, whatever column it arrived in;
  two names of one factor count once (also two report tokens -- the old "a report's own two tokens stay two" is gone); a
  disabled factor counts 0 and is not shown; a retired token (break glass) counts nothing.
- **Tokens the catalog does not know** (a report's own question, the `report_scoped` entry) count the `report_scoped` impact
  (default 1) on the side their column always put them: `RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed` -> asset side (it added to the tier
  base), `RiskFactor_Consequence_Detailed` -> vulnerability side. A report that names no token and gives a number counts that
  many unnamed factors on the asset side (data model `ci`: dropped, the CI decides the asset factors).
- **Finding factors on the row's SI fields** (`Get-RAFindingFactorTokens`): KnownExploited (`si_exploit_verified`),
  ExploitKit (`si_in_exploit_kit`), NetworkNoUserAction (`si_cvss_vector` AV:N + UI:N), ZeroDay (`si_zero_day` or
  `si_fix_available` false), Overdue (`si_due_date` past), OldVuln (`si_published` older than 180 days, editable). A field the
  row does not carry is UNKNOWN and adds nothing (#546); #560 maps the fields per source.
- **Tier counts once**: in `AssetBase`. No factor names tier; the KPI's tier weight (`SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_*`,
  `_TierWeight`) weights the secure-score KPI average and never multiplies `RiskScoreTotal`, so it is unchanged.
- **RiskRating** (`Get-SIRiskRating`, shared with the findings table): Critical >= the first threshold, High >= the second, Moderate >= the third, else Low. **The thresholds are the CUSTOMER'S** (#696: what a band means differs per customer; the four words stay -- the rating is for management), **shipped 50 / 30 / 15** (owner 2026-10-11). They are DATA, not code: the data-model list `risk_rating_bands` (`data-model/lists.locked.json`), three whole numbers above 0, highest first, validated by `Test-SIRiskRatingBands` (engine) and `RiskRatingBands.Problems` (web app). Pro: an Admin sets them on **Admin > Settings > Risk rating** -- the values in force, the shipped default, the item's template conformance, and a preview of how many findings of the newest collection fall in each band with the entered values (counted from the collection's precomputed score distribution, `sidata.FindingFacet` facet `score`; no engine run); Stage writes the list's `cfg.ItemOverride` through Review & commit (the same data-model change path as every other override, audited `datamodel.item.stage`), "Reset to default" stages the override's removal. Community: `lists.custom.json`. The next Risk Analysis run scores with them (`Get-RARiskRatingBands`); a change needs no release. A missing or invalid list falls back to the built-in 50 / 30 / 15 in the engine AND the web app (`RiskRatingBands.Default`) -- a guard test holds the two defaults and the shipped list equal.
- **Built-in factors are never off**: the validation and the web app refuse `state: disabled` on a built-in factor (a factor
  without a `class` is built-in -- the GUI contract), and the run start re-enables one an override disabled and says so
  (`Resolve-SIRiskFactorBuiltinState`).
- **Reports**: the factor columns list short names; every Excel export gets a **"Risk factors"** sheet and the run writes the
  same rows as `<name>.riskfactors.json` for the PDF appendix -- short name, description, Asset / Vulnerability, impact,
  class, group, state, id (`Get-RARiskFactorLegendRows`, twin of the catalog's `Get-SIRiskFactorLegend`). The scope
  preamble's `SI_FactorNames` map and the CI blocks' `si_rf_names_` carry the short names.

**Default impacts** (shipped; customer fine-tunes per factor, Pro: cfg.ItemOverride):

| side | built-in (real risk, impact 3-5) | optional (former hygiene, impact 1-2) |
|---|---|---|
| asset | PortOpenInternet 5, LeakedCreds 5, InternetExposed 4, RecentIncident 4, UnsupportedOS 4, AVDisabled 4, IdentityAtRisk 4, RestrictedData 4, NotOnboarded 3, AVOutOfDate 3, DefenderExcluded 3, HighMachineRisk 3, NoMFA 3, OldPassword 3, HighBlastRadius 3, ClientSecret 3, Production 3, ConfidentialData 3, HighMsCriticality 3 | EnabledNoSignInStale 2, NeverSignedIn 2, PermanentAdmin 2, NoOwner 2, CredsExpired 2, Unmanaged 2, OldAccount 1, CredsExpiring 1, PublisherUnverified 1, MultiTenantApp 1 |
| vulnerability | KnownExploited 4, ExploitKit 4, ZeroDay 4, RCE 4, ExploitAvailable 3, NetworkNoUserAction 3, CVSS9Plus 3, Overdue 3, OldVuln 3 | ReportFactor 1 (report-scoped tokens) |

### Break glass is a classification, not a factor (#559)

`si_is_break_glass` is set by the CI build BEFORE the enrichment rules (`engine/data-model/SI-BreakGlass.ps1`), so the tier
rules and the break-glass reports read it as they read the old factor's field: the provider's value (the identity profiler on
the Entra record), OR a naming pattern of the data-model list `break_glass_patterns` (type `values`: glob patterns `*` / `?`
over letters, digits, space and `. _ @ -`, never wildcards only -- `Test-SIBreakGlassPattern`, the web app's rule too) on the
sign-in name, the display name or a group's name (an emergency-access group), OR the platform signal "excluded from
Conditional Access (`si_ca_excluded_policies`) while holding a permanent Tier 0 role". `si_break_glass_reasons` says which.
`si_ca_excluded_policies` carries `needsRead` (the Conditional Access read is not built yet) -- until then that signal is
unknown and never classifies. The customer overrides the patterns (Community `lists.custom.json`; Pro the list's override).

**The extension attribute you define, and the Break glass page (Pro).** An account that carries the extension attribute
and value you define is a break-glass account. The rule is the data-model list `break_glass_attribute` -- entries
`attribute=value`, shipped empty: the attribute is `extensionAttribute1` to `extensionAttribute15` or the name of a
directory extension (`extension_<application id without dashes>_<name>`), the value 1 to 256 characters, compared whole
and without regard to case. In Pro the list is edited on *Risk factors > Break glass*, next to the naming patterns: an
attribute and a value per row, several rows allowed, clear a row to remove it. The rows become the list's override
through the same staged change, Review & commit, Admin role and audit record as the naming patterns. The web app holds
every row to the engine's own rule (`ConvertTo-SIBreakGlassAttributeRule`; its twin is `Changes/BreakGlassAttribute.cs`,
and one shared table of valid and invalid examples is read by the tests of both), when the change is staged and again
when it is committed -- an entry the engine would skip is never stored.

*How the override reaches a run.* The Pro settings layer exports the templates with the customer's overrides as the run's
data model; the identity collection reads the list from it, asks the directory for an attribute only while an entry names
it and records the entry a user carries (`si_break_glass_attribute`); the CI build classifies from that record and writes
the rule or rules that matched in one sentence (`si_break_glass_reason`). So a new or changed entry takes effect on the
next identity collection -- the page says so.

*The accounts on the page.* The page lists every account classified break-glass with the sentence that says which rule
made it so, and under each entry the accounts that carry it now. Both come from two prepared columns of the CI table
(`BreakGlassReason`, indexed, and `BreakGlassAttribute`; entries of the one list of prepared view columns, filled by the
data sync). The reason is set on a break-glass account and on no other, so the read is a seek on that index for the rows
that have a reason: the page never opens a CI document and never walks the identities. At most 500 accounts are listed
and the page says when there are more; a database that does not have the two columns yet says that the list comes with
the next update.

All Layer-3 multipliers are stored as **basis-100 integers**: `100 = 1.0x`, `150 = 1.5x`, `262 = 2.62x`. This dodges locale-decimal traps (da-DK parses `"1.5"` as `15`).

### Score invariants (owner 2026-10-10: the score is validated by invariant tests)

`tests/pester/SIv3-ScoreInvariants.Tests.ps1` checks these over the shipped index, `Calculate-RiskScore` (with the CI context in front) and the locked report catalog:

Re-baselined to the risk factor model v2 (#559) -- no exception was added.

| # | invariant | how |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Tier orders the score**: the same finding on Tier 0 scores >= Tier 1 >= Tier 2 >= Tier 3 | every matcher set of the SI-keyed index (server / client rows included) and every report's own category / subcategory / configuration id, every severity; scid-2002 = 5 on a server, 1 on a client |
| 2 | **Severity orders the vulnerability side** (same finding, same tier) | every matcher set of the index |
| 3 | **A risk factor never lowers a score** | each token in either column (catalog ids + short names + legacy tokens + report-only ones), each engine signal column and CMDB value, each catalog factor through the CI, each finding factor's SI field, and 300 seeded superset / subset pairs |
| 4 | **One factor counts once** | the same catalog factor under two names (report + engine signal, report + CI, CI + asset baseline, two report tokens) adds its impact once, on its own side; break glass adds nothing |
| 5 | **The formula, exactly**: each side = its base + the impacts of the factors it lists (no cap); total = their product, never negative; weighted = floor(total x weight / 100); RiskRating = Get-SIRiskRating(total); the owner's example = 90 | 400 seeded rows + the example |
| 6 | **Catalog**: every report carries RiskScore_Weight_* to its output; every RiskFactor_*_Detailed a report computes reaches the engine; a constant RiskFactor_* value is scaffolding the engine overrides, the weighted block's no-op default, or a listed constant factor list | known exception, owner decision: Identity_BreakGlass_SignIn_Detected_Summary, Identity_SPN_RoleManagementWrite_Summary / _Detailed compute three consequence tokens and drop them (carrying them = +3 consequence per row) |

**What the token rules are** (`_shared/RA-RiskScore.ps1`, `_shared/RA-FactorKeys.ps1`, `_shared/RA-CiContext.ps1`) -- #559:
- The tokens are gathered as before: the report's own (both columns), the asset baseline (data sensitivity:
  `RestrictedDataAccess` / `ConfidentialDataAccess`, #469; no tier / CMDB-criticality token since #527 (5)), the engine's
  signals, the CI's catalog factors (the CI context marks what it added, `si_ci_factor_tokens`, removed from the output row),
  plus the finding factors evaluated on the row's SI fields. Then `Measure-RARowFactors` puts each factor ONCE on its side
  with its impact (see "Risk factor model v2" above); `RiskFactor_*` are the impact sums, `RiskFactor_*_Detailed` the short names.
- Tokens are compared by the catalog factor they name (`data-model/risk-factors.locked.json`: id, shortName, `legacyTokens`,
  name; only `evaluatedBy: catalog` factors map), else by their letters (RF_P_ / RF_C_ prefix and punctuation ignored).
- Known limit: a number-only report's factors have no names, so a CI factor that is one of them can count twice -- removed when those reports emit RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed (the CI-based reports, #505).

### Risk-factor catalog: factor groups with provider links (#458)

One catalog, `data-model/risk-factors.locked.json` (template kind `risk-factor`, customer overrides per factor id in
`risk-factors.custom.json`). Every factor is defined once over SI fields (V3-DATA-MODEL 2.7) and carries:

| key | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id`, `name`, `description` | what it is: `name` = the one-line description the GUI shows, `description` = the full explanation |
| `shortName` (#558 / #559) | the name reports, Excel, PDF and mails show: PascalCase letters / digits, one word, no editable number (EnabledNoSignInStale, not NoSignIn90d) |
| `appliesTo` | `asset` (evaluated on the CI; adds to the ASSET side) or `finding` (adds to the VULNERABILITY side) |
| `group` | Exposure, Device health, Identity, Privilege, Apps, Importance, Exploitability, Impact, Severity, Lifecycle |
| `class` | `builtin` (always on, never disabled) or `optional`; a factor WITHOUT a class is built-in (the GUI contract) -- every shipped factor says it |
| `impact` | 1..5 (very low .. very high): what the factor adds to its side, summed with the others, no cap |
| `state` | `enabled` or `disabled` (replaces `stage`; a built-in factor is never disabled; a pre-v2 override's `stage: not_used / testing` reads as disabled) |
| `axis` | the report column the short name is listed in by the reports' CI blocks (`si_rf_p` / `si_rf_c`); the score side is `appliesTo`, never `axis` |
| `when`, `combine` | the condition over SI fields; `combine` = its top level, `any` or `all` |
| `providers` | per provider the provider fields that PROVE it -- generated from the field mappings (`data-model/mappings`) for the SI fields the factor reads; `computed` = a field SecurityInsight computes on the CI (the tier from the enrichment rules, the CMDB criticality level, privilege tiers); `network` = a range list |
| `ciColumn` | the factor gets its own `SI_CI_CL` column `si_rf_<id>` |
| `legacyTokens` | the RF_* names and report tokens this factor replaces -- also how Risk Analysis counts one factor once |

The `providers` block is never hand-edited: `Update-SIRiskFactorProviders` (`engine/data-model/SI-RiskFactorCatalog.ps1`)
writes it from the mappings, and `SIv3-RiskFactorCatalog.Tests` fails when the stored block and the mappings differ. How
several providers of ONE field combine is that field's resolution in the field catalog (risk booleans `any_true`, else the
authority order, V3-DATA-MODEL 2.6) -- so "internet exposed" holds when ANY fresh provider says so.

**The factors several providers prove** (the start set, `ciColumn`):

| factor | proven by |
|---|---|
| `internet_exposed` (InternetExposed) | Defender for Endpoint `deviceInfo.IsInternetFacing`; Exposure Graph `exposedToInternet` / `hasInternetExposureSignal`; Azure `derived.isPubliclyExposed`; Defender for Cloud `exposure.internetExposed` (its Unhealthy internet-exposure assessments, Resource Graph `securityresources`, #527 (7)); Shodan `host.ports`; an address (Defender for Endpoint / ServiceNow `si_ip_addresses`) in the network ranges |
| `no_mfa` (NoMFA) | Entra `registration.isMfaRegistered`; Exposure Graph `isMfaRegistered` |
| `has_secret` (HasSecret) | Entra `sp.passwordCredentials` (its own factor since #527 (3); `expiring_credentials` is the expiry) |
| `stale_sign_in`, `never_signed_in` (Stale / NeverLoggedIn) | Entra sign-in activity; Active Directory `lastLogonTimestamp`; Defender for Identity `lastSeenActivity` |
| `unsupported_os` (LegacyEoS) | the OS name of Defender for Endpoint, Exposure Graph, Entra, Intune and Active Directory, matched by the `unsupported_os` list |
| `no_owner` (NoOwner), `expiring_credentials` | Entra only today |
| `identity_high_blast_radius` (HighBlastRadius) | Defender for Identity only today |

A provider is added to a factor by mapping its field to the SI field -- never in the factor.

**Network ranges.** `internet_exposed` also holds for an address in `internet_exposed_ranges` (DMZ, online landing zones).
The shipped list is empty; the customer fills it -- Pro: the database setting `SI_InternetExposedRanges` (Settings page);
Community: the same setting in the custom file, or `lists.custom.json`. The CI enrichment merges the setting into the
list (`Merge-SIRiskFactorRanges`; CIDR or address, IPv4 / IPv6; anything else is left out).

**Pro: the Risk factors page (#527 (4)).** Pro manages the data model in SQL, never in custom files: every factor is a`r
cfg.Template row (kind `datamodel`, key `risk-factors:<id>`), every provider mapping one (`mappings/<provider>:<field|recordTypes|resourceTypes>`),`r
published from the locked JSON (`engine/pro-settings/SI-DataModelTemplateRows.ps1`); the run exports the effective model and validates it.`r
Configuration > Risk factors (`Pages/RiskFactors`) lists the factors with their provider links and state, the provider mappings and the`r
network ranges (the setting `SI_InternetExposedRanges`). An Admin changes an item's JSON, turns it off or puts the shipped one back:`r
staged (`ChangeKinds.DataModelItem`), written on Review & commit as a cfg.ItemOverride row, validated first by `DataModelItemValidator`r
(the C# twin of `Test-SIRiskFactorItem` / `Test-SIDataModelProItem`, which refuse the same on the engine side). A changed source field is`r
an override of the `mappings/<provider>` row. Upgrade available comes from the template conformance view and is decided there.

### The explained risk score -- every part of a finding's score, on the row and on one page

A finding's score is the asset side times the vulnerability side; each side is a base plus the impacts of the factors that
counted; the weighted score is the score times the weight. Risk Analysis writes every part on the row, so a reader can follow
the arithmetic without the risk index or the factor catalogue at hand.

**The columns** (stamped by `Calculate-RiskScore`, `engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-RiskScore.ps1`, after the one score
stamp -- additive: no other column changes; they are appended last in the report's columns, before the trace columns):

| Column | Holds |
|---|---|
| `RiskConsequenceBase` | the asset side's base (the risk index), as the score used it (a base the index does not give is 0) |
| `RiskProbabilityBase` | the vulnerability side's base |
| `RiskFactor_Consequence_Impacts` | each counted asset factor with its impact, `Name=impact;Name=impact`, in the order of `RiskFactor_Consequence_Detailed`; a factor a report gave as a number only (no name) is `ReportFactor=<impact>`, after the named ones |
| `RiskFactor_Probability_Impacts` | the same for the vulnerability factors (`RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed`) |

They hold by construction: `RiskConsequenceBase + sum(impacts) = RiskConsequenceScore`, the same for the vulnerability side,
and `RiskConsequenceScore x RiskProbabilityScore = RiskScoreTotal`. `Measure-RARowFactors` (`RA-FactorKeys.ps1`) returns each
factor's impact beside its name (`AssetImpacts` / `VulnerabilityImpacts`) from the same walk that sums them, so the list and
the sum cannot disagree. The columns travel with the row everywhere the row goes -- the workbook (the bases as numbers, the
impact lists as text), the Log Analytics copy, and the row document of the Pro database (`sidata.Finding.DetailJson`, the whole
row; no database change).

**The page** (Pro): Assets & services > Risk scores > **Explained** opens the risk score page's per-finding view
(`/Collection/RiskScore?view=explain`; the page's default stays the per-asset view). One row per finding of the collection,
highest risk score first, with Tier, Asset, Finding, CVE, the asset base, the asset factors (`Name +impact`), the asset side
(consequence), the same three for the vulnerability side (probability), the risk score, the weight (`225 %` and what set it,
e.g. CMDB criticality and data sensitivity), the weighted score, the rating and the formula in words:
`(4 + HighMachineRisk 3 + InternetExposed 4 + ConfidentialData 3 + HighMsCriticality 3) x (4 + ExploitAvailable 3 + RCE 4 + KnownExploited 4 + NetworkNoUserAction 3 + OldVuln 3) = 17 x 21 = 357; x 225 % = 803`.
Numbers are in the viewer's number format on screen and invariant in a CSV. The grid (`RiskExplainSql.Grid`,
`SI.Management.Core/ProData/RiskExplainSql.cs`) is the collection grid machinery: fixed SQL over one collection, every value a
parameter, paged, the CI lifecycle choice, a department-limited account sees its departments' rows, CSV and Excel exports. Its
typed columns (tier, asset, finding, CVE, severity, domain, report, department, score, weighted score, rating) sort and filter;
the parts read from the row document (`JSON_VALUE` over `DetailJson`) are shown only -- never sorted, filtered or searched -- so
the opening page reads its keys off the risk-score index and the documents of that page alone, and no request reads every
document of a collection to choose its page. The view adds no CI or finding context columns: it shows the score's parts.

**Older collections** (made before the bases and the per-factor impacts were recorded): the base is worked out as the side's
score minus its factors' sum (`RiskFactor_Consequence` / `RiskFactor_Probability`) and shown `4 (derived)`, the factors are
listed by name without impacts, and one sentence above the grid says so. The next collection records every part.

### The rules every risk factor keeps (#527 (5)-(7), owner 2026-10-10)

- **No tier in a risk factor.** Tier is its own dimension -- the risk index's asset base (#559; tier counts once) -- so a
  factor never restates it. Removed: `tier0`, `tier0_or_1` (and its CI column; `si_tier` is on the CI),
  `tier0_blast_radius` and the engine's `Tier0BlastRadius`, `adfs_server` / `exchange_server` (the tier rules already make
  them Tier 0; the engine's ADFS / Exchange tokens too), `business_critical_asset` and the engine's `BusinessCriticalAsset`
  (CMDB criticality is the weighted-score multiplier). The reports' Tier0* / Privileged* tokens map to no factor. Kept,
  because they are facts and not tier: `permanent_privileged_role`, `ms_criticality_high`, `production_environment`, data
  sensitivity. (`break_glass` was kept here until #559 made it a classification -- see "Break glass is a classification".)
- **Exactly one scope.** `asset` = the asset's exposure, hygiene and importance; `finding` = extra about the
  recommendation / vulnerability (`exploit_available`, `known_exploited`, `exploit_kit`, `network_no_user_action`,
  `zero_day`, `remote_code_execution`, `high_cvss_public_ip` -- CVSS 9+ on the finding, on ANY asset (owner-approved widening; the id keeps its historic name), `overdue`, `old_vuln`, `report_scoped`).
- **SI fields only.** A factor's id, scope and condition reference only SI fields (`si_*`); every raw source path lives in
  a provider mapping. A renamed or new source field is a MAPPING change (template ring; Pro: an override of the
  `mappings/<provider>` row), never a factor change.
- `Test-SIRiskFactorRules` (`engine/data-model/SI-RiskFactorCatalog.ps1`) refuses a factor with no or both scopes,
  `si_tier` in a condition, a non-SI field or a raw source path; `Test-SIDataModel` runs it, so a customer override is
  held to the same rules.
### Factor criteria and the wizards (#541 (7))

A static check that reports repeat (unsupported OS, stale-days thresholds, ...) is ONE catalog factor whose criteria are data.
The factor names them in a `criteria` block -- **shape defined here, to be reconciled with the generic-KQL lane (#541 (1)-(6))**:

```
criteria: { kind: list | threshold | range, field: si_*, source: collected | enum | lifecycle,
            list: <lists.locked.json id>, detailField: si_*      (list)
            op, min, max, unit                                    (threshold: the condition's '<field> <op>' value)
            min, max                                              (range) }
```

Shipped: `unsupported_os` (list `unsupported_os`, si_os_name + si_os_version, source collected); `stale_sign_in` (ONE stale
factor since #559 -- the former `very_stale_sign_in` is this factor with more days), `old_password`, `old_account`,
`old_vuln` (threshold, days). `Test-SIRiskFactorCriteria` validates the block (it runs
inside the data-model validation, so a customer override is held to it). In Pro the Risk factors page shows a **wizard**
for a factor with criteria -- the customer never edits criteria as JSON: a threshold is a whole number inside [min, max]; a
list keeps or drops its entries and adds entries built only from the values SI collected (sidata.Ci, the field and its
detail field, most common first; a posted value the server did not collect is refused). The result is the factor or the
list as a cfg.ItemOverride row (Review & commit), validated by `FactorCriteria` / `DataModelItemValidator` (the C# twins).
Microsoft's lifecycle list is not in SI yet (`source: lifecycle` is accepted, nothing fills it). Criteria are evaluated by
the CI build in PowerShell (no KQL); the reports move to the CI factors with the generic-KQL work.
### Risk factors per CI, with their evidence (#464)

The CI build evaluates every catalog asset factor once per CI (`Invoke-SICiRiskFactors`, P3) over the CI's resolved SI
fields -- de-duplicated by construction: one factor entry however many providers prove it. `Add-SICiRiskFactorEvidence`
then adds, per factor:

- `evidence` -- one item per provider that proves it: provider, SI field, the provider fields of its mapping, the record,
  stale. A risk boolean resolved any-true names EVERY provider that said true (the CI build keeps them in
  `si_field_sources.<field>.providers`); a computed field names what computed it (the tier: `si_tier_reason`); an address
  in a network range names the list. For an `any` factor only the fields whose own condition holds are evidence. No
  observed-at time: it moves every build and would make every CI "changed" (the build sends only changed CIs).
- `by` -- the providers of the evidence.

and on the CI: `si_rf_<id>` (true / false) for every `ciColumn` factor and `si_rf_count` (the factors that count:
enabled, impact > 0). #559: only ENABLED factors are evaluated; each entry carries `shortName`, `side` (asset), `impact`
(the catalog's 1..5), `state` and -- for the reports' shipped CI blocks -- `axis` and `stage: production`.

Stored: the whole entry with its evidence in the CI document (`sidata.Ci`); on the `SI_CI_CL` full row `si_rf_<id>`,
`si_rf_count` and each factor's `id / shortName / side / axis / impact / state / stage / by` (the first build after the
update re-posts every CI's full row once: its posted content changed).

**Risk Analysis.** The CI context (`RA-CiContext.ps1`) already adds a row's CI factors as tokens, counted once against
the report's own (the catalog's `legacyTokens` include the tokens the reports emit, e.g. `NoMfaIsRegistered`,
`InternetFacingDevice`). A report that wants the CI's factors in its KQL uses the helper `_SiCiFactors()`: the marker line
`//__SI_CI_FACTORS__` is replaced with a function returning one row per CI (latest full row within `SI_ActiveStaleDays`)
with its provider links (`si_link_mde / _entra / _azure / _eg / _ad / _intune`), `si_rf_<id>` and `si_rf_count`
(`Get-RACiFactorKql`, `_shared/RA-FactorKeys.ps1`). Log Analytics only. No shipped report uses it yet: the reports move to
the CI with the CI-based report rewrite (#505), and InternetExposed / NoMFA already reach every report through the CI context.



### Layer 1 -- the risk index: first match wins, in row order (3.0), keyed by the SI fields (#559)

The risk index is checked **top down, and the first row that fits a finding sets its base score** -- separately for each base. Your own rows (`riskscore.index.custom.csv`, optional) come first, then the shipped rows (`riskscore.index.locked.csv`).

**#559 the SI keys** (`_shared/RA-RiskIndexSi.ps1`). Columns: `si_finding_type, si_category, si_subcategory, si_component,
si_finding_key, asset_class, si_severity, VulnerabilityBase, si_tier, AssetBase, Comments, Precedence`.

- **AssetBase** (the asset side) = the first row with an AssetBase whose filled `si_finding_type`, `si_category`,
  `si_subcategory`, `si_component`, `si_finding_key`, `asset_class` and `si_tier` fit the finding.
- **VulnerabilityBase** (the vulnerability side) = the same with `si_severity` in place of `si_tier`.
- The finding's values: its si_* fields (#560 / #561), else the report's own columns (Category, Subcategory,
  ConfigurationId, SecuritySeverity, CriticalityTier) -- `Get-SIRiskIndexFindingValues`. `asset_class` = the CI's class with a
  device split by its category / OS: `device_server` / `device_client` (`device` when neither is known), `identity`,
  `cloud_resource`, `public_ip`; without a CI, the report's security domain translated. A row's `asset_class = device` fits
  servers and clients (the family); `device_server` fits only servers.
- Severity: `critical, high, medium_high, medium, low, info` -- `medium_high` keeps 2.2's Medium-High band so its own base
  survives.
- **The v2.2 keys are translated, never lost**: `riskscore.index.translation.locked.json` (shipped as data) maps every 2.2
  column and value (SecurityDomain -> asset_class: Endpoint -> device, Identity -> identity, Azure -> cloud_resource,
  PublicIP -> public_ip; Category -> si_category; SubCategory -> si_subcategory; ConfigurationId -> si_finding_key;
  SecuritySeverity -> si_severity; CriticalityTierLevel -> si_tier 0..3; RiskConsequenceScore_SecuritySeverity ->
  VulnerabilityBase; RiskProbablityScore_CriticialityTierLevel -> AssetBase). A file with the 2.2 columns (a customer's
  `custom.csv`, a Pro item stored before) is put in first-match form (the ladder, when it has no Precedence) and translated
  row for row on load. The shipped index IS the translation of the 3.0 index (99 rows, every base value carried over), behind
  the owner's three scid-2002 rows: Defender not responding = AssetBase 5 on a server, 1 on a user client, 4 on a Tier 0
  client (`tests/pester/SIv3-RiskIndexSi.Tests.ps1` proves every row resolves and that a v2.2 reference set scores the same
  bases).
- A blank matcher fits any value; a blank finding value never fits a filled matcher; comparison ignores case. A blank base means "this row does not set that base" (the search goes on). No row fits: 0.
- The order is the `Precedence` column (1 = checked first; a row without one is checked after all numbered rows).

The 3.0 description below (2.2 column names) stays true of the order and the ladder; read `SecurityDomain .. ConfigurationId`
as the SI matchers, "consequence" as the vulnerability base and "probability" as the asset base.

**Why the two lookups stay separate.** 2.2 never took both scores from one row: the consequence came from the best row for the finding's severity and the probability from the best row for its tier. One row supplying both would need a row for every severity x tier combination to give the same results.

**2.2 files keep their scores.** In 2.2 the file order did not decide which row won. Every row was filed under a fixed ladder of 15 column patterns -- domain-qualified before not, severity / tier-qualified before configuration-only (`D C S I V`, `D C S V`, `D C V`, `D V`, `D C S I`, `D C S`, `D C`, `D`, then the same seven without the domain) -- under every pattern whose columns it had filled, ignoring its other columns; per pattern the first row in the file with that key won. A file **without** a `Precedence` column is read as a 2.2 index and converted on load: one row per (pattern, value) 2.2 could ever pick, in ladder order. First match over the converted rows gives the 2.2 score for every finding (verified over every combination of matcher values the shipped index tells apart, against the 2.2 code itself). The shipped index is that conversion of the 2.2 file (59 rows -> 99 rows). Simply reversing a 2.2 file is not equivalent.

**What can be configured.** Rows, their order, the four matchers, severity, tier, both scores and the comments. Not the set of matcher columns: Risk Analysis passes exactly these six values of a finding into the lookup, so another matcher column would be an engine change. "Sort by specificity" (Pro) orders rows the way the 2.2 ladder did, so it never changes a converted index; a row that a row above already covers completely is reported as never used.

**SecurityInsight Pro.** The rows are template items (vendor rows; the customer's changed, own and switched-off rows as overrides) and are written for the engine in `Precedence` order, renumbered. The **Risk index** page edits them: add, delete, duplicate, move (buttons, Alt+Up / Alt+Down), inline edit with per-column checks, reset a row to the vendor's, import / export the CSV (2.2 column names, plus `Precedence`), a dry run that scores current findings with the edited index and the index in force by the same rule as Risk Analysis, and one staged change committed through Review & commit with a change-history row per item. A moved vendor row keeps the vendor's place where it can; moved and own rows get a value between their neighbours.
**Existing overrides converge (CONVERGE-DEFAULTS).** On the next full shipped publish (setup and the updater run it) `SI-ProOverrideMigration.ps1` translates every cfg.ItemOverride row keyed the pre-v2 way through the shipped translation table: a risk index row under its 2.2 key moves to its SI key (body translated, value and place kept, a `disable` moves with its key; when the new key is already overridden the new one wins and the old row goes); a pre-v2 factor override gets `state` for `stage` and the v2 fields it lacks, a value equal to the 1.0.0 default (`riskFactorsV1` in the table) takes the new shipped value, a value the customer changed is kept (impact held to 1..5); a built-in factor is never disabled; an override of a removed factor (very_stale_sign_in, break_glass) is removed with what replaced it. Every write goes through `Set-SIProItem` (validated, ChangeLog); an item that does not validate after translation stays as it was and is reported. Idempotent.
#559: the template rows are published SI-keyed (`SI-ProConfig.ps1`: item key = the eight SI dimensions); an item stored
with the 2.2 columns still validates (its 2.2 key) and is translated when the run file is written. The web app's Risk index
page / preview (`RiskIndex.cs`, `RiskIndexScoring`) move to the SI columns in the GUI lane.

### Top-level fields

| Field | Type | Default | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `outputColumn` | string | `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted` | line 14 | Final weighted-score column name. |
| `baseColumn` | string | `RiskScoreTotal` | line 14 | Unweighted column the multiplier feeds on. |
| `combiner` | string | `RiskScoreTotal * (1.0 + sum(weight_i * factor_i))` | line 15, doc-only | Documents the combine formula. Engine math hardcoded at line 3132. |
| `rounding` | string | `toint(round(<result>))` | line 16, doc-only | Documents rounding. Engine uses `[int][math]::Floor()` at line 3144. |
| `kqlSafetyNote` | string | n/a | line 17 | Documents the `column_ifexists()` wrap the consolidator uses when generating KQL. |

The two `*Column` strings ARE consumed (they decide which row property the engine reads/writes). `combiner`/`rounding`/`kqlSafetyNote` are documentation only.

### `impactNormalizer` — raw severity → 0..10 numeric

Converts string severities (`"High"`, `"Sev1"`, `"informational"`) and free text into 0..10, the input to `severityMapper`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceColumn` | string | `Impact` | KQL column read |
| `outputColumn` | string | `Impact` | KQL column written (usually same as source, in-place) |
| `stringMap` | object {string:number} | (below) | Case-insensitive value → numeric |
| `default` | number | `0.0` | Used when input null OR missing OR no key match |

Default `stringMap`: `{ "critical": 10.0, "very high": 10.0, "high": 8.0, "medium": 5.0, "moderate": 5.0, "low": 2.0, "informational": 1.0, "info": 1.0 }`. Use case: add `"sev1": 10.0, "sev2": 7.0` when ingesting ServiceNow incidents that ship sev numbers.

### `severityMapper` — numeric Impact → human label

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceColumn` | string | `Impact` | numeric input |
| `outputColumn` | string | `SecuritySeverity` | label output |
| `thresholds` | `[{min,label}, ...]` | (below) | Descending min → label. First match wins. |
| `default` | string | `Low` | When no threshold matched |

Default `thresholds`: `[ {min:9.0,"Very High"}, {min:7.0,"High"}, {min:4.0,"Medium"}, {min:0.1,"Low"} ]`. Use case: lower `High` to 6.5 so borderline CVEs trigger High routing.

### `tierMapper` — numeric tier → human label

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceColumn` | string | `CriticalityTier` | integer 0..3 input |
| `outputColumn` | string | `CriticalityTierLevel` | label output, fed into the Layer-1 lookup |
| `valueMap` | object {"0".."3":string} | (below) | Tier number → label |
| `default` | string | `Low - tier 3` | When tier null or missing |

Default `valueMap`: `{ "0":"Critical - tier 0", "1":"High - tier 1", "2":"Medium - tier 2", "3":"Low - tier 3" }`. Labels must match the risk index (`riskscore.index.locked.csv`, and your `riskscore.index.custom.csv` rows).

### `criticalityMultiplierMapper` — legacy single-field weight (deprecated)

Old single-column weighting, superseded by `weightedRiskFactors`. Only fires when `weightedRiskFactors` has no entry for the active engine. Defaults: `sourceColumn=cmdbCriticality`, `outputColumn=RiskFactor_Weight`, `valueMap={ "Critical":1.50,"High":1.25,"Medium":1.10,"Low":1.00 }`, `default=1.00`. Note: legacy uses **decimal** multipliers, not basis-100.

### `weightedRiskFactors` — Layer 3 multi-field business multiplier (the important one)

Cross-engine, multi-field weighting on basis-100 integers. **The engine's primary CMDB amplification mechanism.**

```json
"weightedRiskFactors": {
  "endpoint": { "combine": "...", "maxMultiplier": <int>, "fields": [...] },
  "identity": { "combine": "...", "maxMultiplier": <int>, "fields": [...] },
  "azure":    { "combine": "...", "maxMultiplier": <int>, "fields": [...] }
}
```

**Per-engine sub-object**: `combine` (`product`/`max`/`sum-of-deltas`, default `product` — how per-field multipliers fold together); `maxMultiplier` (int basis-100, default `0` = no cap; set `500` to cap at 5.0x); `fields` (`[{field,valueMap,default}, ...]`, required).

**Per-field entry**: `field` (column name, e.g. `cmdbCriticality`, `cmdbDataSensitivity`); `valueMap` (object {string:int}, case-insensitive value → basis-100 multiplier); `default` (int, default `100` = no amplification, used when value not in map or column missing/null).

**Combine modes** (worked over `cmdbCriticality=Critical (150)` + `cmdbDataSensitivity=Restricted (175)`):

| Mode | Math | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `product` | `(150/100) * (175/100) * 100 = 262` | **262** (2.62x) |
| `max` | `max(150, 175)` | **175** (1.75x) |
| `sum-of-deltas` | `100 + (150-100) + (175-100)` | **225** (2.25x) |

**Default endpoint config**:

```json
"endpoint": {
  "combine": "product",
  "maxMultiplier": 0,
  "fields": [
    { "field": "cmdbCriticality",
      "valueMap": { "Critical": 150, "High": 125, "Medium": 110, "Low": 105 }, "default": 100 },
    { "field": "cmdbDataSensitivity",
      "valueMap": { "Restricted": 175, "Confidential": 150, "Internal": 125, "Public": 110 }, "default": 100 }
  ]
}
```

Use cases: add a third axis (e.g. cost-centre — drop a new `{field,valueMap,default}` into `fields[]`, no code change); cap runaway multiplication (`maxMultiplier: 500`); switch to conservative additive (`combine: sum-of-deltas`); disable Layer 3 (omit the engine's section — engine reads `RiskFactor_Weight = 100`, so `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted == RiskScoreTotal`).

✅ **Nothing to rebuild after editing.** This used to say "re-run `Build-RiskAnalysis.ps1` so the
consolidator regenerates the `__WEIGHTED_FACTORS__` blocks inside report KQL". That was **wrong even
before the tool was retired (#28)**: the catalog ships the `//__WEIGHTED_FACTORS_BEGIN__` /
`__END__` markers (120 of them) as a no-op default, and **the ENGINE substitutes the generated KQL
chain at run time** from the customer JSON — `Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1:2430`, helpers at `:1254`. The
JSON edit takes effect on the next run, with no build step. Following the old instruction would have
rebuilt the whole catalog destructively.

### `riskFactorDetailedMapper` / `riskFactorProbabilityMapper`

- **`riskFactorDetailedMapper`** — `outputColumn` default `RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed`; `perEngineFields` default `{ endpoint:["IsStaleAsset"], identity:["IsExternalIdentity"], azure:[] }`. The consolidator AUTOMATICALLY includes every `bool` column in the profile schema with `purpose: risk` (no need to list those); `perEngineFields` is for **non-risk-purposed** bools you want to count anyway. Output is a semicolon-joined string like `"IsStaleAsset; OutdatedOS"`.
- **`riskFactorProbabilityMapper`** — `outputColumn` default `RiskFactor_Probability`. The integer count of `true` risk-factor bools per row; added to `probBase` (line 3118).

### End-to-end worked example

**Asset**: server, `cmdbCriticality=Critical`, `cmdbDataSensitivity=Restricted`, `SecuritySeverity=High`, `CriticalityTier=0`, two risk-factor bools fired (`IsStaleAsset`, `OutdatedOS`).

**Layer 1**: `Impact` = `impactNormalizer("High")` → 8.0; `SecuritySeverity` = `severityMapper(8.0)` → `"High"`; `CriticalityTierLevel` = `tierMapper(0)` → `"Critical - tier 0"`; `consBase = lookup(Endpoint,Cat,SubCat,"High")` → **3**; `probBase = lookup(Endpoint,Cat,SubCat,"Critical - tier 0")` → **4**.

**Layer 2**: `RiskFactor_Consequence` = 0 (placeholder) → `consAdj = 3+0 = 3`; `RiskFactor_Probability` = count(true) = 2 → `probAdj = 4+2 = 6`; `RiskScoreTotal = 3*6 = 18`.

**Layer 3** (`product`): `cmdbCriticality(Critical)→150`, `cmdbDataSensitivity(Restricted)→175`; `RiskFactor_Weight = floor((150/100)*(175/100)*100) = 262`; `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted = floor(18 * 262 / 100) = 47`.

So this row, raw 18, surfaces in the Excel sort at **47** — ahead of un-amplified Critical-but-non-Restricted assets.

Consumers: `engine/risk-analysis/Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` (lines 2231-2409 build KQL, 3043-3145 apply Layer 3, `:2430` substitutes the `__WEIGHTED_FACTORS__` block **at run time**); `risk-analysis-detection/riskscore.index.locked.csv` + your `riskscore.index.custom.csv` (the Layer-1 lookup table). *(The retired `Build-RiskAnalysis.ps1` used to be listed here as a consumer — see #28; the substitution is entirely a run-time step, so there is no build consumer.)*
