## Risk-analysis queries & report structure

> Source of truth for `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml` and its `_Custom.yaml` companion. Grounded in `engine/risk-analysis/Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` (consumer) and `risk-analysis-detection/risk-analysis.schema.locked.json` (the JSON-schema describing the YAML). When code disagrees with this doc, code wins.

### File pair + merge semantics

| File | Purpose | Edited by | Survives release upgrade? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml` | Shipped 132+ reports + templates | Maintainer | No |
| `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Custom.yaml` | Customer overrides + new reports | Customer | Yes |

**Merge rule** (`Merge-ByReportName`, `Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` lines 4095-4192): same `ReportName` → custom **fully replaces** locked (no partial merge); new `ReportName` → appended at end; locked order preserved, matching custom entries overwrite in-place; ReportTemplates merge by template `ReportName` with the same rules. Merge log line at 4271-4275: `YAML merge: Locked Reports={...}, Custom={...}, Merged={...}`.

### Top-level structure

```yaml
Reports:                     # list -- one entry per report (one Excel sheet / LA write)
  - ReportName: ...
ReportTemplates:             # list -- groups of reports run together
  - ReportName: ...
    ReportsIncluded: [...]
```

Both keys are required; the engine errors if either is missing or empty.

### One structure for every report, and output names that never change (#692)

Every query report has the same five parts, in order: (1) **data in** -- the source provider's findings (a provider
table, or the CI itself for a finding that is a property of the asset); (2) **correlated with the CI** (`SI_CI_CL`: tier,
CMDB, risk factors, links -- by id) through a block the engine generates (`__SI_CI_ASSET__` / `__SI_CI_LINK__` /
`__SI_CI_PEER__`, see *Risk Analysis on CIs*); (3) the **SI profiles** reach a report through the CI (the CI build folds
every `SI_*_Profile_CL` into `SI_CI_CL`; no report reads a profile table past it); (4) checked **against the source
provider** by the report certification; (5) **data out** -- the output columns (`OutputPropertyOrder`), shaped by the
engine. Every report also carries the generated exclusions (`__SI_SCOPE__`), the large-tenant slices
(`__BUCKET_FILTER__`), the weighted factors (`__WEIGHTED_FACTORS__`) and a stable finding key
(`ConfigurationIdInputName`). `ops/report-certification/SI-ReportStructure.ps1` checks the parts statically (read-only;
it never changes a query, so no report fingerprint changes); `Test-SIReportFramework.ps1` reports them per report.
Reports not yet complete are listed with the missing part and changed as a deliberate report change (changing a report
changes its fingerprint and can change its rows).

**Names never change.** The output contract (`tests/pester/fixtures/report-output-contract.json`) pins every report's
output column names and every connector output map's column names (`data-model/outputs`: ServiceNow, the SQL hand-off,
the Excel exports). A rename or removal fails the gate; an addition passes once pinned in the same change; a value fix
keeps its name.

### `Reports[]` — field reference

Every entry maps to ONE Excel sheet / LA write. All fields required unless flagged optional.

| Field | Type | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReportName` | string | line 4320 lookup | Unique id. Referenced from `ReportTemplates[].ReportsIncluded[].Name`. |
| `ReportPurpose` | string | informational | Human description; surfaces in run logs. |
| `SecurityDomain` | string | `Calculate-RiskScore` (1844) | One of `Endpoint`, `Identity`, `Azure`, `Publicip`, `Hygiene`, `RiskAnalysis`. Selects the static Impact lookup table when the row has no `Impact` column. |
| `CategoryInputName` | string | column resolver (1824) | KQL column carrying the risk category. |
| `SubcategoryInputName` | string | column resolver | KQL column carrying the sub-category. |
| `ConfigurationIdInputName` | string | column resolver | KQL column carrying the asset id (DeviceId / UserObjectId / ResourceId). |
| `SecuritySeverityInputName` | string | column resolver | KQL column carrying severity (`Very High`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, …). |
| `CriticalityTierLevelInputName` | string | column resolver | KQL column carrying the tier label (`Critical - tier 0` etc.). |
| `RiskConsequenceScoreOutputName` | string | output naming | Excel column for consequence score. |
| `RiskProbabilityScoreOutputName` | string | output naming | Excel column for probability score. |
| `RiskScoreOutputName` | string | output naming | Excel column for the raw `RiskScoreTotal`. |
| `CriticalityTierLevelScope` | `[string,...]` | scoring filter | Allowed tier labels. Rows outside this set are dropped. |
| `SecuritySeverityScope` | `[string,...]` | scoring filter | Allowed severity labels. Rows outside this set are dropped. |
| `OutputPropertyOrder` | `[string,...]` | strict-mode column projection (1844) | Canonical 21-col order from `risk-analysis.schema.locked.json` plus report-specific extras (CMDB, EG, …). Engine emits exactly these columns in exactly this order; extras appended after the 21 canonical columns. ⚠️ **A column NOT listed here is not guaranteed to be exported at all — see "How a column reaches the .xlsx" below (audit #26). Declare anything you need.** |
| `SortBy` | `[string,...]` | Excel sort | Optional. Sort key(s) — prefer `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted`. |
| `ReportQuery` | `[string]` (one-element list, multi-line KQL) | submitted via `Invoke-GraphHuntingQuery` | The KQL itself. Engine auto-routes pure-LA queries to Log Analytics; mixed XDR queries to advanced hunting. |

#### Submission-path normalization (applies to every routing branch)

`Invoke-GraphHuntingQuery` is the single chokepoint all report queries pass through before
the Sentinel-lake / advanced-hunting / Log-Analytics-direct branches. Two behaviours are
enforced there:

- **Dynamic group-key cast (SEM0001 guard).** Log Analytics refuses to `summarize … by` a
  column of `dynamic` type. The CMDB columns (`cmdbName`, `cmdbId`, `cmdbCriticality`,
  `cmdbDataSensitivity`) are projected with `column_ifexists(…)` and arrive as `dynamic`
  whenever the source column is absent (and the PublicIP open-port / vuln reports surface
  `cmdbName` straight off `SI_PublicIP_Profile_CL`). The endpoint profile table stores `AssetName`
  as `dynamic` as well, so it is on the same list. Before submission, `Add-DynamicGroupKeyCasts`
  wraps any such column appearing as a **bare group key** in `tostring(…)`. It is list-driven
  (never touches numeric columns such as `RiskScore*` / `*Tier`, so ordering and scoring stay
  numeric), idempotent, and skips alias-form keys (`cmdbX = ""`) and already-cast keys. This
  mirrors the `tostring(cmdbName)` cast baked into the catalog's KQL (originally emitted by the
  now-retired `Build-RiskAnalysis.ps1`, #28 — the cast lives in the catalog and stays), so the runtime
  summarize path cannot regress relative to the built template. It covers the PublicIP reports
  and the cross-domain Attack-Path Summary reports, all of which group by `cmdb*`.
- **Deferred multi-path fallback logging.** When the engine tries several routes to the same
  data (Sentinel data lake → EG-hybrid → advanced hunting → LA-direct) and a later route
  **succeeds**, the earlier failed attempts are no longer logged as `[WARN]`/`[ERR]` — they
  were superseded by the success. Each failed attempt is stashed silently (full detail kept at
  `[DIAG]` + in the `ra-laerr-*.txt` dumps); a successful path then emits at most one `[INFO]`
  (`auth/data via <path> (after N superseded fallback attempts)`), and only a **total** failure
  flushes a single consolidated `[WARN]`. This stops operators from reading a successful report
  run as failed.

### Allowed `SecurityDomain` values + their `byCategory` keys

(from `risk-analysis.schema.locked.json → domains.<Domain>.impact`)

- **Endpoint** — Vulnerabilities, CVEs, Application, OS, Security controls, Firmware, Network, Accounts, Endpoint Hygiene, Sensor Health, Onboarding, EDR, Antivirus, Bitlocker, TPM / Secure Boot, Attack Paths
- **Identity** — Authentication, Account Lifecycle, Privileged Access, Workload Identities, Password Policy, Identity Hygiene, Conditional Access, Multi-Factor, Privileged SPN, Stale Identity, Service Account, Guest / External, Shadow Admin, Break Glass, Sign-in Risk, Role Assignment, Mailbox Access, Attack Paths, Admin Account Hygiene, Identity Lifecycle, Privilege Escalation Paths, Sign-in Behaviour, Threat Intelligence
- **Azure** — Public exposure + data sensitivity, Encryption at rest, Encryption in transit, Network exposure, Authentication, DDoS protection, Soft-delete / recovery, RBAC / least privilege, Logging / retention, Workload identity, mdcSecurityRecommendation, mdcManagementRecommendation, Attack Paths, AttackPath_GitHubToAzure
- **Publicip** — Exposed service, Open admin port, Vulnerability, Geo anomaly
- **Hygiene** — Coverage drop, Cmdb orphan, Drift, Pipeline, Stale Asset, Unsupported OS

Categories not present in `byCategory` fall back to `domains.<Domain>.impact.default` (usually 5.0).

### `ReportTemplates[]` — field reference

Templates group reports for a single run. The launcher selects a template via `$global:ReportTemplate`.

| Field | Type | Required | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ReportName` | string | yes | line 4280 lookup | Template id, e.g. `RiskAnalysis_Detailed`, `RiskAnalysis_Summary`. |
| `ReportPurpose` | string | no | informational | Label like `Detailed` / `Summary`. |
| `ReportsIncluded` | `[{Name: <string>}, ...]` | yes | `Resolve-ReportInclude` (4320) | Ordered list of report ids to run when this template is selected. |
| `Mail_To` | `[string,...]` | no | lines 4306-4310 | Per-template recipient override (see Email). |
| `Mail_SendMail` | bool | no | lines 4313-4315 | Per-template send toggle. |

### Email / notification surface

**Recipient-resolution precedence (highest wins)**:

1. **Per-template YAML override** (`Mail_To` / `Mail_SendMail` on the active `ReportTemplates[]` entry) — lines 4292-4316.
2. **Per-runmode globals** — `$global:RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To` / `RiskAnalysis_Summary_To` (and legacy `$global:Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To` / `_Summary_To`) — lines 3884-3910 (AutomationFramework branch) / 3979-4003 (community branch).
3. **Global** — `$global:SendMail` + `$global:MailTo` — lines 4002-4003.

When a per-template override applies, the engine logs: `Mail recipients overridden by template '<TemplateName>': <a@x.com,b@x.com>` or `Mail send-flag overridden by template '<TemplateName>': SendMail=<true|false>`.

**Override caveat**: because the merge is **full-replace by ReportName**, putting only `Mail_To` in the custom file loses the entire `ReportsIncluded` list from the locked entry. To override mail without losing reports, repeat the full `ReportsIncluded` list verbatim in the custom template alongside `Mail_To`. To suppress mail for one template, set `Mail_SendMail: false` (overrides global `SendMail=true`).

**Other mail globals (set in `LauncherConfig.custom.ps1`)**: `$global:SendMail` (master on/off), `$global:MailTo` (default recipients), `$global:SMTPFrom` (sender), `$global:SmtpServer` (relay host), `$global:SMTPPort`, `$global:SMTP_UseSSL`. Validation at line 241-243: if `SendMail=true` but no recipient source resolves, the engine throws.

### Do the Summary and Detailed reports show the same figures?

**They count different things, and always will.** The Summary report counts distinct **assets**; the Detailed report counts individual **asset findings** — one asset can carry many. The same estate therefore produces different totals and percentages in the two reports. Neither is wrong, and no setting makes them equal. Both mails carry a line under the Risk Score saying exactly this, so a reader who receives both is told why rather than left to guess.

What you *can* choose is whether the two reports are made to agree.

| `$global:SI_AISummary_Mode` | behaviour | use when |
|---|---|---|
| **`Consistent`** *(Community default)* | both mails show one set of figures — one report's executive block is copied onto the other | management receives **both** reports |
| **`PerReport`** *(SecurityInsight Pro default)* | each mail shows its own figures; nothing is borrowed | management receives **one** report, or (Pro) compares the two in the web app |

**The default depends on the edition (#346, operator 2026-10-05).** An explicitly set value wins in both editions; only an unset (or unrecognised) value takes the default. The engine decides the edition without a licence call: a run whose settings came from the Pro settings database carries `$global:SI_ProSettingsVersion` (set only by `Invoke-SIProSettingsLayer`, which stops the run when the database cannot be read), so `Get-RAAISummaryEdition` returns *Pro* exactly then, *Community* otherwise, and `Resolve-RAAISummaryMode -Edition` applies `PerReport` (Pro) or `Consistent` (Community). The settings catalog keeps `default: null` with a `defaultText` that names both. In `PerReport` nothing is shared: the snapshot is neither read nor written, `Test-RAAISummaryShouldAdopt` never adopts, and every site that would put a cached Risk Score into this report's mail, executive view or source line asks `Test-RAAISummaryUseCachedKpi`, which refuses in `PerReport` -- so each report computes its own KPI.

In `Consistent` mode, `$global:SI_AISummary_Leader` (default `Summary`, or `Detailed`) names **whose figures the other report adopts**. It is a tie-breaker, not a claim that one report is more accurate: once the two mails are required to agree, one of them has to be copied onto the other. The leader always builds its own figures and adopts from nobody, so **the follower's figures can never appear in the leader's mail**.

**What is shared, and what never is:**

| copied onto the follower | never copied |
|---|---|
| the AI narrative | the **Excel attachment** — always built from that report's own data |
| the headline Risk Score KPI and band | that report's own rows, findings, evidence and asset detail |
| the Top-50 asset list and top findings | |
| the per-domain severity table in the mail body | |

⚠️ **The cost of `Consistent`, stated plainly:** the follower's *email headline* shows the leader's figures while its *attached workbook* still contains its own rows — so totalling the spreadsheet will not match the headline above it. `PerReport` is the mode that avoids that.

**There is deliberately no time window deciding who wins.** An earlier design said "the first report of the cycle wins", but a cycle cannot be identified from a clock: the two runs may legitimately fall on different UTC days (Summary late evening, Detailed early morning), and a long run can straddle midnight by itself. Naming a leader removes the question — the pairing survives any schedule, timezone or run duration. `$global:SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours` (default 24) remains only as a **staleness backstop**, so a snapshot left by a host that was offline for a week is not carried into today's mail; it does not decide who leads, and it is ignored entirely in `PerReport` mode.

Decision logic: `engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-AISummaryMode.ps1` (pure — no globals, disk, network or clock of its own).

### Token substitutions inside `ReportQuery`

The engine recognises these markers and substitutes them at run time. None are valid KQL on their own — they MUST live in the YAML, never in a hand-run AH portal copy.

| Token | What's substituted | Source | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__BUCKET_FILTER__` | `where <hash-bucket-clause>` — e.g. `where hash(DeviceId, N) in (0,1)` | `AutoBucketCount` probe (~line 4000) | Query may exceed AH 30k-row ceiling. Engine probes 1→2→4→…→`AutoBucketMax` to find the largest size that fits. Kept per (`ReportName`, queryHash) in the Pro database (`cfg.RaBucketState`, #640 -- see "Bucket sizing" below); without the Pro database in `$SettingsPath/OUTPUT/AutoBucketCache.json`. |
| `__EXCLUDED_CVES_BEGIN__` … `__EXCLUDED_CVES_END__` | Per-report CVE blacklist injected as `\| where CveId !in (...)` | `risk-analysis-detection/SecurityInsight_RiskAnalysis_Excludes_Custom.json` | Suppress known false positives for ONE report without touching the locked KQL. |
| `__EXCLUDED_CONFIGURATION_IDS_BEGIN__` … `__EXCLUDED_CONFIGURATION_IDS_END__` | Per-report config-id blacklist | same exclude file | Suppress noisy config IDs for ONE report. |
| `__WEIGHTED_FACTORS_BEGIN__` … `__WEIGHTED_FACTORS_END__` | KQL `case()` chain mapping cmdb columns to `RiskFactor_Weight` integer (basis-100) | `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.json` (see Risk-score model) | Always present in modern reports; substituted from the weighted-factor JSON. |

`AutoBucketCount` controls: `$global:AutoBucketCount` (default `$true`), `$global:AutoBucketMax` (default `64`), `$global:AutoBucketCache` (default `$true`), `$global:ResetCache` (forces re-probe).

**Summary reports across buckets.** Each bucket returns its own row for a Summary group, aggregated over that
bucket's assets only. The engine combines those rows into one per group using the report's own
`summarize ... by` clause. Each column is combined the way the summarize built it: lists are unioned, delimited
lists are unioned token by token, max and min stay max and min, `arg_max` companions come from the winning row,
and counts are summed. A distinct count of assets is summed; a distinct count of anything else is recounted from
its list, or else takes the largest per-bucket count, so a finding present in two buckets is not counted twice.
Columns derived after the summarize are recomputed: counts from `array_length`, joined names from
`strcat_array` of the merged list, and a severity band from the row with the highest `Impact`. The group therefore
lists every asset from every bucket. When the `by` clause cannot be read, the rows are kept as they are rather than
combined on a guess. When one group has a column that cannot be recomputed and whose value differs between buckets,
that group's rows are also kept separately. Afterwards, a Summary row is dropped as a duplicate only when every
column matches.

### Bucket sizing — the core of Risk Analysis (#640)

With the Pro database the bucket count of every report is kept **in the database only**. The rule is "better too small
than too big", and the engine heals itself. Code: `engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-BucketStore.ps1` holds the statements
and the sizing rules (all pure apart from the `-Invoke` seam). `RA-AutoBucketing.ps1` holds the store behind
`Read-AutoBucketCache` / `Write-AutoBucketCache`. The probe, the challenger and the stale-query eviction are unchanged;
only where their state lives has moved. Schema: `sql/si-pro-settings.sql`.

| Table | Holds | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `cfg.RaBucketState` | per template + report + query fingerprint: the last known count, and when a run last *decided* it | the Risk Analysis jobs (db_datawriter) |
| `cfg.RaBucketHistory` | per report and run: the query fingerprint, the start and end count (the end count is the count KEPT for the next run), how it was decided (`cache`, `probe`, `measured`, `down`, `raised`, `configured`), the measured result (rows, the largest bucket's rows and estimated bytes, the largest request, and since #833 the longest slice in whole seconds `MaxBucketSeconds` and the count the slices ran at `RanCount`), the usual count, and the jump flag. The newest 30 per report are kept | the jobs |
| `cfg.RaBucketReset` | one-time resets staged on Operations > Risk Analysis query splitting; `ReportName` NULL means every report; `AppliedUtc` / `AppliedRunId` record the run that consumed it | the web app (INSERT only, `SI-ManagementGrants.ps1`) |
| `cfg.RaBucketImport` | per template: the counts kept in the storage account before were imported once | the jobs |

**Run start** (`Initialize-AutoBucketSqlStore`):

1. **One-time import.** The container passes the old storage-account cache once (`Get-SIRaAutoBucketCacheForImport`). It
   is written only where the database has no count for that report and query, and then recorded as imported. The blob is
   neither read nor written again.
2. **ResetCache.** If the setting is on, every count of the template is forgotten.
3. **Pending resets.** They are consumed in one transaction: the reports' counts are removed and the reset rows are
   marked applied with the run id. A reset therefore happens exactly once.
4. **Load.** The template's counts and the reports' history are read.

If the database cannot be read, the run sizes every report again and keeps nothing. It never reads a count from anywhere
else.

5. **Test template rows** (#833, `Invoke-SIRaBucketTestTemplatePrune`). The report certification
   (`ops/report-certification`) runs its own test template (default `Test688_Detailed`) through the real engine, which
   leaves bucket state under that template. A run of any other template removes the `cfg.RaBucketState` rows of templates
   named `Test<digits>_...` that no run has used for 7 days (no history row of that template in 7 days). It never removes
   the run's own template, nothing when the run itself is such a template, and never a history row. A failed statement
   never stops the run.

The schema columns `MaxBucketSeconds` and `RanCount` are added in place (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD`, nullable). The run checks
for them (`Test-SIRaBucketTables`, `HasTime`) and reads and writes them only when they exist, so an install one schema
version behind keeps working exactly as before.

**The lowest count** (#833, `Get-AutoBucketLearnFloor`). The configured count (2 for every report;
`SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed` for Detailed) is where a report STARTS when nothing is known. Until #833 it was also the floor
of every way down, so no report could run fewer than 2 slices (audit #56.1, 2026-08-10). Measured at internal on
2026-10-20: 58 of 69 Detailed reports returned under 100 rows, 18 returned none, and every one ran 2 or more slices. That
floor was not a safety rule. One slice is the whole query: the slice filter (`% 1`), the lookups, the overflow split (into 4
sub-slices, which together are exactly that slice) and the loss count work the same at 1. With the Pro database the floor
of the learned size is therefore **1**. A count the report's own template sets (`BucketCount` in the report entry) stays the
floor (v2.2.281: "you don't need to try less than 64"). Without the Pro database the floor is the configured count as
before. The bucketing gate is unchanged: a report is bucketed when its configured count is above 1.

**Per report:**

- **Step 4 — from measured size.** A report with no count for its current query (after a reset, or after its query
  changed) but with a measured earlier run starts from `Get-SIRaBucketCountFromMeasure`. The count is the next power of
  two of the largest of these needs, at least 1:
  - result rows / (30,000 / 2);
  - rows × bytes per row / (64 MB / 2);
  - inlined lookup rows × bytes per row × 1.15 / (1 MB / 2 − request overhead);
  - (#833) the longest slice in seconds × the count the slices ran at / (900 s / 2). The longest slice at N slices did at
    most N times its time of work, so at M slices the longest takes at most that / M.

  A run whose slices returned no rows is a measurement too (#833: an empty slice is measured, `Add-AutoBucketMeasure -Rows 0`).
  It needs 1 unless its time says more.

  **A changed query starts here** (#833). The engine asks this plan FIRST, and takes the earlier query's count
  (`Get-AutoBucketPreviousCount`) only when the report was never measured. Before #833 the earlier count came first and was
  raised to any count proved under the report's earlier queries. Live 2026-10-20: `Credential_Based_Lateral_Movement` had a
  remembered count of 2, and its changed query started at 16 slices (a count from its earlier queries' history). It returned
  at most 80 rows a slice and took 372 s, where the same report took 36 s the day before.

  With no measurement at all the report starts from the configured count and doubles (2, 4, 8, ...), or from the earlier
  query's count, as before.

  The request need is **bounded by the request the report really sent** (#697): its largest request
  (`MaxRequestBytes`) was sent at its bucket count, and only the split part shrinks with more buckets, so the need is
  never more than `MaxRequestBytes × BucketCount / (1 MB / 2)`. The smaller of the two request needs is used, so the
  bound never raises a count. The request numbers of the history row are **the report's own**: the rows and bytes of
  the lookups it split per bucket (summed over its buckets), and the largest part of one of its requests that no
  bucket count shrinks (`Get-AutoBucketRequestMeasure`, from the shape of each request it sent). They are never the
  run-wide largest snapshot, row width and query text of the hybrid inlining. Measured on a live estate, those run-wide
  values sized three attack-path reports with 1-112 rows to 16 buckets while every request they sent was a few KB; one
  of them took 884 s for 25 rows.

  The start is never below **the count a failed query proved necessary** (`Get-SIRaBucketProvenCount`): the largest
  count of the report's history that had to be raised during a run (`raised`), or that a probe climbed to above the
  configured count because a smaller count failed (`probe`). A probe whose first rung held is recorded as `measured`
  (when it started from a measurement) and proves nothing. A 900 s compute ceiling does not show in the rows or the
  request size, so only the failure itself can keep such a count.
  **#833: only the report's CURRENT query proves a count** (`-Fingerprint`; a history row without a fingerprint still
  counts). A count proved under an earlier query stopped a changed query from starting at its measurement. It also kept
  the count from coming down for as long as that row was among the newest 30. The time now shows in the measurement, so
  the proof of an earlier query is no longer needed for it. **The one exception** is a measurement without the slice time
  (a history row written before #833): the counts proved under the report's earlier queries still apply, because without
  the time a count set by compute would not show.
- **Step 5 — a count no failure proved comes back down** (#697, `Get-SIRaBucketShrinkCount`). For a remembered count,
  when the report's last run ran at that count, this run uses the largest of: the configured count, the measured need
  of that last run (step 4's rule), the count a failure proved, and half the count. The count therefore comes down
  **half per run** until it reaches what the report measured, and never below a raise or a climbing probe. If the
  smaller count does not hold, a bucket is refused or times out, the run raises the count again, and that raise is then
  proved, so the count cannot swing up and down. Step 5 is tried before step 3; the history records it as `down`.
  #833: "the configured count" in that rule is now the learn floor (1 with the Pro database), and the measured need
  includes the slice time. A report far inside every limit (rows, bytes, request AND time) therefore comes down to 1,
  half a step per run (8 → 4 → 2 → 1). A report with few rows but slow slices stays where its time needs it. Example: one
  slice of 400 s at 2 slices needs 2.
- **Step 3 — sizing down.** The count is halved only after **3 runs in a row** at that count in which every bucket stayed
  under 25 % of every limit, and none of them raised or resized it. It never goes down to the count that last overflowed
  (`Get-SIRaBucketDownCount`).
- **Self-healing.** Each case is handled as follows:
  - Platform failure (429, 503, 504, auth): retried with back-off, then retried late after the other buckets (existed).
  - Timeout or 502 ("too large / too slow"): that bucket is split by the sub-bucket pass (existed).
  - Overflow ("too many rows", 413): that bucket is now split and re-run alone. Before, the whole report was re-run at
    a higher count. **Added.**
  - After any split: the next run starts from twice the count. **Added.**
  - Query defect: not retried, the report fails (existed).
  - A slice that still fails after its recoveries: counted as a bucket loss, and the report is incomplete, never
    silently short (existed: #62 / #641).
- **The log says what the state keeps** (#833). Live 2026-10-20, the log said "16 bucket(s) kept for the next run" while
  the state and the history held 8. The early save (#713) writes a count as soon as a slice has succeeded at it, so a run
  stopped part-way does not lose it, and its line said "for the next run". The end of the same report then halved the count
  (#737: every slice far below every limit) and wrote 8. Now the early save says only "kept in case the run stops part-way".
  The end-of-report write prints the ONE line "N bucket(s) kept for the next run (this run: M)" with the value it writes to
  the state (the same value as the history row's end count). A count kept lower than the run started with is recorded as
  `down`, never as `cache`.
- **Stale fingerprints are removed** (#833). After a report ran complete at its current query, the end-of-report write
  removes the counts kept for the report's earlier fingerprints (`Remove-AutoBucketStaleSiblings`, the same eviction the
  probe uses), with their confirmed stamps. The database then receives a delete for each. Before #833 that eviction ran
  only in the probe, which a changed query that took its earlier count never reached, so old fingerprints stayed.
- **Confirmed only when decided.** The end-of-report write stamps `confirmedAt` only when this run probed, sized, raised
  or set the count (`Test-AutoBucketCountDecidedThisRun`). Stamping every run had kept the challenger's 7-day pause open
  forever on a daily schedule. A second defect is also fixed: once the challenger had flagged a count, the old-format
  fallback matched the report's own key and handed the same count straight back, so the re-probe never ran.
- **Step 2 — the jump warning.** A count of at least 4 × the report's usual count (the median of its earlier runs; at
  least 3 runs needed), or above 256, is flagged. The run raises one warning event, guard `ra.bucket.count-jump`. It is on
  by default, shows on the Guards page and goes to the report to Invardia; the run completes.

**Configuration** is read from the database settings like every setting: `AutoBucketCount`, `AutoBucketMax`,
`AutoBucketCache`, `ResetCache`, and the challenger's `AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier`, `_MinEntries` and
`_ConfirmDays`. The thresholds approved in #640 (4 ×, 256, 25 %, 3 runs, half the limits) are fixed in the code.

**Web app:** Operations > Risk Analysis query splitting (`Pages/Admin/QuerySplitting`, `QuerySplitting/*`). Readers see
one row per report and template:

- buckets now;
- the last run's start and end count (before and after);
- the run before;
- the usual count;
- the last change;
- the jump flag;
- what the row means.

An Admin stages a one-time reset of one report, or "Reset all", through Review & commit (kind `bucket-reset`, audited as
`riskanalysis.bucket-reset.stage`). The commit writes one `cfg.RaBucketReset` row per template with its `cfg.ChangeLog`
row.

### Cross-domain query shape — EG-native bucket re-key

The cross-domain **Attack-Path Summary** reports walk ExposureGraph (nodes + edges) to detect a path, then enrich the final target (and, for the vulnerable-device report, the source device) with CMDB metadata from a `SI_*_Profile_CL` snapshot inlined as a KQL `datatable`. The CL enrichment is a **leftouter join on an identity key** (e.g. `… on $left.FinalTargetId == $right.Target_AzureResourceId_Guid`), where the CL projection's join column **equals the EG NodeId hex** for matched rows — CL contributes only `cmdbName` / `cmdbCriticality` / `cmdbDataSensitivity` / `cmdbId`; EG owns path detection, tier and scoring.

Bucketing splits a too-large query into N hash partitions. For the partition to actually **bound the ExposureGraph work** (the expensive side), the `__BUCKET_FILTER__` block must hash on a column that exists *on the EG scan*, before the joins — an **EG-native** column such as `NodeId`. If, instead, the engine partitions on the CL-side enrichment key (a `cmdb*` / `Target_*` column that only exists *after* the joins), the EG scan runs in full for every bucket and the report hits the **900s advanced-hunting HttpClient ceiling** at large-tenant scale.

Each cross-domain Summary report therefore declares a per-report **`crossDomainBucketCoalesce`** block that maps its CL bucket-key column to the EG-native column it equals:

```yaml
- ReportName: Attack_Paths_Summary_Github_to_Azure_Resources
  crossDomainBucketCoalesce:
  - ClColumn: Target_AzureResourceId_Guid   # CL-side enrichment join key
    EgNativeKey: NodeId                       # the EG column it equals (NodeId hex)
```

Given this declaration the engine:

1. Keeps the **EG-side `__BUCKET_FILTER__` active** (it no longer suppresses it as "cross-domain lossy"), and leads the EG `__bucket_key` coalesce with the declared `EgNativeKey` — so the ExposureGraph scan is genuinely partitioned to ~1/N of nodes per bucket (a real partition that **bounds** EG work, not a row cap or sample).
2. Buckets the inlined CL snapshot on the matching `ClColumn`, whose value is the same EG NodeId hex, using the **same SHA256-modulo math** — so the EG subset and CL subset of each bucket align, and the per-bucket leftouter joins keep **every** match (lossless). Across all N buckets the union is identical to the un-bucketed result; only the query path changed.

The CL enrichment columns (`cmdbName`, …) are still projected by the report exactly as before — the re-key changes only *which column the partition hashes on*, never the output. The vulnerable-device report declares two entries: `Source_AadDeviceId → AadDeviceId` (the source-device node, where the bucket filter sits, surfaces `AadDeviceId` so it can hash the same value the CL source row carries) and `Target_AzureResourceId_Guid` (target enrichment, applied downstream). Reports **without** a `crossDomainBucketCoalesce` block keep the prior conservative behaviour (EG bucket filter suppressed when a CL let carries a non-EG key) — correct, just slower; the declaration is the opt-in that makes the EG side bounded.

### Three-layer risk computation (where these YAML values feed)

Every row that survives the report's `Scope` filters goes through:

1. **Layer 1 — base** (lines 3114-3115): `consBase = lookup(SecurityDomain,Category,SubCategory,SecuritySeverity)` and `probBase = lookup(...,CriticalityTierLevel)` — index lives in `risk-analysis-detection/riskscore.index.locked.csv` (shipped), with your own rows in `riskscore.index.custom.csv` checked first.
2. **Layer 2 — additive risk-factor adjustment** (lines 3117-3119): `consAdj = consBase + RiskFactor_Consequence` (today always 0); `probAdj = probBase + RiskFactor_Probability` (count of true risk-factor bools); `RiskScoreTotal = consAdj * probAdj`.
3. **Layer 3 — multiplicative business multiplier** (lines 3122-3144): `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted = floor(RiskScoreTotal * RiskFactor_Weight / 100.0)`, where `RiskFactor_Weight` is a basis-100 integer from the weighted-factor JSON.

Excel sort uses `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted` (preferred) — `Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` lines 5289-5297. The `__WEIGHTED_FACTORS__` blocks are substituted into report KQL **at run time** by the engine (`Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1:2430`), not by a build step.
---

### Generic SI finding fields, and one classification mechanism (REQUIREMENTS #560, #561, #562)

**The finding fields (#560).** Every finding carries the same SI fields whatever its source: si_title, si_description
(WHAT), si_category / si_subcategory, si_finding_type, si_severity / si_cvss / si_cvss_vector, si_remediation (HOW),
si_remediation_type (patch | configuration | upgrade | policy | manual), si_fix_reference, si_fix_available,
si_remediation_effort, si_user_impact, si_compliance_tags, si_mitre_tactics / si_mitre_techniques, si_affected_product /
_vendor / _version / _cpe, si_reference_url, si_portal_link, si_published, si_first_detected, si_last_seen, si_due_date,
si_risk_factors, si_asset_criticality, si_risk_score, si_owner, si_services, si_exemption, si_ticket_state, si_detected_by,
si_component. They live in `data-model/field-catalog.locked.json` once: a CI field a finding also carries (si_category,
si_last_seen, si_owner, si_services, si_risk_factors) has a `finding` block instead of a second definition.

**Mapped per source** in `data-model/mappings/<provider>.locked.json`, as FINDING record types (object class `finding`):
mde `vulnerability` (DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities + KB) and `configuration` (DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessment +
KB), mdc `assessment` (securityresources assessments + regulatory compliance), eg `finding` (the CVE node), shodan
`vulnerability`, servicenow `vulnerable_item` (the ticket read back). The ONE mapper (`ConvertTo-SIRecord`) maps them;
`Test-SIDataModel` lets a finding record type map finding fields (or a CI field with a `finding` block) and nothing else,
and an asset record type no finding field. A path the shipped Risk Analysis queries do not already read is marked
`verify: true` until it is confirmed on internal's live rows. A field no source gives stays absent -- never guessed.

**SI's own reports' texts are data** (`data-model/finding-texts.locked.json`, kind `finding-text`, one item per report,
`engine/data-model/SI-FindingTexts.ps1`): each report's WHAT (its fixed Impact text, else its purpose), its MITRE and
compliance references, and -- written later -- its HOW. `rowColumns` says which Risk Analysis row column fills which SI field;
`inference` holds the keyword rows that used to be code in RA-RiskScore.ps1 (first match over SecurityDomain + Subcategory +
ConfigurationName, then the security domain's default). Precedence, one rule: the row's own columns (the source's text) ->
the report's item -> (MITRE / compliance only) the inference rows -> nothing. SI_Finding_CL carries the result
(`ConvertTo-SIFindingRows -FindingTexts`). Pro: `finding-texts:<report>` per item; Community: finding-texts.custom.json.

**Every finding carries its fix (#590).** Four finding fields say what the finding is about and how to fix it, on every
Risk Analysis row (Detailed and Summary), SI_Finding_CL and the Pro database: `si_fix_remediation` (how to fix),
`si_fix_recommended_update` / `si_fix_recommended_update_id` (the security update Defender vulnerability management
recommends, DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities RecommendedSecurityUpdate / RecommendedSecurityUpdateId) and
`si_affected_software` ("Name Version (Vendor)"); lists are joined with `;`. Who fills them, one rule -- the source first,
then SI's text, never guessed:
- the CVE reports join DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities by device + CVE (`_swKey`) and project the four; the Summary keeps
  each value once per row. The fix text is the update when Defender names one ("Install the security update KB... on the
  device"), else the software to update. The Detailed description (`CVSSDesc`) is the graph node's, else the
  DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB description;
- the Defender configuration reports take the KB's RemediationOptions (the Summary also its ConfigurationDescription and
  RiskDescription); the Defender for Cloud reports the assessment's remediation;
- every other report's how-to-fix text is data: `si_fix_remediation` on its finding-texts item. Risk Analysis
  (`RA-RiskScore.ps1`, next to the MITRE / compliance fill) sets it on a row that has none; the row's own fix always wins.
  In SI_Finding_CL, `si_remediation` (the generic HOW) and `si_fix_remediation` fill each other.
The new columns are born si_ (the Risk Analysis output rename keeps a si_ name as it is). In the Pro database the data
sync derives `sidata.Finding` FixRemediation / FixRecommendedUpdate / FixRecommendedUpdateId / AffectedSoftware from the
stored row (DetailJson) with the other views' columns (`Get-SIDataDeriveFindingSql -Fix`, only when
`Get-SIDataFixSchemaCheckSql` finds the columns), counts the findings per recommended update as facet `update`, and the
Summary load writes the same four plus ConfigurationDescription / RiskDescription into `sidata.SummaryRow`. Mapped per
source too: mde vulnerability (update + id), mde configuration (RemediationOptions), mdc assessment (remediationDescription).

**Identity context (rich context, identity).** What Entra ID knows about an identity beyond the user and service-principal
lists is read ONCE per run for the whole tenant and added as parts to the records the discovery already captured
(`engine/asset-profiling/discovery/Get-SIEntraContext.ps1`; after the identity sources, before the records are handed on).
Read only: every call is a GET, one paged call per kind, summarised page by page -- never one request per identity. The
only reads per object go per policy object (the groups Conditional Access names, the owners of groups that hold a role,
the instances of an access review). Ids and names always travel together.
- **Service principals**: the application registration (part `app`: credentials, requested permissions, owners, publisher
  domain, notes, federated credentials); the delegated permission grants of the tenant in one read, per API with the
  consent type and how many users consented; last sign-in as a client and for a user; when each secret or certificate was
  last used; a managed identity's Azure resource. Owners are the principal's AND its application's, each person once: an
  application owner means the principal is not orphaned, and "no owner" is unknown when the applications could not be read.
  `si_credentials` lists every secret and certificate (expiry, state, last use, never used, used after expiry) and
  `si_credential_fix` says in one text what to rotate; four service-principal reports turn it into the row's how-to-fix.
- **Roles**: every assignment keeps its scope (`si_entra_role_scopes`: tenant, administrative unit or one object, with the
  scope's name). A role scoped to an administrative unit or one object is not a tenant-wide role and does not decide the
  privilege tier. `si_role_paths` says how each role is held (direct, through a group, through a group it can activate
  into), `si_pim_activation_requires` what activating an eligible role takes, `si_controls_privileged_objects` the
  role-holding groups and service principals the identity owns.
- **A role held through an activated group membership is an eligible role.** An identity can be a member of a
  role-holding group only because an eligible membership is activated right now (Privileged Identity Management for
  Groups). It then holds the group's roles only until the activation ends, so they are counted as ELIGIBLE roles, never
  as permanent ones -- the same rule as a directory role that is activated. How it is read: for every role-holding group,
  ONE paged read of the group's assignment schedule instances (`Get-SIPimGroupActivatedMemberships`, made at the end of
  the scan of the role-holding groups and kept for the run; never a read per user; the permission that scan already
  uses). A member counts as activated only when the group lists an activated membership for it and no assigned one; an
  activated ownership is not a membership. What changes for such a member: the roles through that group -- the ones the
  group holds and the ones the group is eligible for -- go to the eligible roles (`Get-SIInheritedRolesForPrincipal`), so
  the permanent roles, the permanent privilege tier and every report built on them no longer list them; `si_role_paths`
  reads `<role> via <group> (eligible, activated until <time>)`; `si_entra_role_scopes` lists the role as activated with
  the group (`via`, `viaGroupId`) and until when the membership lasts (`membershipActivatedUntil`). When the read is
  refused, or the tenant has no Privileged Identity Management for Groups, nothing changes: every member counts through
  the group as before (active = permanent), said once in the log; a refusal is not asked again for the other groups, and
  the completeness of the role read is not affected. Not covered: a membership that reaches the role-holding group
  through a nested group whose own membership is the activated one still counts as permanent.
- **Users**: manager and (guests) sponsors; interactive against non-interactive sign-in; MFA strength from the methods
  registered; Conditional Access per user from the enabled policies -- how many apply, whether one enforces MFA for all cloud
  apps with nothing else able to satisfy it, and the policies that would apply but exclude the user (conditions on location,
  device platform and risk are not evaluated; a group that cannot be read leaves the answer unknown); Identity Protection
  risk and the detections of 30 days as a count and their kinds; the last access review of the roles and groups held.
- **Devices** (endpoint discovery): the registered owners of Entra devices, one read.
- **Defender for Identity**: the account's tags and manager from the row already read, and 30 days of logons summarised
  inside one hunting query (last on-premises logon, cleartext LDAP binds, NTLM logons).
A read that fails never fails the run and never becomes a finding: its values stay unknown. A read the tenant is not
licensed for is recorded once and said on each identity it concerns in `si_not_licensed` (which fields, which licence,
`not licensed (<licence>)`) -- never in a security field, where it would read as a fact about the identity.

**One classification mechanism (#561 / #562)** -- `engine/data-model/SI-Classification.ps1`, built once and used for the
asset type, the asset subtype, the component of findings and assets, and every later dimension:
- `data-model/dimensions.locked.json` (kind `dimension`, Pro key `dimensions:<id>`): only each dimension's values --
  asset_type, asset_subtype, component (OS, SQL, Network, Hardware, Browser, Office, Application, Other).
- `data-model/classification.locked.json` (kind `classification`, Pro key `classification:<row id>`): rows of
  `source` + `field` (an SI field or a source path) + `match` (equals | in -> `values`; prefix | pattern -> `pattern`, a glob)
  -> `target` (the SI field) = `set`, `priority` 0..10000 (higher wins), `state` enabled | disabled, optional `when` (an
  extra condition over SI fields: "a server AND SQL Server installed"). The header's `targets` say per target field its
  dimension, asset or finding, `multi` (an asset carries every matching value) and the fallback when no row matches:
  si_asset_type `$keep` (the sources' value, kept in si_asset_type_source), si_asset_subtype General, si_components /
  si_component Other. Never blank.
- Evaluated with the risk factors' tri-state condition engine (`Test-SIConditionTri`): a field in si_unknown_fields never
  matches. Assets: the CI build (`Invoke-SICiClassification` in `Invoke-SICiCore`, after enrichment; build version 3),
  targets in header order, each written before the next (a SQL subtype gives the SQL component). The SQL IaaS registration
  (microsoft.sqlvirtualmachine/sqlvirtualmachines, now collected; si_sql_vm_resource_id) marks its VM si_sql_iaas within the
  build set. Findings: every Risk Analysis row (`Set-SIRaRowDimensions` in RA-RiskScore.ps1; si_component is a forced
  column of every report, cached per distinct field combination), from the row's finding fields (title, category, the
  affected product / vendor / CPE -- the CVE report now joins them from DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities -- and the Azure
  type of the asset it is on). A finding gets ONE value: an OS vulnerability on a SQL Server VM stays OS; the VM carries
  OS and SQL.
- **SQL** comes from every source that can prove it: the product / CPE (SQL Server, SSMS, Native Client, ODBC / OLE DB
  drivers, Reporting / Analysis / Integration Services), a SQL category / subcategory / name, an Azure SQL / PostgreSQL /
  MySQL / MariaDB resource (PostgreSQL / MySQL count as SQL -- a customer who wants them apart overrides one row), the SQL
  IaaS registration, Defender's software inventory (SQL Server itself, not SSMS or the drivers alone), the Exposure Graph
  SQL role, the ServiceNow MSSQL classes.
- **Carried to:** SI_CI_CL (si_asset_type refined, si_asset_type_source, si_asset_subtype, si_components), the CIs grid /
  Excel CI sheet (Subtype, Components), every Risk Analysis row and SI_Finding_CL (si_component), the Excel Detailed sheet
  (Component), and the ServiceNow vulnerable-item hand-off: `u_si_component` (contract `SI-CmdbHandoff.ps1`, the
  vuln.VulnerabilityItem Component column and snowstage.vImportVulnerableItem, the close-loop desired set / targets / sync,
  the Import Set push, the output map servicenow-vulnerable-item, the test pack). The ServiceNow CI output keeps proposing
  its class from si_asset_type_source (its transform map's contract is unchanged).
- Validators the web app calls: `Test-SIClassificationRule`, `Test-SIDimensionItem`, `Get-SIClassificationShape` (the closed
  sets as data); the C# twin `SI.Management.Web/Changes/ClassificationItemValidator.cs`, wired into `DataModelItemValidator`.
### Risk Analysis on CIs -- the `ci` data model

`SI_DataModel = ci` (default `legacy` until installs move to the new data model) makes the CI decide what one asset contributes to every
finding's score: its tier (probability base), its asset risk factors (the catalog's production factors on the CI --
they REPLACE the tokens a report derived from provider columns, so one factor is one definition and is never counted
twice; finding factors such as exploit or remote code execution and report-scoped factors stay the report's), its
criticality factor as the weight (`weighted = score x factor`) and its owning CMDB's values. The score formula, the
risk index and the rating bands are unchanged. The CI index reads `SI_CI_CL`: the CI set from the latest build, each
CI's properties from its latest full row within `SI_ActiveStaleDays` (30), stale CIs marked. `engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-ModelCompare.ps1` scores the same rows in both models and explains every
difference; a moved score without a reason fails the comparison.

### Risk Analysis -- the scope preamble, the factor support model, criteria (REQUIREMENTS #541, #550-#553)

A report query states WHAT it finds over SI fields and SI factors. WHICH assets and findings are in scope, and WHICH risk
factors fit the report, are data -- the engine generates them per run and feeds them to the query
(`engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-ScopePreamble.ps1`, one call: `Resolve-RAScopePreamble`, before the install filter and
bucketing):

1. **The scope block** -- `//__SI_SCOPE_BEGIN__ ... //__SI_SCOPE_END__` at the top of every query: one `let` per value the
   query may name (`SI_ScopeTiers`, `SI_ExcludedAssets`, `SI_ExcludedAssetTags`, `SI_ExcludedConfigurationIds`,
   `SI_ExcludedCves`, `SI_CveMinAgeDays`, `SI_ExcludedIpRanges`, `SI_ReportFactors`, the functions `SI_InScopeIp`,
   `SI_InScopeCve`, `SI_InScopeConfiguration`) plus the data-model lists and criteria the query names (`SI_List_<id>`,
   `SI_InList_<id>`, `SI_Factor_<id>`). The YAML carries the shipped copy (so a pasted query runs); the engine replaces it
   (`tools/ra-ci/Update-RaCiBlocks.ps1` regenerates the shipped copy).
2. **The CI blocks** carry the same scope INLINED (they run alone in Log Analytics on the hybrid path, so they cannot name the
   scope block): `_ciAsset` keeps the CIs in scope (`| where <predicate>`); `_ciLink` marks `si_in_scope_` and every report
   keeps `| where coalesce(si_in_scope_, true)` after its join (a finding with no CI has nothing to scope it by). Both restrict
   `si_rf_p` / `si_rf_c` to the report's factor set.
3. **The excluded configuration ids** end every query (every report emits a ConfigurationId).

**What applies to which report** is the data-model template `data-model/report-scope.locked.json` (kind `report-scope`,
one item per report; Pro: `cfg.ItemOverride` key `report-scope:<report>`, Community: `report-scope.custom.json`):
`subjects` (identity-user, service-principal, managed-identity, device, azure-resource, public-ip; finding kinds
vulnerability, recommendation), `scope` (disabled = setting | exclude | include, stale, tier, excludedAssets, assetTags,
configurationIds, cves, ipRanges) and `factors.include` / `factors.exclude` (exceptions only).

**The factor set is derived**, never listed (`Get-RAReportFactorSet`; the web app mirrors it in `ReportFactorMatrix.cs`):
an asset factor fits when a record type its providers map is one of the subjects' record types (a CMDB factor fits every
asset subject; a factor without providers fits by its fields' classes) AND every field its condition reads exists on one of
the report's classes (so `old_account`, which reads `si_identity_type`, never reaches a device report); a finding factor fits
the finding kinds it names (`findingKinds`) and, with `assetClasses`, only reports on that asset; then the exceptions. An
identity report never gets a network or device factor; a factor a customer adds reaches every report it fits with no query
edit. Reports consume the fed set generically -- `RF_P_CiFactors = coalesce(si_rf_p, dynamic([]))`, counted
(`array_length`) and listed in `RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed` -- so the scoring contract holds unchanged: the tokens are
the catalog's display names (see below), keyed to the factor id and deduplicated against what the CI context adds (`Add-RACiContext -FactorSet`). A joined object's factors are ITS fed set too: the device an
admin logs on to (`DeviceFactorIds` / `DeviceFactorNames`, the report's own question -- e.g. internet exposure -- left out
by its id and its fed name), an attack path's end asset (`TargetFactorIds` / `TargetFactorNames`) and source.

**Reports show the catalog's display names** (owner 2026-10-10: a customer renames a factor once, in the catalog). The scope
preamble feeds the name map with the factor set -- `let SI_FactorNames = dynamic({"<id>": "<name>", ...})` in the scope
block, and the same map inlined in the CI blocks, which add `si_rf_names_` (the names of `si_rf_p`'s factors, the id where
the catalog has no name). A report lists the names (`RF_P_CiFactorNames`) in `RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed` and its
score text, and keeps the ids in the technical column `RiskFactorIds` (machines and exports; Summary reports carry it in
their arg_max with the Detailed text, or as the sorted set). No name is written in KQL. A name is a token of its factor:
the alias map (RA-FactorKeys.ps1, the run's catalog when the data model is loaded) and the CI context's catalog key it to the
factor id, so "Client secret in use" and has_secret count once, and the tokens the CI context adds are display names too.
The appended configuration-id filter is safe for the Summary bucket merge: `Get-RASummaryMergePlan` reads only the final
summarize and the extends after it (verified for all 56 Summary reports).

**The disabled part** is one decision through `Resolve-SIDisabledAssetsRaFilter` (`engine/_shared/SI-DisabledAssets.ps1`):
`setting` follows SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis, `exclude` never shows a disabled asset (the report asks about usable
accounts -- no MFA, stale password ...), `include` always does (the disabled state is part of the finding, and the two hygiene
reports GuestWithPrivilegedRole / SPN_OwnsResourcePublicAccess). The CI predicate is
`coalesce(tobool(si_account_enabled), true)`: only a KNOWN disabled asset leaves; users, service principals and Entra
devices alike (a device finding of a disabled computer follows the same setting -- decided on this branch). A legacy marked
line (a customer query written for #533) is still rewritten from the same decision.

**Criteria reach Kusto only through typed builders** (`ConvertTo-RAKqlString` -- escaped, control characters refused;
`ConvertTo-RAKqlNumber` -- invariant; `ConvertTo-RAKqlDynamic`; `ConvertTo-RAKqlRegex` -- RE2-safe verbatim, no look-around,
back-reference or double quote; `ConvertTo-RAKqlCondition` -- the closed op set of the data model). A conditions list
compiles to `SI_InList_<id>(<fields>)`, a factor to `SI_Factor_<id>(<fields>)` (parameters named after the SI fields, sorted).
The criteria shape is the factor-wizards contract (`criteria: { kind: list|threshold|range, field, source, ... }`,
`Test-SIRiskFactorCriteria`, C# `FactorCriteria.cs`); the Kusto half is `Test-RAKqlCondition` (pure: field name, op, value
shape per op -- scalar <= 256 chars, list 1..500, number, days 0..36500, pattern, listid) and `Test-SIRiskFactorCriteriaKql`
(the pure checks + compile + a `print <fields> | where SI_Factor_<id>(...) | take 0` dry run against the workspace). The C#
side mirrors the shape checks; it does not run the Kusto dry run yet.

## Risk Analysis report catalog (model & inventory)

The full per-report catalog (every report's purpose, mode, severity/tier scope, source tables,
output columns, bucketing flag, and full KQL) is **auto-generated** from the single authority file
`risk-analysis-detection/RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml` by
`engine/risk-analysis/tools/Build-QueriesDoc.ps1`. **That YAML is the authority itself — it is
hand-maintained, not consolidated from anything** (audit #28: `_source/` +
`Build-RiskAnalysis.ps1` were retired and deleted 2026-08-06; regenerating would have replaced the
118-report catalog with an incompatible 264-report one and broken every run). The
`__WEIGHTED_FACTORS__` and `__BUCKET_FILTER__` placeholders live in the catalog and are substituted
by the **engine at run time**, not at build time. This section documents the **model** — how the
catalog is organised and how to read a report block.

### Catalog shape

- Reports are grouped into four **security domains**: `Identity`, `Endpoint`, `Azure`, `PublicIP`.
- Each domain has paired **Summary** and **Detailed** reports. Summary = one row per finding type;
  Detailed = one row per affected asset.
- Every report runs against the `SI_*_Profile_CL` Profile tables (latest snapshot via
  `summarize max(CollectionTime)`), with cross-domain Attack-Path reports additionally reading
  `ExposureGraphNodes` / `ExposureGraphEdges`.
- Each report carries a `__BUCKET_FILTER__` placeholder so the engine can split queries that would
  exceed Defender Advanced Hunting's ~30k-row ceiling (see [bucketing](#container--keda-deployment)
  and [troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)).
- The catalog summary line (counts per domain, Summary vs Detailed splits) is recomputed by the
  generator each release; the README teaser table and §6.9 inventory are re-counted from the YAML
  on every README touch — never quote stale numbers.

### How to read a generated report block

Each report block in the generated catalog has:

- **Purpose** — verbatim `ReportPurpose` from the YAML (one-line summary of what it flags).
- **Mode** — `Summary` or `Detailed`.
- **Severity scope** — which `SecuritySeverity` bands the report includes (Very High / High /
  Medium-High / Medium / Low / Informational).
- **Tier scope** — which `CriticalityTierLevel` rows are included (Critical-tier-0 / High-tier-1 /
  Medium-tier-2 / Low-tier-3). Engine post-filter at collection time drops any non-blank value
  outside the report's `CriticalityTierLevelScope` / `SecuritySeverityScope`; never emit "Unknown"
  defaults — use an in-scope value or blank.
- **Source tables** — the `*_CL` and Defender-XDR hunting tables the KQL reads.
- **Output columns** — the projected columns, in XLSX/JSON output order.
- **Sort by** — usually `RiskScoreTotal_Weighted`.
- **Bucketing** — whether the engine auto-splits the query (`enabled`/`disabled`, with the
  starting bucket count; AutoBucket grows to fit the ceiling).
- **KQL** — the full query, with `__BUCKET_FILTER__` substituted at runtime.

### Report-authoring rules (lint-enforced)

The pre-publish gate validates report structure (`RAReportStructure` / `TemplateCoverage` checks):

- Every report has the required fields; `ReportName` is unique across the catalog.
- `SecurityDomain` is in the allowed set (`Identity` / `Endpoint` / `Azure` / `PublicIP`).
- `ReportPurpose` is ≥ 80 characters (forces a meaningful description).
- Every report appears in at least one `ReportTemplate.ReportsIncluded` (no orphan reports, no
  ghost references to non-existent reports).
- **RA sources risk/finding signals from ExposureGraph** (nodes + edges) as the primary source;
  `*_Profile_CL` Profile tables join in only for tenant correlation (Tier, UnsupportedOsDetected,
  `cmdb*`, `IsStaleAsset`). `CriticalityTier` ALWAYS sources from `SI_*_Profile_CL.Tier`
  (engine-computed) — never coalesce in EG `criticalityLevel`.
- KQL comment hygiene: no inline `//` comments between expressions in a `project`/`extend` body
  (breaks LA's parser even when XDR tolerates it); `// Step X:` headers inside `|-` blocks drop the
  colon. Put doc comments above the `let`.

### Report templates (orchestrators)

`ReportTemplate` entries name the set of reports to run for a given launch mode (e.g. a Summary
template and a Detailed template, plus focused/complex test templates). The launcher's CLI flags
(`-ReportTemplate`, `-Detailed`, `-Summary`) win over config-set `RiskAnalysis_*_Override` values.
Override flags only BUMP a mode flag to `$true`; they never force it to `$false`.

### Lateral-movement routes for the SOC (#691)

Four routes that no earlier report covered, each a Summary + Detailed pair on the report standard (data in -> the CI ->
`si_*` / report columns out). All four are in both templates, in `data-model/report-scope.locked.json`,
`severity-model.locked.json` (the attack-path bands, then the report's own severity), `finding-texts.locked.json` and the
output contract; each has a certification spec under `ops/report-certification/specs/` that names the live reads it still
needs before it is certified.

| Report pair (`Attack_Paths_{Summary,Detailed}_...`) | Data in | Route (step 1 -> step 2) | What the SOC learns | Row asset / tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ServicePrincipal_Impersonates_Users` | Exposure Graph | application -[can impersonate as]-> user | which applications can act as which users, and how critical those users are | the application / the user's CI tier |
| `Workload_ManagedIdentity_to_Azure_Resources` | Exposure Graph | workload -[can authenticate as]-> managed identity -[has role on / has permissions to]-> Azure resource | which VMs, container apps, web apps, databases and AI services reach which resources through their identity (code on the workload = that access) | the workload / the resource's CI tier |
| `SignIn_Entitlement_to_Tier0_Servers` | Exposure Graph | user (-[member of]-> group) -[has role on / has permissions to]-> Tier 0 server | who is ENTITLED to sign in to or administer a Tier 0 server without being Tier 0 (the logon EVENTS stay the admin logon reports) | the user / the server's CI tier (0) |
| `Owner_to_Privileged_Service_Principal` | the CI (Entra ownership) | owner -[owns]-> Tier 0 / 1 service principal | which accounts on a less critical tier can add a credential to a privileged application and sign in as it | the application / its CI tier; the owner's tier is `SourceCriticalityTier` |

**How they are built.** The tier is the CI's (`si_tier`, through `_ciPeer` for the other end) -- never the Exposure Graph
criticality; a node without a CI keeps an empty tier level. Each graph route is sliced ONCE, on the path's source in the
edge set that names it, and the second hop is bound to the first (a semi-join, so the scan shrinks with the slice); the other
end's CI is joined after the cut point (`//__SI_LOOKUP_KEYS_HERE__`) with its reduction declared (`LookupNeededKeys`). The
Detailed row names its path by its graph node ids (`ConfigurationId`), carries an `Impact` sentence that names both ends,
and projects the standard columns plus `SourceCriticalityTier`. Severity = the attack-path priority (target tier weight +
10 per tier the path climbs). The probability factors are the target's fed CI factors and the graph's own node risk
factors; the owner route adds the OWNER's factors (an owner without MFA is the easier route). The Summary groups by route,
lateral-movement type, tier and CMDB values and counts what it is sliced on.

**No overlap.** The impersonation, workload-identity and entitlement edges were read by no report before; the workload
route leaves out credential nodes (the credential-based report's paths); the entitlement route reads no
can-authenticate-to edge and no logon event (the admin logon reports'). A route Microsoft's own Exposure Management attack
paths provide by default is retired from SI (#691 rule) -- not provable today (no Microsoft attack path is readable), and
re-checked by the weekly context discovery below (its ROUTE proposals).

---

## Report enrichment model

**Purpose.** A single shared enrichment vocabulary that applies across all RA (RiskAnalysis) reports, sourced from the field gaps in the MDE/ExposureGraph field-gap audit. Removes per-report bespoke columns; lets any report opt into the enrichment that's relevant.

> **v2.2 status:** `MITRE_Tactics`, `MITRE_Techniques`, `ComplianceTags` are emitted as always-exists columns on every report row, but **only the two `Device_Missing_CVEs_*` reports populate them today** (their KQL projects from `DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessmentKB.RelatedMitre*` + `Tags` + `ConfigurationBenchmarks`). The other 122 reports query Profile tables / Identity sources that don't carry equivalent fields, so the columns are present-but-empty. Broader coverage requires a per-`ConfigurationId` lookup table — slated for v2.3 (Tier B + F per the rollout below).
>
> `MoreDetails` is now built per row from harvested URLs + Defender / Entra / Azure portal links + MITRE links. v2.2 also injects `MdeDeviceId` / `EntraAccountObjectId` / `AzureResourceId` into every `summarize ... by` block (via `any(column_ifexists(...))`) so the engine can build portal links even on Summary aggregates that previously dropped these IDs.

### Design principles

1. **Generic over bespoke** — one column per signal family, not one column per report.
2. **Separate WHERE from HOW** — *new column* for hard data, *MoreDetails* for human-readable links + descriptions.
3. **Extend existing patterns** — don't invent new shapes if the `RiskFactor_*_Detailed` semicolon-list pattern already covers it.
4. **Always-emitted, ever-empty** — every report row has every column (even if empty); KQL filters and downstream consumers don't have to handle "missing".
5. **Engine-derived, not YAML-hardcoded** — the engine's per-row enrichment pass populates these from row-level signals; YAML doesn't have to know.

### A. New columns to add (per-row, all reports)

These become first-class columns in the report row, alongside `RiskFactor_*` and `cmdb*`.

| Column | Type | Source | Sample value | Used when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`MITRE_Tactics`** | string (`;`-list) | `DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessmentKB.RelatedMitreTactics` | `TA0006;TA0007` | Endpoint config / vulnerability reports |
| **`MITRE_Techniques`** | string (`;`-list) | `DeviceTvmSecureConfigurationAssessmentKB.RelatedMitreTechniques` | `T1003;T1110.003` | Same |
| **`ComplianceTags`** | string (`;`-list) | `KB.Tags` + `KB.ConfigurationBenchmarks` | `CIS;NIST 800-53;PCI-DSS` | Endpoint config reports |
| **`MsCriticalityLevel`** | string | `EG NodeProperties.rawData.criticalityLevel` | `High` | All reports (every asset has a node) |
| **`MachineRiskState`** | string | `EG NodeProperties.rawData.machineRiskState` | `High` | Endpoint reports |
| **`Defender_Alert_Active`** | int (0/1) | `AlertEvidence` (new source) joined on AssetId / DeviceId | `1` | All reports |
| **`Defender_Alert_Count_30d`** | int | `AlertEvidence` aggregated 30d | `3` | All reports |
| **`LastSeen_Days`** | int | `MDE_LastSeen` or `EG.lastSeen` → `now() - lastSeen` in days | `12` | All reports (already `IsStaleAsset` boolean — this is the underlying number) |
| **`RecommendedAction`** | string (short imperative) | Per-report engine logic | `Patch CVE-2025-15556 on <hostname>` | All reports |
| **`MoreDetails`** | string (newline-separated raw URLs) | Engine-built per row from: harvested `http(s)://` values across all columns + Defender/Entra/Azure portal URLs computed from `MdeDeviceId` / `EntraObjectId` / `AzureResourceId` + `attack.mitre.org` URLs from `MITRE_*` | `https://security.microsoft.com/machines/<id>/overview\r\nhttps://portal.azure.com/...` | All reports (always emitted, empty when no source IDs present) |

#### Notes

- `RecommendedAction` is short (≤120 chars). Long remediation steps go in `MoreDetails`.
- `MoreDetails` collects all per-row URLs (raw URL columns, portal links, MITRE links) into one cell, one URL per line (`\r\n`-separated, no label prefix). Deduped, capped at 25 URLs / 4000 chars to stay Excel-readable.
- `MITRE_*` are semicolon-lists same as `RiskFactor_*_Detailed` — for grep/filter consistency.

#### `ImpactedAssetCount` vs `ImpactedAssetsList` — currently NOT the same population (audit #25)

A reader seeing a number beside a list assumes the number counts that list. **Today it does not.**
Every Summary report computes them independently, over **different columns**:

```kql
| summarize
    ImpactedAssetCount = dcount(DeviceKey),          // distinct DEVICE KEYS, and dcount is ESTIMATED
    ImpactedAssetsList = make_set(AssetName)         // distinct ASSET NAMES, exact
```

They diverge **by construction**, not by rounding: two DeviceKeys sharing one AssetName, or a device
whose AssetName is null (`make_set` drops nulls), gives count > list; inconsistent name casing gives
list > count. Kusto's `dcount` is HyperLogLog-**estimated** on top of that, so it need not be exact
even over one column.

🔒 **Intended contract, for whoever fixes it:** the count must be **derived from the set that is
displayed** — `ImpactedAssetCount = array_length(ImpactedAssetsList)` — so the two cannot disagree.
✏️ **Corrected 2026-08-06 (#28): fix it in `risk-analysis-detection/RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml`
directly.** This used to say the YAML is *generated* and the fix belongs in `_source/` — it is not,
and `_source/` has been retired and deleted. Two practical notes from re-verification: the count and
the list sit in the **same `summarize`**, so the fix is a FOLLOWING `| extend`, not an in-place swap;
and `Endpoint_ActiveCompromise_Detected_Summary` has **no `ImpactedAssetsList` at all**
(`dcount(PrimaryEntityId)` only), so `array_length` cannot apply there — decide that one separately.

#### How the workbook is WRITTEN — one bulk load, not a cell at a time (v2.2.445)

The export used to pipe the finished rows into `Export-Excel`, which walks each row's properties in
PowerShell and writes cells individually. Measured on the 5.1 runtime that is **~0.55 ms per cell**,
and a Detailed workbook of 121,111 rows × 291 columns is **35.2 million cells** — the rate alone
predicts a **5 h 34 m** export to within 3.4% of the observed figure.

🔑 **Cost tracks cell SLOTS, not values.** At 3,000 × 291, dropping **86% of the values** saved **9%**
of the time (455.8 s populated vs 413.0 s mostly-empty). Every declared column is visited whether or
not it holds anything, and the `Details` sheet is the cross-report **union** of ~60 reports' columns —
so a CVE row carries ~40 real values in 291 slots and the sheet is ~85% structurally empty.

`Export-Worksheet` now makes **one pass** over the data, which simultaneously:

1. flattens non-scalars and scrubs XML-illegal characters,
2. records the widest rendered value per column (replacing `AutoFitColumns`), and
3. notes which columns hold `[datetime]`,

emitting each row as a preallocated `object[]`. The whole block then goes to EPPlus via a single
**`LoadFromArrays`** call, after which the table style, autofilter, frozen bold header, column widths,
wrap targets, vertical alignment and date formats are applied per column.

| measured | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| write only, 3,000 × 291 | 455.8 s | **3.2 s** |
| end to end, 3,000 × 291 | ~520 s | **17.5 s** |
| end to end, 20,000 × 291 | — | **148.9 s** |
| end to end, **121,111 × 291** (a real customer shape) | **20,051.92 s** observed in production | **1,261.6 s** measured |

| at 20,000 × 291, like for like | old path | bulk path |
|---|---|---|
| time | 3,472.09 s | **107.17 s**  (32×) |
| peak memory | 10,032 MB | **1,887 MB**  (5.3× less) |
| file size | 4.44 MB | **4.44 MB**  (identical) |

🔑 **The bulk path also uses ~5× LESS memory**, because a row held as a preallocated `object[]` is far
lighter than the `[pscustomobject]` rebuild it replaced. The faster export is also the one less likely
to exhaust a collection host.

🪤 **STYLING A COLUMN MATERIALISES A CELL IN EVERY EMPTY SLOT OF IT** (v2.2.448). `LoadFromArrays`
correctly writes NO cell for a null, and this sheet is ~85% structurally empty — so applying vertical
alignment to all 291 columns inflated the workbook **3.6×**: 0.67 MB → 2.40 MB at 3,000 × 291, and
4.44 MB → 16.03 MB at 20,000 × 291. **Nulls themselves cost nothing** — 0.56 MB with 251 null columns,
0.56 MB without. Range-based styling is **not** cheaper (2.41 MB, measured); the saving comes from
styling **7 columns instead of 291**. Top alignment is therefore set only where `WrapText` is, which
is the only place it is visible — in a normal-height single-line row `Top` and the default `Center`
are indistinguishable. ⚠️ Not merely a disk concern: the mail attachment cap is 20 MB, so an inflated
workbook can silently stop being attached for a customer who was previously under it.

**Nothing observable about the workbook changes.** Rows, columns, order, table, filter, header,
widths, wrapping and alignment are all identical — pinned by `SI-ExcelBulkExport.Tests.ps1`.

⚠️ **Three traps this path carries, all found by running it:**
- **A `[datetime]` has no format of its own.** EPPlus stores it as an OLE serial, so without an
  explicit number format the cell reads `46260,125`. Hence step 3 above.
- **The package is opened/created here**, not by `Export-Excel`. A workbook accumulates sheets across
  calls (index sheet, `Details`, AI summary), so an existing file must be **opened** and the target
  sheet deleted — creating a new package instead silently destroys the earlier sheets.
- **PS 5.1 cannot parse a multi-argument indexer nested inside a method-call argument.**
  `$ws.Tables.Add($ws.Cells[1,1,$r,$c], $n)` is a *parse* error, not a runtime one, so it fails before
  a line executes and looks nothing like a type problem. Hoist the range into its own variable.

🔑 **The InvariantCulture swap around the write is no longer load-bearing, and is kept anyway.**
`LoadFromArrays` hands EPPlus the **boxed** .NET value, so a `[double]` is never stringified and the
comma-decimal hazard (`9.8` → `"9,8"` → `98`) cannot arise on this path at all. Verified under `da-DK`.
A side effect worth having: dropping `AutoFitColumns` also drops the `System.Drawing.Common`
dependency, so Linux containers stop falling back to a default width of 10 and now produce the same
workbook as Windows.

#### How a value reaches Log Analytics — column types

A Log Analytics column keeps the type it was created with, and a value of a different type would be dropped
without any error. Before posting, the engine therefore reads the table's real column types and converts every
value to them, parsing numbers with a dot as the decimal separator on every host. Two cases cannot be converted,
and each gets a companion column so the value still lands:

- **A decimal in a whole-number column**, such as a CVSS of 7.9 in `Impact`. The exact value goes to
  `<column>_Exact` as text with a dot, for example "7.9", which KQL reads back with `toreal()`. The column itself
  gets the rounded value (8). "7.9" and "7,9" are both
  read as 7.9, never as 79.
- **Text in a number column**, such as a sentence describing the impacted assets. The text goes to
  `<column>_Text`, and the number column is left empty for that row.

Once a table has a companion column, it is filled on every later run. The workbook and JSON always carry the
original value.

#### How a column reaches the .xlsx — and how it silently does not (audit #26)

⚠️ **Emitting a column from KQL is NOT enough to get it into the output.** The export column list is
built in `Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` (~3319) and everything outside it is discarded by a single
`Select-Object -Property $DesiredColumns`, which feeds **all three sinks at once — the .xlsx, the
JSON sibling and the Log Analytics ingest.** The list is assembled from three sources:

1. **`OutputPropertyOrder`** from the report's YAML — *declared*, therefore reliable. A declared
   column that is missing on a row still appears, empty.
2. **`$ComputedCols`** — engine-added columns (scores, `AssetDetectedInReportName`, …).
3. **Everything else discovered from `$RiskScoreArray | Select-Object -First 1`** — i.e. **the FIRST
   ROW ONLY**.

🔴 **Step 3 is why columns disappear.** Advanced-Hunting rows are rebuilt from
`$r.AdditionalProperties.Keys`, and that bag **omits null-valued columns**. So a column that happens
to be empty on the first row is simply *absent from that object*, never enters `$DesiredColumns`, and
is then dropped for **every** row of that report — from Excel, JSON and LA together. The loss is
intermittent and data-dependent, which is exactly why it reads as "columns sometimes go missing"
rather than as a broken report.

**Consequence for report authors:** `MoreDetails` is declared in `OutputPropertyOrder` (120 uses) and
is safe. `RemediationOptions`, `RecommendedAction` and `Recommendation` are **declared nowhere**, so
they survive only when the first row happens to have a value. 🔒 **If a column matters, DECLARE IT in
`OutputPropertyOrder` — do not rely on discovery.**

**Trace columns** (`CollectionTime`, `SolutionVersion`, `TraceName`, `TraceID`) are deliberately kept
out of every YAML `OutputPropertyOrder` and pinned last by the engine.
