- **Report only by default.** Until `SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply` is on, the job changes nothing: it runs every rule and
  records each tag it *would* set. Only a real *true* turns writing on; an empty or unreadable value stays report only.
  Writing needs both the setting and the identity's write permissions.
- **Every planned and executed write is logged** to the asset-tag activity table (`SI_AssetTagActivity_CL`, through
  `dcr-si-assettag-activity`), one row per machine, resource or identity: `WouldApply` in a report-only run, `Applied`
  when written, and `AlreadyPresent`, `Skipped` or `Failed` (with the reason). The run ends with the counts.
- The tagging identity also keeps its activity rows and run log in SecurityInsight's own workspace and storage, and
  reads its rules from the Pro database (setup prints the one `CREATE USER ... WITH SID` statement for it).
- On a VM the Community launcher runs the same engine, signed in as the server's managed identity or a service
  principal (certificate or secret).

### 9. Template versions and conformance (Pro)

Every template item carries a content hash that ignores comments, key order and descriptions, so a documentation edit is not a change. When a new release changes a template you had overridden, the item shows **upgrade available** with what changed -- never merged for you; on the **Templates** page you take the new template or keep yours. A release whose templates would change what runs at your install is held until it is accepted (setup, or the updater), and the accepted set is recorded only after it has been written and read back. Who did what is always the signed-in identity.

### 9b. Template releases (Pro) -- by update ring, reviewed per detection method

**The default templates are template pack 1.0.** Like the `.locked` files of a Community install, the templates arrive with the install and are in force at once: every setup and update path (the guided install, the container setup, the settings import and the update that follows a new release) prepares the database, installs the templates shipped with the code as **Default templates 1.0**, and records it as installed -- so Template releases shows *Installed: Default templates 1.0* and lists it, and Template conformance compares against it. An install that already had templates but no pack recorded is adopted: with exactly the shipped content it is recorded as 1.0; with other content it is recorded as *customised, based on 1.0* and kept as it is, and 1.0 is offered for release. Template pack versions are their own series -- 1.0, then 1.1, 1.2 and so on as we release new templates -- and are independent of the code version. A newer pack you already run is never replaced by an older one. Where the install is still being prepared, the pages say so in plain words ("the next update or setup run installs them") instead of asking you to run anything.

The templates SecurityInsight Pro runs on -- mostly detection methods (tier rules per method) and Risk Analysis reports -- are released as versioned *template packs*, separately from the code, and rolled out by update ring. Your updater fetches the pack your ring approves, checks it against its SHA-256, and stages it. On **Template releases** you see what is installed, what is available, and per detection method which rules are new, changed or retired -- including any you have overridden. An Admin releases every method or only selected ones through Review & commit. The release job applies exactly what was reviewed and nothing else; it writes, reads back and only then records the release. Your overrides are never changed. History lists every release, and any method can be rolled back to an earlier version the same way.

**Every template pack installs automatically (#581, owner decision 2026-10-11 "Automatic").** A template pack -- Microsoft content, or a pack that carries more (SecurityInsight's own templates) -- is installed by the updater on its own, like a code fix, in every ring. Nothing an Admin could decide changes the outcome: your edits are overrides beside the template rows and an update never writes them, so a pack that touches an item you edited keeps your version and Template conformance shows where SecurityInsight's default now differs (information, no action). A pack waits only when (a) you switched on **Hold template packs** (your opt-in to approve by hand -- the only setting that creates a badge, together with (b)), (b) you rolled back from that pack, or (c) it needs newer code than the install runs (its `MinCodeVersion`; a pack without one that carries more than Microsoft content needs the code it was built by) -- (c) waits for the updater, never for a person. A pack that is already in force, or older, reads **installed**: nothing to press; an older pack is never put back automatically (a roll back is its own path). The decision is `Get-SIProTemplatePackDecision` (engine) and `TemplatePackState.Of` (web app), run on one shared case file. **Ring 1** installs the current templates directly on every deploy (`Publish-SITemplates -InstallCurrent`); that deploy records the shipped pack it put in force as the installed pack (`cfg.InstallState` TemplatePack = the shipped pack version, TemplatePackStatus = as-released; a newer pack in force is kept), and the page treats the newest pack staged from the shipped code as in force on a direct install -- so the pack whose content is in force reads installed there, with no badge and no Install button.

**Vendor console contract.** Input: a local folder of packs (SecurityInsight's own update feed, which this used to read, is retired). `Get-SITemplateReleases.ps1` returns JSON, read only: `{ Schema:1, Container, Rings:{ r0|r1|r2|r3:{Version,Sha256,ApprovedAt,ApprovedBy} }, Packs:[ { PackVersion, CodeVersion, Commit, Sha256, ShaVerified, Full, Kinds[], Methods[], Items, Fingerprint, Previous, Changes:{New,Changed,Retired,Unchanged}, ChangedMethods:[{Id,Engine,Method,New,Changed,Retired}], ApprovedNow[], ApprovedEver[] } ] }`, newest first; a pack that cannot be read or does not match its SHA-256 is listed with `Error`. Actions: **build** = `New-SITemplatePack.ps1 -Ref <ref> [-Method|-Kind|-ItemKey] [-PackVersion <v> | -ExistingPackVersions <v,...>] -PassThru` (the same ref always gives the same bytes and SHA-256; without -PackVersion the first pack is the shipped pack, 1.0, and later packs are the next minor after the highest published -- 1.1, 1.2, ...); **publish + release to a ring** = `Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Kind templates -PackPath <file> -Ring <0-3> -Apply` -- Invardia holds the pack, SecurityInsight decides the ring (framework UPDATE-1.7), and a published version never changes. Without `-Apply` both report a plan.

### 10. Azure access without the Az modules

SecurityInsight reaches Log Analytics queries, Resource Graph, Resource Manager, storage (OAuth only) and Key Vault with its own REST client, signing in with the run's identity (managed identity, certificate or secret) and needing no Connect-AzAccount. Throttling and server errors are retried as the service asks; any other refusal stops at once with the service's own message. Together with the REST ingest client (4a) and Microsoft Graph over REST, no engine, launcher or container needs a PowerShell module -- on a VM (Community or internal) nothing has to be installed besides PowerShell itself. There is no setting for this: earlier `SI_AzureAccess_Engine` / `SI_LogIngest_Engine` values left in a configuration file are ignored.

**Internal installs sign in to the platform natively.** On an internal (platform-managed) VM, the launcher reads the platform's `bootstrap\platform-config.json`, signs in as the bootstrap identity (managed identity when the host has one, else its certificate), reads the run identity from the platform Key Vault (certificate preferred when it is installed on the host, else the client secret) and sets the platform's public globals (`$global:HighPriv_Modern_*`, `$global:Context`, ...) exactly as the platform's own sign-in did -- without loading the platform's PowerShell module. A configuration file that reads a platform secret with `Get-PlatformSecret` keeps working: the same call is answered over REST.

### 10a. Setup runs with no PowerShell modules -- how it signs you in

Every setup, install, bootstrap, wizard, validation and grant script runs on plain REST, Azure Resource Manager and .NET. Nothing is installed from the PowerShell Gallery, and no script asks you to install a module or to run a separate sign-in command first. The scripts load one shared file (`setup/_shared/SI-SetupAzure.ps1`) that switches the process to SecurityInsight's REST client (section 10) and signs in:

| Who | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| A person | Azure Cloud Shell | The Cloud Shell token endpoint hands out tokens for the person who opened Cloud Shell, per service (Azure Resource Manager, Microsoft Graph, Key Vault, storage, Log Analytics, SQL), with no prompt. A Cloud Shell signed in to another tenant is refused with what to do. |
| A person | A workstation or server | Your browser opens the Microsoft sign-in page (OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE). The answer comes back to a short-lived listener on `http://localhost:<free port>/` on the same machine; the state value is checked and the code can only be redeemed with the verifier that never left the process. Tokens for the other services come from the refresh token, on first use. The client is the public Azure PowerShell client, so consent and the Microsoft Graph rights are the same as before. |
| An app | Unattended setup, pipelines | A certificate (from the machine or user certificate store) or a client secret; the sign-in is proven at once, so a wrong secret fails at the start, not three steps later. A managed identity works the same way. |

- **No device code.** Device-code sign-in is blocked by Conditional Access in many tenants and is never offered.
- **Memory only.** Tokens and the refresh token stay in the PowerShell process; nothing is written to disk. A script started from another script in the same process reuses the sign-in -- you sign in once per session.
- **One identity for Azure and Microsoft Graph.** The identity that creates the SecurityInsight app is the identity that grants it Azure roles.
- **What setup does over REST that the engines never needed:** Key Vault vaults (find, create, soft-deleted, name check) and certificates (read, import); resource providers (read, register); removing a role assignment and reading what a person holds through their groups; reading any resource, virtual machines, managed identities, SQL servers and databases, Azure OpenAI accounts, tenants and Log Analytics tables; storage tables, containers and queues, the lifecycle policy and name checks (never an account key) through Resource Manager, so setup needs no storage data role and no account key.
- **No Azure CLI either (#521).** Setup is not dependent on `az`: the Container Apps steps, the image build, Key Vault, SQL, managed identities, role assignments and storage all go through the same REST client. `setup/_shared/SI-SetupArm.ps1` holds what setup creates and changes (Container Apps jobs, apps and environments, the registry, Key Vault secrets and names, the SQL server, firewall rule and databases, storage, role assignments, Microsoft Graph counts); `setup/_shared/SI-AcrBuild.ps1` builds the engine image in the install's own registry -- it packs the folder itself (the `.dockerignore` honoured, so no customer configuration is uploaded), uploads it to the registry's build upload URL and asks the registry to build it (the four calls `az acr build` made). A Container Apps job is changed **read-modify-write**: the whole job is read with its secret values, the change is applied, and the whole job is written back in one request, so the job's command, probes, other identities and a manual trigger stay as they are.
- **Support staff work inside an Invardia Support session -- every change is recorded.** When Invardia support changes something in an environment (its own or a customer's), they first open that environment's Support session and then run the same setup script a customer would run. With a session open in the shell, setup signs in to nothing itself -- no browser, no certificate, no token request: it works as the environment's Support app, only in a subscription the session names, and every request goes through the session's recording command, so each change is written to that environment's audit log before it is made (reads are noted too). A subscription or a tenant the session does not name, and a sign-in as another app or a managed identity beside the session, are refused with what to do instead; a session whose recording command is missing is said and nothing is done. `setup/Grant-SIIdentity.ps1 -OnlyAppPermissions` (or `-Only <names>`) grants exactly the application permissions that are missing and nothing else, so the change made is the change that was approved; the plan shows each permission as present or missing, and `-Apply` prints the result per permission. Two steps have no request the session can carry and take a token from the session instead -- the sign-in to the SQL database of a database step, and the container registry's own token exchange when an image tag is checked: the token is recorded, what is done with it is not. Without a Support session nothing changes: a person signs in as described above.
- **Nothing is left on `az` -- and no exception is allowed (owner 2026-10-10).** The Pro web app's deploy (`pro-management/deploy/*`: the image build, the managed identities, role assignments, the two Container Apps, the SQL firewall rule and database users, the app registration over Microsoft Graph, the sign-in credential guard and the in-environment probe with its log read from Log Analytics) runs over the same REST client (`pro-management/deploy/SI-ManagementArm.ps1` over `SI-SetupArm.ps1` / `SI-AcrBuild.ps1`; Container Apps api 2025-07-01, whole objects read-modify-write). The retired SI Analyzer and its `az` sign-in helper (`auth/Connect-SIAzCli.ps1`) are deleted. The vendor release tool (`setup/Release-SI.ps1`) rolls and checks over REST too, signed in as the release identity (certificate, ids from Key Vault through the bootstrap identity). **Proof: a parser scan**, `tests/pester/SIv3-NoAzNoModulesParser.Tests.ps1` -- every shipped, customer-run and release `.ps1` is parsed, and any `az` command, `Connect-AzAccount` / `Connect-MgGraph` / `Connect-AzureAD` / `Connect-MsolService` / `Connect-ExchangeOnline`, Az / Mg module cmdlet, `Import-Module` / `Install-Module` / `Save-Module` / `Install-PSResource` or `#Requires -Modules` fails it with file:line. Its allow-list is empty.

### 11. Guided install

`setup/Install-SecurityInsight.ps1 -ConfigPath <config.json> [-LicencePath <file>] -Reporter <scriptblock> [-PreflightOnly] [-Resume] [-StatePath <dir>]` installs SecurityInsight unattended from the guided-install wizard's answers, as the signed-in person, in Azure Cloud Shell or locally. It checks first and changes nothing (sign-in, tenant and subscription, permissions, providers, free names); it then runs stable, repeatable steps built on the product's own setup scripts and reports each step's start and end, with nothing secret in it. Grants the person installing cannot make end as a warning with the exact command for the right person, and the install still completes; only a problem nothing can work around stops it, and `-Resume` continues from there. Keys for optional features are asked for in the shell and stored straight in the install's Key Vault. Exit codes: 0 installed, 1 a step failed, 2 a check failed, 3 invalid answers. Version 1 hosts on Container Apps with a managed identity.

**The checks before anything is created.** The install asks Azure first and creates nothing until every check passes: the sign-in (a person in Azure Cloud Shell or the browser, the Invardia Support session, or a sign-in the installation page hands over -- then nothing is signed in again, and an application installing is treated as the service principal it is: its own Azure roles and directory roles are read, Contributor with User Access Administrator is enough, and the people who administer the web app must be named and exist in the directory), the tenant and subscription, the permissions, the resource providers, the names, the region and the quota. The region check reads Azure's own metadata for every resource type SecurityInsight creates -- Log Analytics, the data collection endpoint, storage, Key Vault, the container registry, the Container Apps environment and jobs, the managed identity and, for Pro, the database server, the database and the web app -- together with the storage SKUs' restrictions for the subscription and the regions the subscription may use. A refusal stops the install with one line: which resource, which region, and which regions accept everything (the same geography first); the default region itself is never changed. The quota check makes sure the region has room for one more Container Apps environment and, when the install's environment already exists, that it allows the cores SecurityInsight's own job sizing can use at once. A tenant without Exchange Online is told that mail is not set up and can be set up later in Get Started -- information, not a warning. Long waits (registering resource providers, building the image, creating the database) say what they are waiting for about once a minute, so the progress on the installation page never goes quiet. A sign-in handed over by the installation page cannot be renewed by the install: when it is about to run out, the next step does not start and the install says to restart it with a fresh code -- it resumes where it stopped.

### 12. Licence bound to your tenant

A Pro licence names the tenant(s) it is for. SecurityInsight checks it against the tenant the run really works in: with a managed identity, the tenant in the identity's own sign-in token (which no setting can change); with a service principal, the tenant it signs in to. A licence copied to another tenant does not unlock Pro there.

### 12b. The install requests and renews its own licence (Pro)

A Pro install asks Invardia for its licence itself, and renews it before it ends. The client is
`engine/_shared/SI-LicenceRequest.ps1`; the updater job runs it on every update run, right after it signs in
(`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterLicence.ps1`), and `setup/Request-SILicense.ps1` runs it by hand
(`-Status` shows where a request stands, `-Force` asks now).

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Knock** | When there is no valid licence for this tenant, or it ends within 30 days (the licence's end date minus today, both UTC dates): `POST <base>/api/licence-requests` with `{ product: "securityinsight", version, tenantId, installId, edition?, contactEmail?, currentLicenceId?, currentValidTo: "yyyy-MM-dd"? }`. Invardia answers `202 { requestId, pullToken, status, pollAfterSeconds }`. Optional fields are sent only when they have a value (`contactEmail` only when `SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail` is set). |
| **Pull** | Each run, never sooner than `pollAfterSeconds` (Invardia sends 1800; 1800 when absent): `POST <base>/api/licence-requests/pull` with the header `X-Invardia-Pull-Token` and the JSON body `{}`. Answer `{ status: Pending \| Rejected \| Approved }`, with `licence: { fileName, sha256, contentBase64 }` when approved. |
| **Verify, offline** | The SHA-256 of the decoded file; the signature against the trusted signers (the framework verifier `engine/_shared/AitLicense.ps1`); valid dates today; the real tenant among its `tenantIds`; product SecurityInsight; only features SecurityInsight has. A file that fails any check is never installed, and the failure is reported. |
| **Install** | `setup/Set-SILicense.ps1` writes the `SI-License` secret (it verifies again first) and reads it back; the cycle then reads it back once more and requires the licence it verified. |

**The tenant is the token's.** The tenant sent and checked is the `tid` of the identity's own access token: the
managed identity's token, or the service principal's token in the updater (`az account get-access-token`). A
configured tenant id is never used; when the tenant cannot be proven, nothing is sent.

**What is kept where.** In the install's Key Vault: `SI-InstallId` (a GUID created once and reused by every
request), `SI-LicenceRequest-PullToken` (the pull token only -- it is never printed, logged or copied anywhere
else; a repeat knock returns the same request with a new token, which overwrites it) and `SI-LicenceRequest-State`
(status, request id, requested / next check / last check times, valid-to, the reason of a rejection, the last
problem -- no token). A Pro install also mirrors the state into the Pro database (`cfg.InstallState`
`LicenceRequest`, a `cfg.ChangeLog` row when the status changes), and the web app shows it at the top of
**Settings**. `diagnostics/Test-SIInstall.ps1` reports it too; a rejected request counts as wrong.

**Answers that are not a licence.**

| Answer | What the install does |
|---|---|
| `Rejected` (`reason`?) | Stores it with its reason and shows it. Does **not** ask again by itself for 7 days; `Request-SILicense.ps1 -Force` asks at once. |
| `401 { error: "token" }` | The token is unknown or expired: asks again in the same run (a token older than 30 days is not used at all). |
| `422 { error: "invalid", fields }` | Reports the fields; the request is not repeated for a day. |
| `429` + `Retry-After` | Waits at least that long (a pull also never sooner than `pollAfterSeconds`). |
| any other 4xx, 5xx, no answer | A warning; tried again on a later run. |

**Never fails the update run.** Every network failure and every unexpected error is one warning line; the
update carries on. All HTTP goes through `Invoke-WebRequest` with a timeout.

**Settings.** `SI_LicenseRequest_BaseUrl` (https only, default `https://invardia.com`),
`SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail`, `SI_LicenseRequest_Edition`. On the updater job the same values are the
environment variables `SI_LICENSE_REQUEST_BASE_URL`, `SI_LICENSE_REQUEST_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
`SI_LICENSE_REQUEST_EDITION`; `SI_UPDATER_KEY_VAULT` (written by `setup/Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1`) names the
vault and switches the step on. The updater image is built with the SecurityInsight folder as its context so it
carries the client, the verifier and the setter under `/si`; its service principal needs Key Vault Secrets
Officer on that vault (`Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -GrantSpnRoles` grants it).

### 12c. Updates from Invardia (Pro)

SecurityInsight Pro takes its new releases -- the code and the template packs -- from Invardia, the Pro update
platform. The vendor publishes each release to Invardia; Invardia releases it ring by ring (0 dev, 1 test,
2 design partners, 3 broad, always in that order) and signs, per ring, a small **manifest** that names the release
and its SHA-256. Your updater job asks for the manifest of *its* ring every night, checks it, downloads the release
and applies it with the same build / roll / verify / roll-back steps as before. Community installs keep updating
from GitHub with `Update-SecurityInsight.ps1`.

**How your install proves who it is.** Two things together: your Pro **licence** (it says what you may fetch) and
the install's **install key** (it says which environment, and so which ring, you are). The install key is created
automatically: when the install has none, it claims one from Invardia with its licence and the tenant taken from its
own sign-in token -- never from a setting -- and keeps it as one secret in the install's Key Vault
(`SI-Invardia-InstallKey`). The guided install stores the key from your installation page when it has one, and
claims none then. The key is never printed or logged. (The same key identifies the install's status reports -- see "Status reports to Invardia (telemetry)"; updates need only the licence and the key.) If a
claim is refused because a key already exists (for example after it was reset), the install says so and does not
keep asking: ask Invardia support to reset it.

**What is checked before anything changes.**

| Check | What it protects against |
|---|---|
| The manifest's **signature** (RS256 over the manifest bytes) against Invardia's update-signing **public** keys, which ship inside SecurityInsight (`engine/_shared/SI-InvardiaUpdateKeys.json`) and are chosen by the manifest's key id | a manifest someone else made, or one changed on the way. A key list fetched over the network is never trusted on its own; a new key is trusted only once it ships in this list, which is also how keys are rotated (old and new side by side, then the old one removed). An empty list refuses every manifest. |
| The manifest is for SecurityInsight and for the kind asked for (code or templates) | a valid manifest of another product or kind |
| Its **sequence** is not lower than the one this install already applied, per kind | an old, validly signed manifest being replayed to move you back |
| A code release whose **minimum starting version** is newer than the version the install runs waits, with the reason | a jump the release was not built for |
| The downloaded file's **size and SHA-256** equal the signed manifest's | a file swapped or damaged on the way -- it is deleted and nothing is applied |
| The code archive holds SecurityInsight with exactly the version the manifest names | a release in the wrong place |

**When an update waits.** A manifest that names a **manual step** is held and shown -- in the updater's log, in the
web app's **Settings** (Updates) and in `Test-SIInstall` -- and applied only after you set
`SI_UPDATER_ACCEPT_MANUAL_STEP = code:<sequence>` (or `templates:<sequence>`) on the updater job. A release that
needs a newer starting version (`minFromVersion`) waits for it. The first manifest from Invardia never moves your
jobs to an *older* version; after that, a deliberate roll-back by the vendor arrives as a new, higher sequence that
names the older version, and is applied. Template packs go through the same review gate as before: a pack that would
change templates in force is staged and held until an Admin releases it on **Template releases**. A pack is checked
by the code your jobs run, so it waits while the code is behind its ring. If Invardia asks the install to slow down,
it waits as long as asked.

**What you see.** The update source, the last manifest per kind (version, sequence, ring), the last check, anything
on hold and the last problem are kept in the install's Key Vault (`SI-Update-State`; never the key) and, on a Pro
install, shown in the web app's **Settings** under **Updates**. `diagnostics/Test-SIInstall.ps1` reports them too: a
refused manifest, or an install key that could not be claimed, counts as wrong; a hold is a note.

**Configuration.** `setup/Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1` installs the job with the ONLY source, Invardia (SecurityInsight's
own update feed is retired, 2026-10-06: `-Source feed` / `-SourceUrlSecretName` are refused, a leftover feed link is
removed). On the job: `SI_UPDATER_SOURCE=invardia`, `SI_UPDATER_RING` (`-UpdateRing`), `SI_UPDATER_KEY_VAULT`,
`[SI_UPDATER_INVARDIA_BASE_URL]`, `[SI_UPDATER_ACCEPT_MANUAL_STEP]`. The service principal needs Key Vault Secrets
Officer on the vault (`-GrantSpnRoles`).

**The vendor's side.** `setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1` publishes a release to Invardia: the code as
`securityinsight-src-<version>.zip` (`git archive` of a commit, one top folder `securityinsight-src-<version>/`), or a
template pack (`New-SITemplatePack.ps1`). It shows the request by default and sends it only with `-Apply`, signed in
as a publisher app registration with a certificate (app id, tenant, certificate thumbprint and API scope are
parameters, or read by name from a Key Vault), and checks that Invardia stored the same SHA-256.

**SecurityInsight decides the ring (framework UPDATE-1.7, operator 2026-10-06: "Solution (si, pim) decides WHAT version
and WHICH Ring to release in updates, Invardia relays only").** Invardia's back office releases nothing any more:
`Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Ring <0-3>` publishes AND releases to that ring in one call (`&ring=<n>`); without `-Ring` the
version is only registered; `-ReleaseOnly -Version <v> -Ring <n>` releases a version Invardia already holds to one more
ring (`POST /api/releases/securityinsight/<kind>/rings/<n> {version}`). Ring 2 / 3 need `-OperatorApproval` with the
operator's own words. On the install side every pull carries the environment's OWN ring (`{kind, licence, ring}`): the
updater's `SI_UPDATER_RING`, else the ring recorded for the install (`cfg.InstallState 'Ring'`, set by the guided
install, `setup/Set-SIInstallRing.ps1` or *Update ring* on the Settings page). With no ring known the updater asks for
nothing and says so (the Updates panel and `Test-SIInstall` show the reason); a manifest signed for another ring, or for
none, is refused. Invardia answers a pull without a ring with 422.

### 12d. What Pro does with Invardia by itself -- two switches, both ON by default

Owner decision 2026-10-05 (the same treatment as the status reports, framework UPDATE-1.4; PIM's equivalents are the
features `licence.autoRequest` and `updates.invardia`): a Pro install asks Invardia for its licence by itself (12b) and
takes its Pro updates from Invardia by itself (12c). Both are **on** for fresh and upgraded installs -- there is no
opt-in -- and each has one switch:

| Setting (Settings page, category *Licence & updates*, Pro) | On the updater job | Off means |
|---|---|---|
| `SI_LicenseRequest_Auto` -- *Automatic licence request* | `SI_LICENSE_REQUEST_AUTO` | the updater's licence step makes no call to Invardia; the log, and the Settings page's Licence panel, say "automatic licence request is off" |
| `SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled` -- *Pro updates from Invardia* | `SI_INVARDIA_UPDATE_ENABLED` | the updater claims no install key, asks for no manifest and applies nothing; the run says "Pro updates from Invardia are off" and ends with 0; the Settings page's Updates panel says so |

**Where a switch is read** (`engine/_shared/SI-ProAutomation.ps1`, `Get-SIProAutoSwitches`): the Pro settings database
first (`cfg.Setting`, scope `solution` -- what the Settings page writes), then the job's environment, else **on**. The
updater opens the Pro database once after signing in; if it cannot be opened or read, **both** Invardia steps are
skipped for that run, so a customer's "off" is never overruled by an unreadable database. The web app reads the same
rows (`ProAutoSwitches.IsOn`). SI's own update feed is retired (12f); Community installs have neither switch (they update from GitHub, 4. Updating).

**When the licence step asks** (unchanged client, 12b): no licence, a licence for another tenant, one that ends within
30 days, one in its **grace period** (named as such), or an expired one. A valid licence is quiet.

**After a request** (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterLicence.ps1`, `Send-SIUpdaterLicenceNotice`, decided by the pure
`Get-SILicenceRequestNotice`):

| Result | Audit trail (`cfg.AuditEvent`, source `job`) | Mail |
|---|---|---|
| a request sent | `licence.request.send` (ok) | -- |
| a licence installed | `licence.request.install` (ok) | yes: "new licence installed", valid until |
| rejected / refused as incomplete / not reachable / did not pass the checks / error | `licence.request.fail` (refused or error) -- when Invardia was asked, or the request could not even be made | yes, the same failure at most once every 7 days (the last mail is kept in the Key Vault secret `SI-LicenceRequest-Notice`) |
| nothing new (valid, waiting, a rejection still waiting out its 7 days) | -- | -- |

The mail goes to the guard-mail recipients (`SI_GuardMail_To`, else `MailTo`, else the SuperAdmins) through the
install's own relay settings, read from the Pro database with secrets from the Key Vault, and sent with the Risk
Analysis transports (`RA-Mail.ps1`, now carried by the updater image). The audit row is written by the updater itself
with the product writer's statement (the updater image carries no Pro settings code). A failed audit or mail is one
log line and never fails the run.

**The one-time notice** (`SI-FirstRun.ps1`, notice id `pro-auto`): the first run of a Pro install (its database is
configured) after the update explains both, with the setting and the job variable that turn each off, while at least
one is on. Shown once per install, recorded in the install state like the telemetry notice.

### 12e. The install's update ring -- recorded when it is installed (Pro)

The update ring (0 development, 1 internal, 2 early release, 3 broad) is a property of the install and is known
when it is installed, so it is recorded then -- not only after the updater has run. ONE record in the Pro database,
`cfg.InstallState` row `Ring`, compact JSON `{ ring, channel, setBy, source, setAt }`
(`engine/_shared/SI-InstallRing.ps1`), written by:

| Writer | When | Which ring |
|---|---|---|
| `setup/Set-SIInstallRing.ps1` | run by an admin, or by the two below | `-Ring` when given; else the setting; else the resource-group name |
| the guided install (step *Pro settings*) | after the settings import, as the person installing | the setting; else the resource-group name; channel `invardia` |
| `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1` | at the end of a Pro container install | the setting (Pro database, else `$global:SI_UpdateRing`); else the resource-group name |
| the updater job | every run that resolves a ring | its own ring, `SI_UPDATER_RING` (UPDATE-1.7: SecurityInsight decides it; never the ring a manifest names) (channel `internal`) |

- **The setting `SI_UpdateRing`** (0-3, Settings page, group *Sign-in & Azure resources*) is honoured by every writer
  that is not given a ring itself. The ring an install pulls for is SecurityInsight's
  decision (UPDATE-1.7): `SI_UPDATER_RING` on the job, else this record; with neither, the updater asks for nothing.
- **The resource-group name** follows setup's pattern `rg-si-<r0|r1|r2|prod>-<edition>-<hosting>` (`prod` = 3). A ring
  taken from the name is DERIVED: it is recorded when nothing is there yet and never replaces a recorded ring.
- **The header** (UPDATE RING) shows, in order: the ring the updater last updated by (its update state) > the recorded
  ring > the setting. *not recorded* appears only when none is known, and its tooltip says where an admin sets it.
- Recording never fails an install, a Bootstrap run or an update: a database that cannot be reached is one warning.

### 12e-2. ENVIRONMENT and TENANT in the header -- always shown, as in PIM Manager (Pro)

Operator 2026-10-09: *"why is the header experience between si and pim inconsistent. in si i dont have the environment
field, and it doesnt exist in settings and tenant name is missing from header"*. The header's context groups follow
PIM Manager (framework BRAND-2.2): ENVIRONMENT, MODE, UPDATE RING, SEARCH, TENANT, TENANT ID. Before, ENVIRONMENT and
TENANT were left out while their two web-app settings were empty -- and nothing filled them, so a fresh install showed
neither. Now both groups are ALWAYS shown (`Pages/Shared/HeaderContext.cs`, `EnvironmentOf` / `TenantOf`):

| Group | Value, first known wins | Not named |
|---|---|---|
| ENVIRONMENT | the setting *Environment name* (`SIWeb_EnvironmentName`) > the install's resource group (`Jobs:ResourceGroup`, else the setting `SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName`) > the container app (`CONTAINER_APP_NAME`) > *not named* | shown lighter; an Admin sees a small *name it* link straight to the field (`/Admin/Settings?cat=environment#s-SIWeb_EnvironmentName`) |
| TENANT | the setting *Tenant name (override)* (`SIWeb_TenantName`) > the tenant's own name as setup recorded it from Entra ID > its onmicrosoft.com domain (recorded with it) > *not recorded* | the tooltip says how it gets filled (setup, `setup\Set-SIInstallTenant.ps1`, or the override) |

- **The tenant's name is read from the tenant, never typed** (as PIM Manager's `Get-PimManagerTenantContext`, which reads
  Graph `/organization` and caches it). ONE record in the Pro database, `cfg.InstallState` row `Tenant`, compact JSON
  `{ tenantId, name, initialDomain, setBy, setAt }` (`engine/_shared/SI-InstallTenant.ps1`), written by
  `setup/Set-SIInstallTenant.ps1`: Graph `GET /organization` (display name + the verified domain marked *isInitial*),
  token from `-GraphToken`, else the guided install's own sign-in, else `az account get-access-token`. The guided install
  runs it in its *Pro settings* step (as the person installing), `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1` at the end of a Pro
  container install. A sign-in to ANOTHER tenant than the install's records nothing; the web app also ignores a record
  whose tenant id is not its own. Recording never fails an install.
- **The data sync refreshes it every run** (`engine/pro-data/Invoke-SIDataSync.ps1`, after the audit step): Graph
  `GET /organization` as the engine identity (`Get-SIGraphToken`; `Directory.Read.All` is already in its grants), written
  to the Pro settings database only when the name or domain CHANGED (`-OnlyIfChanged`). So installs made before setup
  recorded the name, and renamed tenants, show the right name the next day without anyone running a script. Read-only
  towards the tenant; a dry run reads nothing; a failure is one warning and never fails the sync. The data sync stays
  "not a connector" (it changes nothing outside SecurityInsight).
- **PIM shows no environment name until one is set**; SI shows the resource group instead (the operator asked that the
  group is never missing), so several open windows are still told apart.
- **Settings:** both settings sit in the FIRST category of the Settings page, *Environment*, on the card *Environment
  and tenant* (PIM Manager puts *Environment name* first on its Settings page). Before, they sat on the *General* card of
  the twelfth category, *Web app*, labelled "... (header)" -- present and searchable, but nowhere an admin looks first.
  The browser tab carries the environment's name only once it is named.
- **Since #909 (2026-10-27) MODE, UPDATE RING, TENANT and TENANT ID are no longer on the band itself** but in the
  environment's details card (§12e-4), in this same order; their values and fallbacks are unchanged.

### 12e-4. The header band fits a laptop on one line (#909, Pro)

Owner 2026-10-27, with a screenshot of the band at laptop width wrapping into two rows: *"page header looks bad on a
laptop device, maybe consider to remove this and restructure a bit so it fits"*. The dark band (`Pages/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`,
`header.topbar[data-brandbar]`, styles in `wwwroot/css/site.css`) carried twelve caption groups. It now carries, left to
right, on ONE line from a 1024 px window up:

| On the band | How | Hook (unchanged unless new) |
|---|---|---|
| Logo + version pill | as before | `[data-version]` |
| ENVIRONMENT (name + ring chip) | a disclosure: click, Enter / Space, or hover with a mouse opens the details card | `details[data-hdr-env][data-hdr-details]`, `data-named`; ring chip `[data-hdr-env-ring]` (new) |
| Data health | a compact chip (dot + state), link to Admin > Data health, warning colour when Unhealthy | `a[data-hdr-data-health]` |
| Search | takes the band's free width (110-460 px); below 1100 px an icon (the box's label) that opens into the box while it has the focus -- CSS only | `form[data-hdr-search]`, `#hdr-q` |
| Pending / Tasks | chips: icon, word (dropped below 1280 px), count badge; the warn badge only when non-zero; `aria-label` says the count | `[data-pending-count]`, `[data-task-header]`, `[data-task-open]`, `[data-task-overdue]` |
| Theme | an icon + the native select (keyboard and screen readers as before) | `select#theme-choice[data-theme-choice]` |
| The user | name + role, a menu (full name, preferences, sign out) | `[data-user-menu]`, `[data-role-badge]` |

**The details card** (`.hdr-details-panel`, light/dark from the theme tokens) holds what left the band, in PIM's order:
the environment's name and where it comes from (with the admin's *name it* link while it has no name), MODE
(`[data-hdr-mode]`), LICENCE (`[data-hdr-licence]`), UPDATE RING (`[data-hdr-ring]`, `data-utc`), GUARD MODE
(SuperAdmins, only while strict: `[data-hdr-guard-mode]`), TENANT (`[data-hdr-tenant]`) and TENANT ID
(`[data-hdr-tenant-id]`); for admins it ends with a link to **Settings > Licence & updates**
(`HeaderContext.LicenceUpdatesUrl` = `/Admin/Settings?cat=licence-updates`, `[data-hdr-details-settings]`), where the same
values are kept. Nothing is lost: every value that left the band is one click away. `js/site.js` treats the card as one
of the header's menus (one open at a time, Escape and a click outside close it); with a fine pointer it also opens on
hover and closes 250 ms after the pointer leaves, unless it was clicked open.

**Widths.** < 1440 px: tighter gaps, shorter name. < 1280 px: the chips drop their words (icon + count + tooltip /
`aria-label` stay), a smaller logo. < 1100 px: the search is an icon, the ring chip and the captions above the
environment and the user are visually hidden (still read by screen readers). A phone (<= 560 px) is the one width where
the band may take two rows (the logo, then the controls); nothing scrolls sideways at any width.

### 12e-3. The install's own resource names -- read from its record, never a literal (CR5 step 1, framework §12.11c item 6)

Every place SecurityInsight finds ITS OWN resource (the web app, its MCP server, the updater job, their identities, asset
tagging's identity) reads the name from one resolver, `engine/_shared/SI-InstallNames.ps1`, so the names every install
runs with today and the shorter names a NEW install gets in a later step work side by side. **Today's name is the
default**: an install with no record and no variable resolves exactly what it runs with now -- nothing is renamed and
nothing has to be set.

| Role | Today's name (the default) | Job variable |
|---|---|---|
| `web` | `ca-si-management` | `SI_UPDATER_WEB_APP` |
| `mcp` | `ca-si-mcp` | `SI_UPDATER_MCP_APP` |
| `updater` | `caj-si-updater` | `SI_UPDATER_JOB_NAME` |
| `templates` | `caj-si-templates` | -- |
| `webIdentity` / `mcpIdentity` / `updaterIdentity` | `uami-si-management` / `uami-si-mcp` / `uami-si-updater` | -- |
| `taggingIdentity` | `uami-securityinsight-tagging` | -- |

- **Resolution** (`Get-SIInstallName -Role`): the install record (`cfg.InstallState` row `InstallNames`, compact JSON
  one name per role + `recordedUtc`; per process `$global:SI_InstallNames`), then the updater job's variable, then
  today's name. A value that is not an Azure resource name is never used; an unknown role throws. A FINDER that must work
  on either name asks `Get-SIInstallNameCandidates` (the resolved name, then today's).
- **The record is written by the updater** on every run, right after it opens the Pro database and before anything acts
  on a name (`Invoke-SIUpdaterInstallNames`): the job's own variables win, its own execution names the updater
  (`CONTAINER_APP_JOB_NAME`) when no variable does, else what is recorded, else today's name; stored only when it
  changes; never fails the run. **This is how an existing install reaches the recorded state -- by the update, never by
  hand**: the first run after this release records today's names. Community (no Pro database): nothing stored, the
  names resolve the same way.
- **Setup records the names on the updater job** (`setup/Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1` sets `SI_UPDATER_WEB_APP`,
  `SI_UPDATER_MCP_APP`, `SI_UPDATER_JOB_NAME` from `-WebAppName`, `-McpAppName`, `-JobName`); the guided install passes
  the names from its names table (`Get-SISetupComponentNames` in `setup/_shared/SI-SetupNaming.ps1`, part of
  `Get-SISetupResourceNames`) to every script that creates or checks a component.
- **Readers**: the updater (secret hand-over, install links, database grants, the web app and MCP roll, its own roll),
  the release's update (`setup/Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1`, the web app's size), the pipeline's "is an update running"
  check (the updater's executions), the guided install. The web app reads the updater job from its own setting
  `Jobs__UpdaterJob` (today's name by default) to start the short "apply settings" run; a configured name only ADDS to the
  SuperAdmin-only lifecycle jobs, so a renamed job never loses that guard.
- **The names a NEW install gets (CR5 step 2) -- behind the setting `SI_Setup_NewInstallNames`, OFF by default**
  (REMOVE-ME once a fresh test install has proven them; read from the install's values, else the environment; only
  true / 1 / yes / on turns it on). Off, a new install gets today's names, exactly as before. On:

  | Component | Today's name | New install (setting on) |
  |---|---|---|
  | the web app | `ca-si-management` | `ca-si-web` |
  | its MCP server / the updater job | `ca-si-mcp` / `caj-si-updater` | unchanged |
  | the engine's identity | `id-si-<ring>-<edition>-<hosting>` | `id-si-engine` |
  | the web app's / MCP server's / updater's identity | `uami-si-management` / `uami-si-mcp` / `uami-si-updater` | `id-si-web` / `id-si-mcp` / `id-si-updater` |
  | asset tagging's identity | `uami-securityinsight-tagging` | `id-si-tagging` |
  | the web app's sign-in app registration (display name) | "SecurityInsight Management" | "SecurityInsight" |

  No ring or environment in any of them (the resource group and its tags say which environment). The names come from
  `Get-SISetupComponentNames -New` / `Get-SISetupResourceNames -NewNames` (`setup/_shared/SI-SetupNaming.ps1`); the guided
  install hands each one to the script that creates or uses the component: Bootstrap (the engine's identity; asset
  tagging's identity, passed and written to the install's settings as `SI_Bootstrap_TaggingIdentityName` only when it is
  not today's name), the web app deploy (its app, identity, MCP server and `Jobs__UpdaterJob`), the sign-in credential
  step, the updater job (which records the names in the install record), the database grants.
- **An existing install keeps today's names -- never renamed, never half-renamed** (`Resolve-SIInstallExistingNames`, run
  before anything is checked or created): the names an earlier run of this install recorded win (state `facts.names`,
  which now holds the component names and the sign-in display name as well); else, when the install's resource group
  holds ANY component under today's name (an identity, the web app, the updater job), every component and the display
  name keep today's names; else, when the group exists but cannot be read, today's names too; only an empty or new group
  gets the new names. With the setting off this decides nothing.
- **The sign-in registration under the new name** ("SecurityInsight") shares its name with SecurityInsight's ENGINE app
  registration (a Community install's sign-in with a secret). Under any name but today's, an app found by name is taken
  only when it carries one of the web app's own stable app role ids, so the engine's app is never patched into the web
  app's sign-in; today's name keeps today's behaviour.
- **The web app deploy** (`pro-management/deploy/Deploy-SIManagement.ps1 -UpdaterJobName`) sets `Jobs__UpdaterJob` when
  it is given (the guided install always gives the install's updater job); the release command's ring defaults read
  today's names from the same table.
- **Not built yet:** the display names of EXISTING installs (the sign-in app "SecurityInsight", the SQL admin group shown
  as "SecurityInsight SQL admins") -- renamed by the update in a later step. Resources Azure cannot rename keep their
  names on existing installs.

### 12f. Every ring updates itself daily -- from Invardia, the ring SecurityInsight released to (#350, UPDATE-1.7)

Operator 2026-10-05: *"si must handle updates 100% like pim handles ring 1 updates. they run like ring 2, 3 -- but the
only difference is that we also deploy/update manually, but the ring 1 env must be updated daily as other rings."*
Operator 2026-10-06: *"I tell in the solution that the release is approved to ring 1 (sample) / the solution publishes to
invardia backend / the solution pulls down and checks. solution owns the update engine and logic for this, but the source
is invardia platform / we are not having separate platforms like a si storage account fo si updates. one solution:
invardia"*. **SecurityInsight's own update feed is RETIRED** (the storage container `si-src-*`, its read-only link, the
ring map and `channel.json` in it, `Publish-SISourceArchive.ps1`, `Update-SISourceAccess.ps1`, `Publish-SITemplatePack.ps1`,
the updater's feed and ring-channel paths). An updater still configured for it (`SI_UPDATER_SOURCE=feed`, or a feed link
`SI_UPDATER_SOURCE_URL` without `SI_UPDATER_SOURCE=invardia`) changes NOTHING -- no sign-in, no read -- and its log says
how to move: `setup/Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -Source invardia -UpdateRing <n> -Apply`, which also removes the feed link
(env var first, then the `src-url` secret). `-Source feed` and `-SourceUrlSecretName` are refused.

**Which build.** SecurityInsight decides: `setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Ring <n>` publishes a build to Invardia AND
releases it to ring n (`-ReleaseOnly` releases a version Invardia already holds to one more ring). Every ring-1 build of
the same VERSION is released as its own number, `-Build` = `<VERSION>.<UTC yyyyMMddHHmm>` (Invardia keeps a version
immutable); the archive keeps VERSION, and the updater accepts an archive whose VERSION the signed version is a build of.
The updater job carries its ring (`SI_UPDATER_RING`, `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -UpdateRing`, else the ring recorded for
the install, 12e) and asks Invardia for what was released to that ring (12c): the signed manifest must name that ring;
its sequence is never lower than the one applied (a rollback is a NEW, higher sequence naming an older version); the
first manifest never moves the jobs backward.

**What runs here** is read from a record on the updater job itself -- Azure tags `si-installed` / `si-installed-commit`
(a tag MERGE: no new revision, no other tag touched) -- written by the updater after every update and by a manual deploy.
A release whose version is recorded there (a manual deploy of exactly that build) counts as applied: nothing is built or
rolled twice.

**The update** (`_shared/SI-UpdaterInvardia.ps1`): verify and download the archive (size + SHA-256 from the signed
manifest); then -- the guards below -- an SI job with an execution in progress does **not** hold the update (it finishes
on the version it started with); only a release carrying `UPDATE-NEEDS-QUIET.txt` waits for the running jobs (up to
`SI_UPDATER_WAIT_MINUTES`, 60; still busy = **deferred** to the next run); then
the release's own template gate and `setup/Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1 -Apply` (build, roll, verify, restore on failure)
for the engine jobs -- ring 1 installs the release's templates directly (#405) -- then, Pro, `_shared/SI-UpdaterWebApp.ps1`:
the web app and its MCP server (image built from the release, app rolled, healthy revision + `/healthz` 200 awaited,
previous image restored on failure; a failure = exit 1); then the record, the updater itself (last), and the run's state.

**The database first (#352, framework UPDATE-1.6 (j)) -- never new code on an old schema.** The update (Invardia, the only
source) rolls through `Invoke-SIUpdaterRoll`, and on a Pro install (the Pro database is
configured on the job) its FIRST step -- before the template gate, before any image is built or any job / app is rolled --
is `Invoke-SIUpdaterDatabase` (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterDatabase.ps1`), with the APPROVED RELEASE's own code:

1. **Schema** -- `engine/pro-settings/SI-ProSchema.ps1` `Invoke-SIProSchemaApply`, the ONE apply that setup uses too
   (`Initialize-SIVulnTargetSql`, `Initialize-SIDataSql`, `Import-SIProSettings -CreateSchema`, and through them the guided
   install and the internal ring-1 build), so list, order, batching and gate cannot drift. The set, in setup's order:
   `sql/si-vulnerability-target.sql`, `sql/si-data-schema.sql`, `sql/si-cmdbsync-schema.sql` (one batch each) and
   `sql/si-pro-settings.sql` (a batch per blank-line block -- a later block reads a column an earlier one added). Every file
   passes `Test-SISchemaIsAdditive` BEFORE anything is sent; one non-additive file refuses the whole set. Each file runs in
   its own transaction: a one-batch file is wrapped in `SET XACT_ABORT ON / BEGIN TRANSACTION / COMMIT`; the multi-batch
   file runs on one connection in one transaction (`New-SIProSchemaRunner`, the updater's store); a failed file is rolled
   back and nothing after it is sent. NOT in the unattended set: `sql/si-identity-schema.sql` (its own database; SCHEMA-1
   needs a recorded human approval per tenant and version) and `sql/si-cmdb-handoff-target.sql` (the customer's hand-off
   database, applied by its connector).
   **Indexes on large tables** are not built inside a file: on a database that builds resumably (Azure SQL Database,
   Managed Instance, Enterprise) an index the file would add to a table of 1,000,000 rows or more -- or one whose build is
   in progress -- is replaced by `PRINT 0` in the batch, and AFTER the files are committed it is built on its own, outside
   any transaction, `WITH (ONLINE = ON, RESUMABLE = ON, MAX_DURATION = <budget> MINUTES)` (10 minutes when the update
   applies new schema, 40 when the schema is current and its code rolled); at the end of the budget it PAUSES, the next
   update RESUMES it, a RUNNING one is left alone, and a pending index never fails the update. Order inside the schema
   step: the files (migrate) first, then the index step.
   **A paused build that blocks a file.** SQL Server refuses any change to a table while one of its index builds is
   paused (error 10637, *"... as one or more indexes are currently in resumable index rebuild state"*), so a release that
   adds a column to that table would fail at the schema. Only on that failure (`Get-SIProSchemaResumableBlock`, by the
   error's number or its text): the builds on the object the error names (`sys.index_resumable_operations`; by the tables
   the file changes when the error names no id) are read; a RUNNING one is waited for inside the update's budget (10
   minutes, read every 30 s -- it pauses at its own MAX_DURATION or ends), never aborted, and still running = the file
   fails with a plain reason (the next update tries again); each PAUSED one is stopped with `ALTER INDEX [name] ON
   [schema].[table] ABORT` (outside any transaction, the updater's db_ddladmin holds the ALTER it needs) and one plain
   line (*"an index build that was paused on <table> (<index>, <n>%) was stopped so the update could change the table;
   it is built again by the update after the change"*); then the file is applied again ONCE (a second refusal fails it).
   The index step after the files finds the index missing and builds it again in its budget. A schema that changes
   nothing on that table never meets the refusal, so its paused build is left to finish over the next updates
   (`Clear-SIProSchemaResumableBlock`, `engine/pro-settings/SI-ProSchema.ps1`).
2. **Grants** the new code needs -- `pro-management/deploy/SI-ManagementGrants.ps1`, the one list `Deploy-SIManagement
   -GrantSql` uses (the web app: cfg.Setting / cfg.ChangeLog, `si_audit_writer`, every `WebWriteGrants` table; the MCP
   server: `DENY SELECT` on cfg.WebKeyRing). The principals are DISCOVERED: the user-assigned identity on `ca-si-management` /
   `ca-si-mcp` (`SI_UPDATER_WEB_APP` / `SI_UPDATER_MCP_APP`), its database user found by SID (whatever the install named
   it). The update grants only -- never `CREATE USER`, never a fixed-role membership (those are the install's); an identity
   without a user is skipped with a warning. One transaction.
3. **Record** -- `cfg.InstallState 'SchemaVersion'`: `{"hash","files","grants","at"}` + the release in `[Version]`; the hash
   covers every file's SHA-256 and the grant statements. A run whose hash equals the record is a visible no-op (*"the
   database schema is current"*), nothing sent.

A refused set trips `schema.gate.refused`; a failed file or grant trips `update.schema.failed` (Guards view, mail,
telemetry). Either way `Invoke-SIUpdaterRoll` returns Code 1 with the reason, nothing is built or rolled, and the run's
`UpdateState` says *"the database was not updated, so nothing was rolled: ..."*. No Pro database (Community, VM) or a
release without `SI-ProSchema.ps1` = skipped. **Rights:** the updater's identity needs db_datareader, db_datawriter,
db_ddladmin and db_securityadmin on the Pro database -- given once by the server's Entra admin with
`setup/Grant-SIUpdaterDatabase.ps1 -Apply` (or `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -GrantSql`); its user is found by SID, so an
existing one is reused. *Honest limit:* db_securityadmin can revoke the append-only DENYs on the audit tables, so the
updater identity is a deploy identity of the same trust as setup, never a runtime one (the jobs, the web app and the MCP
server stay ordinary users bound by the DENYs). Still open: the sync-driven container update of a VM-managed install
(`setup/Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1` run by the sync engine, not by the updater) does not apply the schema itself.

#### The security baseline quick wins -- registry password off, Key Vault purge protection, SQL auditing (framework §12.11f items 4 + 5, §12.23 P7 / P8)

Three Azure settings of the install itself (`setup/_shared/SI-SecurityBaseline.ps1`, one library for both ways they reach
an install). No SQL statement is involved: each is an ARM setting.
- **The container registry's admin user OFF.** It is a fixed user name + password that can PUSH images -- and every job
  runs its image with the collection identity. A managed-identity install pulls as its identity (AcrPull) and builds over
  ARM, so nothing needs it. Turned off only when no job and no app of the install still pulls with a registry password
  (`Get-SIRegistryAdminDecision`; a job that does is named and the setting stays on). Reversible.
- **Key Vault purge protection ON** for the vault the jobs name (`SI_KeyVaultName`), only in the install's resource group.
  A deleted vault and its secrets then cannot be purged before their retention ends (90 days by default) -- and the vault's
  NAME stays taken for those days after a delete (a reinstall with the same names then needs another name or the vault
  recovered). ONE-WAY: Azure never turns purge protection off.
- **SQL auditing ON** for the install's database server (every database on it), the same model as PIM: a diagnostic setting
  `si-sql-audit` on the master database sends `SQLSecurityAuditEvents` (resource-specific table) to the install's
  workspace (`SI_WorkspaceResourceId`), the server's auditing setting on with Azure Monitor as target (Azure's default
  audited groups: successful and failed sign-ins and every batch), and the table's retention RAISED to 90 days (never
  lowered; the table may only appear with the first events -- said, and set by a later check). The Microsoft.Insights
  provider is registered first; Azure's 409 "register Microsoft.Insights" is tried again for 5 minutes, then said plainly.
  Reversible (the auditing setting put back, the diagnostic setting SI made removed; the retention stays).

Every change is READ BACK (tried again a few seconds apart while Azure finishes it).

**New installs** -- only while `SI_SECURITY_BASELINE_NEW_INSTALL` is on (REMOVE-ME, `Test-SISecurityBaselineNewInstall`,
**OFF by default** until a fresh test install proves it): `Initialize-SIInfra.ps1` creates the vault with purge protection;
`Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1` turns the registry's admin user off after the jobs exist (the registry is still created
as today); the guided install's `pro-sql` step turns SQL auditing on (`Set-SISqlServerAuditSetup`). None of them fails
setup: a refusal is one line.
**Existing installs** -- `setup/Set-SISecurityBaseline.ps1` through the Support app (the pattern below), steps `proof`,
`registry-admin-off`, `keyvault-purge-protection`, `sql-audit`. The proof also REPORTS (never changes) whether the web
app holds "Container Apps Jobs Contributor" on the resource group.
**The updater** changes none of it.

#### Support-app cut-overs -- the shared pattern (framework §12.23 P8)

`setup/_shared/SI-SupportCutover.ps1`, used by `Set-SISecurityBaseline.ps1` and `Move-SIEngineToLeastPrivilege.ps1` (the
pattern PIM used to move all its environments, 2026-10-14):
- **PLAN by default.** Every run first prints the install's SHAPE (`Get-SIInstallShape` + `Add-SIInstallSqlShape`):
  resource group, image, the user-assigned identities with client ids and who uses them (the engine's marked), the SQL
  server and its Entra admin, the database users with their roles, the admin group's members.
- **The SQL server is found from the install's own jobs** (`SI_Pro_DataSqlServer` / `SI_ProSqlServer`, matched EXACTLY to a
  server's FQDN; the database from `SI_ProSqlDatabase`; the engine identity from `SI_UAMI_ClientId`) -- never by a name
  pattern (a pattern found a Community server).
- **The admin group read from both sides**: its member list can read back empty for the Support app; each identity's
  `memberOf` is read too.
- **`-Apply -Steps <names>`** with STRING step keys (an `[ordered]` hashtable with integer keys treats `$h[2]` as an
  index); unknown names refused; `-Apply` without `-Steps` refused. The first step is a read-only proof. A step with
  nothing to do says so and writes nothing.
- **ONE rollback record per run**: the BEFORE value of everything changed, written before each change -- a JSON file on the
  support machine (`%ProgramData%\si\logs\cutover\<script>-<environment>-<utc>.json`) and a short copy in the install
  (`cfg.InstallState`, which steps when and the file's name; the engine move keeps its own `EngineSqlAccessBefore`).
  `-Rollback <record> -Apply` restores it, newest first.
- **Every write read back**, the new state printed. Add before remove; nothing restarts.
- **After an environment**: wait `-ObserveMinutes` (default 6), then COUNT the runs since the cut-over and the failures
  (`Wait-SICutoverObservation`, from the jobs' executions) -- one environment at a time, never "it looked fine".
- **Only through the Support session**: ARM via `Invoke-InvardiaSupportArm`, SQL via `Invoke-InvardiaSupportSql`, Graph
  via `Invoke-InvardiaSupportGraph` -- all in the customer's audit log. Without a session the scripts refuse; tests pass
  their own seams.
#### The engine identity's database rights -- the least-privilege role `si_engine` (#672, framework §12.23 SQL-ACCESS)

The design (P1-P8) is the framework's (`DOCS/REQUIREMENTS.md` §12.23) and is not restated here; this is SI's engine part.
Before #672 the engine identity (`id-si-<label>`, shared by every engine job) was db_datareader + db_datawriter on the WHOLE
Pro database: it could read the web app's sign-in key ring and the secret hand-over, and write access assignments, settings
and every other component's data.

**The role** -- `engine/pro-settings/SI-EngineGrants.ps1`, the ONE list (the same shape as the web app's
`SI-ManagementGrants.ps1`), applied by `Get-SIEngineGrantSql` (one batch, idempotent, every grant only where its schema /
object exists):

| kind | what | why |
|---|---|---|
| schema | `sidata` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE | the data sync, Risk Analysis' stream to SQL, the CI build own this data |
| schema | `vuln`, `cmdbsync`, `snowstage` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE | the vulnerability loop, the CMDB sync, the ServiceNow hand-off; no DELETE on the schema |
| object | DELETE on `cmdbsync.SyncStage`, `snowstage.BatchCi` / `BatchCiKeyValue` / `BatchCiRelation` | the only deletes in those schemas |
| DENY | INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on `sidata.CiOverride` | an Admin's manual CI override is the web app's; the engine reads it |
| object | SELECT on 24 cfg tables / views it only reads (settings, documents, departments, rules, exemptions, CMDB views, access for the guards' SuperAdmin mail ...) | object-level: cfg is not the engine's |
| object | SELECT + exactly the verbs it writes on 36 cfg tables: its run / guard / connector / mail / report / pipeline / flow / bucket / verification records, `cfg.InstallState` (tenant record, licence-superseded mark, proven mail restriction, template release state), `cfg.AuditEvent` / `ChangeAttribution` / `ChangeLog` (INSERT only), and the template tables for `caj-si-templates` (`cfg.Template` INSERT / UPDATE, `cfg.TemplateRevision` INSERT, `cfg.TemplatePackStaged` read) | DELETE only on `cfg.DataOutItem`, `cfg.RaBucketHistory`, `cfg.RaBucketState` |
| object | EXECUTE on `cfg.AuditRetentionApply`, `ConfigBackupPrune`, `ConfigBackupTake`, `ConfigJournalRetentionApply`, `ConnectorChangeRetentionApply`, `CmdbImportSnapshot` | the only way the engine removes audit / journal / backup / change-log rows |

Never the engine's (`$script:SIEngineNeverGranted`, enforced by the static test): `cfg.WebKeyRing`, `cfg.PendingSecret`,
`cfg.SecretHandoverKey` (no right at all), writes to `cfg.AccessAssignment`, `cfg.Setting`, `cfg.Document`,
`cfg.ItemOverride`, `cfg.Connector`, `cfg.Exemption`, `cfg.ConfigJournal`, `cfg.ConfigBackup`, UPDATE / DELETE on the audit
trail, writes to `sidata.CiOverride`. No DDL, no security right, no fixed-role membership. The five procedures that let only
"a job identity" in (`IS_ROLEMEMBER('db_datawriter')`) now let `si_engine` in too (`sql/si-pro-settings.sql`).

**The inventory** -- `Get-SIEngineSqlReference` reads the engine's own code (engine\, container\ but not the updater,
launcher\, and `setup/Publish-SITemplates.ps1`, which `caj-si-templates` runs as the engine identity) for every statement on
a product object, with file, line and function: FROM / JOIN / APPLY = SELECT, a quoted name = VIEW (OBJECT_ID / COL_LENGTH
answer NULL for an object the caller holds no right on), INSERT, UPDATE (also through an alias), DELETE, MERGE = INSERT +
UPDATE (+ DELETE with `THEN DELETE`), EXECUTE, and DDL (never granted -- every DDL statement in engine code must be guarded,
so it runs only on a database one schema version behind). Code that runs as ANOTHER identity is listed in
`$script:SIEngineNotEngine` with the reason (setup's `Set-SIProSetting` / `Set-SIConnector` / template staging, the
updater's schema and install-name records, the schema-text builders). Summary on 2026-10-14: 63 files, 1,645 statement
sites, 505 object / permission pairs: sidata 71 objects (SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE), vuln 2 (SELECT / INSERT /
UPDATE), cmdbsync 9, snowstage 13 (with the hand-off tables), cfg 66 (24 read only, 36 written, 6 procedures executed); 21 guarded DDL sites
(`SI-DataSql.ps1`, `SI-DataCi.ps1`). The identity ledger (`si.*`, its own database `sqldb-si-identity`) is NOT in this
step: the engine keeps db_datareader + db_datawriter there.

**Who applies it** (framework §12.23 P8 -- the updater changes no security):
- **New installs** -- the guided install's `pro-schema` step: `Get-SIEngineDatabaseAccessSql` (the contained user by SID,
  the role, its grants, the membership); the `pro-settings` step applies `Get-SIEngineGrantSql` again once the cfg tables
  exist. **Behind a switch until a fresh test install has proven it** (decided 2026-10-14 by SI, PIM and Invardia: no
  setup change reaches new installs before that): `SI_Setup_EngineLeastPrivilege` (REMOVE-ME, `Test-SIEngineLeastPrivilegeSetup`;
  read from the install's values, else the environment of the shell that runs the install -- the parameter file does not
  carry it), **OFF by default**. OFF = the engine gets today's db_datareader + db_datawriter AND `si_engine` with its
  grants (harmless; it prepares the cut-over). ON (`true` / `1` / `yes` / `on`) = `si_engine` only. The step's message
  says which. When the test install has proven it: the default becomes ON, then the switch and `-KeepBroadRoles` go.
- **Existing installs** -- `setup/Move-SIEngineToLeastPrivilege.ps1`, run per environment by Invardia support through the
  Support app, in the shared cut-over pattern (see "Support-app cut-overs" below). EVERY statement through Invardia's
  audited `Invoke-InvardiaSupportSql` (audit row first: server, database, SHA-256, the purpose line). Without that function
  the script REFUSES (it never opens a connection of its own). The server, the database and the engine user are read from
  the install's own jobs (`-ResourceGroup`); `-Server` / `-Database` / `-EngineUser` override. PLAN by default (the shape,
  the read-only proof, what each step would do). `-Apply -Steps`: `proof` (read again after the changes), `grants` (the
  grant script), `membership` (the user into `si_engine` + the in-database rollback record, its roles before,
  `cfg.InstallState 'EngineSqlAccessBefore'`, written once, one transaction; the broad roles stay), `remove-broad-roles`
  (a separate later run after a green pipeline: the proof again, and only when it is green db_datareader + db_datawriter
  are removed, one transaction that refuses without the role membership or the record). `-Rollback <record> -Apply` puts
  the recorded roles back and clears the in-database record.
- **Every update** -- `Invoke-SIUpdaterEngineAccessCheck` (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterDatabase.ps1`) only
  READS: the engine user(s) (Entra users in `si_engine` or db_datawriter other than the updater, the web app and the MCP
  server), their roles and the role's real grants, against the RELEASE's inventory (`Get-SIEngineAccessDrift`): `ok`,
  `not-moved` (still has the broad roles -- said once, no warning), `drift` in plain words (a statement the role would
  refuse with file:line, another role such as db_owner, an old gated procedure) as a WARNING line. Never a grant, never a
  block, never throws.

**Grants in a later release -- the certificate-signed grant procedure `cfg.ApplyComponentGrants`** (#672; framework §12.23
P4 + P9 "five years without contact"; BUILT 2026-10-15 on branch `si-v3-scale/signed-grant-proc`, not merged, not run on
any install). ~95% of installs have no Support app and no contact: after setup the SQL admin group may be EMPTY for years,
so every update's schema AND grants are applied by the updater's OWN contained user -- no admin, no person. Code:
`engine/pro-settings/SI-GrantProcedure.ps1` (pure T-SQL builders + the rules' mirror), the procedure's text is in it.

- **The procedure** takes the release's shipped grant list as ONE JSON array and returns every row's outcome (applied /
  skipped / refused / failed + the reason); one refused row never stops the others. Every rule is checked INSIDE it (a signed
  module never trusts its caller), every name is QUOTENAME'd, the permission comes from a fixed list. **The frozen rules**:
  GRANT / DENY / REVOKE only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, EXECUTE; target `SCHEMA::<s>` or `<s>.<object>` with `<s>` in the
  compiled product schemas (sidata, cfg, vuln, cmdbsync, snowstage); never EXECUTE on a whole schema, never the procedure
  itself, only a table / view / procedure / function (never a synonym -- it could point outside), a missing object is
  SKIPPED; grantee one of the compiled COMPONENT ROLES, `public` only for a DENY or GRANT EXECUTE on a procedure, a user only
  as the target of a REVOKE when it is a member of a component role (the web app's legacy direct grants); a GRANT or REVOKE
  that would lift an existing DENY is refused (only an admin lifts a DENY). MEMBER: an existing user into one of ITS
  component's roles, never the caller, dbo, a role or a db_owner member. USER: a contained Entra user (`WITH SID = <client
  id>, TYPE = E` -- the SI way, the server needs no directory identity; on the test VM's local SQL Server a user without
  login stands in) only for a compiled component and only into its main role; an SID that is there is reused, a name held
  by another principal is refused. **The compiled components**: engine `si_engine`, web `si_web` + `si_audit_writer`, mcp
  `si_mcp`, updater `si_updater`, tagging `si_tagging`, templates `si_templates`, and RESERVED for later components (P9
  point 3) loader `si_loader`, api `si_api`, worker `si_worker`, report `si_report`. Every role is created once by the
  admin run (AUTHORIZATION dbo), so the procedure never creates a role.
- **The certificate.** Created by the admin run, INSIDE the database: `si_grant_signer_<utc>`, EXPIRY_DATE 2099-12-31, a
  random password generated inside SQL and never returned, ADD SIGNATURE, then the PRIVATE KEY REMOVED -- nothing stored,
  rotated or maintained (owner 2026-10-15: "Keep the in-database certificate"). Its user holds exactly what the procedure
  exercises: CONTROL on each product schema that is in the database, ALTER ANY USER, ALTER on each component role (never
  ALTER ANY ROLE, never a database-wide right). Proven on real SQL 2026-10-15: a database-level `WITH GRANT OPTION` is NOT
  enough (the signed module cannot even see the object); CONTROL on the schema is, and the grants it makes are recorded
  with the schema owner (dbo) as grantor, so they outlive the certificate. Module signing ignores the certificate's expiry
  (a test signs with an expired one); 2099 is belt and braces.
- **A release can NEVER re-sign a changed procedure without an admin -- by design.** Any ALTER drops the signature (proven:
  the procedure then runs with no rights and every grant in it fails), and ADD SIGNATURE needs the private key, which no
  longer exists; keeping a key the updater could use would make the updater an admin again. So the procedure is FROZEN: a
  release never ships a changed one (it is in no schema file, a test enforces it, and si_updater is DENIED ALTER on it so
  an update cannot drop the signature by accident). A new version is installed only by the admin run (setup / the cut-over):
  it re-creates the procedure when the marker (`si-component-grants v1`) differs, drops the old signer certificate and user,
  signs with a new certificate -- earlier grants stay (grantor dbo). A design that needs a changed procedure at a
  no-contact install is a design error (P9 point 2); an install whose procedure is older keeps using it (its rules are
  general) and the updater says so once per run.
- **The updater's path** (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterDatabase.ps1`): before the schema it reads (read-only) whether
  the procedure is there, signed, and whether its OWN identity may EXECUTE it (HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME -- a ddladmin cannot read
  other principals' grants). Yes: step 2 sends the whole shipped list through it (`Get-SIReleaseGrantRows`: the web app's
  and MCP server's members first, the schema files' own GRANT / DENY, `si_engine`'s grants and DENYs from
  SI-EngineGrants, `si_web`'s from SI-ManagementGrants plus the revokes of what an earlier release gave the web app,
  `si_mcp`'s DENY on the sign-in key ring); the list is part of the schema fingerprint; a REFUSED row is a WARNING line, a
  FAILED row stops the update before any code is rolled (as today's grant step); the outcome is recorded in
  `cfg.InstallState 'GrantProcedureLastApply'`. No: today's path (direct grants, db_securityadmin) -- nothing changes for an
  install that has not been cut over. The engine's user is NOT made a member here (the engine's own cut-over does that,
  with its record). The schema files' 17 GRANT / DENY statements are each guarded by
  `IF IS_ROLEMEMBER(N'db_owner') = 1 OR IS_ROLEMEMBER(N'db_securityadmin') = 1` on the line before: an admin and today's
  updater run them as before; an updater without db_securityadmin skips them and the procedure applies the same rights
  right after (proven: the whole schema re-applies as a ddladmin-only user).
- **New installs**: `setup/Grant-SIUpdaterDatabase.ps1` (run by `Install-SIUpdaterJob -GrantSql` in the guided install, as
  the server's Entra admin) behind `SI_Setup_SignedGrantProcedure` (REMOVE-ME, `Test-SIGrantProcedureSetup`, read from the
  environment of the shell that runs the install), **OFF by default** until a fresh test install has proven it (customer
  sites install with today's setup this week). ON = the full model: the roles, the signed procedure, the updater in
  `si_updater` and NO db_securityadmin. P9: setup must ship this model (switch ON by default) before the first no-contact
  install.
- **Existing installs**: `setup/Install-SIGrantProcedure.ps1`, run per environment by Invardia support through the Support
  app, every statement through Invardia's audited `Invoke-InvardiaSupportSql` (refuses without it). PLAN by default (a
  read-only state read; prints every statement); `-Apply` runs `-Steps` (default `record;roles;procedure;sign;rights;updater`,
  one call per step with its purpose line), then the read-back (current, signed, 2099, private key gone, si_updater
  EXECUTE, the updater a member). The rollback record `cfg.InstallState 'GrantProcedureBefore'` = {user, roles before,
  procedure there before, at}. db_securityadmin STAYS. `-RemoveSecurityAdmin` (a later run) refuses until the read-back is
  green AND the updater's own `GrantProcedureLastApply` shows an update through the procedure with no failed row; then it
  removes db_securityadmin in one transaction. `-Rollback` puts db_securityadmin back if the record had it, takes the
  updater out of si_updater if it was not there before, clears the record (the procedure stays, unused).
- **Recovery without anyone in any group** (P9 point 4): the SQL admin group is an Entra group -- a Global Administrator or
  Privileged Role Administrator adds a member (no SQL access needed); if the group is gone, an Owner of the SQL server
  re-points the server's Entra admin (ARM `administrators/ActiveDirectory`). That admin then runs
  `setup/Install-SIGrantProcedure.ps1` (or the guided install's database step) to re-sign / re-install the procedure, or
  `-Rollback` to give the updater db_securityadmin back. The Support app is added only on request, for troubleshooting.
- **Honest limits.** db_ddladmin is itself powerful (a ddladmin can create a module in a dbo-owned schema and reach any
  dbo-owned table through ownership chaining); the procedure limits who gets WHICH RIGHT, not what the updater's DDL can
  do -- that is P4's accepted "DDL only". A product schema that appears only after the admin run (e.g. snowstage in the Pro
  database) gets no CONTROL for the signer: the procedure REFUSES its rows with that reason (a warning, the update goes on) until an admin re-runs the
  `rights` step. A new schema or a new component name beyond the reserved ones needs an admin (a changed procedure).

**What you see.** Every run writes the update state (12c: source `invardia`, the last manifest per kind with its ring,
what was applied, holds, the reason, any error) to the Key Vault and `cfg.InstallState 'UpdateState'` -- the header's
UPDATE RING and the Settings page read it -- and the ring is recorded as the install's ring (#308). Both of the customer's
switches (12d) are stated on every run.

**Sign-in.** `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -UseManagedIdentity` (#222): the job signs in as its own identity
`uami-si-updater` (`SI_UPDATER_AUTH=ManagedIdentity`) -- no certificate in any vault, as PIM's update job; `-GrantSpnRoles`
grants that identity Contributor on the registry and resource group and Key Vault Secrets Officer on the vault. A Pro
install also gives it a database user (read the settings, write `cfg.InstallState` and the template tables).

**Schedule.** Daily at 03:00 UTC (`-Schedule`, a deploy parameter, the same for every ring -- PIM's default); clear of
