the evening pipeline. Ring 1 is also updated at once whenever a build is released to it.

**Releasing a build to a ring** = `setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Ring <n>` (ring 2 / 3 with `-OperatorApproval`, the
operator's own words). For ring 1 the machine-local `fast-deploy-r1.ps1 -Jobs -Web` releases every manual deploy the same
way (`Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Build -Ring 1`) and records the released version on `caj-si-updater` (`si-installed`), so the
next daily run counts it as applied instead of fighting the manual deploy.

**Never at the same time** (found live 2026-10-05: the first updater run and a manual fast deploy PATCHed the same jobs in
the same minute; Azure refused one update with *ContainerAppsJobOperationInProgress*, and the updater's rollback then put
seven jobs back on the image from BEFORE both). Three guards now: (1) a manual deploy refuses to start while
`caj-si-updater` has an execution running; (2) while it changes anything it marks itself on the updater job (tag
`si-deploy-running = <UTC time> <who>`, removed at the end), and the updater **defers** while that mark is younger than
3 h (an older one is a deploy that died -- ignored and said so; `Test-SIUpdaterDeployLock`); (3) a rollback is
**compare-and-restore** (`Get-SIContainerRollbackPlan -NewImage -Current`): a job is restored only while it still runs the
image THIS update set -- a job someone else moved meanwhile keeps theirs.

**The updater updates itself, LAST (#350 (c); PIM's `ca-pim-update`: "itself, last").** After the engine jobs, the web app
and the MCP server are rolled and healthy and what now runs is recorded, the very last step of the run
(`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterSelf.ps1`, both editions) builds the updater image of the SAME verified release --
`si-updater:v<build>-<commit 12>` from `container/updater/Dockerfile`, the SecurityInsight folder as the context, exactly
as `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1` builds it; an image already in the registry is not rebuilt -- and points its OWN job
(`caj-si-updater`) at it, then reads the job back. Last because a Container Apps job's template is read when an execution
STARTS: changing the image does not touch the execution that is running (it finishes on the image it started with), the
next run starts on the new one, and nothing that follows in this run depends on it. An operation still in flight on the
job (409) is waited out (0, 10, 20, 40, 60 s), as PIM's self-stamp. Recorded on the job as tags (a merge, no new
revision): `si-updater-image`, `si-updater-previous` (the image to point it back at by hand if the new one cannot start)
and `si-updater-pending`. **A failed self-roll never fails the update:** the product IS updated and healthy, the job keeps
its image, `si-updater-pending` names the wanted tag, the run's `UpdateState` carries `updater: {action, image, previous,
reason}`, and the exit code stays 0. The next run that rolls nothing tries again with the image in the registry
(`Invoke-SIUpdaterInvardiaSelfRetry`); when that image was never built, the next release builds it. A release without the updater's Dockerfile is *skipped* (not failed);
`SI_UPDATER_SELF_UPDATE=0` switches the step off, visibly. An up-to-date run with nothing owed does nothing extra.

**A deep install path builds from a short copy (#350).** `az acr build <folder>` packs the folder with the Azure CLI's own
Python, which on Windows cannot open a file whose full path passes 260 characters (unless long paths are switched on for
the machine) -- found building ring 1 from a deep worktree. Every build in the product goes through
`setup/_shared/SI-BuildStage.ps1` (`Invoke-SIInBuildContext`): when the longest file path below the context would pass
240 characters (or the tree cannot even be listed), the context is copied with robocopy (it reads long paths; `.git`,
`bin`, `obj` and `node_modules` left out) to a short folder under the temp directory (`sib-<8 hex>`; the system drive's
`\sib` when the temp path itself is long), the build runs there, and the copy is removed. The image is the same -- the
`.dockerignore` travels with the files and the tag is computed from the install itself. Used by
`Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1` (engine image), `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1` (updater image), `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1`
(first engine image) and the updater's own builds (web app, MCP server, itself). Linux (the updater container) never
stages. (Since #521 the update packs the context itself with .NET -- no Azure CLI -- and the short copy is kept for the
Windows hosts that still read a deep path through the older .NET Framework file APIs.)

**The updater runs without the Azure CLI (#521 phase 1, operator 2026-10-09: *"we dont support az modules. pure rest or
arm only"*, *"modern single connect only"*; framework 12.17).** The updater image is PowerShell 7 + `ca-certificates` --
no Azure CLI, no `containerapp` extension, no PowerShell module. Everything the updater and the release's
`Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1` do in Azure is ARM / data-plane REST:
- *ONE sign-in, no fallback.* `setup/_shared/SI-UpdateRest.ps1` `Connect-SIUpdateRest` records the identity in
  SecurityInsight's own token client (`engine/_shared/SI-AzRest.ps1` + `auth/SI-ManagedIdentity.ps1`): the job's managed
  identity (`SI_UPDATER_AUTH = ManagedIdentity`, `SI_UPDATER_CLIENT_ID`) or the SPN by certificate (`SI_UPDATER_CERT_PFX_B64`
  / `_PASSWORD` / `SI_UPDATER_TENANT_ID`; the PFX goes into the store the token signer reads and the temporary file is
  removed at once -- no PEM kept for the whole run any more). Without `SI_UPDATER_*` (the VM sync hook) the run's own
  sign-in from the config. Never `az login`, never `Connect-AzAccount`.
- *ONE seam.* `-Rest { param($Method, $Uri, $Body, $Resource, $Headers) } -> @{ Status; Body }` (the shape the queue-scaling
  step introduced, #519): `$Resource` is the token audience, `''` = no bearer token at all (a SAS upload, a SAS log link,
  the registry's own token exchange). Every 4xx but 401 is an answer for the caller; 401 refreshes once; 429 / 5xx retry.
  The image's own steps call ARM through `Invoke-SIUpdaterArm`.
- *What replaced each `az` call.* Registry: ARM `registries` (in the resource group, else the subscription). Jobs:
  ARM job list at the fast roll's api-version; the roll and the rollback as above; the updater's own image and the web /
  MCP apps by one read-modify-write PATCH of their template (first container's image; never configuration); revisions
  and executions read over ARM; tags by an ARM tag MERGE. SQL size: ARM `Microsoft.Sql` servers / databases list, the
  permissions read, the sku PATCH; Graph `$count` with the Graph audience. Job size: the job read and PATCHed whole
  (template with the new CPU / memory, the trigger with the new run time), never a template fragment. Key Vault (install
  key, update state, licence): the Key Vault data plane (`-Mode Rest` of the licence / Invardia seams; `Set-SILicense`
  writes with this process's sign-in). Pro database token: the REST client's `https://database.windows.net/` token.
  The customisation overlay (VM sync hook): the blob data plane.
- *The image build* (`setup/_shared/SI-AcrBuild.ps1`, ported from PIM4EntraPS's proven `PIM-AcrBuild.ps1`): the context
  packed with .NET (`System.Formats.Tar` on PowerShell 7, a ustar writer on 5.1; gzip; `.dockerignore` applied before
  anything leaves -- customer files never uploaded; `.git` never packed; a Dockerfile outside the context as
  `.si-build/<name>`), `listBuildSourceUploadUrl` -> PUT to the SAS (no bearer token, `x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob`) ->
  `scheduleRun` (DockerBuildRequest, Linux / amd64, the image registry-relative, an agent pool for a registry with public
  access Disabled: `SI_UPDATER_ACR_AGENT_POOL`, else its first pool) -> `GET runs/<id>` until it ends (Queued / Started /
  Running = still going); a failed run's log (`POST runs/<id>/listLogSasUrl`, read without a token) is printed, its tail
  kept. ACR tasks api-version pinned (2019-06-01-preview). The tag check reads the registry's data plane (ARM token ->
  `oauth2/exchange` -> pull token -> `HEAD /v2/<repo>/manifests/<tag>`).
- *The move from an updater image that still has the CLI.* That image runs the new release's `Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1`
  (which signs in over REST itself) and calls the release's build functions with `-Az`: accepted and ignored -- they build
  over REST -- so it rolls the release and, last, itself onto the image without the CLI.
- *Guarded.* `tests/pester/SIv3-UpdaterNoAzCli.Tests.ps1` fails on any `az` invocation (AST) in the updater path and on an
  Azure CLI install line in its Dockerfile. Setup (Bootstrap, the guided install, the small scripts) is #521 phase 2.

### 12g. Releasing in minutes -- the fast gate, one command, the fast roll (#416)

Operator 2026-10-06: *"release must comedown to 10 min"*, *"bug fixing must take 0-15 min max"*, *"we solved the updater
yesterday by the changes you made like paralle"*, *"where did those learning go"*, *"we must have the fastes release
ever!!!! fix it"*. And on images: *"do they build today themselves, if yes, that is fine to continue with, i dont ike
that we deiver a image out"* -- so a release PROMOTES a signed source package and every install keeps building its own
images in its own registry; what changed is how fast that build and roll are.

**One command** (`setup/Release-SI.ps1`, vendor tool, in no archive and not in the Community edition):

| Step | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `git fetch origin`; `-Ref` (default `origin/si-v3`) must BE the checked-out HEAD and the SecurityInsight tree clean -- the gate tests the tree, the release ships the commit. Never a pull or a rebase inside a release (PIM's lesson the same day: a `git pull --rebase` mid-release built the archive from the wrong HEAD). | seconds |
| 1 | *(retired 2026-10-09: there is no nightly run -- owner: "we will drop nightly full run and the screenshot every night". Nothing reads or waits on a night's result.)* | -- |
| 2 | A FEATURE release: THE FULL SUITE (`tests/Invoke-GateOnTestVm.ps1 -Full -Lane release`: every Pester suite and every dotnet test project, sharded; a 3 h lease). A HOTFIX: `tests/Invoke-FastGate.ps1 -Hotfix -Base <commit released last to this ring>` (state: `C:\SI-ENVS\_build\release-state.json`, lane `hotfix`). Both ON INVARDIA'S TEST VM (the exact commit as a git bundle, the result JSON back, plus the offline `Test-Smoke.ps1 -Offline`); on mgmt1 ONLY with `-GateOnMgmt1` (the operator's word); an UNAVAILABLE VM stops the release -- nothing gated, nothing released, said plainly (2026-10-09: offline tests never run on mgmt1). docs/TESTS.md 5b. | hotfix 2-5 min, full suite longer, + VM start |
| 3 | `setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Ref <commit> -Build -Ring <n> -Apply` -- the signed source package to Invardia, released to the ring (UPDATE-1.7). Ring 2 / 3 need `-OperatorApproval`. | ~10 s |
| 4 | Ring 1 (its environment is known on this machine, `C:\SI-ENVS\_build\release-rings.json`): `az containerapp job start` of the updater at once -- no waiting for 03:00 -- followed to the end; the job's `si-installed` tag must name the released version. | 4-5 min |

**Two cycles (2026-10-09).** Operator: *"it is simply taking too long whenever i want simple things fixed. customer is
frustrated and i am loosing business"*, *"a simple fix in si and pim must take max 15 min before it is released, you must
support ful and hotfix cycles"*. Measured that day: ring-1 gates of 36 and 40 min (139-250 suites plus the WHOLE web test
suite, ~4,000 tests, on a test VM at 99% CPU); a one-file fix (`config/guard-catalog.locked.json`) gated 102 suites in
14-15 min on the VM before it could ship. The safety net of a hotfix moved from BEFORE the deploy to AFTER it:

| | **HOTFIX** `.\setup\Release-SI.ps1 -Ring 1 -Hotfix` | **FULL cycle** `.\setup\Release-SI.ps1 -Ring 1` (features) |
|---|---|---|
| size | said (files, product-code files, lines); a large one is told to split -- never refused | same |
| night | none -- there is no nightly run (2026-10-09) | none |
| Pester | `Invoke-FastGate.ps1 -Hotfix`: EVERY suite that covers the changed files (a changed suite, the explicit map, a suite that names the file; one hop / the folder only for a path nothing names), ranked -- the suite named after the file, then by how often a suite names it -- and measured against 300 s: a covering suite over the budget still RUNS and the gate says it takes longer because that suite covers the change (never left out: no nightly run would catch it) + the SMOKE set (`fast-gate.map.json` smoke: 14 guard suites, ~64 s measured). A changed path NO suite covers makes the hotfix gate THE FULL SUITE (said) | THE FULL SUITE (`-Full`): every suite, including the tests tagged `Nightly` |
| dotnet | the BUILD always; the web tests only for the classes that cover the changed web files (named after it, or whose code names its class, its route or the file); the whole web suite only for a shared piece (Program.cs, `Pages/Shared`, navigation, authorization, project files) | same |
| VM lane | `hotfix` (Invardia priority lane: never waits at `-Start`, AboveNormal CPU), clean-up + `-Stop` detached | `release` (priority lane), same |
| beside the gate | the support scripts build in their own process (was ~1 min after the gate) | same |
| after the roll | THE HOSTED CHECK + automatic ROLL-BACK | same |
| live smoke (5b) | the jobs that RUN the changed code on every ring-1 canary at once, 5-min time box; a failed run or a log line such as "CIs could not be built" / a SQL schema error = LIVE SMOKE FAILED -> ROLL-BACK | same, 30-min time box; a red live smoke FAILS the release, no roll-back |
| target | released at Invardia <= 10 min; live and checked on ring 1 <= 15 min -- shown, met or MISSED | the same marks; it may take longer |

**The hosted check** (step 5, after the updater's roll): every job there before the roll is still there and every engine
job runs `si-orchestrator:v<released version>-...`; the updater job records the version (`si-installed`); the web app's
newest revision is the ready, healthy one and `/healthz` answers 200 (asked for up to `-HostedCheckSeconds`); the settings
page `/Admin/Settings` answers through the whole pipeline -- the sign-in challenge (302 / 401), never a 5xx or 404 (it
needs a signed-in person to RENDER; there is no anonymous back door, by design); the MCP server's revision is healthy.
**The roll-back** (step 6, automatic; `-NoRollback` switches it off): when the roll or the hosted check fails, the
version the ring ran before (`release-state.json`) is released to the ring again (`Publish-SIRelease -ReleaseOnly`: a new,
higher sequence -- the vendor's deliberate roll-back, UPDATE-1.7), the updater rolls it and the hosted check runs on it;
the result says `ROLLED BACK to <version>` and the release still FAILS. No previous version recorded = said, fix forward.
A database step (#352) is not undone by a roll-back -- schema changes stay additive.
**The live smoke** (step 5b, 2026-10-09 -- customer H found a database schema problem internal ring 1 had not, because internal never RAN the new code first): the changed paths -> the jobs that run them (data model / correlation -> `asset-correlation`, Risk Analysis -> `risk-analysis`, pro-data -> `asset-datasync`, a collection engine -> itself, `sql/` -> correlation + data sync, shared code -> `endpoint`; at most 4) are started on every ring-1 CANARY at once -- internal ring 1 always, plus the ring's `canaries` in the machine-local `release-rings.json` (another ring-1 install such as a test tenant: its updater is rolled first; a customer only when the operator lists it). Ordinary job runs: a job that writes outside the install (CMDB, tickets, tags, mail) is never run. The typical minutes of each job (the median of its last five runs) are said BEFORE the start; a run still going at the time box is reported NOT finished (a warning, its execution named) -- correlation (~8 min) and Risk Analysis (~7 min) usually do not fit a hotfix's 5 minutes, said plainly. Each finished run's console log is read from the environment's Log Analytics (`ContainerAppConsoleLogs`). `-NoLiveSmoke` skips it. Checked live (read-only) 2026-10-09: the newest internal correlation run had exited 0 with `[WARN] CIs could not be built this run` -- the live smoke reports exactly that as LIVE SMOKE FAILED.

**The fast gate** (`tests/Invoke-FastGate.ps1`; data `tests/pester/fast-gate.map.json`; durations
`tests/pester/suite-durations.json`): the changed paths since `-Base` (plus the working tree's own changes) -> the suites
that NAME a changed file (its file name, or its name without the extension), one hop further the suites that name a
PowerShell file that loads it (comments do not count), a changed suite itself, an explicit map for what no suite names
(VERSION, the gate's own files, the web app's projects -> their dotnet test projects); a path nothing covers runs the
suites of its folder. ALWAYS ON: the safety suites of the map (payload / sanitization, no PowerShell modules, the schema
gate, the release archive payload, the licence and update verifier, the close guards, role parity, the audit action list,
no internal numbers). Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 run AT THE SAME TIME, each with half the cores as workers;
the suites go in short batches (measured duration, heaviest first) and every batch runs in a FRESH process from a queue
(`tests/pester/_Invoke-GateShard.ps1`; the suite list travels in a file, never an array parameter through `-File`; a 5.1
worker gets the 5.1 module path) -- a 5.1 process that runs suites for half an hour slows several-fold (measured). Tests
tagged `Nightly` (slow by nature; the tag keeps its old name) are left out of the dev fast gate only -- the full suite and
the hotfix gate (a covering suite runs whole) run them. dotnet builds the solution once and runs `--no-build` only
for touched test projects, alongside. A suite that fails to LOAD fails the gate. `-Full` (the full suite of a feature release) runs everything the same way;
`-Paths 'a;b'` answers "what would a change to these files run" without a commit.

**The nightly full gate -- RETIRED 2026-10-09** (owner: *"we will drop nightly full run and the screenshot every night"*;
framework §12.1 TEST-RUN-1's NIGHTLY tier dropped). It was `C:\SI-ENVS\_build\Invoke-SINightlyGate.ps1` (scheduled task
`SI-FullGate-Nightly`, now disabled) and its RED `last.json` blocked the next release. What stays: the FIX tier (a hotfix
runs every suite that covers the change) and the FEATURE release (the full suite on the test VM). #520.

**The fast roll** (`setup/_shared/SI-FastRoll.ps1`, the release's own code, so every install gets it with the release):
- *Two-layer images.* A Dockerfile whose expensive lines come before its first COPY is split: `<repo>-base:<hash>` = the
  same FROM pinned to its digest + those lines, built ONLY when the hash is missing; the per-release image is FROM that
  base + the COPY lines. The hash covers the FROM digest, the base lines, the newest gallery version of any
  `-MinimumVersion` module and -- when the base RUNs something -- the ISO week (OS patches arrive weekly). The
  engine Dockerfile has no such lines since #305, so its per-release build is already the thin code layer; the updater's
  image (apt) is the one that gains. A Dockerfile the split cannot map (multi-stage, `COPY --from`, a parser directive)
  is built as it is, never guessed.
- *Every job swaps at once.* One ARM PATCH of `properties.template` per job (the REST seam, api 2025-07-01 -- the
  version the jobs are read with) -- never a PUT (ARM returns secrets without values; a PUT drops them, see
  `ConvertTo-SIArmJobTrigger`), never one job update after another (16 jobs = ~11 min). All PATCHes go out back to back; a job busy with another operation
  (409) is sent again; then ONE job list per poll reads every job back, and each is verified: its image, and nothing else
  changed (trigger, schedule, secrets, env, command, resources, identity, registries, tags, volumes). A failure restores
  the changed jobs the same way (only those still on this update's image, #350).
- *Builds queued together.* The updater (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterFastRoll.ps1`) queues every OTHER image of
  the release right after the database step and the template gate, BEFORE the engine roll: the web app and the MCP
  server only when THEIR sources changed (tag `src-<hash>` of exactly what their Dockerfile copies, BUILD.json left out --
  an app whose sources did not change keeps its image: the header then shows that build), and the updater's own image as
  a thin layer on its cached base. The web app / MCP roll and the self-roll then wait for the build already running; the
  web app and the MCP server are updated together and health-checked together. The order of the update is unchanged:
  database (#352) -> template gate -> engine jobs -> web app + MCP -> the installed record -> the updater itself, last.
  The deploy lock and the pipeline wait (#350) are unchanged.
- *The shipped templates are read once per process.* `Get-SITemplateRows` (780 templates, each validated, serialised and
  hashed: ~20-30 s on PowerShell 7, minutes on 5.1) ran THREE times in one update (the template gate's plan, the split
  check, the install). The rows are now kept for the process, keyed by every input file's path + size + write time (the
  template sources, the shipped config the validation reads, the code that builds them; `Get-SITemplateRowsCacheKey`);
  every caller gets its own copies; a caller's own `-Context` is never cached.

### 13. No module needed for YAML or Microsoft Graph

SecurityInsight reads its YAML with its own reader. It reads exactly the YAML its files use (block mappings and lists, one-line lists, plain and quoted values, block text, comments) and JSON; anything else is refused with the file and line, so a rule never loads as something other than what was written. The whole rule tree loads in about 3 seconds on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (it took 33). Setup and asset tagging call Microsoft Graph over plain REST with the token of the Azure sign-in setup already uses -- one sign-in, paging and retries built in, Graph's own message on a refusal -- so no part of SecurityInsight needs the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.

### 14. One report of every deviation from the shipped defaults

"What have we switched off, changed or exempted -- and why?" is answered by one report, the same in both editions: one row per deviation, with the columns **Kind, Item, Scope, Shipped/Default, Current, Reason, Owner, Changed by, Changed at, Expires, Status**.

| Kind | What it lists |
|---|---|
| Exemption | every exemption that is not revoked -- one finding, one issue on every asset, or every finding of one asset |
| Exclusion | one row per excluded CVE, configuration id or asset tag, and a report's minimum CVE age |
| DisabledDetection | a tier rule or a Risk Analysis report that is turned off |
| TierMove | a whole rule moved to another tier, or a custom rule that sets other tiers than the shipped one |
| ItemOverride | any other item that replaces or adds to the shipped configuration (a report, a rule, a risk index row, an ownership entry, ...) |
| RiskWeights | weighted risk factors set for an engine (none ship) |
| Setting | a setting whose value differs from its **shipped default** |

- **Only real deviations.** A setting equal to its default (25 and 25.0, an empty list and nothing) is not one. A setting with no shipped default -- a workspace name, a mail address -- is configuration of the install, not a deviation, and is left out. A secret's value is never read. An item that follows the template and a revoked exemption are not deviations.
- **Expiry is visible.** Status is *expired*, *expiring* (within 30 days) or *active*; an expired exemption stays in the report, flagged, until someone revokes or renews it.
- **Who and why.** *Owner* is whoever introduced the deviation (the first change since it was last reset), *Changed by / at* the latest change, and *Reason* the latest reason given -- read from the change history; without one, from the item's own record (Pro) or the file's time (Community).
- **Pro:** the web app's **Operations > Deviations** page (Admin role, like Settings) reads the settings database, never writes, filters by kind, owner, age and expiry, links every row to its change history, and exports the filtered view as CSV. Excel export appears when the web app's workbook writer is installed.
- **Community / VM:** `setup\Get-SIDeviationReport.ps1` reads the custom files against the shipped ones -- the custom settings files against the shipped defaults files, the Risk Analysis exclusion and weights files, custom tier rules (and the rule overlay folder) against the shipped rules, and the custom report catalog -- and writes nothing to the install. It returns objects; `-Kind` narrows them and `-AsCsv` writes a CSV instead. Who changed what comes from the Settings page's change log where it has the file.
- **One rule set.** The report is built by one PowerShell function and its C# twin in the web app; a shared test fixture holds both to exactly the same rows. Connector suppressions are not reported: there is no place they are stored yet.

### Asset responsibility (Pro)

Every asset, and every finding on it, belongs to a **department**: the team that is responsible for fixing it and accountable for the risk it carries.

**Departments and their people.** An Admin defines departments on **Configuration > Departments (setup)**: a name, an optional shared mailbox, optional *also matches* values (for example a cost centre number that a tag may carry instead of the department's name) and the maintenance windows (recorded now; used by the remediation flows of a later release). Each department has people in five roles:

| Role | What they do |
|---|---|
| Technical owner | fixes things; receives the operational reviews (a later release) |
| Business owner | accountable; receives the **monthly status report** |
| Approver | decides requests for the department |
| Delegate | works on the department's findings |
| Advisor | a trusted outside consultant or company advising the owners |

A person is an Entra user or group (by object id, with a display name), or -- for someone without an Entra account yet, such as an outside advisor -- just a mail address, marked as external. A department is retired, never deleted, so the history of the findings that were its stays readable. Every change is recorded in the change history.

**How an asset gets its department.** The first answer in this order wins:

1. **A recommendation override** -- one security recommendation (a configuration check or a CVE) assigned to a department on *every* asset. It wins over everything below: "this vulnerability is the database team's, wherever it is".
2. **An asset override** -- one asset assigned to a department.
3. **The policy**, in the order the settings name (*Department sources, in order* on the Settings page, under *Data & retention*; default: tags, then rules):
   - **platform tags** -- the tag names you choose (default *Department*, *Owner*, *CostCenter*), read from what SecurityInsight already collects: Azure resource tags (and the subscription's, as a fallback), Defender device tags written as `Name:Value` or `Name=Value`, and the Entra *Department* attribute. A tag's value matches a department by its name or one of its *also matches* values. An earlier tag name wins over a later one.
   - **department rules** (*Configuration > Department rules*) -- the asset name (`SRV-FIN*`), its kind (endpoint, identity, azure, public IP), the CMDB / business service SecurityInsight placed it in, a group it is in (Defender device group, Azure resource group or subscription), or any tag. The first matching rule wins.
4. **The default department**, if one is set -- otherwise the asset waits in the **Unassigned** queue.

Every finding records *which* of these placed it (and which tag, rule or override it was), so "why is this mine?" always has an answer -- on every finding row, and for any asset with **Why is this asset there?** on the rules page.

**Where it is worked out.** The data sync that copies each completed collection into the Pro database also stamps every finding with its department, and adds up each department's numbers per collection. The department pages and the monthly report read those results directly -- opening a page never re-computes responsibility, and never queries Log Analytics.

**When a change takes effect.** On the next data sync (daily, after the close-loop). A change to the policy -- a department, a rule, an override or one of the settings -- re-resolves **every collection the database keeps**, newest first, so a department's trend always reads by today's rules. A tag that changes on an asset does not rewrite the past: the asset follows its new tag from the next collection on.

**The pages.**
- **Departments** -- every department side by side: weighted risk, open findings, critical and high, assets with findings and assets owned, and the Unassigned queue.
- **A department** -- its weighted risk and trend, open findings by severity and by tier (each number opens the matching findings), its assets, its CMDB services (the same service membership as the Services view) with their weighted risk, the size of the Unassigned queue, and its findings in the same grid as the collection views (sort, filter, search, select, export) with *Placed by* and *Why* columns.
- **Unassigned** -- the findings nobody owns yet. Filter or select them and an Admin assigns them in one go, either **by the asset** (every finding on it) or **by the recommendation** (that issue on every asset) -- the action bar's *Assign to department* (see "One action bar for selected findings"). Without a selection it applies to every row the filter matches.

**Who sees what.** Admins and Viewers see every department. Someone who is a person of a department -- a business owner opening the link in their monthly report, for instance -- signs in with their normal work account and sees **only their own departments'** assets and findings; every view that spans the whole estate is closed to them. A Delegated user whose scope is a department (assigned by a SuperAdmin on the Access page) sees only that department, in the findings browser, the collection views and the department pages alike.

**The monthly report.** With *Monthly report to business owners* switched on, each department's business owners get one mail a month (from the day you choose, for the previous month): the weighted risk and how it moved, open findings by severity, how many vulnerabilities were fixed in the month and how many are overdue (open longer than the target for their severity), the ten highest risks, the services, the exemptions expiring in the next 30 days, and one link to the department's page. It goes through the same mail relay as the Risk Analysis mail; a day the relay fails is retried the next day, and a month is never sent twice. Fixed and overdue need the vulnerability close-loop; without it the mail says so instead of showing zero.

#### One thread per finding, and follow-up tasks (Pro)

A **finding** here is one vulnerability (a CVE, or a configuration recommendation) on one asset. Everything people say and do about it hangs on that pair -- not on a collection -- so it stays with the finding from run to run, and comes back if the finding comes back.

**The thread.** A finding's page (*Findings > a finding*) and its department page show ONE thread, oldest first: the governance log (comments and statuses, with the remediation flow's planned windows and accepted-risk requests), the comments, recommendations and approvals of the department's advisors and people, and every step of the finding's follow-up tasks. Each kind of entry stays where it has always been stored; the thread only reads them side by side, so nothing was moved and nothing can be lost. Everyone who may see the finding sees its thread; someone limited to departments sees the threads of their departments' findings only. Who may write is unchanged: a comment or a status -- the people who may write to the finding's governance log; a recommendation or an approval -- the role framework, as before (an approval by a sign-in link still asks for the one-time code first). The older advisor thread link opens this page when the finding is in the newest collection.

**Follow-up tasks.** From the thread, whoever may write to the finding's log creates a task: a title ("waiting for the vendor to confirm the patch date"), an optional note, who it is for, the day it is due and an optional reminder day. It can be given to yourself, to a person or advisor of the finding's department, or -- for someone whose view is not limited to departments -- to any Entra user or group by its object id (with a name, and a mail address for the digest). In **Findings**, select findings and choose *Create a task for each selected*: one task per finding, at most 200 at a time, and if you may not write to one of them, none is created. A task is completed (with what came back), cancelled (with a reason) or reopened -- by its assignee, its creator, or someone who writes to the department's findings -- and never deleted. Every change is written together with its history entry and a change-history record in one step, and shows in the finding's thread. When the vulnerability close-loop closes the finding, its open tasks say **Finding resolved -- close the task?**; they are never closed by themselves.

**Overdue.** A task is overdue the day after its due day while it is open; due soon when it is due within the next 7 days.

**The overviews.** *Operations > My tasks* -- the tasks given to you, to a group you are in, or to the department person you are (advisors and department people signed in by link see theirs too); *Delegated tasks* -- the tasks you created for someone else, and where they stand; *Operations > All tasks* -- every task, filterable by department. Each is one list sorted, filtered and paged in the database: open, overdue, due soon, done recently, cancelled or all; a department; a search over the task, the finding and the people; any column. The header shows your open tasks and how many are overdue.

**The daily digest.** With *Daily task digest to assignees* switched on (off by default), each person with open tasks that are overdue, due within *Task digest: days ahead counted as due soon* (default 7), or whose reminder day has come gets one mail a day listing them, overdue first, each with a link to the task. It goes out with the close-loop's daily mail through the Risk Analysis relay, is recorded only after it went out (nobody gets two the same day; a failed day is retried), and is never sent to an address nobody gave -- a task without one is counted in the job's log instead.

#### One action bar for selected findings, on every view (Pro)

Every grid that lists findings -- *Findings*, the collection views of finding rows (raw rows, a CI's findings, risk rating, MITRE, compliance, CVSS), a department's findings and the *Unassigned* queue -- carries the SAME action bar under it. Tick rows and the bar shows *N selected · clear* with every action you may use; *Apply to all N matching the filter* is offered beside it only for an action that allows it, and only while the filter narrows the collection and matches at most *Exemption: most findings in one bulk request* (a whole collection is never acted on in one go). An action opens its form in a dialog; the answer lists every finding: done, or refused and why. Without script the same buttons open the form on a page of its own.

**The actions.** *Request exemption* (one request per security domain; an approver of each domain decides -- the exemption flow), *Comment* (the same entry in each finding's governance log, so it is in the finding's one thread), *Set status* (open, in progress, planned, fixed pending verification, not applicable -- with a comment), *Create task* (a follow-up task on each finding, for you, a person of the finding's department, or -- for someone not limited to departments -- an Entra user or group), *Escalate to vendor* (offered only where a remediation flow names a vendor contact; one mail per finding, recorded as escalated), *Assign to department* (Admin: the findings' assets or recommendations belong to a department from the next data sync) and *Export selected* (just those findings, CSV or Excel).

**Who may do what.** The bar offers only the actions your role allows. The server then checks EVERY finding again, through the same rules as everywhere else: what you see (a user limited to departments sees only theirs), and what the action needs on that finding's security domain, asset kind, tier and department. One finding outside what you may change refuses the whole request; nothing is written. Each request is ONE event in the audit trail, under the action's own name, with the outcome per finding in its detail.

**How it is built -- and how to add an action.** One registry and one endpoint:
- `Actions/FindingActions.cs` -- the interface `IFindingAction`: `Key`, `Label`, `Icon`, `Group`, `Order`, `Hint`, `AuditAction` (an action on the closed audit list), `SupportsAllMatching`, `BulkLimit`, `FormPartial` (the fields it asks for, named `a.<field>`), `Downloads`; `OfferedAsync(user)` (a quick role check: is the button shown), `CanAsync(user, finding)` (the per-finding decision -- always through the service that owns it and the role framework), `ExecuteAsync(user, findings, form)` (one transaction where the store allows; a result per finding). `FindingActionRegistry` lists them in the bar's order.
- `Actions/BuiltinActions.cs` -- the seven actions. Each one only wraps an existing service (the exemption workflow, the governance service, the task service, the responsibility override, the findings export); none holds a rule of its own.
- `Actions/FindingSelection.cs` -- what a request acts on: the selected keys (collection + finding id) or *all matching* plus the filter, ALWAYS read back on the server (one grid read, under the user's department visibility and the bulk guard), each finding with its department.
- `Pages/Shared/_FindingActions.cshtml` -- the bar (rendered inside the page's selection form), `js/app/finding-actions.js` -- the dialogs, `Pages/Actions/Apply` -- the one endpoint (JSON for the dialog, a page for a form post, a file for an export), `Pages/Actions/Prepare` -- the form without script (writes nothing).
- A grid shows the bar when its page says where its selection comes from (`ActionSource` on the collection page model: finding rows or a department grid); the findings browser builds its bar itself.

**A dialog starts from what was selected (#330).** When a dialog opens on a selection, the script asks `/Actions/Prepare?handler=Count` (the same resolver Apply uses; it writes nothing) and the answer names the selection: the dialog's title is the action's `Title(what)` over `SelectionSummary.What` -- *Exempt CVE-2026-33824 on 3 assets* (a CVE row = that CVE on the assets it is on in this collection), *Exempt 1 finding: CVE-... on dc1*, *Exempt 12 selected findings*, *Comment on ...*. An action whose form depends on the selection implements `IFindingActionPreview` and its preview rides along: *Request exemption* returns the approvers' names per request, whether the user may approve all of it (only then *Approve now*), the real alternative approvers (people who decide EVERY part; none = no *Change approver*) and the one wider scope that fits (one issue: that issue on every asset, now and later; one asset with several issues: every finding on it; nothing for a mixed selection); *Assign to department* returns the scope to open on. The default is always exactly the selection; the server refuses a wider exemption scope the selection does not fit. A count that fails answers `ok = false` with the reason, and the script stops waiting after 30 s -- it never stays at "counting". An aggregated row is resolved by an EXACT read of its issue (`CollectionViewSql.RowsOfIssue`) or asset, never by the grid's free-text search. The no-script page renders the same title, names and approve-now from the server (`ActionFormModel.Targets`). The reason *"all matching"* is not offered sits behind *Why not?*.

**On a department's page, its business approvers decide (#391).** When *Request exemption* is used on a department's own page (the selection's source is that department's findings grid -- `FindingSelection.DepartmentContext`; never the Unassigned queue, never a posted field) and every finding the server read back belongs to that department (`RequestExemptionAction.DepartmentOf`), the endpoint hands the department to the workflow (`ActionForm.Department` -> `RequestForm.DepartmentId`, and the count's preview the same). The workflow asks `IDepartmentDeciders.BusinessApproversAsync` (the department's `business-approver` people -- the old `approver` rows count): with any, each request is asked of them (names in the dialog, mailed to those with an address when exemption mail is on, *Change approver* = them + the security owners who decide every part, *Approve now* for one of them) and stored as `cfg.ExemptionRequest.DepartmentId` + `Routing = 'department-business-approver'`; with none, the security domain / category owners are asked as everywhere else, the request records `Routing = 'department-no-business-approver'` and the dialog and the result say so. A business approver (on the role ladder) decides exactly the requests the record says were routed to their department -- checked in `ExemptionWorkflow.DecideAsync`, not only on the page; the owners / approvers of the domain and Admins still decide. The request's change-log row ends *"; asked of ..."*, the action's audit row carries the same sentence, the request page shows *Routed to*, and *Waiting for my decision* lists routed requests for their business approvers. A database without the two columns yet writes the request without them, the owners decide, and the result says to run the Pro settings setup. Requests made anywhere else, and the governance log's *accept the risk* (#335), are unchanged.

To add an action: write one class implementing `IFindingAction` (wrapping the service that already decides and writes), one form partial under `Pages/Shared/FindingActions/`, add its audit action to `config/audit-actions.locked.json` if it is new, and add ONE line `s.AddFindingAction<YourAction>();` in `FindingActionRegistration`. No page changes: every bar offers it.

### Risk Analysis executive view (Pro, #288) -- the mail, in the web app

**What it is.** Overview > *Risk Analysis (executive)* shows the Risk Analysis mail management reads: the banner (report, tenant, time), the Risk Score KPI x/100 with its band and legend, the domain x severity table with its Total row, the *"Summary counts assets, Detailed counts asset findings"* line, the four *Risk by domain* tiles, the AI-written analysis and the Top-50 risky assets (each linked to its CI). A selector shows the **Summary** or the **Detailed** report's data; the choice is remembered in the browser (cookie `si-exec-grain`) and deep-linkable (`?grain=summary|detailed`). Readers and up (the `/Management` folder policy). Light/dark, full width, regional number format, and a print view (`@media print` in `wwwroot/css/exec.css`: menus and the selector left out, colours kept).

**One source -- the mail's own figures, never recomputed.** At the end of every Risk Analysis run, after the KPI roll-up (and its cache override) and before the mail, the engine keeps the object the mail renders (`engine/risk-analysis/_shared/RA-ExecView.ps1`, `New-RAExecViewSnapshot`): the KPI as the mail shows it (`$global:RA_KPI`), the Top-50 assets and Top findings the AI was given (live, adopted from the leader, or adopted in either race re-check -- the four sites that decide the mail's Top-50 each set it), the AI text, the agreement mode and leader in force, and **whose figures they are** (`FiguresFrom`: this report, or the leader when it adopted them). It is written to the output folder and to `<SI_RATop50_BlobContainer>/risk-analysis/RiskAnalysis_ExecView_<Grain>.json` (one per grain, beside the shared Top-50 snapshot). It is written in **every** mode and **never read back by the engine**, so it cannot change a mail; a dry run and a run with no rows (whose mail is suppressed) write nothing; a failure is a warning, never fatal. The Top-50 aggregate now carries its key (`AssetKey` = `id:<asset id>` or `name:<name>`) so the page can link the asset.

**Into the Pro database.** The data sync (`engine/_shared/data-sql/SI-DataExecView.ps1`, called from `Invoke-SIDataSync.ps1` after the findings load) reads both blobs with its own identity (`SI_StorageAccount`; the identity needs read on that container, as the Risk Analysis job has), refuses a file that is not a view of the expected grain, and upserts `sidata.RiskExecView` (one row per grain, `PayloadJson` = the engine's text) only when the view is **newer**. A missing table, a missing blob or a read failure is said and never fails the sync.

**What each selection shows -- the agreement mode** (`RiskExecSelector` in `SI.Management.Core/ProData/RiskExecView.cs`; the mode and leader are the ones the newest view was written under, i.e. what the last mail did):
- **Consistent** (with the AI summary on): both selections show the **leader's** view -- KPI, table, tiles, narrative and Top-50 -- as both mails do; the banner stays the selected report's own (its report name and time). The page says *"Figures from the <Leader> report, as in the mails."* A report without a view yet still shows the leader's figures, and says so.
- **Consistent with the AI summary off**: the engine shares figures only through the AI summary snapshot, so each mail carries its own KPI; the page shows each report's own and says why.
- **PerReport** (the SecurityInsight Pro default since #346): each selection shows its own report's figures, and the notice reads *"Each report shows its own figures: Summary counts distinct assets, Detailed counts individual findings."* (`RiskExecGrain.PerReportNotice`, on the executive page and every page using `_ExecSelector`).
- No view of the selected report in PerReport (or none at all): a clear empty state.

**The Summary / Detailed switch is a segmented control** (`.seg` in `site.css`, the same component as the range chooser `.range`; the pill tabs `.tabs` in `app.css` carry the same states): a surface-alt track; each choice an outlined segment (`--seg-line`, 3:1+ against the surface in light, OS-dark and explicit dark) with full-strength text; the chosen one filled with `--accent-fill` and white text; hover and keyboard focus visible. It replaced white-on-white chips with a hairline border that the operator found hard to read (2026-10-05).
The Top-50 asset links: the CI page when the engine's asset id is a CI key or a known identifier (`sidata.AssetIdentifier`), else a search by the name -- never a guessed CI. The AI's own *"Top N risky assets"* section is replaced, in place, by the table of the same numbers; everything else of the narrative is rendered as the mail renders it (`RiskExec/ExecNarrative.cs`, escaped first: only http(s) links, headings, bullets, bold, italic).

**The settings are dropdowns.** `SI_AISummary_Mode` (Consistent / PerReport) and `SI_AISummary_Leader` (Summary / Detailed) are catalog type `enum` with `values` and plain `valueLabels`, in the group *"Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view"* (with `SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours`). The catalog builder takes `type` / `values` / `valueLabels` from the setting's help entry in `config/settings.descriptions.locked.json`; the Settings page renders an enum as a `<select>` with the labels; `Test-SISettingValue` and its C# port refuse any other value (case-insensitive, as PowerShell compares). The engine reads the same value; a Community config file that still says `Actual` / `FirstCome` keeps working through the engine's own resolver.

**The management summary report (#291).** `MgmtReports/MgmtReports.cs`: definitions in `cfg.MgmtReport` (Configuration > Reports & outputs > Management summary; Admin edits, readers view), composed by the pure `MgmtSummaryComposer` from the kept view (grain + agreement mode via `RiskExecSelector`) and `sidata.VulnLifecycleDaily` (opened vs closed per Monday week, last 30 / 91 days), in the RA mail's look with inline styles (a mail) -- shown in the app only in a sandboxed frame whose response carries its own CSP. The schedule is pure (`MgmtSchedule`: newest slot at or before now, period key ISO week / month, due when that period is not yet sent and the slot is after creation); `MgmtReportScheduler` (hosted service, every 5 min) claims the period with one conditional UPDATE before queuing, so a period goes out once and a run of missed periods is one catch-up send. Delivery: the outbox `cfg.ReportMail`, sent by the close-loop mail job with the exemption and sign-in outboxes (one SMTP path); the web app wakes the mail job as it does for exemption mails. Overview > Management summary shows the whole report for the chosen grain. **New context in the mail.** When the continuous discovery found properties that are new since the report's last summary mail, the mail ends with a small block -- *Also new this week* (a monthly report: *this month*) -- holding ONE line: "N new properties are available from <sources>" with a link to Configuration > New context available (the page's week or 30-day window; without the web app's public address the page is named in words). It is counted by one grouped read of the prepared discovery rows (`sidata.SourceProperty`: first seen after the starting point and at or after the last summary mail; a report never sent looks one period back) -- never from a JSON document. Nothing new, no discovery tables, or a read that fails: the block is left out and the mail is the mail of before. There is no mail of its own for it.

**The mail sections as pages (#290).** Overview > *Top 50 risky assets* (`/Management/TopAssets`), *Top 50 critical findings* (`/Collection/TopFindings`) and *Top 10 asset drilldown* (`/Management/Drilldown`) read the same kept view through `RiskExec/ExecViewLoader` (grain from `?grain=`, the cookie, else the leader; `RiskExecSelector` for the mode) and share the selector partial `_ExecSelector`. The critical findings page is a collection grid (`CollectionViewSql.TopIssues`) whose source rows are the kept view's top findings passed as `@Keys` JSON (`OPENJSON ... WITH`): the mail's numbers, joined to this collection's count per issue and the close-loop's first-seen per CVE. Its rows act through `FindingRowMaps["topissues"]`: a row = every finding of that CVE / configuration in the collection, read back by key through `CollectionViewSql.IssueKeys`; "all matching" is not offered (the list cannot be rebuilt on the server). The drilldown reads the top 10 CIs' findings in the newest complete Detailed collection (`RiskExecSql.AssetGroups` / `AssetTop`; category = the row's `Category`, else its report).

### Build identity -- version, pre-release number and build (#304)

Every deployed build says which build it is. **One identity, computed once at build/package time, read at run time** (`engine/_shared/SI-BuildInfo.ps1`, PS 5.1 + 7):

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | the product version, the `VERSION` file (`3.0.0`) |
| `display` | what people see: `3.0.0` for the release (HEAD carries the tag `SI-<VERSION>` or `SecurityInsight-v<VERSION>`), else `3.0.0-rc.<n>` |
| `rc` | n = `git rev-list --count <commit that last changed VERSION>..HEAD`; `null` for a release |
| `commit` / `shortCommit` | the full commit / its first 7 characters |
| `builtUtc`, `channel`, `ring` | when it was built; where it is going, when the builder knows |

- **Computed** by `Get-SIBuildInfo` (git in a source tree; without git it returns the BUILD.json already there) and written as `BUILD.json` next to `VERSION` by: `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1` (before `az acr build`, so the engine image has `/app/BUILD.json`), `Deploy-SIManagement.ps1` (staged explicitly; the Dockerfile copies it, the csproj links it next to the app), and the release package (`Publish-SIRelease.ps1`: `git archive --add-file` through `New-SIBuildArchiveArgs`, because BUILD.json is gitignored and never committed). `setup/_shared/Get-SIBuildInfo.ps1 [-OutFile]` is the command-line entry point.
- **Read** by `Read-SIBuildInfo` only -- never git at run time. No BUILD.json: the VERSION file and "build unknown"; nothing at all: `(dev)`.
- **Shown:** the Pro web app header pill and footer show the version only (`v3.0.0-rc.12`); `/about` (signed in) and the Help page add commit, build time, channel and ring. Container banners (`Start-SIInContainer.ps1`, `Start-RiskAnalysisInContainer.ps1`, `Invoke-ShardProducer.ps1`) and VM launcher banners (`Get-PublishedVersion`) print `SecurityInsight <display> (build <sha>, <time> UTC)`. The guided installer prints it first and keeps it in `state.json` (`build`).
- **"A new version is available" (#345, framework BRAND-2.11 -- the same bar as Invardia and PIM Manager):** every signed-in page of the Pro web app carries the build it was served from on `<html data-app-build data-app-version>` (`BuildIdentity.Id`: the commit when BUILD.json names one, else the version). `wwwroot/js/version-check.js`, loaded by both layouts, asks `/about` (signed-in, `Cache-Control: no-store`) every 5 minutes and at once when the tab is shown or focused; a hidden tab does not ask, and errors (a deploy restarting the app, offline) make it ask less often. When `/about`'s commit (else display) differs from the page's build, a calm bar opens at the top of the page (the accent colour, white text) -- *A new version of SecurityInsight (v`<display>`) is available. Reload when you are ready.* -- with **Reload** and **Later** (for that build; a later build shows it again). It is in the flow (sticky), so it covers no header control. A POST form someone has typed into and not submitted (or a designer form marked `data-dirty`) adds *You have typed something that is not saved yet -- finish or save it first.* Search and filter forms (GET) do not count. When the server refuses the poll (401, or a redirect to sign in) the page really cannot save: PIM's orange bar says *Your sign-in session has expired. This page can no longer save. Reload to sign in again -- committed data is safe.* The page is **never reloaded by itself**; the wall board shows the same bars and its own refresh tick applies them.
- **The sign-in key ring (#345):** the ASP.NET data-protection keys that encrypt the sign-in cookie and every form's antiforgery token are kept in the Pro database (`cfg.WebKeyRing`, `Auth/SqlKeyRing.cs`, application name *SecurityInsight Pro*), so every revision and both replicas use the same keys: a deploy no longer signs open pages out or refuses their next save -- which is what makes "reload when you are ready" true. The web identity may INSERT a key (ASP.NET never changes or removes one; it expires them); the MCP server's read-only identity is DENIED SELECT. Without a database (local, tests) or when it cannot be reached, the process keeps its own keys in memory -- the behaviour before, never a failure.
- **Recorded:** `SI_RunHealth` carries `SolutionVersion` (display) and `Build` (short commit), additive columns. Telemetry carries `<display>+<shortCommit>` in `Version` -- semver build metadata, because the uplink refuses unknown fields. Every Container Apps job carries the Azure tag `si-build=<display>+<shortCommit>`.
- **Not changed:** the `SolutionVersion` stamped on profile and Risk Analysis rows stays the product version (`3.0.0+v3`) -- the Tier dry run finds "this install's newest run" by that exact string, which a per-build rc would break after every update.

### "More info" for every setting (Pro web app, framework SETTING-INFO-1)

Every setting -- the engine catalog's and the web app's own -- carries an `info` block: **what** it does, **when on** and
**when off** (a bool) or **if you change it**, **risk** (security impact and whether it can be undone), **requires**, the
**default**, the **recommended** value, and its page `https://invardia.com/docs/si/settings/<name>/`.

- **One source, generated:** `engine/pro-settings/Build-SISettingsCatalog.ps1` composes `info` from the help words of
  `config/settings.descriptions.locked.json` (`SI-SettingInfo.ps1`: the effect is split at a capitalised `On:` / `Off:`;
  the default words describe the default state; `needs` becomes "Works only while ... is on"; Pro, Key Vault and the
  engines that read it are named) plus `config/settings.info.locked.json` -- a risk text per group and, per setting, the
  hand-written risk / recommendation and the **confirmation**. Run it with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (it keeps the JSON
  layout). The web app's own settings are composed the same way at load (`Settings/SettingInfo.cs`). The Community
  configuration reference carries risk, recommendation and the page too.
- **Shown:** each setting's field has a **More info** button (risk in the alarm colour when it confirms) ending *Read more
  on invardia.com*; the single-setting page shows the same list.
- **Confirmation:** a destructive or security-reducing value names when it asks (`confirmWhen`: `on`, `off`, or `lower` for
  a retention or grace period -- "not set" counts as kept for ever) and the words. The Settings page and Get Started ask in
  the shared dialog before saving (*Save anyway*); the single-setting review shows the words above *Save anyway*. Every
  safety check (and its mail) asks when turned off; writing into the tenant, bypassing governance or sending data to AI
  asks when turned on.
- **Hand-over:** `setup/Release-SI.ps1` writes the catalog of the RELEASED commit to
  `C:\ProgramData\Invardia\handover\docs\si\<version>\settings-catalog.json` for Invardia's settings pages.
- **Enforced:** a setting without complete info fails `SIv3-SettingInfo` and the xunit `SettingInfoTests`.
### The documentation of this version inside the web app (#679)

**Why.** Private-network installs and most installs run without contact (framework §12.23 P9). The documentation a customer
reads must therefore travel WITH the release and always describe the version they run -- never be fetched from outside.

- **One source, the published pages.** The pages Invardia publishes for a version (the hand-over docs pack:
  `C:\ProgramData\Invardia\handover\docs\securityinsight\<version>\` -- `docs.json` with slug / title / order / file, the
  `*.md` pages, `images\`) are copied by the vendor tool `setup/Import-SIProductDocs.ps1` into
  `pro-management/src/SI.Management.Web/ProductDocs/` and committed with the release. The tool checks the pack (product
  `securityinsight`, plain slugs and file names, every listed page present, only .png / .jpg / .gif / .webp images -- an SVG
  can carry script and is never copied), copies exactly that set, and proves the copy; `-Check` changes nothing and exits 1
  when a published page has no identical in-app counterpart (or the web app carries one no longer published). The tool is
  not in any release archive (`SI-ReleasePayload.ps1`, `solution.publish.json`); its result is.
- **Shipped inside the image.** The web project EMBEDS `ProductDocs\**` (`SI.Management.Web.csproj`, logical names
  `ProductDocs/<path>`; not content, nothing is copied next to the app). Every image build already carries it: the
  Dockerfile copies `pro-management/src/`, the deploy stage copies `src\**`, the updater's web-app source list holds
  `pro-management/src/SI.Management.Web`. `Docs/ProductDocLibrary.cs` reads the embedded pages once.
- **Help > Documentation** (`/Docs`, `/Docs/<slug>`; menu item need `home` = every role with a start page; the page itself
  needs only a sign-in -- no new permission). The page list beside the page, an "On this page" list for longer pages, a
  search over the shipped pages (every word in one section; hits link to the section's anchor), the version you run and the
  pages' version, and a **Published version on invardia.com** link (`https://invardia.com/docs/securityinsight/`, on a page `.../securityinsight/<page>/`) -- only a link (`target=_blank`, `rel=noopener
  noreferrer`); the page makes no outbound call. Images are served by the page itself (`/Docs?handler=Image&name=`), only
  names the pack carries. Help + glossary links to it.
- **Safe by construction** (`Docs/SafeMarkdown.cs`): every character of a page is HTML-encoded and the only tags are the
  ones the renderer writes (headings with GitHub-style anchors, paragraphs, lists, tables, code, quotes, emphasis, links,
  images). Raw HTML shows as text; a link is kept only when it is http(s) / mailto or a shipped page + anchor (anything
  else -- `javascript:`, `data:`, a page that is not shipped -- is plain text, so never a dead link); an image only when it
  is a shipped image (an external image is never loaded; its words stay). The CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`) is unchanged.
- **More info per setting.** `ProductDocs/more-info.json` (SecurityInsight's own; the import never replaces it) maps a
  Settings-page **category** of the settings catalog (`config/settings.catalog.locked.json` `categories`) -- or one setting
  by name, which wins -- to `page` or `page#anchor`. Under a setting's More info the Settings page (and Get Started, the
  same partial) shows *Read in this version's documentation: <page>: <section>* when, and only when, that page and anchor
  are shipped; otherwise nothing. Today by category: Guards, Schedules (the daily pipeline, *When it runs*), Departments & owners,
  Connectors & CMDB, Exemptions, Licence & updates, Sign-in & Azure resources (identities and permissions); by setting:
  Pro updates and the automatic licence request (Updates and upgrades), telemetry and log retention (Operations).
  *Read more on invardia.com* stays beside it.
- **Enforced:** `SIv3-InAppDocs` (the import, the folder, the embedding, the image builds, a Pro archive of HEAD carrying
  every file of the folder and not the tool) and the xunit `ProductDocsTests` (sanitising, rendering, the page for every
  role, the menu, every More-info entry resolving to a shipped anchor and naming a real catalog category, and the Settings
  page showing the link exactly where one resolves). Changing a page: re-run the import for the version and commit.

### What blocks work, loudly in the menu (Pro web app, framework PENDING-1)

Anything that waits for a person's decision and blocks work carries a **count badge in the attention colour** on the
top-menu group AND on the entry where it is decided (and on its tab), plus **one line on Home (the wall board) and the
Overview** naming each item, who decides it, and a link for whoever may open that page. Counted from the data on every
page load (`Navigation/BlockingItems.cs`) -- no acknowledgement; it is gone once decided or expired:

| item | counted from | decided on | by |
|---|---|---|---|
| a held guard set | `cfg.GuardRelease`, held and not expired | Operations > Guards | a SuperAdmin releases (an Admin acknowledges) |
| a guard release waiting for a second person | `cfg.ConfigApproval` kind guard-release, pending, not expired | Operations > Guards | another SuperAdmin |
| a restore waiting for a second person | `cfg.ConfigApproval` kind restore, pending, not expired | Configuration > Backups | another SuperAdmin |
| an exemption request (Ignore / Accept the risk) waiting for its approver | `cfg.ExemptionRequest`, state requested | Security recommendations > Exemptions | an owner or approver of its domain / category, or an Admin |
| template packs held from installing | the staged template packs held -- Hold template packs is on, or you rolled back from the pack (split install; every other pack installs automatically, #581) -- kept 30 s | Configuration > Templates > Template releases | a SuperAdmin installs |

Every reader sees the badges of the entries they can open and the Overview line for all of it (read-only, with who can
act). Informational counts (staged changes, tasks) keep the warning colour. A read that fails counts as nothing.

### Mails that lead somewhere, notifications per recipient, one view of every report (Pro web app, framework MAIL-2, #485)

- **The mail look** (`Notify/MailBrand.cs`): the brand bar (the Invardia SecurityInsight Pro wordmark on the brand ink --
  a mail client cannot load the web app's SVG logo, which sits behind the sign-in), a summary first, ONE blue button that
  deep-links to the recipient's audience page, and a plain "Open SecurityInsight" home link in the footer. Without the
  web app's public address (`SIWeb_PublicBaseUrl`) the mail says it carries no link instead of a broken button.
- **Audience** (`MailAudience`): SOC analyst -> `/Findings`, posture / risk -> `/Management` (the default), manager ->
  `/Management/Summary`. A management summary goes out ONCE PER AUDIENCE, each mail with its own button.
- **Notifications** (Configuration > Settings > Notifications, Admin; also a button on E-mail + links): every recipient on
  any list, their audience, every report and alert on / off for them, an alert severity floor, and whether they can open
  the links. Stored as ONE web setting, `SIWeb_MailNotifications` (JSON at scope engine:management-web) -- saved,
  journaled, backed up, exported and undone like every setting; the engine's mail steps can read it from `cfg.Setting`.
  A recipient not listed gets everything with the posture audience. Followed NOW by the mails the web app composes
  (management summaries, the Get Started reminder); the Risk Analysis, daily vulnerability and safety-check mails are
  composed by the jobs and follow it once their mail step reads it (open -- each line of the view says which).
- **Auto-Reader** (`Notify/AutoReader.cs`): a recipient added on Notifications or on a management summary who is not a
  user yet is found in Entra by address (the Access page's directory lookup) and added as **Reader** through the Access
  store (`cfg.AccessAssignment` + its change log), said in the toast and on the audit trail. An existing user keeps their
  role (never raised or lowered), a group is never added, removing a recipient never removes a role. With the directory
  lookup off it says "not checked".
- **Reports and alerts** (Configuration > Settings > Reports and alerts, Admin): `NotifyCatalog` -- the Risk Analysis
  Summary / Detailed reports, the daily vulnerability mail, the safety-check alert, the Get Started reminder, the
  exemption mails, and one line per management summary -- with cadence, recipients (the effective list: an engine-scoped
  value before the solution value, else the default list), last sent, next run, PDF ("link only") and the Configure link.
- **Export PDF** (`Pages/Shared/_ExportPdf.cshtml`, `css/report.css`, `js/print.js`): on the environment report and the
  Overview report pages (Risk score, Tier-0 exposure, Top 50 risky assets, Top 10 drilldown, Risk Analysis, Management
  summary) -- the browser's own print to PDF through a print stylesheet (A4, page numbers, "Confidential", logo, no menu).
  Attaching a PDF to the report mail needs a renderer in the mail job: open.

### A daily mail while Get Started is not finished (Pro web app, framework MAIL-2 item 8, #489)

`Notify/GetStartedReminder.cs`. A web-app background pass every 15 minutes evaluates Get Started from the install's data
(the same `GetStartedService` as the page) and, from `SIWeb_GetStartedReminderHourUtc` (default 07:00 UTC) while a
REQUIRED step is open, queues ONE mail per audience group in the existing outbox `cfg.ReportMail` (ReportId 0, period
`gs-<date>`; the insert runs only when no row of that day exists, under a range lock -- two replicas never send twice) and
wakes the mail job. Recipients: the customer's alert recipients (`SI_GuardMail_To`), else the installing admin
(`SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail`) -- never Invardia; minus those who switched it off on Notifications. The mail lists
each open required step with why it matters and a blue button to `/Admin/GetStarted?step=<id>`; optional steps are listed
apart as optional and never make it go out. Mail step open = no working mail = nothing queued. Stops by itself when every
required step is done. Off with `SIWeb_GetStartedReminder`. Audited `getstarted.reminder.send` (source job). SI's Get
Started has no "skip for now", so there is no skipped state yet.

### The environment report (Pro web app, framework ENV-REPORT-1, #482)

Configuration > Environment report (Admin and SuperAdmin), `EnvReport/`. Built at report time from the live install:
1. **Summary** -- customer (the licence), tenant, edition + dimension, licence state, version, ring, environment, install
   date, health (Get Started). 2. **Architecture** -- the install's resource group through ARM with the web app's own
   Reader (`ArmAzureFactsReader`: one list, one GET per resource type whose network facts are shown -- public network
   access, default network rule, anonymous blob access, external ingress + IP restrictions -- and the group's role
   assignments with role names), plus a diagram. 3. **Identities** -- managed identities (user- and system-assigned, who
   uses them), the web app's sign-in app registration, each engine's identity (from its permission self-check), the mail
   sender. 4. **Permissions** -- every item of `config\permissions.locked.json` (now linked next to the app) per identity:
   present / missing / not checked / not checked yet / not needed now (a `when` setting off), from the engines' newest
   self-checks; Azure role assignments as granted; "extra" grants are not visible to the web app (said). 5. **Features**
   -- every setting with a More info confirmation (security-relevant) and every switch away from its default, with what
   its current value does (the SETTING-INFO-1 text). 6. **Data flows** -- every connection in and out (sources, SQL, Log
   Analytics, browser, ARM, mail, uplink, update, licence, connectors) with its state here, plus a diagram. 7. **Change
   history** -- the newest 25 configuration commits. 8. **Findings** -- missing permissions, public endpoints, open
   default network rules, internet ingress without IP restrictions, a licence not valid, open required setup steps --
   each with its fix. **Export PDF** (print stylesheet: cover, contents, page numbers, "Confidential -- customer") and
   **Export JSON** (`?handler=Json`, audited `report.environment.export`). Only named facts are taken from ARM answers; no
   secret value appears anywhere. Each part that cannot be read says so; the others still show.

### Export and import of the configuration, choose what to import (Pro web app, framework CONFIG-IO-1, #490)

Configuration > Settings > Export / Import (SuperAdmin), `ConfigIo/`. **One format:** the export IS the signed
configuration backup file (CONFIG-1.3) with the CONFIG-IO-1 header added -- product, productVersion, schemaVersion (1),
tenantId, environment, exportedUtc, exportedBy, sections[] and secrets[] -- so an export imports on Backups (restore) and a
backup file imports here. A section = one entity of the configuration set. **Never a secret value**: a secret setting holds
only its Key Vault secret NAME; the header lists each secret as set / not set with that name (connectors: their secret
references). **Import, select which:** upload (checked, kept 30 minutes for that person, nothing written) -> refused when
the schema or product version is newer, the product is not SecurityInsight or a section is unknown -> per section and
item: NEW, CHANGED, UNCHANGED, ONLY HERE (importing it would REMOVE it: never ticked by default) -> a record with an Entra
object id (access, department people, advisors) from another or an unstated tenant is FLAGGED and never ticked by default
-> Preview (WhatIf, nothing written) -> Apply: the file is kept as a backup (`cfg.ConfigBackupImport`) and the ticked items
become pending changes committed on Review & commit through every gate (Source restore, undoable), or -- with
`SIWeb_ConfigSecondPerson` -- a restore request a second SuperAdmin decides on Backups. MSP-owned items: SI has no managed
tenants yet, nothing to protect. **Script pair** (`setup/Export-SIConfig.ps1` / `Import-SIConfig.ps1`): open.

### Pro Business and Pro Enterprise (framework LICENCE-DIMENSION)

Both are the same **Pro edition** with the same features (framework section 12.6a LICENCE-FEATURES, #510: the sku names
the edition, never `features[]`). The **signed** licence decides: `limits` in the signed payload = **Pro Business** (SecurityInsight reads `devices`), none =
**Pro Enterprise**; Community has no limits. `Get-SILicense` reads `limits` only from the verified payload bytes (an
unsigned `limits` on the outer document is ignored; only whole numbers count), and the updater records them in
`cfg.InstallState` 'Licence' for the web app. **Shown** wherever the edition is shown: the header (*Licence*), the
Licence card on Settings, Get Started's licence step and Help's support facts ("Pro Business (250 devices)").
**A warning, never a stop:** the devices are the CIs of class device that are not retired (`sidata.Ci`, kept 5 minutes);
from 90 % of the limit every page shows a banner, above the limit + 10 % in the alarm colour -- nothing is refused,
switched off or skipped, no feature gate reads the limit, every collection and every run goes on. SecurityInsight adds
no devices by hand, so there is no "new item" to refuse. **At collection** the endpoint run counts the devices it
discovered against the same limit, right after discovery (`engine\_shared\SI-LicenceLimit.ps1`): from 90 % it warns with
how many are left, above the limit it says how many are above it (alarm above + 10 %), always adding that every device
was collected and nothing is left out, and what to do; the message also goes on the run's END record, the outcome
unchanged. **First enforcing version:** none released yet -- the first
SecurityInsight release that carries this is the one Invardia may issue a Business licence to.

### AI integration in Get Started -- one switch, the key in Key Vault (Pro web app)

Operator review 2026-10-09: *"i want ai integration on, what to choose ... there must be one on/off. on = on for all"*.
- **One switch:** the AI step shows **AI integration** (`SI_EnableAI`, on = AI for every engine with an AI step), the
  endpoint, the deployment and the key. The per-engine switches (`SI_EnableAI_azure`, `SI_EnableAI_endpoint`,
  `SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI`) left the step; they are **advanced** overrides on the Settings page whose More info
  says they only turn ONE engine on or off against the main switch. Note: the privilege tier classifier follows its own
  switch (on by default) and calls AI whenever the Azure OpenAI settings are set -- its text says so.
- **The key is pasted once and HANDED TO THE UPDATER (#537, owner 2026-10-10: *"can we commit this to the engine and
  then the engine commits it, so the gui keeps read only"*):** see *The secret hand-over* below. The web app writes no
  secret and holds no Key Vault right; the old refusal (a role, a vault name, an `az` command) is gone with it. ONE key
  field: the paste box with the key's state beside it; the secret NAME (`OpenAI_apiKey`) is under *Advanced*.
- **Every secret-name field refuses a key:** `SettingsWriter.LooksLikeKey` (32+ hex characters, base64 characters, or a
  long run of letters and digits without a dash) -> *This field takes the name of the secret in your Key Vault, not the
  key itself*, and the typed value is never echoed back.
- **Status in plain words:** *AI is off* / *AI is on -- connected to &lt;deployment&gt;* / *AI is on, but the key is not
  in Key Vault yet -- ...* / *AI is on, but the endpoint ... is not set yet -- ...*.
- **A switch's On / Off words follow its box** live on every page with a setting field (`main.js`), also when the
  browser restores a page. On the AI step the status line follows too: ticked but not saved = *On -- not saved yet*
  (and the reverse); set back = the saved status again.
- **A long setting label wraps** clear of its *More info* pill (`site.css` `.set-label` reserves the pill's width).

### The secret hand-over -- the web app never writes a secret (#537)

- **Key pair:** the updater (`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterSecretHandover.ps1`, every run) keeps an RSA 3072
  **key** `SI-Settings-Handover` in the install's vault (`SI_UPDATER_KEY_VAULT`; Key Vault keys are never exportable, so
  the private half never leaves the vault) -- created once (`keys/create`), read every run (`keys/get`), Key Vault REST
  7.4 through the run's one REST seam. Its PUBLIC half (JWK `n`/`e`) and version go to `cfg.SecretHandoverKey`.
  Deviation from "a Pro setting": `cfg.Setting` is customer-editable and catalog-gated, and `cfg.InstallState.Value` is
  400 characters (a 3072-bit modulus is 512) -- so a table of its own, read-only for the web app.
- **Web app** (`Settings/SecretHandover.cs`): a random AES-256-GCM data key encrypts the secret in memory (12-byte
  nonce, 16-byte tag, additional data = setting + secret name + key version), RSA-OAEP-256 with the public key wraps the
  data key; ONLY the ciphertext, wrapped key, nonce, tag, key version, target secret name, setting and who/when go to
  `cfg.PendingSecret` (a newer paste for the same setting replaces the row still waiting), logged in `cfg.ChangeLog`
  (scope `secret-handover`, `keyvault:<name>` -- never the value); the request's audit row names the target and never
  the pasted field. Then the updater's short run is started (`caj-si-updater` with `SI_UPDATER_MODE=apply-settings`,
  the Jobs page's own start); without jobs access the next nightly run stores it and the page says so. No published key
  yet = nothing stored, the updater is asked to prepare it, the page says to paste again after its run.
- **Updater apply:** per row: the data key is unwrapped INSIDE the vault (`keys/<name>/<version>/decrypt`,
  RSA-OAEP-256), the secret decrypted locally, written (`secrets` PUT) to the Settings page's vault (`SI_KeyVaultName`,
  where the engines read it; else the updater's), and in ONE transaction the setting names the secret
  (`KeyVaultSecretName`), the change is logged "stored" and the row deleted. A failure keeps the row with a reason in
  plain words (`FailureText`: no command, no resource id, no code) and counts the attempt; a key version that no longer
  exists and a row waiting > 3 days are REPORTED in the run's failure report -- never dropped.
- **Page state** -- read on EVERY load from `cfg.PendingSecret` + the setting: *Stored in your Key Vault* / *Waiting to
  be stored -- the updater stores it within minutes* (after 2 days: *... has not stored it yet*) / *Not stored: <the
  updater's reason>*; a failure stays until it is stored or replaced. Never the value. No red box.
- **Rights:** the web app identity needs NO Key Vault permission for this (the magic-link key, an opt-in, is still READ
  with Key Vault Secrets User on its own vault). The updater needs *Key Vault Crypto Officer* (keys) + *Key Vault Secrets
  Officer* (already) on the vault -- `setup\Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -GrantSpnRoles`.
- **Existing installs (CONVERGE-DEFAULTS):** every updater run makes the key pair, and removes the web app's *Key Vault
  Secrets Officer* -- ONLY the one SecurityInsight's own refusal text asked for: that role, assigned to the web app's
