  identity (from `ca-si-management`), at EXACTLY the vault's scope (`Select-SIWebSecretGrant`); inherited, other-scope,
  other-role and other-identity assignments are never touched. No setup script ever granted it (checked), so that
  command is the only way SecurityInsight caused it. The updater's Contributor cannot delete role assignments, so a
  refusal is reported in plain words and `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -GrantSpnRoles` (run by an Owner) removes the same
  assignment with the same matcher.
- **Captured, not built -- keyless sign-in:** every engine's AI call still sends the key (`api-key` header: profiling
  Classify / Enrich / SchemaPropose, the privilege tier classifier, Risk Analysis summaries), so "no key needed" (the
  managed identity with *Cognitive Services OpenAI User*) cannot be offered until those calls take a managed-identity
  token -- with the AI-infrastructure item (`Set-SIAiIntegration.ps1`).

### "Set value": any connector or integration secret, from the web app (#822)

- **What a person sees:** beside a secret-name field -- a secret setting on Settings (the SMTP password, the AI key, the
  Shodan key), and a connector's credential (the ServiceNow instance / user / password / API key, a REST connector's
  token or OAuth client) -- the box `SecretSetViewComponent` (`<vc:secret-set target=… secret-name=… label=… />`): the
  secret's state (*Set 2026-10-20 10:12 UTC by <who> -- stored in your Key Vault* / waiting / the updater's reason / not
  set), and for a SuperAdmin a password box with **Set value**. Inside a page's form the box has no form of its own (forms
  do not nest): its button posts the page's form to `/Admin/Secrets/Set` (`formaction`) and names the secret by its value
  (`target|name`); the value field is `SecretValue:<target>`. Outside a form (`own-form="true"`) it brings one.
- **The way in is the hand-over above, unchanged in its security:** the value is sealed in memory and handed to the
  updater, which stores it in the install's OWN vault -- the web app holds no Key Vault right and never writes a secret
  (the owner's 2026-10-10 rule; `AiKeyStoreTests.No_Key_Vault_secret_write_remains_in_the_web_app` keeps it so). No new
  Azure role: the updater's *Key Vault Crypto Officer* + *Secrets Officer* (already granted by
  `Install-SIUpdaterJob.ps1 -GrantSpnRoles`) do it, and every updater run still removes a *Secrets Officer* the web app
  was once given.
- **The allow-list** (`Settings/SecretAllowList.cs`, and the SAME rules in the updater's `Test-SIHandoverAllowed`; a test
  keeps them equal): the settings `OpenAI_apiKey`, `SMTPPassword`, `SI_Shodan_ApiKey` / `SHODAN_ApiKey`, each under its
  ONE product name; a connector's references `instance / user / password / apikey / token / clientId / clientSecret`
  under a name starting `SI-ServiceNow-` or `SI-Connector-` (the hand-over key is `connector:<name>/<ref>`; the connector
  row already names the secret, so no setting is pointed at it). EVERYTHING else is refused -- above all the secrets
  Invardia issues or the product keeps (`SI-Invardia-*` such as the per-install key, `SI-License`, `SI-Update-State`,
  `SI-InstallId`, `SI-Settings-Handover`, `SI-LicenceRequest-*`): refused by the handler (audited *refused*) and again by
  the updater before it decrypts or writes anything.
- **Handler** (`Pages/Admin/Secrets/Set`): SuperAdmin only (page policy AND the handler), anti-forgery checked, audited
  `secret.value.set` (audit names are domain.object.verb) with the secret's NAME (target `/Admin/Secrets/Set, secret=SI-ServiceNow-Password (connector:vuln-snow/password)`), never the
  value; the value is read from its own field and dropped -- not in SQL, a log line, the audit row or the response. Back
  to the page it came from (a local path only).
- **Updater:** a connector secret is stored and logged with a `secret-stored` line in `cfg.ChangeLog` (who handed it
  over, `keyvault:<name>`, never the value) -- a setting secret gets the same line besides its setting row. The page
  reads that line for *Set at … by …*.
- **ServiceNow with an API key:** a connector naming an `apikey` secret sends it as `x-sn-apikey` (ServiceNow API Key
  authentication) instead of the integration user's Basic header (`New-SISnowConnection -ApiKey`; one of the two, never
  both).
- **Read for use:** unchanged -- the engine reads a connector's secrets by NAME from the vault with its own identity.
  Narrowing that to *Key Vault Secrets User* on each secret (per-secret RBAC) is NOT built here: it changes what every
  existing install's engine may read and needs its own proof; captured with #822.

### ServiceNow: set up, verify, alert, and every row it would send (#844, #845)

- **One guided place per ServiceNow connector** (Configuration > Connectors > Setup, a connector of kind `servicenow`;
  its direction picks the output: `cmdb` = the CI hand-off `servicenow-ci`, `vulnerability` = the vulnerable items
  `servicenow-vulnerable-item`). **What is needed**, each item ticked from what the install has (done / missing / not
  known yet), never a secret value: the instance address (the connector's `settings.instance`, or the name of its
  `instance` secret); the API key (its secret NAME and *set at … by …* from the hand-over, else "named, not set here");
  the ServiceNow roles (below), ticked from the newest check; the Import Set table (its setting) with the ServiceNow schema
  (JSON) to create it; REST Insert Multiple with *Column mappings = Column name*; the transform map (the ServiceNow team's
  own -- never read, so never ticked).
- **The instance URL** is validated (`ServiceNowInstanceUrl.Validate`: https only, a host name with a domain -- an
  instance of service-now.com or your own --, no user, no path, no query; normalised to `https://host`) and STAGED as a
  change of the connector's settings (Review & commit); the connector's own check refuses the same addresses.
- **The API key** is the "Set value" box of the hand-over above, beside each secret reference of the connector
  (SuperAdmin; the web app never sees the value again).
- **Verify connection / Verify table schema.** The web app holds NO Key Vault right, so it cannot read the key and never
  signs in to ServiceNow. Both buttons start the mail job once (`SI_SNOW_VERIFY=<output>`, `SI_SNOW_VERIFY_BY=<who>`, the
  outbox-only switch -- the same pattern as the mail restriction's Verify); that run does only the ServiceNow checks, with
  the engine identity, and records the result; the page shows the newest result per output on reload. The check gets its
  connection the ONE way the push does (`Resolve-SISnowOutputConnection`): the ServiceNow connector of the output's
  direction (switched on first) -- its instance, its API key (`x-sn-apikey`) or user + password, read by NAME from the
  install's Key Vault -- else the install's own ServiceNow secrets. The data-out push now uses that same connection
  (before: always the install's secrets), so a key set on the connector is the key the push sends with.
- **What is checked** (`engine/asset-cmdb/_shared/SI-SnowVerify.ps1`, reads only -- nothing is written in ServiceNow):
  the connection (one read of the table's `sys_db_object` record; DNS / TLS / timeout / 401 wrong key / 403 missing role
  with the role ServiceNow names, else the role the call needs / the table missing / not an import set table); the
  table's columns (`sys_dictionary`: name, internal type, max length, label -- a list that did not come back whole is no
  list); the column mapping (`sys_rest_insert_multiple` for the table and its `sys_rest_insert_multiple_column_mapping`:
  by name, by label -- no record means label --, or not known; a record of another table is never taken).
- **The roles** the key's user needs (from ServiceNow's documentation; confirmed on a real instance before delivery):
  `import_set_loader` and `import_transformer` to send through the Import Set API; `personalize_dictionary` to read the
  table and its columns; `import_admin` to read the REST Insert Multiple mapping. The engine and the web app hold the same
  list (a test keeps them equal).
- **The schema comparison** (web app, `ServiceNowSchemaCompare.Compare`, PURE): the columns IN FORCE of the output as the
  ServiceNow schema builds them (name, type, ServiceNow type, the length to create) against the table's columns:
  *missing* (red: its values would be lost), *too short* (red: a text column shorter than the length to create -- values
  would be cut), *type differs* (amber: the value arrives as text the transform converts), *extra* (info: a column of the
  table SecurityInsight does not send; ServiceNow's own `sys_` columns are never listed), and the mapping (red when by
  label, amber when not read). Built on each view of the page from the newest check's column list.
- **Before every run of a ServiceNow output** (the data-out writer's ServiceNow destination) the same checks run against
  what THIS run sends (`Compare-SISnowSendColumns`, PURE): a column the table does not have, a value longer than its
  column (measured as it is sent: text as is, a list as its JSON), or a mapping by label where a sent column's label is
  not its name HOLD the push -- nothing reaches the Import Set API, nothing is marked as sent (the output's state does not
  move, so every row goes on the next run once the table is right), the run row says *held* with the rows held, and the
  run carries a FAILED issue saying why. Absence is never remediation: a column is never dropped to let the rest through.
  A type that differs, a mapping that could not be read (the first batch is read back anyway) or a table's own column
  are said, never held. A run with nothing new to send still checks and says what it found.
- **Every check is recorded** (`cfg.ServiceNowCheck`: output, connector, table, trigger run / daily / verify, who asked,
  when, outcome ok / warning / failed, a summary and the facts as JSON -- never a key, a user or a password; the engine
  identity may SELECT and INSERT; run logs, outside the configuration backup). **Alerts** come from the newest check per
  output: the daily check (the verification job, after the data health check, for every output with an Import Set
  table), a warning card on Configuration > Connectors > Data-health hold, a *Warnings* line in the daily close-loop mail
  (with *Action*), and the heartbeat Warning `si-snow-1301` (a FAILED newest check; since = its first check that was not
  ok after the last ok one).
- **The rows it would send (#845)** -- for BOTH ServiceNow outputs, test mode or live: "N rows would be sent" with the
  filter it applies, counted from stored data (the vulnerable items by the scope's indexed count; the CIs by one count of
  the CI table with the output's own filter on the CI's class -- a filter on another field is said and applied by the
  export), and **every** such row as Excel and as CSV (`ScopeExport.WriteServiceNowAsync`): the columns in force in their
  order, each value exactly as the connector sends it (`OutputMapper.SentRow`: true / false, a list as JSON, ISO dates; a
  run value says *(set when sent)*), read a page at a time (the CIs by their key, the findings as the vulnerability
  export reads them) and written to a temporary file -- no row cap; Excel continues on "Would send 2" past 1,048,575 rows
  and ends with a sheet naming the output, the filter, the mode and the counts. CSV: UTF-8, comma, RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF
  line ends, the header = the column names; only a text a spreadsheet would run (`=`, `+`, `@`, a tab, a `-` that is not a
  number) gets a leading apostrophe. The vulnerable items apply the ServiceNow vulnerability connector's scope -- on
  Connectors > Scope the one being edited when it was counted (it travels in the export link), else the one in force,
  said on the file --, the CI hand-off the output's own filter. Offered on the connector's setup page (Admin), on
  Connectors > Fields sent beside the ServiceNow schema and team pack (every reader of the page) and on Connectors > Scope
  for the vulnerable items; every download is audited `data.export.download` with the filter and the row count.

### The ServiceNow staging status table: every Import Set push is one batch (#912)

Owner 2026-10-27: *"if it runs using a scheduler, we need a way to tell their importer that sync is running and when it is
ready ... all must be documented in si very detailed"*, *"performance is not critical, but data trust is critical"*,
*"if servicenow team must create a new third table, you must make that in the gui with schema etc"*. The SQL hand-off
already had its batch (`snowstage.Batch` / `vImportBatch`: writing, complete, held, failed; the import views show only the
newest complete batch). The Import Set push had none: no start, no end, no count -- a push that stopped halfway looked like
a finished one. The customer-facing words are `release/product-info/content/docs/servicenow-sync-complete.md (merged there by #914)` (to be merged into the
ServiceNow team guide).

- **The table.** ONE import set table per install for both outputs, the setting `SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable`
  (**not set at all = `u_si_staging_status`**, label *SecurityInsight staging status*; set to `''` = none). Same name rule
  as a data staging table (`Test-SISnowStagingStatusTable`: u_/x_, never a record table) and never one of the data tables.
  Columns (`Get-SISnowStagingStatusColumns`, `engine/asset-cmdb/_shared/SI-SnowImportSet.ps1`; the web app's copy
  `Outputs/ServiceNowStagingStatus.cs` is held to it through the generated test pack): `u_si_batch_id` (100), `u_si_output`,
  `u_si_state`, `u_si_connector`, `u_si_target_table`, `u_si_source_run`, `u_si_started_at`, `u_si_finished_at`, `u_si_batch_time`,
  `u_si_planned_rows`, `u_si_sent_rows`, `u_si_failed_rows`, `u_si_import_set_ids` (4000, cut with "(+N more)"), `u_si_reason` (1000),
  `u_si_version`. Every column carries the si prefix (owner 2026-10-27, like every SI column); the ones with a twin in
  `vImportBatch` mean the same there (`Get-SISnowStagingStatusSqlTwin`: `u_si_batch_id` = `u_batch_id`, `u_si_connector` =
  `u_connector`, `u_si_state` = `u_state`, `u_si_started_at` = `u_started_at`, `u_si_batch_time` = `u_batch_time` = when it
  became complete, `u_si_reason` = `u_reason`); the four states are `CK_SnowBatch_State`'s.
- **A batch** = one output's push in one run, id `<run id>:<output>` (`Get-SISnowBatchId`). ONE ROW PER STATE CHANGE, always
  `writing` -> `complete | failed | held` (owner: minimal and unambiguous): the writing row before the first data row
  (`u_si_planned_rows` when known -- data out compares page by page, so its writing row has none and the end row has it), every
  data row carries `u_si_batch_id`, then the end row with the counts and the import sets. `complete` = every planned row
  accepted and no error; `failed` = a call failed / rows not accepted (`u_si_failed_rows`, `u_si_reason`); `held` = the push
  stopped before or while sending (the ceiling, the ServiceNow check, a value that would be cut) -- **refused before
  sending is still writing -> held** (one shape for every batch). Nothing to send = writing (planned 0) -> complete. Rows
  are written one per call to `POST /api/now/import/<table>` (mapped by column name) and read back by `u_si_batch_id` +
  `u_si_state`: a row that landed without its batch id is a failure.
- **Data trust first** (decided with the existing check pattern, `Invoke-SISnowOutputCheck`): a staging status table that
  is named but missing, not an import set table or short of a column FAILS the output's check and holds the push -- nothing
  is sent, never data rows without their marker (`Add-SISnowStatusTableCheck`; recorded in `cfg.ServiceNowCheck` with a
  `statusTable` block, so Data health, the heartbeat and the daily mail say it). The writing row that cannot be written
  refuses the push the same way (`Invoke-SISnowBatchedPush` / `Open-SIDataOutSnowBatch`). An end row that cannot be
  written leaves the batch `writing` (never imported) and is an error of the run. The setting EMPTY (an existing install,
  below) = sent exactly as before, no `u_si_batch_id`, with a WARNING in the run log, the run's why and the check
  (`Get-SISnowNoStatusTableWarning`).
- **The three push paths.** Data out (`servicenow-ci`, `servicenow-vulnerable-item`, `engine/data-out/SI-DataOut.ps1`):
  `Open-SIDataOutSnowSession` checks both tables and opens the batch, `Send-SIDataOutSnowPage` adds `u_si_batch_id` and counts
  the import sets and the rows not accepted, `Close-SIDataOutSnowSession` writes the end row first. The CMDB job
  (`Invoke-SICmdb.ps1`, `SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetTable`) and the close-loop hand-off (`Invoke-SIVulnLoop.ps1`,
  `SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowImportSetTable`; a paged run hands each page off as a batch `<run>-p<n>`) go through
  `Invoke-SISnowBatchedPush`. All three use the one setting.
- **A batch that did not end complete is sent again whole.** Data out sends only what is new or changed, and records a page
  as sent when it lands -- so a failed / held batch would leave rows recorded as sent that the importer never imports. At the
  end of such a batch every row this run recorded for the output is marked to go again (`Reset-SIDataOutRunState`: the row
  hash cleared to 64 zeros, a value no row has); at the start of every batch the rows of an earlier run that never recorded
  its end (`cfg.ConnectorRun` has no row for it: the job stopped mid-push; last 7 days) are marked the same way
  (`Reset-SIDataOutOrphanState`). The CMDB job sends every CI each run; the close-loop plans from the target, so neither
  needs it.
- **Overlap.** One output's batches do not overlap: the pipeline holds the install's run lock and never starts a job that
  is already running (`engine/_shared/SI-JobFlow.ps1`). The guide still says how to order batches if they ever did
  (`u_si_batch_time`).
- **Existing installs (update step 9n, `setup/_shared/SI-SnowStagingStatus.ps1`).** The table lives in the customer's
  ServiceNow, so an update cannot switch it on: ONCE, only while the setting has no row, an install that already sends to
  ServiceNow (any of `SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable`, `SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable`, `SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetTable`,
  `SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowImportSetTable` set) gets the setting `''` with its cfg.ChangeLog row, read back. Every other
  install takes the default; a new install's ServiceNow team creates the table as part of the setup.
- **The GUI** (`_ServiceNowGuide.cshtml`, "For your ServiceNow team" > *Tables to create in ServiceNow*): all three tables
  -- the two data staging tables from their ServiceNow schema (`ServiceNowSchema.Build`, which now ends with `u_si_batch_id`)
  and the staging status table -- each with every column (name, label, type, max length, meaning), a JSON definition per
  table (the data tables' `?handler=Schema`, the status table's `?handler=StagingStatusSchema`, the same schema format),
  the REST Insert Multiple setting, the UI steps (`ServiceNowStagingStatus.Steps`) and Copy; the team text and its
  download carry the definitions (`TABLES TO CREATE`, `HOW TO CREATE THE STAGING STATUS TABLE`). The team lines say
  whether the table exists, has every column, the data tables have `u_si_batch_id`, the import rule and retention. The schema
  comparison treats a missing `u_si_batch_id` as amber while no staging status table is set, red once one is.
- **The test pack** carries `rest/u_si_staging_status.json` (a complete, a failed and a held batch, each writing first),
  `u_si_batch_id` on every pushed row, the columns in `columns.csv`, three cases and the how-to section.
- **Retention** is the customer's: SecurityInsight only inserts. The guide names ServiceNow's *Import Set Deleter*
  (System Import Sets > Import Set Tables > Scheduled Cleanup; default: import sets and rows older than seven days --
  verified in ServiceNow's public docs, to be checked on the customer's release), keep the two newest complete batches of
  each output, how the per-import-set cleanup meets a batch of several import sets, and the sizing formula.

### One trusted contract for every data-out target: ServiceNow and the SQL connectors (#914)

Owner 2026-10-27: *"performance is not critical, but data trust is critical"*. Before #914 SecurityInsight had three
routes into ServiceNow with three sets of rules: the hand-off database, the OLDER push (the CMDB job and the
vulnerability close-loop's ServiceNow connector, each behind its own setting, every in-scope row every run with
`u_action` / `u_row_hash`) and the DATA-OUT connector (#903: only new or changed rows, no `u_action`, no row hash or
batch on vulnerable items, no output scope, lower-case state values, a row id as `u_source_record_id`). #914 makes the
DATA-OUT connector THE ServiceNow push and gives it, the hand-off database and the two SQL connectors ONE contract.
The rules of #217 hold unchanged and are golden-tested: absence is not remediation, a close comes only from a complete
run, a scope never closes anything as fixed.

**The code.** `engine/data-out/SI-DataOutContract.ps1` (PURE: the columns, the action table, the scope, the clear marker,
the status counts, the requests) + `engine/data-out/SI-DataOut.ps1` (the ServiceNow writer uses it) +
`engine/asset-cmdb/_shared/SI-SnowImportSet.ps1` (the staging status row, the read-back) + `sql/*` (the run tables).

#### 1. One route; the older push is removed
- The jobs `asset-cmdb` (ServiceNow CMDB) and `asset-vulns-servicenow` (the close-loop's ServiceNow connector) STAY
  steps of the pipeline, without their ServiceNow paths: the CMDB job plans and reports and sends nothing (its run says
  so); the close-loop's ServiceNow job ends at once; the close-loop skips a `servicenow` vulnerability connector. Retiring
  the two steps (the `retired` mechanism of `asset-properties`) was built first and taken back: about ten pipeline-behaviour
  suites use them as their example connectors, so retiring the steps is its own follow-up (job map, Bootstrap, missing
  jobs, Get started cards, those suites).
- Removed: `Invoke-SISnowBatchedPush`, the CMDB job's Import Set and direct-write paths, the close-loop's ServiceNow
  hand-off; the settings `SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetTable`, `SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetMaxRows`,
  `SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowImportSetTable`, `SI_ServiceNow_DirectWrite`, `SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowDirectWrite`; the
  close-loop skips a `servicenow` vulnerability connector (one line; the SQL and REST connectors run as before).
- The update (step 9o, `setup/_shared/SI-SnowOneRoute.ps1`) reads those settings once: a value that is set is logged ONCE
  (`the older ServiceNow push was removed ...`), the setting rows are left in the settings database (never customer data
  deleted) and are ignored by the code; it records that it said so (`cfg.InstallState` `SnowOneRoute`).

#### 2. The columns (every pushed row of both outputs; the hand-off database views carry `u_si_batch_id` on `vImportVulnerableItem` and keep their existing columns -- they carry no `u_action` / clear marker)
| Column | Object | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `u_si_correlation_id` | both | THE CI key (existing). A CI's coalesce key |
| `u_vulnerability` | vulnerable item | The finding key (existing). Vulnerable item key = `u_si_correlation_id` + `u_vulnerability` |
| `u_source_record_id` | vulnerable item | Existing column, now STABLE: `<CI key>|<finding key>` (it was a row id) |
| `u_action` | both | `new`, `update`, `close`, `reopen`, `held`, `out_of_scope` |
| `u_row_hash` | both | SHA-256 of the content columns (the envelope and the run columns are not part of it) |
| `u_si_batch_id` | both | The batch that delivered the row (`<run id>:<output>`) |
| `u_si_cleared` | both | THE CLEAR MARKER: comma-separated column names whose value SecurityInsight now knows is empty |
| `u_si_reason` | both | Why the row is `held` or `out_of_scope` (empty otherwise) |
| `u_si_replaces` | both | The key this record replaces (a device re-onboarded or merged): the importer moves the record |
| `u_source_run` | both | The collection run the values come from (can be older than the batch; existing on CIs, added on vulnerable items) |

Never renamed: `u_batch_id` (hand-off database, existing) stays beside `u_si_batch_id` with the same value. The #912
staging status table was never released: its key is `u_si_batch_id` from the start.

#### 3. u_action, per record type
Each row is decided from what the record IS now and the BASE: what the target last received in a COMPLETE batch
(`cfg.DataOutItem`: the row hash is cleared to 64 zeros when its batch did not complete, and the row keeps `__base`, the
last delivered class). Pure: `Get-SIDataOutContractAction`.

| Now (SecurityInsight) | Base: none | Base: open / active | Base: closed / retired | Base: out of scope / gone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CI active (incl. not-seen) / finding open | `new` | `update` | `reopen` | `reopen` |
| CI retired / finding closed | `close` | `close` | `close` | `close` |
| finding open, absence still counting (`u_absent_runs` > 0) | `new` | `held` | `reopen` | `reopen` |
| out of the output scope | no row | `out_of_scope` (once) | no row | no row |
| disabled / a report that could not complete / CI not delivered (vulnerable item) | no row (counted held) | `held` (last values) | `held` (last values) | no row |
| not in SecurityInsight's data any more | -- | `held` once, then no row | `held` once, then no row | no row |

`out_of_scope` on a vulnerable item carries `u_state` = `Closed`, `u_close_reason` = `Out of scope` (never fixed). A
`held` row tells the importer to change nothing. Every row is sent EVERY run (full current scoped state); an unchanged
record is `update` with the same `u_row_hash`.

#### 4. One set of values
CI state (`u_si_state`): `active`, `not-seen`, `retired` (value map `servicenow_ci_state`). Vulnerable item state
(`u_state`): `Open`, `Closed` (`open_closed`). Close reasons (`u_close_reason`, value map `servicenow_close_reason`):
`Remediated`, `AssetRetired`, `NoLongerMonitored`, `Out of scope`, `Duplicate`, `Report changed`, `Linked`, `Rekeyed`,
`ClosedByEngineer`, `No longer reported by SecurityInsight`. The same in the hand-off database, the push and the SQL
vulnerability connector.

#### 5. The staging status table (#912, now with the contract)
Every column carries the si prefix (#912's final naming): `u_si_batch_id`, `u_si_output`, `u_si_state` (`writing` ->
`complete | failed | held`, plus an information row `feedback`), `u_si_connector`, `u_si_target_table`, `u_si_source_run`,
`u_si_started_at`, `u_si_finished_at`, `u_si_batch_time`, `u_si_planned_rows`, `u_si_sent_rows`, `u_si_failed_rows`,
`u_si_import_set_ids`, `u_si_reason`, `u_si_version`, and from #914 `u_si_contract_version`, `u_si_mode` (`live`, `resync`,
`test`), the counts per action `u_si_new_rows`, `u_si_update_rows`, `u_si_close_rows`, `u_si_reopen_rows`, `u_si_held_rows`,
`u_si_out_of_scope_rows`, and the read-back `u_si_import_inserted`, `u_si_import_updated`, `u_si_import_ignored`,
`u_si_import_skipped`, `u_si_import_errors`, `u_si_import_pending`. One batch per output; the counts are per action of that
output (= object). The web app's copy (`Outputs/ServiceNowStagingStatus.cs`) and the test pack are held to the engine's list
by the parity test.
- **`u_si_batch_id` on the data rows is a column of the output maps** (token `$batch_id`, like the other envelope tokens
  `$action`, `$cleared`, `$reason`, `$replaces`), so it is in every schema definition -- and, being a system token, it is
  never part of `u_row_hash`: the hash stays "the record's content changed" (#912 kept it out of the maps for exactly that
  reason; #914 keeps the reason and drops the exception).
- **#912's re-send of a batch that did not complete stays** (`Reset-SIDataOutRunState`, `Reset-SIDataOutOrphanState`), with
  a new role: every row is sent every sync anyway, so the reset no longer decides WHETHER a row goes -- it decides its
  `u_action` (an undelivered row's base is the class it was sent over, `__base`, never what the failed batch said).
#### 6. The contract items (decision 8)
- **(a) clear vs unknown.** A `new` / `update` / `close` / `reopen` / `out_of_scope` row is SecurityInsight's whole current
  record: every CLEARABLE column that is empty is listed in `u_si_cleared` (the column catalogue says which columns are
  clearable). A column that is empty and not listed, or any column of a `held` row, is unknown: keep your value. SQL
  connectors: SecurityInsight writes the whole row, so `NULL` on a row it wrote this batch is the clear; a held record is
  not written.
- **(b) feedback.** At the start of each sync of an output, SecurityInsight reads back the import result of its newest
  complete batch that has none yet: `GET /api/now/stats/sys_import_set_row` grouped by `sys_import_state` for the batch's
  import sets. Recorded in `cfg.DataOutBatch` and as a `feedback` row in the staging status table. Errors raise the
  output's issue through the run's failure path (the heartbeat and support uplink carry it). Rows still pending = asked
  again next sync. Not readable (a role) = a warning, never a failure. SQL connectors: the rows the apply statement wrote
  (`LandedRows`).
- **(c) a batch that never ends.** At the start of a sync, every `writing` batch of the same output (cfg.DataOutBatch;
  cmdbsync.SyncRun / vuln.SyncRun for SQL) is ended `failed` with the reason (`a later sync started while this batch was
  still writing`), a `failed` row is written to the staging status table, and its rows go again. Never two open
  batches per output.
- **(d) counts per action and object** on the end row and in `cfg.DataOutBatch`.
- **(e) `u_si_contract_version`** = `1` on every batch. Rule: add only; renaming or removing a column, or changing a value's
  meaning, needs a new version.
- **(f) re-keying.** `sidata.AssetIdHistory` (`rekey` / `merge`, PreviousId -> CurrentId): the new key's row carries
  `u_si_replaces` = the old key while the old key is in the output's delivered state; the old key gets no row of its
  own and leaves the state once that batch is complete. Vulnerable items: `<old CI key>|<finding>`.
- **(g) order and references.** The CI output runs before the vulnerable item output (catalogue order, golden-tested). A
  vulnerable item whose CI key is empty, or not in the CI output's delivered state, is `held` (or not sent when the
  target never had it), reason `its CI is not delivered yet`. With the CI output switched off the check is off and
  the end row says so.
- **(h) who wins.** One rule, the SQL connector's: SecurityInsight still sees the finding -> its row is `update` with `Open`;
  an engineer's close is reopened by the importer (ServiceNow) / by the connector (SQL). A `held` row (SI does not see the
  finding in this run) changes nothing. SecurityInsight never closes on the target's word.
- **(i) full resync.** The setting `SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest` = `resync:<token>` (an Admin button on the connector
  page; staged, Review & commit, change-logged): the next sync treats every base as none (every in-scope record `new`,
  every closed one `close`), mode `resync`, and records the token as done.
- **(j) test batch.** `test:<token>`: the next sync first sends one batch per output with at most 5 rows each, mode
  `test`; it never touches the state. The importer ignores every `test` batch.

#### 7. The SQL connectors
- **CMDB SQL** (`cmdbsync.SyncRun`, added in place): `SiBatchId`, `BatchState` (`writing|complete|failed|held`),
  `ContractVersion`, `Mode`, `OutOfScope`, `LandedRows`. A `writing` row is inserted before the apply (Outcome `error`,
  Reason `writing` -- a run that never ends reads as an error); the apply's ONE transaction turns it into `applied` +
  `complete` together with the CI changes; refused = `held`, error = `failed`. `ConfigurationItem.SiBatchId`.
- **Vulnerability SQL** (`vuln.SyncRun`, new, same shape) written by the close-loop; `vuln.VulnerabilityItem.SiBatchId`.
  The close-loop writes record by record (not one transaction). The batch row is written FIRST (`writing`); every write of the run
  (open, refresh, absence count, close, reopen, re-key) stamps `SiBatchId` AT WRITE TIME, with `LastAction` (new / reopen in this
  batch, NULL otherwise); the batch end writes the clear marker (`Cleared`) of the batch's records and its counts. A record
  of a writing or failed batch is always recognisable by its id; one the newest run did not write keeps a complete batch's id.
  (Stamping at the end, as first built, left a changed record carrying the PREVIOUS complete batch's id while its batch
  was still writing -- the reader rule could not see it.)
- **The database route carries the push's contract** (owner gap list 2026-10-28, append only): `vImportCi` (both hand-off
  databases) and `vImportVulnerableItem` end with `u_si_batch_id`, `u_action`, `u_si_cleared`; the connector database's
  `vImportBatch` / `vImportCiKeyValue` / `vImportCiRelation` with `u_si_batch_id` (= `u_batch_id`, which stays). Columns:
  `snowstage.BatchCi.Action` / `Cleared` (InsertCis: the action table against the previous complete batch; CarryFrozen
  keeps the row's), `snowstage.HandoffCi.SiBatchId` / `LastAction` / `Cleared` (schema level 4; the lifecycle step sets
  reopen), `vuln.VulnerabilityItem.LastAction` / `Cleared`. One clear list per record type, held equal to the push's
  (`Get-SIHandoffClearedColumnMap`, `Get-SIVulnSqlClearedColumnMap`). The Pro database's CI hand-off write is a batch of
  its own (coordinator 2026-10-28, "a reader that can see two runs mixed while the batch says complete breaks the one
  contract"): `snowstage.HandoffRun` (same shape as `vuln.SyncRun`), id `<run>:cmdb-handoff`. `Start-SIHandoffBatch`
  writes it `writing` before the first chunk (an earlier writing one ended `failed`); every upsert chunk stamps
  `SiBatchId` with it; the state signal (`Update-SIHandoffSiState -BatchId`) stamps the rows whose state moves; only
  then `Stop-SIHandoffBatch` sets `complete` with the counts; an error ends it `failed`. `vImportBatch` lists it
  (`u_connector` `cmdb-handoff`; a guarded `ALTER VIEW` adds the third `UNION ALL` on an existing database). A
  database without the table stamps nothing (the schema adds it).
- **One rule for every reader:** act only on rows whose batch is `complete` -- `snowstage.vImportBatch` in SecurityInsight's
  own database lists both (`u_si_batch_id`, `u_output`, `u_state`, the counts).

### The top lists without the AI summary, a fix's findings, and SI's own SQL target always on (#863, #864, #865)
- **The Top 50 lists never depend on the AI summary (#863).** Risk Analysis builds the Top 50 risky assets and Top 50
  critical findings rollup on EVERY run with rows (`engine/risk-analysis/Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1`, `$script:_RATopListsOnly`
  when `BuildSummaryByAI` is off): the AI configuration, the shared AI snapshot (read and write) and the AI call are skipped,
  the rollup runs alone and its lists go into the executive view (`sidata.RiskExecView`) with `AISummaryEnabled` false. A
  rollup that fails is a warning, never a failed run. The web app, for a kept view WITHOUT a list (written before this
  change), builds the list from the database (`RiskExecSql.TopActiveCis`): the ACTIVE CIs (`sidata.Ci.Lifecycle = 'active'`)
  with risk on them, Criticality Tier first (Tier 0, no tier last), then Weighted Risk Score -- the mail's order -- each
  linked to its CI page (`ExecViewLoader.TopAssetsAsync`; Top 50 risky assets, Top 10 asset drilldown). FIRST, wherever a
  part depends on the AI summary and the run had it off, the page says "The AI summary is turned off at this install" and
  what turns it on (an Azure OpenAI deployment; `OpenAI_endpoint`, `OpenAI_deployment`, the key in Key Vault,
  `BuildSummaryByAI`; Get Started's AI step) -- never "Top 0 risky assets" (`Pages/Management/_AiSummaryOff.cshtml`,
  `RiskExec/AiSummaryNote.cs`). The Risk Analysis page points to the database list when the run kept none.
- **A remediation's link opens exactly its findings (#864).** `/Collection/Rows?c=..&fix=<key>` swaps in
  `CollectionViewSql.RowsOfFix` (`f.RemediationKey = @Fix`). It inherited `Rows`' #812 keyset (the opening view paged off
  the collection's risk index, whose "applies" test only looks for an AssetKey the fix plan removes): the page read the
  collection's top 50 by risk and kept those the fix closes -- almost always none -- so a fix with 578,285 findings showed
  "0 rows". `RowsOfFix` now has no keyset (as `RowsOfIssue`) and its source is built by `NarrowRows`, which throws when the
  one-CI condition it replaces is no longer in `Rows`' source (never every finding under a narrowed name). An address that
  names a set (`fix=`, `ViewState.SetKeys`) never gets a person's remembered filters, even from the menu; the page says
  "Showing the N findings ... the fix closes" and names any filter chosen on the page, with "All of this fix's findings".
- **SI's own SQL close-loop target is always on (#865).** The connector of kind sql + direction vulnerability
  (`vulnerability-sql`) is SecurityInsight's own record of every vulnerability's lifecycle (Changes & trends >
  Vulnerabilities over time / per collection); in test mode it records nothing. The import creates it apply + create +
  close whatever `SI_VulnSync_Run` says (`Get-SIConnectorImportPlan`); the web app saves it so
  (`ConnectorRepository.AlwaysOn`, the Connectors page and Get Started) and does not offer whatif for it (it says why);
  the update's step 9k (`setup/_shared/SI-OwnSqlConnector.ps1`, free payload, loads no Pro file) moves an existing install's
  target there on every update -- one transaction per connector with its `cfg.ChangeLog` row, only while it is still off,
  read back, never a ServiceNow / REST connector or the SQL CMDB hand-off, Enabled left to the customer (a switched-off one
  is said), Pro only, never fails the update, `-DetectOnly` plans. The two pages say plainly why they are empty
  (`Changes/OwnSqlTargetStatus.cs` over `cfg.Connector` + `cfg.ConnectorRun`): not set up, switched off, in test mode, not
  run yet, or its last run failed / was a test run -- never just "0".

### Set-SIMail and Exchange Online: its own sign-in client, and a refusal said as a refusal

- **The Exchange token.** Exchange Online's admin API (the InvokeCommand endpoint the Exchange Online module uses) takes a
  person's token only when it carries the Exchange administration permission (Exchange.Manage). Setup's browser sign-in
  uses the Azure PowerShell public client, which does not carry it, so the Exchange token comes from the Exchange Online
  PowerShell public client instead: one more browser sign-in in the same flow (code + PKCE on localhost, the account
  filled in, no account picker), then that client's own refresh token. Every other resource stays on setup's sign-in.
- **The role, read from the token.** Before the first Exchange call the script reads the token's directory roles and says
  whether Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator is active in this sign-in -- or that it is not, and that an
  eligible role must be activated in PIM first.
- **A refusal is never "the mailbox does not exist".** When Exchange refuses the sign-in (401 / 403) or does not answer,
  whether the mailbox exists is unknown: the script says Exchange refused this sign-in (with the status), the likely
  reasons (an eligible PIM role not activated -- activate it, wait a few minutes, run again in a new PowerShell window; or
  the account lacks Exchange Administrator), prints the commands for the Exchange administrator (New-Mailbox only when the
  mailbox is to be created, "only if it does not exist yet") and ends NOT DONE (exit 2, handed over).

### The company names the shared mailbox -- in two steps (framework MAIL-1)

Owner 2026-10-09: *"companies have their own naming"*; *"maybe 2 steps - create + validate ... you build the cmdlet after
user fills in the name"*.
- **`setup\Set-SIMail.ps1`**: `-MailboxName` (default `SecurityInsight`), **`-MailDomain`** (default: the tenant's initial
  domain) and `-DisplayName`; `-SharedMailbox` still wins. The Exchange objects follow the mailbox name: the scope
  `<name>-Sender`, the role assignments `<name>-MailSend-<first 8 of the app id>` (the defaults are unchanged for the
  default name). **Adopted, never duplicated:** with no `-ScopeName`, a scope that already filters exactly this mailbox is
  used whatever it is called, and an assignment that grants `Application Mail.Send` on it counts whatever its name.
- **The web app** (`Settings/MailSetupFlow.cs`) names them the same way and reads Exchange first (`Get-ManagementScope`,
  `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment`) to adopt what is there.
- **Two steps** (`Pages/Shared/_MailboxSteps.cshtml`, on Settings > E-mail and in Get Started's mail step while the shared
  mailbox is chosen): **Step 1 "Name and create"** -- mailbox name, domain (a list of the remembered one, the admin's and the tenant's
  initial domain, or "Another domain..." typed -- no directory read), display name, create / already exists; the `Set-SIMail.ps1` command is built from the fields as they
  are typed (`mailbox-steps.js`, the same string as `SharedMailboxSteps.Command`) and shown once the name is filled in,
  with the script's doc page and download; Save remembers the address (`SI_Mail_From`). **Step 2 "Validate"** -- shows
  the remembered address; ONE button makes it the sender (`SI_Mail_Mode = sharedMailbox`, the admin as the probe mailbox
  when none is set), starts the mail job's restriction check and queues a test mail to the admin. The address is typed
  only in step 1 (Get Started shows `SI_Mail_From` only for SMTP; the SuperAdmin one-click setup has no address field and
  uses step 1's, or says to name the mailbox first).

### Keeping your own SMTP relay by choice (Pro web app)

The mail verdict (`Settings/MailHealth.cs`, shared by the Home banner and Settings > E-mail) is amber for an SMTP relay:
*Move to an Office 365 shared mailbox*. An Admin who keeps the relay on purpose presses **Ignore** on that banner (operator
2026-10-09: "make option to ignore"): `SI_Mail_SmtpKept = true` (Community setting, Mail card, advanced, default off) is
written through the settings writer, audited `mail.smtp.keep`. From then the verdict is **set up** -- *Mail goes through
your own SMTP relay (kept by choice)* -- no banner on Home, and Settings > E-mail shows *SMTP relay kept by choice* with
**Undo** (writes false, audited the same) instead of the move hint. **A failed test mail stays red whatever the choice**;
a shared mailbox and "mail off" are not touched by it. Mail is sent the same way either way.

### One subject format for every mail (framework MAIL-3)

Every mail SecurityInsight sends -- the Risk Analysis report, the guard mails, the close-loop, exemption, governance,
department, task-digest, data-quality and licence mails, and the mails the web app queues (exemption requests and
decisions, Get Started reminders, findings for a vendor's review, management summaries, sign-in links, the test mail) --
gets its subject in ONE place, `Get-SIMailSubject` (`engine/_shared/SI-MailTransport.ps1`), which `Send-SIMail` calls for
every mail:

    [<Environment>] <severity word if relevant> <what happened> [<ticket number if any>] [SecurityInsight]

- **`<Environment>`** is the name the web app's header shows (`SIWeb_EnvironmentName`, else `SI_EnvironmentName`, else the
  install id). The ring and the edition are NOT in the subject; the footer and the PDF keep them. A name that carries
  them itself (`Internal (ring 1, PRO)`) is shown as `[Internal]`.
- **The severity word**, only when relevant: `Failed` (a failed run, step or update, a Risk Analysis report that is not
  complete, a failed licence request), `Warning` (a guard warning, a data-quality alert), `Action needed` (a guard that
  stopped, refused, held or skipped something; an exemption request, an expiry warning, the monthly exemption review, a
  technical review, a finding sent for a vendor's review, a Get Started step or decision that waits). Reports, digests,
  close-loop, department and information mails carry none. A sender passes `-Severity` (Send-SIMail,
  Send-SICloseLoopMail, Send-SIGuardMailDefault) or writes the word first in its subject (`Action needed: ...`); the
  transport places it.
- **The product is named once, at the end.** A leading `SecurityInsight · `, `SecurityInsight - `, `SecurityInsight -- `,
  `SecurityInsight: ` or `Security Insights | ` is taken out centrally -- so a mail an older web app queued before the
  update is put right as it is sent. The senders no longer write it.
- **At most 120 characters.** Only `<what happened>` is shortened, with `...`; the brackets, the severity word and the
  ticket number are always kept.
- **Never wrapped twice**: a subject already in the format is sent as it is.
- **The body is unchanged.**

Example: `[Contoso] Action needed: Monthly exemption review: Endpoint -- 1 active, 1 ending soon, 1 expired [SecurityInsight]`.

**The environment name to Invardia.** Identified heartbeat and run reports can carry the same name as `environmentName`
(`ConvertTo-SITelemetryWire`; never on an anonymous report, and left out when the install has no name -- never the
tenant id). Invardia accepts the field (it reads `environmentName` and `EnvironmentName`).

### Verification service -- data-collection gaps (Pro)

SecurityInsight can only report what its sources deliver. A Defender for Cloud plan that is off, a VM without a
Defender for Endpoint sensor or an empty Advanced Hunting table does not show up as a finding -- it shows up as
*nothing*, which reads as "secure" when it is "unknown". The verification service (docs/V3-DATA-MODEL.md 2.11) finds
those gaps and keeps a decision on each one.

- **Engine:** `engine/verification/Invoke-SIVerification.ps1`, the container job `caj-si-verification`, the last step
  of the Deliver stage (`config/job-flow.locked.json`: after the collectors, timer 11:00 UTC in schedules mode). Licence
  gate `data-backend`; without a Pro database the container skips it with the reason.
- **Read-only.** It reads Resource Graph (subscriptions, `microsoft.security/pricings`, VMs, security connectors),
  Defender for Endpoint `/api/machines`, Graph `/devices`, Advanced Hunting, the security workspace and
  `SI_RunHealth_CL` -- all with permissions the collection identity already has (Reader, `Machine.Read.All`,
  `Device.Read.All`, `ThreatHunting.Read.All`, Log Analytics Reader). It never sends a write verb (a test enforces it).
- **The checks** are a catalog, `config/verification-checks.locked.json` -- a stable id (never renamed: decisions and
  history are keyed by it), title, why, fix, severity, scope, source:

  | id | finds | severity / scope |
  |---|---|---|
  | `defender-plan-off` | a Defender for Cloud plan (Servers, Storage, SQL, Key Vault, App Service, Containers, ARM, DNS) not on Standard on an enabled subscription | high / subscription |
  | `vm-not-onboarded` | a running Azure VM no Defender machine matches (resource id, VM id or name) | high / resource |
  | `device-not-onboarded` | an enabled Windows / macOS Entra device signed in within `SI_ActiveStaleDays` (30) with no Defender machine | medium / device |
  | `sensor-unhealthy` | a Defender sensor not Active, or quiet for more than 7 days (stale machines are not gaps) | medium / device |
  | `os-unsupported` | a machine on an operating system past its end of support (Windows 7 / 8 / 8.1 / 10, Server 2008 R2 / 2012 / 2012 R2) | high / device |
  | `multicloud-connector-absent` | no AWS or GCP connector in Defender for Cloud | info / tenant |
  | `hunting-table-empty` | `DeviceInfo`, `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`, `ExposureGraphNodes` or `IdentityInfo` has no rows | high / tenant |
  | `signin-logs-missing` | `SigninLogs`, `AuditLogs` or `AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs` had no rows in the last day in the security workspace | medium / workspace |
  | `collector-incomplete` | a collector (endpoint, identity, azure, publicip, the classifier) whose newest run in 26 hours did not end `success`, or did not run | high / engine |

- **Not checked is never "no gaps".** A source that cannot be read (or a partial machine list -- it would report every
  machine it missed) makes the checks that need it `not-checked` with the reason; the run's health is
  `success-partial`, naming them. A finding is resolved only by a run in which its check ran; parts of a check that
  could not be read (one hunting table) are kept, never resolved.
- **Store** (`sql/si-pro-settings.sql`, guarded, additive): `cfg.VerificationRun` (run + summary JSON),
  `cfg.VerificationCheckRun` (ok / gaps / not-checked per check per run), `cfg.VerificationFinding` (current state,
  key `<checkId>|<scope key>`), `cfg.VerificationFindingEvent` (opened / reopened / resolved per run),
  `cfg.VerificationDecision`. The engine writes the first four; the web app writes only the decisions (grant
  `INSERT, UPDATE` on `cfg.VerificationDecision`).
- **Decisions:** `ignored` (not a gap for this organisation) or `accepted` (a known gap whose risk is accepted for
  now), with a reason, a reviewer and who / when; due for review after `decisionReviewDays` (180). Append-only: a review
  or a change is a new row and the replaced one gets `RevokedAt`, so every decision's history stays. **Why not
  `cfg.Exemption`** (2.11 proposed reusing it): an exemption hides a *finding of a report* from its scores and is keyed
  by report / configuration / CVE / asset, and its scope CHECK has no place for a tenant- or subscription-scoped gap;
  widening that CHECK means dropping it, which the additive schema gate refuses. The decision table has its own small
  review cycle instead.
- **Web app:** Operations > Verification (data gaps) (`/Admin/Verification`, readers may view): the checks with their
  last result, the gaps with a filter (check, open / resolved / all, decision, review due, severity), the review queue
  (decisions due within 30 days, overdue first, with the reviewer), a gap's history; an Admin ignores / accepts,
  reviews (saves again) or withdraws -- audited as `verification.decision.save` / `verification.decision.revoke`.
- **Setup telemetry hook (#491):** `Get-SIVerificationControls` turns the run's summary into one control per check
  (`verification.<checkId>`: pass / fail / unknown, with counts and never the customer's object names); the engine
  leaves it in `$global:SI_VerificationControls` for the telemetry step to send.
- **Not built yet** (2.11 items): the Defender for Identity sensor on domain-controller CIs, mailing the review due list
  to the reviewer, and gaps as CI risk factors.
- **The job (#685):** `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1` creates `caj-si-verification` at every Pro install as
  infrastructure (like `caj-si-config-backup`: whatever the engine list), licensed, one replica, timer
  `SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleVerification` (default `0 11 * * *`) -- in flow mode a step of the pipeline (Manual, the timer
  remembered). An existing install gets it from the update (`setup/_shared/SI-MissingJobs.ps1`, step 9a of
  `setup/Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1`): built from a Pro job of the install (`caj-si-asset-datasync`, else
  `-close-loop-mail`, `-asset-cmdb-sql`, `-asset-correlation`) -- its image, identity, sign-in, settings and secrets,
  without what only that job's engine needs -- by one ARM PUT, read back until created, removed again when it does not
  read back right; a job that exists is never touched. Once it exists, the default pipeline runs it as the last Deliver
  step (a job not installed is not a step). A pipeline a person saved (`cfg.JobFlow`) keeps its own steps.

### Continuous discovery -- what every source offers, found again on every run

SecurityInsight does not decide once which properties of a source are worth having. On every run it lists what each source offered, and once a week it asks the sources what they offer; what was not there before is shown in the web app, where an Admin puts it to use in one step.

**One mechanism, a provider list** (`engine/data-model/SI-SourceDiscovery.ps1`).

| Kind | Sources | How | Extra requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| the records | every source SecurityInsight reads: Defender for Endpoint, Entra ID, Azure (per resource type), Exposure Graph, Intune, Defender for Cloud, the public IP scan, Defender for Identity, Active Directory | the collectors hand every object they read to the record capture; when the records are published, the property names of every part are counted | none |
| what the source says it offers | Microsoft Graph (user, device, service principal, application, risky user, risky service principal, Intune managed device) | Graph's published model, read forward-only | one anonymous request a week |
| | Defender advanced hunting | the column list of the tables SecurityInsight reads | one query per table a week |
| | Exposure Graph | the node types SecurityInsight does not record yet | the weekly sweep's own queries |
| | Defender for Cloud | a sample of assessments and of sub-assessments | two Resource Graph queries a week |
| | ServiceNow | the dictionary of the tables the CMDB import reads | one request per table, at most once in six days |

**How a property is named.** As the Full details export names it: a top-level value is `key`; a top-level object gives one property per child, `key.child`; anything deeper is the child's own value. A list of objects also gives `key[*].child` -- the form a mapping reads. Wrappers a source puts around its properties are walked through. The tenant's own keys (tags, extension attributes) are listed, not opened.

**What is kept.** Two small tables in the database: one row per source, record type, Azure resource type, record part and property -- first seen, last seen, how many records carried a value in the newest run, a sample value, the value type, the SI fields that already read it, the full-details source it is a column of, and whether SecurityInsight reads it or the source only offers it; and one row per source / record type / part with its first run, its newest run and, when the source could not be asked, why. The first run of a source / record type / part is its **starting point**: nothing of it is new. Everything first seen later is new context. A source that could not be asked is recorded as "not read" with the reason -- never as "nothing new", and what was listed before stays.

**Cost.** The record pass makes no request: it walks objects the run read anyway, once, when they are published. Every object of a part is walked until the part was seen 2,000 times in one pass; from there one in ten is walked and counts for ten, so a very large collection costs little more than a small one (its counts are then close estimates). Discovery never fails a run: a problem is said once and the run goes on.

**Collectors read the whole record where the volume allows.** A property a source adds can only arrive without a code change when the read does not name its properties. Read whole: the Defender device row, Defender machines, Intune managed devices, Azure resources, Exposure Graph nodes, the public IP scan answer, application registrations, the Identity Protection risk objects, and -- when full asset details are collected -- the Entra device. A read that keeps a property list says why, next to it: Microsoft Graph returns only a default set of a user without a list; a service principal's custom security attributes are returned only when named and Microsoft's own service principals are very large; a join or look-up read needs two or three values; 30 days of risk detections are summarised per user; a ServiceNow reference needs its name asked for by name. What a source offers beyond a kept list is shown as "offered, not read".

**The page: Configuration > New context available.** Per source, the properties first seen this week (or in 30 days, since the starting point, or everything known): the property as a mapping reads it, its record type, first seen, a sample value, "n of m records", and where it is already used. The page reads the prepared rows only -- it never walks a document. An Admin can, in one step each:

- **add the column to a default layout** -- of every view of CIs, or of one view. The column joins the layout the view opens with (the shipped one, or the tenant default) for everyone without a layout of their own; a person's own layout is not changed. The list is kept with the column layouts.
- **map the property to an SI field** -- the mapping row that already fills the field gets the property added as its last source (what it reads today keeps winning); a field the source did not fill yet gets a new row. The change is staged and written only at Review & commit; the next run of that source fills the field, which is then a column of every view and can be used by rules and risk factors.

**Permissions.** Discovery reads only. When a read is refused, or a property is known to need a read permission of its own, the page lists it as a proposal: for a permission of SecurityInsight's own permission set, the two-line command an administrator runs (download the script, run it with the install's names); any other permission is named and not requested.

### Weekly context discovery for Risk Analysis -- the chain mapped up, as proposals (#689)

The collection side finds what every source offers (above). Once a week, Risk Analysis walks the rest of the chain --
**source column -> provider mapping -> generic `si_*` field -> output map -> report rows** -- and saves what it could carry
next as PROPOSALS (`engine/data-model/SI-ContextDiscovery.ps1`):

| Kind | Found when | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| `MAP` | a property the records carried (`sidata.SourceProperty`, records > 0) that no SI field reads, and a catalog field has its name | one mapping row in that provider's mapping |
| `NEW` | the same, and no catalog field has its name | a new `si_*` field, for the owner's one list |
| `CARRY` | a catalog field FILLED on the CIs (fill rate > 0, read from the CI documents) that no output map carries (Excel sheets, ServiceNow CI / vulnerable item, the SQL hand-off) | a new column of the Detailed findings map, its name checked free |
| `ROUTE` | an Exposure Graph edge label the graph holds that no report reads | a candidate route for a new attack-path report |

**Names never change.** Every proposal is an addition; one that would touch an existing output column name or redefine an
existing field is refused (`Test-SIContextProposalAdditive`). A candidate with no valid data is not proposed. A part that
cannot be read this week (the CI fill rates, the source properties, the graph) is not evaluated, so its earlier proposals
are not marked gone.

**When and where.** At the end of every Risk Analysis Detailed run, at most once in six days (the last row of
`sidata.ContextDiscoveryRun`) -- every install has that job, so a new and an existing install get it with the code and
nothing is created by setup or the update; the weekly schema sweep runs the same step where that job is installed. The
proposals are in `sidata.ContextProposal` (kind, subject, target, why, fill rate, evidence, first / last seen, still seen;
`Decision` is the owner's -- the engine never writes it), and the run's log says how many of each kind and how many are new.
Read only; it never fails a run.

### Defender findings on the record -- summarised per device and per resource

The findings from Defender (vulnerabilities, security settings) and from Defender for Cloud (assessments) arrive through Risk Analysis, one finding per device and CVE. The device and resource RECORDS carry a summary of the same data, so the context is on the CI itself -- in every view, without opening a finding:

- **per device** (one advanced hunting query per batch of devices): how many vulnerabilities, per severity, how many with a known exploit, the highest CVSS, how many software products are affected, the newest and oldest publication date, and the top ones as id and name ("CVE -- software (severity, CVSS, exploit available)"); how many security settings were assessed, how many the device does not meet, their categories and the top ones as id and name.
- **per Azure resource** (one Resource Graph query): how many assessments, how many unhealthy and per severity, the oldest first evaluation and the newest status change, and the top ones as id and name.

Everything is summarised inside the query -- there is never one record per CVE row. The top items are collected per severity, not by row order. A device or resource the source has no row for gets no summary: unknown is never written as "none" or "healthy". A tenant whose table holds no row at all says "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)" -- an empty table does not prove a missing licence, so none is claimed. No report and no score is changed.

## Delivery limits — what the run will trim, and how it tells you

> Added v2.2.441. Three places bound how much data leaves a run. **None of them is silent any more**:
> every one states what it dropped, because a limit an operator cannot see is indistinguishable from
> "that was all the data there was".

**The row path itself is uncapped.** No shipped report query limits rows (the only `take` statements
are `take 0` / `take 1` existence probes); `AssetLimit` defaults to `0 = no limit` and prints as such
in the config snapshot; whole-report dedup is disabled; and paged REST never discards pages it has
already collected. The per-row dedup that *does* drop rows only ever removes rows indistinguishable
across every column in its key, and it reports the count it removed.

| limit | default | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Excel worksheet rows** | 1,000,000 (`$global:SI_ExcelMaxDataRows`) | A sheet holds 1,048,576 rows *including* the header. The workbook keeps the **top N by the sort column** — the cut is applied **after** the sort, so the highest-risk rows survive — and the warning names how many were left out. **Nothing is lost from the run:** the `.json` sibling and the Log Analytics ingest still carry every row. |
| **Mail attachment** | **24 MB of message** (`$global:SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB`) | Measured **base64-encoded**, which is how relays measure it: attachments inflate ~37%, so 24 MB of budget admits a workbook of roughly **17 MB on disk**, and an on-disk check would pass while the send still failed. Over budget the report is sent **without the attachment** and the body gives the file's location, so the summary always arrives. 🔑 **The default is sized for the RELAY, not for the report.** Most relays cap a message at 25 MB (Exchange Online's default; on-premises is often lower) and that cap covers the whole message — body and headers as well as the attachment — so 24 leaves about 1.7 MB of headroom. ⚠️ **Lowering it is always safe; raising it is only safe against a known relay limit**, because a budget above what the relay accepts means the relay rejects the *entire* message and the recipient loses the summary too — strictly worse than dropping the attachment alone. Raised to 34 in v2.2.458 and corrected to 24 in v2.2.459 for exactly that reason. Documented in the sample config (section 9) and the README so it is discoverable rather than reference-only |
| **MoreDetails cell** | 25 links, 4,000 chars | Both now state the remainder — `[+87 more link(s) not shown -- 112 total]` and `... [truncated at 4000 chars]`. A field larger than 4,096 chars is skipped during URL harvesting and the run reports how many fields it passed over. |

The schema-audit and tag-activity rows sent to Log Analytics are NOT capped: every row is ingested. The
old `SI_SchemaAuditRowCap` / `SI_TagActivityRowCap` settings limit nothing; a run that still has one set
says so once. The AI prompt's per-finding asset/link slices carry `[+N more of M total]` so the model is
never handed a partial list as if it were complete.

Row size on ingest is SecurityInsight's own: batches are sized from their measured payload under the Log Ingestion
API's 1 MB limit, and a single row larger than the limit is refused, never truncated.

## Operations & runbook

> How to **monitor**, **diagnose**, and **right-size** SecurityInsight asset-profiling runs after they are deployed. This is for the operator after first run.

### Per-shard heartbeat — `SI_RunHealth_CL`

Every replica of `Invoke-SIEngineRun.ps1` writes two rows to `SI_RunHealth_CL` in the customer's Log Analytics workspace:

| Phase   | Emitted at        | Carries                                                           |
|---------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Start` | top of run        | `RunId`, `Engine`, `ShardIndex`, `ShardCount`, `Computer`         |
| `End`   | `finally` block   | adds `AssetCount`, `PeakWorkingSetMB`, `DurationSec`, `ExitReason`, `ErrorMessage` |

Both rows carry the shared `CollectionTime` so they join cleanly with the engine's own output rows.

**Critical property:** a `Start` row with no matching `End` row is the signal that the replica was *killed* before it could finish (OOM, container kill, infrastructure timeout). This is the only way to detect those — Container Apps Job execution status alone won't tell you which shard died, only that *something* did.

The heartbeat is best-effort: if the LA ingest itself fails, the warning is swallowed (verbose only). Telemetry never kills the run it's measuring.

The table + DCR (`dcr-si-run-health`) auto-provision on first ingest through SecurityInsight's REST ingest client. No bootstrap step required.

**Table schema** (`SI_RunHealth_CL`):

```
├── TimeGenerated         (ingest time, automatic)
├── CollectionTime        (run-level shared timestamp; same for both rows of one shard)
├── RunId                 (e.g. 20260426T144109Z-identity-7d8c743d)
├── Engine                (endpoint | identity | azure | schema-discovery)
├── ShardIndex            (0-based replica index)
├── ShardCount            (total shards planned for this run)
├── Phase                 (Start | End)
├── AssetCount            (-1 on Start row; populated on End from Discover stage)
├── PeakWorkingSetMB      (process peak working set at End)
├── DurationSec           (UtcNow - StartedAt at End)
├── ExitReason            ('' on Start; 'success' or 'error' on End)
├── ErrorMessage          (exception text if ExitReason == 'error')
└── Computer              (replica hostname)
```

Later additive columns: `Execution` (the container job execution), `SolutionVersion` / `Build` (the build that wrote the
row) and `PermissionGaps` (below).

The heartbeat helper lives at `v2.2/engine/asset-profiling/shared/Send-SIRunHealthRow.ps1` and is invoked from `Invoke-SIEngineRun.ps1` (Start before stages, End in `finally`).

#### Each engine checks its own permissions — `PermissionGaps`

At run start every container engine checks the permissions of the identity it runs as (`engine/_shared/SI-PermissionCheck.ps1`),
against ONE list, `config/permissions.locked.json` (which identity each engine runs as, and what that identity must hold):

| Area | How it is checked | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Application permissions (Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Threat Protection, Defender for Endpoint) | the `roles` claim of the engine's own access token for that API | the token the engine needs anyway |
| Azure | one read of the caller's own permissions (`Microsoft.Authorization/permissions`) at the collection scope: Reader (`*/read`); asset tagging also Tag Contributor, only while it may write | one call |
| Pro database (SecurityInsight Pro only) | the settings layer's sign-in: refused = no database user; after sign-in `IS_ROLEMEMBER` for the roles | one query |

The check never stops a run: what cannot be read is *not checked*, never *missing*, and a permission the run actually
needs still fails the run exactly as before. The run-health END record carries the result in `PermissionGaps` (JSON:
the engine, the identity's client id, each gap with how to fix it, and what could not be checked; empty when the run
did no check). The Community edition has no database area. In the Pro web app, **Get Started > Permissions** reads the
newest check of each engine from the last 7 days: done when nothing is missing; it lists the gaps per identity with the
fix.

### Status reports to Invardia (telemetry)

At the same END moment, the run-health sender also hands the run to the telemetry sender (`engine/_shared/SI-TelemetrySend.ps1`),
which reports it to Invardia through the framework's uplink client. SecurityInsight carries its own, byte-identical copy of that
client (`engine/_shared/AitUplink.ps1`), because containers and Pro installs have no `sync/` folder.

| Report | When | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `heartbeat` | the first engine run of each UTC day | product, edition (community / pro / trial), version, hosting (container / vm / arc), the *kind* of sign-in identity (mi-container / mi-vm / mi-arc / spn-certificate / spn-secret), licence state (valid / grace / expired / none) |
| `run` | every engine run, at the run-health END | the job id (below), outcome (`success` → ok, `success-partial` → warning, `error` / `settings-error` → failed), duration, the stage that failed, an **error class** and a count (assets, identities or findings) |

**Job ids:** `si-ptc`, `si-endpoint`, `si-identity`, `si-azure`, `si-publicip`, `si-schema-discovery`, `si-ra-summary`,
`si-ra-detailed` (the engines that record run health today), plus `si-trend`, `si-asset-tagging`, `si-correlation`,
`si-asset-properties`, `si-cmdb`, `si-vuln-closeloop`, `si-datasync`, `si-updater`, `si-web` (reserved). A sharded run is one
report: a successful shard other than the first is not reported separately; a failed one is.

**The heartbeat every half hour (its own job, outside the pipeline).** A run report arrives only when an engine run ENDS, so a long
step (a several-hour Detailed report or correlation) used to leave Invardia without a word for hours -- the install looked
stopped. Every Pro install therefore has a small job of its own, `caj-si-heartbeat` (`engine/heartbeat/Invoke-SIHeartbeat.ps1`,
`engine/_shared/SI-HeartbeatJob.ps1`), on its own timer every 15 minutes (`7,22,37,52 * * * *`, `SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleHeartbeat`). It is never
a step of the pipeline (a Schedule trigger in both orchestration modes), so it reports whether or not a pipeline runs and
whether or not the pipeline's runner is alive; the runner itself is unchanged. Size: the floor every job gets (2 CPU /
4 GiB) with its own 30-minute run limit (a hung tick never blocks the next hour; the update's floor step leaves that limit).
A new install gets it from setup (infrastructure, whatever the engine list); an existing install from its next update (the
missing-jobs step: built from a Pro job of the install -- same image, identity and settings -- on its own hourly timer, read
back, an existing job never touched). Each tick sends ONE **identified** heartbeat -- the same record as the end-of-run
heartbeat -- once per HALF hour (:00-:29 and :30-:59 UTC): it claims the half hour in the Pro database first, so the second
tick of the same half hour (or a manual start) sends nothing. A claim left by the earlier hourly version counts as that
hour's first half hour, and the update moves a job still on the old hourly timer to the 15-minute one. An
anonymous install sends nothing from it (its one heartbeat a day stays with its engine runs). One attempt, the 5-second
timeout; a failure is said once and the job still ends well.

Two optional fields are built and tested but go out only where a switch allows them, because the receiver refuses a record
with a field it does not know: `runProgress` (`SI_Uplink_SendRunProgress`) -- `{ state: running | idle | stalled, runId,
stage, step, stepSinceUtc, runSinceUtc }` from the pipeline's run record -- and `Collections` (`SI_Uplink_SendCollections`) --
at most 12 entries `{ kind, state, lastCompleteUtc, lastAttemptUtc, expected, collected, note }`, kind one of `identity`,
`endpoint`, `azure`, `publicip`, `riskAnalysisSummary`, `riskAnalysisDetailed`, `correlation`, `ciBuild`, state one of
`complete`, `partial`, `running`, `failed`, `never`, times ISO-8601 UTC or null, counts whole numbers or null, the note one
plain line of at most 300 characters or null; every field present (null rather than absent). The state comes from what
SecurityInsight already records (each source's last good and last attempted collection and whether a feed of it was held,
the Risk Analysis collections with their partial marks and per-report expected / stored rows, the CI build's own state, and
the step the pipeline runs now) through a few index reads -- never the findings table; `expected` for identities is the
tenant's user count (one Microsoft Graph count). Each switch: `on`, `off`, a ring list (`0` / `0,1`: on for those rings), or
`auto` (the default: on only for the rings confirmed for the field -- none yet). A heartbeat the receiver does not take with
them is sent again once without them, so a heartbeat is never lost to a new field.

**The pipeline's progress and estimated end (the `Pipeline` field, every half hour).** So that the back office and the
customer portal can show where every install's pipeline is and when it should be done (refreshed every half hour, not in
real time), the `Pipeline` field of the heartbeat -- `{ runId, state, startedUtc, step, stepSinceUtc, lastEndedUtc,
nextStartUtc }` -- carries seven more keys, behind their own switch `SI_Uplink_SendPipelineEta` (on by default on every
ring; `off` or a ring list as for every other field):

| key | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `stepsDone` | whole number or null | the run's steps that ended (succeeded, failed or skipped) |
| `stepsTotal` | whole number or null | the run's steps that are not switched off |
| `runningSteps` | array, at most 12 | each step running now: `{ step, sinceUtc, prevMin, endUtc, estimate }` |
| `remainingSteps` | array, at most 30 | each step still waiting: `{ step, group, estimateMin }` |
| `estimatedEndUtc` | ISO-8601 UTC or null | when the run should end |
| `estimateConfidence` | `known` / `partial` / `overdue` or null | how sure that end is |
| `queuedRuns` | whole number or null | the pipeline requests waiting after this run |

`step` is the job's short name (`identity`, `risk-analysis-detailed`, ...); `prevMin` and `estimateMin` are whole minutes;
`group` is the step's place in the run. **How the estimate is made:** each step is expected to take as long as its job
took in the newest run that succeeded (a job that only succeeded in a run that failed elsewhere takes that time). The steps
of one group start together and the next group starts when all of them ended, so a group takes as long as its LONGEST step,
and the groups follow one another. A running step ends at its earlier duration (`estimate: known`, `endUtc` its end); a step
running past its earlier duration is `overdue` and gets no time at all (never a time in the past -- it counts as ending
now); a step that has never succeeded before is `unknown`. `estimatedEndUtc` is now plus what the remaining groups take,
or null when nothing known lies ahead. `estimateConfidence` is `known` when every remaining step has an earlier duration,
`partial` when one has none, and `overdue` when a step runs late -- for `partial` and `overdue` the end is AT LEAST that
time. A run that is not running carries only the counts (no steps, no estimate). Everything is read in the same small read
of the settings database as the rest of the field (the newest ten runs and their steps, and a count of the waiting
requests). If the receiver refuses the heartbeat with these keys, it is sent again with `Pipeline` without them, so the
rest of the record is never lost to them; anything that cannot be read or does not pass the agreed shape is left out with
one plain line and the heartbeat still goes.
**Error classes** (one per failed run, from the failure text — first match wins): `settings-error`, `licence-invalid`,
`mi-unavailable`, `sql-login`, `config-missing`, `ingest-short-count`, `table-missing`, `platform-timeout`, `platform-5xx`,
`kql-query-defect`, `throttled`, `ingest-4xx`, `graph-401`, `graph-403`, `defender-403`, `arm-403`, `kv-403`, `storage-403`,
`ai-error`, `unknown`. A cancelled or service-side query failure is a platform class, never `kql-query-defect`.

**Two modes.**
- **Community — anonymous.** Sent with the public community code. The report carries a random install id (created once, kept in
  `%ProgramData%\SecurityInsight\telemetry` — or `~/.securityinsight/telemetry`, or `SI_TELEMETRY_STATE_DIR`) and **no tenant
  id, no host name and no error text** — those fields are never put in the record — and counts only as ranges
  (`0`, `1-100`, `100-1k`, `1k-10k`, `10k-100k`, `100k+`).
- **Pro / trial — identified.** Sent with the install's key (the Key Vault secret `SI-Invardia-InstallKey`, the same key the
  updater uses), read as the engine's own identity. The tenant and host are included and the error text is shortened to 8 KB
  with secrets removed (tokens, `Bearer`, `client_secret=` / passwords / keys, SAS signatures, PEM blocks). A Pro install with
  no key yet reports anonymously. A Community install never reads a Key Vault for telemetry.

**Never fails or slows a run.** One attempt per report with a 5-second timeout and no retry. The first answer that is not
accepted stops telemetry for the rest of the process — nothing is queued or repeated — and is said once as a warning.

**Off:** `$global:SI_Telemetry_Enabled = $false` (or the environment variable `SI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false`). Then nothing is
built, no file is written and nothing is sent. `SI_Telemetry_Endpoint` changes the address (https only; default
`https://invardia.com/api/uplink/v1/report`).

**Report causes, capabilities and licences (#709, the framework's UPLINK-CAUSES contract; `engine/_shared/SI-UplinkCauses.ps1`).**
- **`Reports` on the Risk Analysis run report** -- every report that failed, is not complete, did not apply in this tenant or
  returned more rows than the source counted; at most 20, failures first, the most severe first. Each item names the report
  (an id such as `identity-spn-ownermismatch`, never a title), a **stable error code** and a **cause class** (`no-data-source`,
  `missing-column`, `query-defect`, `platform-timeout`, `too-large`, `count-more`, `count-less`, `settings-unreachable`,
  `permission`, `missing-licence`), the missing table / column, what the catalogue says to do (`none`, `fixed-in` with the
  version, `support`, `customer`) and the numbers: run time, rows, what the source counted, the slices, the 429 / 502 / 504
  answers, the query fingerprint and whether it changed since the report's last complete run, that run's rows, the region and
  the start time. A number that is not known is empty, never guessed. An identified report also carries **Detail**: the
  engine's first error line with secrets removed, at most 500 characters; an anonymous report never carries text.
- **The error catalogue** is `data-model/errors.locked.json`: per code a title, the customer's sentence, who acts, the action,
  the version that fixes it and the steps. A cause that has no code of its own gets the generic code of its class
  (`si-ra-0901`..`si-ra-0910`); a failure nothing recognises is `si-ra-0900`. Each code has a page:
  `https://invardia.com/docs/si/errors/<code>/`. The Risk Analysis mail of a run that is not complete names the codes of
  its failures, each linked to its page.
