- **The daily status report** carries `Capabilities` (Defender XDR, Defender Vulnerability Management, Defender for Identity,
  Intune, Entra ID P2, a CMDB, Sentinel, the Sentinel data lake -- each only when it was measured), `CiColumns` (the optional
  CMDB / ServiceNow columns of the CI table, at most 40) and, identified only, `Licences` (the tenant's subscription SKUs, read
  from Microsoft Graph with the permission the collection identity already has; without it the licences are left out). One
  workspace query, one advanced hunting query and one Graph read, once per process when the status report is due.
- **Never at the cost of the report.** Anything here that fails is left out; a report that Invardia does not take with these
  fields is sent again once without them; the report is kept under the uplink's size limit by shortening, then leaving out,
  the details and the least severe items.

### Guard events — a tripped safety check mails a person and tells Invardia (#277)

A **guard** is any place where SecurityInsight holds, refuses or stops a step to protect data (the vulnerability connector's
close ceiling, an incomplete collection, a CMDB update that would retire most CIs, a refused schema, ...). Before #277 a guard
wrote a log line and nothing reached a person. Now every guard makes ONE call, `Send-SIGuardEvent`
(`engine/_shared/SI-Guard.ps1`, PS 5.1 + 7, free code: Community mails its guards too), which never throws and never fails the
job that tripped it.

**The closed list** is `config/guard-catalog.locked.json` (read by PowerShell and by the web app, linked by the csproj): a stable
dotted id per guard (`area.object.what`), its area, its telemetry job, what it **protects** and the **action** a person should
take — both in plain words, they are the mail. Outcomes: `halted` / `refused` (severity **critical**: the step did not
happen), `held` / `skipped` (severity **warning**), and SI's own `warning` (nothing held — a licence in grace, a report that lost
findings; sent to Invardia as `held` with severity warning, the receiver has no `warning`).

**Which guards are on by default (#577 the guard relief, owner 2026-10-11).** Only TWO brakes -- where damage does not heal
by itself: (a) the **CI retire brake** -- `cmdb.sql.collapse` and `cmdb.handoff.mass-change` hold a run / batch when far more
CIs would vanish than allowed, and a CI retires only after its asset has been unseen `SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays` (default 7; a
floor under every grace period, run count and early retirement, in `New-SICmdbSqlPlan` and `Resolve-SIAssetRetireSettings`);
(b) the **duplicates brake** -- `vuln.connector.target-incomplete` (a target read only in part = that connector writes nothing
that run). Every other guard carries `"defaultOff": true` in the catalog (the web app's `GuardSwitches.DefaultOff` is the same
list): no hold, no event, no mail -- the step goes on; vulnerabilities heal on the next collection, and database, update and
licence states are telemetry, not guards. A customer switches any check on again in Settings > Guards
(`SI_Guard_<Token>_Enabled = true`); its mail then follows the check unless `SI_Guard_<Token>_Mail` is off. A guard off by
the catalog default logs ONE INFO line per process; WARN is kept for a brake (or the master) an install switched off.
**Off is never the integrity stop itself:** where the catalog's `whenOff` says "the step itself still stops" (a database change
that could remove data -- `schema.gate.refused` --, a failed database update -- `update.schema.failed` --, an incomplete
snapshot, a collection that could not be read in full, ...), the refusal is the code's own and happens whatever the switch;
the switch only stops the event and its mail.

**One event, five places** (each failure-safe, in this order):

| | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Mail | to `SI_GuardMail_To`, else `MailTo`, else the Pro SuperAdmins whose sign-in name is a mail address; through the Risk Analysis relay settings and transports (`RA-Mail.ps1`). ON by default (`SI_GuardMail_Enabled`). Subject `SecurityInsight: <what was protected> -- action needed`; body: what happened, the numbers against the limit, what was held ("nothing was lost"), what to do, the link (`SIWeb_PublicBaseUrl` + `/Admin/Guards`). Priority High for critical. | the relay |
| Telemetry | the GUARD-1 record below, posted with the framework client's `Send-AitUplink`; follows `SI_Telemetry_Enabled` (ON by default) and halts with the run reports on the first non-ok answer. | Invardia |
| Guards view | one `cfg.GuardEvent` row (Pro database): guard, area, measured text + values JSON, outcome, severity, held, trips, mail and telemetry state. | Operations > Guards (safety checks) |
| Run health | one `SI_RunHealth_CL` row with **Phase `Guard`**, ExitReason `guard-<outcome>`, AssetCount = held, ErrorMessage `<guard id>: <detail> \| <measured>`. Every run-health reader filters `Phase == "End"`, so a guard row never counts as a run. | Log Analytics |
| Audit | AUDIT-1 event `guard.event.trip` (outcome refused for critical, held for warning). The action is three-part (`domain.object.verb`, the trail's rule), so not `guard.trip`. | `cfg.AuditEvent` |

**Once per run, once a day.** A guard (+ subject: which connector / report / job) reports ONCE per run (`$global:SI_GuardRunId`;
a second call in the same run is `duplicate`). Its episode lives in `cfg.GuardState` (Pro database) or, without one,
`%ProgramData%\SecurityInsight\guards\guard-state.json` (`SI_GUARD_STATE_DIR`; a container without a disk starts fresh each run).
A trip within 24 h of the last one continues the episode (trip count + 1, first seen kept) and mails only when the last mail is
24 h old — that mail says "still tripping, N times since <first seen>"; 24 h without a trip starts a new episode. A mail that did
not go out is tried again on the next trip. Telemetry is sent on every trip (the receiver de-duplicates per environment + guard
and says "still tripping" at most hourly).

**Guards heal themselves, say which release, and can be accepted everywhere.** A guard that held or warned is an open
episode. Where a step checks a guard it names the check (`Invoke-SIGuardCalls -Checked ... -Complete`); a checked guard that
did not trip, in a complete run, with its measured values back within their limits, CLEARS its episode once -- one
`cfg.GuardEvent` row Outcome `cleared` ("Back to normal in run <id> on version <v>."), run health `guard-cleared`, audit
`guard.event.clear`, no mail. Every holding or warning data check is wired: the source asset count, the three Risk Analysis
output checks, the data sync (collection held -- only once nothing of it is held any more --, not read in full, rows without
their key, asset kinds the filter cannot show), the vulnerability connector (close limit -- only once no held close set is
left --, empty, collapse, run / results incomplete, scope changed, target not read in full, connector not set up), the SQL
CMDB (collapse, empty, incomplete, no correlation map, changed by another run), the CMDB hand-off, the asset metadata, and
Log Analytics rows not accepted (cleared by the first full post of that table in a process). A held set is never applied by
a heal: the newer complete run decides again and supersedes it. Every trip carries the version it happened on and the one
before ("the first run after the update to <v>" or "has run on <v> since <time>"). The owner accepts a guard per install
through the procedure `cfg.GuardAcceptSet` (plan first, the plan's hash to accept, held sets released only on request and
only through the release path's checks, each acceptance in `cfg.GuardAccept` and on the audit trail); the support script runs
it at many installs in one action -- several guards at once (one set names the checks a code change to the CIs trips: the
hand-off, the CMDB table, the asset metadata, the source asset count) -- with one line and one record entry per install and
guard.

**The GUARD-1 record** (Invardia's receiver, built to its contract 2026-10-04; `POST /api/uplink/v1/report`, the install key or
the community code as today):

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `Schema` 2, `Kind` `guard`, `Product`, `Version`, `Ring` (when known), `Edition`, `Hosting`, `RuntimeIdentity`, `LicenceState`, `Job` | as the run record |
| `GuardId` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,99}$` (every catalog id fits) |
| `GuardOutcome` | `halted` \| `refused` \| `held` \| `skipped` |
| `Severity` | `critical` \| `warning` |
| `Area` | the catalog's area |
| `Measured`, `Thresholds` | objects of at most 10 NUMBERS each, camelCase keys `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,30}$` (e.g. `closeShare 25.9 / 10`, `closeCount 3767 / 50`, `openRecords 14519`) |
| `HeldCount`, `TripCount`, `FirstSeenUtc`, `LastSeenUtc` | integers / ISO 8601 UTC |
| anonymous only | `InstallId` (the random install id) — nothing else: no tenant, host, subject, detail, action text or link |
| identified only | `ClaimedTenantId`, `Host`, `ActionText` (the catalog's action, redacted, at most 500 characters), `Link` (https only) |

The framework's own builder (`New-AitUplinkReport`) knows `heartbeat | run | install` only, so SI builds this record itself
(`New-SIGuardTelemetryRecord`) and posts it with the unchanged `Send-AitUplink`. Invardia opens / updates ONE support ticket per
Pro environment + guard (P1 critical, P2 warning, auto-resolved after 7 quiet days); for Community it sends a release-health mail
when 3 or more installs trip the same guard on the same version within 24 h.

**Where each guard trips** (adapters in `SI-Guard.ps1` turn an area's result into its events, so the mapping is provable offline):

| Guard id | Outcome | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `vuln.connector.close-ceiling` / `empty-snapshot` / `collapse` / `scope-changed` / `run-incomplete` | halted | `New-SIVulnSyncPlan` sets `HaltGuard` / `HaltValues` / `HaltHeld`; `Invoke-SIVulnLoop.ps1` per connector (SQL, REST, ServiceNow) |
| `vuln.connector.snapshot-incomplete` | held | results not known complete, closes held |
| `vuln.connector.target-incomplete` | refused | a partial read of the target (ServiceNow) |
| `vuln.connector.refused` | refused | a connector that is not set up completely |
| `cmdb.sql.snapshot-incomplete` / `collapse` (below 50 %) / `empty-snapshot` / `no-correlation-map` | refused | `Invoke-SICmdbSql.ps1` |
| `cmdb.sql.stale` | skipped | another run changed the CI table meanwhile |
| `cmdb.servicenow.unreachable` / `create-gate` / `service-model` | halted / held / refused | `Invoke-SICmdb.ps1` |
| `datasync.collection.held` / `short-read` | held / refused | `Invoke-SIDataSync.ps1` |
| `audit.retention.refused` | refused | the data sync's retention step (below 13 months / not a number) |
| `ra.output.row-drop` (LARGE-DROP, WENT-TO-ZERO, MISSING) / `ra.output.column-emptied` (COLUMN-EMPTIED, COLUMN-VANISHED) | warning | `Invoke-RiskAnalysis.ps1` — ONE event per run each, listing every report |
| `ingest.rows.short-count` | refused | `Send-SILogDataRest` (the REST ingest path) when Log Analytics accepted fewer rows than sent (then it throws, as before) |
| `schema.gate.refused` | refused | `setup/Initialize-SIDataSql.ps1`, the guided Pro install |
| `licence.state.invalid` / `licence.state.grace` | refused / warning | `Assert-SIFeatureOrSkip` (once per feature per process; no licence at all = Community, not a trip) |
| `flow.run.catch-up` / `flow.step.skipped` / `flow.step.interrupted` | held / skipped / held | `Invoke-SIJobFlowRun.ps1` — not the 5-minute wake-ups while a flow runs (normal), and not a start that was late only because the previous run was still going and that was made as soon as it ended (normal on a large install; the run's note says it). `flow.run.catch-up` is a scheduled start MISSED for any other reason |
| `job.execution.previous-running` | skipped | the container execution guard (`Start-SIInContainer.ps1`) |
| `exemption.bulk.refused` | refused | the web app (`FindingSelectionResolver`): no narrowing filter, or more findings than the limit |

**The web app's own guard** writes the SAME row shape from C# (`Guards/GuardEvents.cs`, `GuardEventWriter`; the INSERT is the
PowerShell statement word for word, a test compares them) with mail and telemetry `pending`, and starts one execution of the
mail job (as the exemption mails do). The mail job (`Invoke-SICloseLoopMail.ps1`) runs `Invoke-SIGuardOutbox`: mails and
reports every pending row with the same de-duplication and marks it. Web identity grant: `INSERT` on `cfg.GuardEvent`.

**Operations > Guards (safety checks)** (`/Admin/Guards`, readers and up): a server-side grid (BRAND-2.7, the shared `GridSql`) over
`cfg.GuardEvent` — time window, search, a filter per column (guard, area, measured text, outcome, severity, held, times, mail,
reported, where), sort, paging; *What to do* per row. Run health links to it. It opens newest first (*When* descending).

**Operations > Jobs > Run health** (`/Admin/RunHealth`): every `SI_RunHealth_CL` record of the window, newest record first. A
run's Start and End records carry the same `CollectionTime` (the run's start), so the page orders by when each record was
written (`TimeGenerated`) and says a run by its End when it has one. *Latest run per engine* groups the records per run
(engine + RunId) and merges an engine's own records with the job flow's step records (`flow:<engine>`): the run whose last
record is newest is the latest (the engine's own record on a tie); *Recorded by* says which. The flow's own `flow` record is
its own line; guard records are never a verdict. An engine sends its End record once, from a `finally` around everything
after its Start, so a failure anywhere in the run still leaves an End (`error`).

**Every table opens newest first.** The shared browser table component (`wwwroot/js/app/tables.js`, BRAND-2.7) sorts a
table with a time column -- a date column headed When / Started / Time / Ran / Last run / Recorded -- on that column,
newest first, when the page loads; every header still sorts and the filter row is unchanged. A page keeps its own order
with `data-default-sort="off"` (the flow's steps on Admin > Jobs) or names the column and direction
(`data-default-sort="<header>"`, `data-default-dir="asc"`). The server-side grids of Guards and the audit trail default to
*When* descending.

### Stricter safety checks for 24 hours after a release that changed engine code (CR4, #654)
**Why.** A defect in new engine code is most likely to do mass damage in the first day after it is installed. For that day
every numbered safety check is stricter, so a broken release is stopped earlier -- and a release that changed only templates,
texts or the web app changes nothing.

**The trigger -- the engine fingerprint.** The updater computes a SHA-256 fingerprint over the engine folders of the release it
has just installed (`engine/`, `launcher/`, `risk-analysis-detection/` -- the same folders the publish call judges
`engineChanged` by): one line pair per file, `<path relative to the solution, '/' separators>\n<sha256 of the file's
bytes>\n`, the list sorted ordinally, and SHA-256 over that text (`engine/_shared/SI-GuardStrict.ps1`,
`Get-SIEngineFingerprint`). It is recorded after a successful roll in the Pro database (`cfg.InstallState`
`EngineFingerprint`: hash, version, since, strictFrom, strictVersion). A fingerprint that differs from the recorded one
starts the stricter period (strictFrom = now, the release); the same fingerprint keeps the record; the **first** fingerprint
an install records starts nothing -- an install that never recorded one behaves exactly as before.

**The rule.** While the period lasts every numbered damage brake is halved from the value the customer **configured**:
`effective = max(1, floor(configured x 0.5))`, never above the configured value (a limit of 1 stays 1; 0 = "no limit" stays
0), never below a limit a SuperAdmin approved for one run. One helper (`Resolve-SIGuardLimit`) at each brake:

| Safety check | Limit | Normally -> strict (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `vuln.connector.close-ceiling` | close at most % of the open vulnerability records (`SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent`) and, when set, at most N records (`SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute`) | 10 % -> 5 %; 0 (no absolute limit) stays 0 |
| `asset.properties.collection-change` | change at most % of a source's records (`SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent`) | 10 % -> 5 % |
| `cmdb.handoff.mass-change` | the CMDB hand-off connector's change limit (default the setting above) | 10 % -> 5 % |
| `collection.source.asset-drop` | asset drop of a source (`SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent`) | 30 % -> 15 % |
| `exemption.bulk.refused` | most findings in one bulk exemption request (`SIWeb_Exemption_BulkMax`, the web app) | 500 -> 250 |

Floors (the share of the records that must still be seen: `SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor`, the CMDB SQL table's collapse floor)
are not halved -- halving a floor would loosen it. Data-quality warnings and warn-only checks have no damage limit and are
unchanged.

**Duration and early end.** 24 hours from the time the updater recorded the changed fingerprint. A SuperAdmin may end it early
with a reason on Operations > Guards (audit action `guard.strict.end-early`); the web app writes only the one row
`cfg.InstallState` `GuardStrictEnd` through `cfg.GuardStrictEndSet`, and the end names the period it ends (fingerprint and
start), so it never ends a later one.

**What a person sees.** A strict trip is a normal trip: it holds, refuses and mails exactly as always. Its numbers say
"limit 5 % in the stricter period after a release, normally 10 %", and the mail adds one calm sentence ("This safety check is
in its stricter period after release X until <time>: its limit is halved for 24 hours after a release that changed the engine,
as planned."). Operations > Guards shows the period, the limits "configured -> effective while strict" and, to a SuperAdmin,
*End the stricter period now*; the header shows **Guard mode** to SuperAdmins while it is strict (or was ended early).

**To Invardia.** A strict trip's guard report carries `Strict`, `ConfiguredLimit` and `EffectiveLimit` (whole numbers), and on
an identified install the guard mode. The identified heartbeat carries `guardMode`: `{ mode ('strict' | 'normal'), until,
startedBy (the release), version (the same), endedEarlyAt, endedBy (a role, never a person) }` -- left out while no
fingerprint is recorded and on an anonymous heartbeat. Anything that cannot be read means normal: the limits as configured.

### Release anomaly control -- waves, release mode, components Testing / Stable, the 409 notApproved (CR3, #657)

Framework DOCS/REQUIREMENTS.md 12.11e (approved by the owner 2026-10-14). The code: `engine/_shared/SI-ReleaseControl.ps1`
(pure decisions + the SQL), `config/release-scopes.locked.json` (the component map), with its callers below.

**The wave.** Invardia may serve a wave member a version already released to a lower ring, early, with no ring move; the
signed manifest then carries `"wave": "<name>"`. The updater keeps it with the applied code (`SI-Update-State` code
`appliedWave` / `lastWave`; the compact row `cfg.InstallState 'UpdateState'` gets `code.wave { name, version, ring }` only
while there is one). The header's UPDATE RING reads **Ring 2 - Pre-release (<name>)** (`HeaderContext.RingOf`), Settings >
Updates says it in a line. **Never moved back:** while the applied code came from a wave, the ring's own manifest (no wave)
with a LOWER sequence is not refused as a replay -- an older version is kept as `current` (the install keeps its version until
the ring reaches it), the same version ends the wave (`appliedWave` cleared, the install back on the ring's sequence), a newer
one is an update; under a HIGHER sequence an older version is not rolled to (`Get-SIUpdaterInvardiaCodeDecision`
`-AppliedWave`). Without a wave every rule is as before (a lower version under a higher sequence stays the vendor's rollback).

**Release mode.** The same trigger as the stricter safety checks: the updater's engine fingerprint changed (`strictFrom`).
For 12 hours from then the install reports every 30 minutes, counts only: the identified heartbeat (users / guests /
devices, `guardMode`, `wave`) with `releaseMode { version, sinceUtc, untilUtc, everyMinutes: 30 }`. The pipeline runner
(`engine/flow/Invoke-SIJobFlowRun.ps1`, wakes every 5 minutes) asks at each wake-up and from its lock heartbeat during a long
run (`Invoke-SIReleaseModeReportTick`, at most once per 4 minutes per process); the half hour is CLAIMED first in one statement
(`cfg.InstallState 'ReleaseModeReport' { since, slot, sentUtc }`, UPDLOCK), so it goes out once. A SuperAdmin ending the
stricter checks early does not end release mode. The daily heartbeat of every engine run carries both fields too
(`wave: null` / `releaseMode: null` when none; left out while nothing is recorded -- an older install sends nothing new).

**The switch (framework 12.22).** `SI_Telemetry_ReleaseControl` (setting) / `SI_TELEMETRY_RELEASECONTROL` (job variable):
`auto` (default) = only the rings in `$script:SIReleaseControl.ConfirmedRings` (ring 0 until Invardia confirmed the stored
result of a ring-0 call; a later release adds 1 and 2), `on`, `off` (exactly the heartbeat as before, no release-mode
reports). A heartbeat refused WITH the fields is sent again once WITHOUT them; when that one is taken the fields are held for
24 hours (`cfg.InstallState 'ReleaseControlHold'`) and one warning is written. Never on an anonymous heartbeat or a run report.

**Components: Testing / Stable.** SecurityInsight's components: the collections per source (`collection.identity`,
`.endpoint`, `.azure`, `.publicip`, `.privilege-tier`, `.asset-properties`), `correlation`, Risk Analysis per report
(`risk-analysis.<ReportName>`, one per report block of `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml`), data out per channel
(`data-out.cmdb`, `.vulnerabilities`, `.mail`, `.sql`, `.outputs`, `.tagging`). The map assigns each engine file to one
component, a group (Risk Analysis: every report), `none` (samples, docs, verification / trend / schema discovery) or core;
a file the map does not know is core. A component's fingerprint covers its own files, its group's and the core files, so a
core change changes every component (PIM's rule). Three uses:
- the publish call's `changedScopes` (`setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -EngineSinceRef <previous release commit>` or
  `-ChangedScopes`): `&changedScopes=id,id` on the upload, `"changedScopes": [ ... ]` on the ring call; `*` = every component
  or more than 30; behind `SI_PUBLISH_CHANGEDSCOPES` (auto = ring-0 calls only);
- the updater, after a successful roll, writes the fingerprints into `cfg.ReleaseScope` (one transaction): a changed
  component gets `ChangedUtc` / `ChangedVersion`, `GoodDays 0` = **Testing**; the FIRST record marks nothing Testing;
- every engine run's END record (`Send-SIRunHealthRow` -> `Invoke-SIReleaseScopeRunEnd`; the engine's own first record
  only) counts for its components (the map's `engines`): a successful run once per UTC day (started after the change), a
  failed run starts the count again while Testing; partial / throttled / skipped change nothing; a Risk Analysis run with an
  incomplete report is not good. 3 good days = **Stable**. Settings > Updates shows "N of M components are testing" with the
  list. The engine role gets SELECT, UPDATE on `cfg.ReleaseScope`; the updater writes the rows.

**The 409.** Invardia refuses a ring 2 / 3 release (or a wave) of a version without the owner's APPROVED: 409 `notApproved`
with a reason. `Get-SIInvardiaNotApproved` recognises it (JSON `error` / `code` / `status` / `title`, or the word in the text)
and both the upload and the ring call say **NOT APPROVED -- ... needs the owner's APPROVED (Invardia's back office: Updates >
the release). Invardia's reason: ...**; a 409 "version exists" keeps its old words.

**Not built here:** answering the release review (Invardia's review-thread route is not defined yet); the Invardia support
agent's spot check and the release view are Invardia's.

### Data health -- SecurityInsight checks its own data every day (CR2, #656)
**SecurityInsight only.** This model is SecurityInsight's own design (owner 2026-10-14: *"it is solely for si"*). Where the
framework's text (`DOCS/REQUIREMENTS.md` §12.11d) speaks of it as a joint or cross-product model, read it as SecurityInsight
only: no other product implements or mirrors it, and nothing here is aligned with another product. The framework section
remains the contract for the record sent to Invardia and the promotion hold Invardia keeps.

**What is checked (read-only, as the engine identity).** Every day, inside the verification job (after the verification
checks, never failing them; its own run-health records, engine `data-health`), `engine/data-health/Invoke-SIDataHealth.ps1`:

| Source (wire id) | Read from the source | Looked up in the newest collection (`sidata.CiRecord`) | Key fields compared | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Entra users (`entra-users`) | Graph `/users` (id, UPN, enabled, created) | `entra:<id>`, user | UPN, enabled | 1 % |
| Entra apps + service principals (`entra-apps`) | Graph `/servicePrincipals` (Microsoft's own only when `SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns` is on, as the collection) | `entra:<id>`, service principal | app id, enabled | 1 % |
| Defender devices (`devices`) | Defender `/api/machines` | `mde:<id>`, device | Entra device id | 2 % |
| Azure resources (`azure`) | Resource Graph, only the types that become CIs (collection-scope; a child resource is part of its parent) | `azure:<arm id>` | type, location | 3 % |
| Defender for Cloud (`mdc`) | Resource Graph assessments, unhealthy per resource | `mdc:<arm id>` | unhealthy count | 5 % |
| Vulnerabilities (`vulnerabilities`) | Defender `/api/machines/<id>/vulnerabilities` for the sampled devices | the CVE findings of the newest complete Detailed collection | present in any report | 5 % |
| Risk Analysis, per report holding CVE findings | the same answers | the report's findings for those devices | matched / missing / extra | 3 % |

The sample: 10 % of the source's records, at least 50, all when 50 or fewer, picked at random every day. A source read that is
not complete is no read (it would show what it missed as missing). A record the source says was created after the newest
collection is not asked about. A record is **found** when it is in `sidata.CiRecord` and its collection time is within 6 hours
of the feed's newest good collection (`sidata.RecordCollection`); one whose key fields differ counts once as a field mismatch.
Check (b) samples the devices that hold vulnerability findings in the newest complete Detailed collection (their Defender id from
the CI's `mde` record) and asks Defender for each one; a device Defender could not answer for is left out and said. **Like with like:** each report's OWN exclusions apply before anything counts as missing -- its excluded CVEs, its CVE minimum age (judged by the vulnerability's last update in Defender) and its excluded configuration ids -- read through Risk Analysis's one scope reader (`Get-RAReportActiveScope`: the report's scope template, then its exclusion document, a Pro install's database copy first) and judged by `Test-RAInScopeFinding`, the PowerShell form of the scope block's `SI_InScopeCve` / `SI_InScopeConfiguration`, kept beside it. A CVE a report leaves out by rule is never "missing"; for the `vulnerabilities` source a CVE counts when at least one of the device's reports would keep it. Exclusions that cannot be read = every CVE is expected (said).

**The margin.** `allowed = max(minimum, floor(checked x percent / 100))`; a source or report is **anomalous** when more than
that differ (missing + field mismatches; for a report missing + extra). The percents are the approved defaults above, editable
by an Admin (`SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers`, `_EntraApps`, `_Devices`, `_Azure`, `_DefenderForCloud`, `_Vulnerabilities`,
`_RiskAnalysis`); the minimum is `SI_DataHealth_MarginMinimum` (5). A source that answers empty while the newest collection
holds its records is anomalous.

**Verdicts.** `ok` | `anomalous` | `not-checked` (the source could not be read, or the Pro database could not: never ok) |
`not-used` (this install holds no collection of a source that has records, or a part of the check is not set up -- neither good
nor missing).

**The state** (`cfg.DataHealthState`, one row). An install starts Healthy. An anomalous cycle adds one to the anomalous cycles
in a row; at **three** a Healthy install turns **Unhealthy**. A **good** cycle (nothing anomalous, nothing not-checked) sets
the count to 0 and turns an Unhealthy install **Healthy**. A cycle that could not check everything and found nothing anomalous
changes nothing -- an unreadable source never makes the data look healthy. Every cycle (`cfg.DataHealthCycle`), every source
and report result (`cfg.DataHealthResult`) and every record that did not match (`cfg.DataHealthMissing`, for the install's own
page only) are kept; the cycle's end and the state are written in one transaction.

**The effect: data-out is held while Unhealthy.** One call for every writer, `Resolve-SIDataHealthHold -Channel <connector>`
(`engine/_shared/SI-DataHealthHold.ps1`, the state read once per process): the vulnerability connectors (each runs as whatif:
it plans and reports, opens and closes nothing -- this settles #649), the ServiceNow CMDB (`servicenow-cmdb`, whatif), the SQL
CMDB hand-off (`cmdb-sql`, whatif: nothing handed over, nothing retired), asset tagging (`asset-tagging`, report only) and every
data-out output (its connector name; the output's result is `held`, what it last sent stays, not a failed issue). Not held:
no Pro database, no data health tables yet (an install not updated), no cycle run yet, or a state that cannot be read (said
once). A **SuperAdmin** lets ONE channel through with a reason of at least 10 characters on Operations > Data health (audit
`data-health.override.set` / `.clear`); the web app writes only through `cfg.DataHealthOverrideSet` (it checks the data is
Unhealthy and one open override per channel); the override lasts until the data is Healthy again -- the engine clears every
open override in the cycle that turns it Healthy, and an override from an earlier Unhealthy period never counts.

**Shown.** The header shows **Data health** (Healthy / Unhealthy, linked) to readers once a cycle has run; an older install
shows nothing. Operations > Data health: the state, the channels held / let through (SuperAdmin: let through, hold again),
the results per source and report of any of the last 30 cycles, and the records that did not match.

**To Invardia** (framework §12.11d; §12.22): the uplink kind `health` -- `schema, kind, product, version, installId (when
known), tenantId, sentUtc, state, since, cycle { id, startedUtc, finishedUtc, anomalous, consecutiveAnomalous, complete,
notChecked }, sources [ { source, sampled, found, missing, fieldMismatches, margin { percent, minimum }, verdict } ], reports
[ { report, sampled, matched, missing, extra, margin, verdict } ], dataOut { held, overrides [ { channel, byRole, sinceUtc,
reason } ] }`. Counts only: a not-checked / not-used source is left out of the lists (the wire knows ok | anomalous) and
counted in `cycle.notChecked`; an override's channel is SecurityInsight's own connector name or `connector` (a name the
customer gave), its reason only `given`; never a record key, name or person. Identified installs only; at most 50 sources and
200 reports and 32 KB (reports cut first, `truncated` said). Sent at the end of every daily cycle -- the cycle that changes the
state included. **Behind `SI_Telemetry_SendHealth`, OFF by default**: switched on per ring after Invardia has confirmed the kind
through one ring 0 call (framework §12.22 item 3); it switches off without a release.

**Existing installs.** The update applies `sql/si-pro-settings.sql` (five tables, one procedure, additive); until then the check
prints its result and stores nothing, and nothing is held. The first cycle starts Healthy; an Unhealthy state needs three
anomalous days, so a release never holds data-out on its first day.

### Guard events in plain words -- the three parts, release per kind, acknowledge (#351)
**Why.** The Guards page listed technical ids, "Measured vs limit" and a collapsed "What to do"; the operator asked how to release
them and for "cause, what to do, consequence". Decision: every guard event reads as **What happened / Why / Consequence / What to
do**, and what "release" means is decided **per guard kind**, never one generic button.

**One line to act on (#425).** The run log and the run-health record of a guard event carry one plain line built from the
same parts (`Format-SIGuardSummary`): what happened, the cause of this event, **where** (the job -- else the engine -- and
the report, connector, asset or jobs the caller named; `Get-SIGuardWhere`), the numbers against their limits with the held
count, and the numbered steps. The run-health record starts with the check's reference (`<guard id>: ...`); the mail shows
the same Where line, also when the caller named no subject.

**The catalog is the source of the words.** `config\guard-catalog.locked.json` gives each guard `kind`, `what`, `why`,
`consequence`, `steps` -- templates with placeholders filled from the stored event: `{held}`, `{v:<value name>}` (ValuesJson),
`{detail}`, `{subject}`, `{when}`, `{latest}` (web only: the newest collection shown); `{x|text}` falls back to text; a
`[ ... ]` part disappears when a placeholder in it is empty. One rule set, two readers: `Guards\GuardText.cs` and
`SI-Guard.ps1` (`Format-SIGuardText`, `Get-SIGuardParts`). The mail renders the three parts plus a numbered list; the identified
telemetry record's ActionText is what-happened + consequence + steps **without** `{detail}`/`{subject}` (the catalog test refuses
those placeholders in the parts that travel). A caller's own `-Action` still wins over the catalog's steps.

**Kinds.** `release-held-set` (cfg.GuardRelease: vulnerability closes, asset-properties change, CMDB hand-off batch -- one Admin
release of THAT run's set, unchanged, now reached from the row) · `release-collection` (below) · `fix-source` (not releasable:
data without key columns cannot be placed in a day) · `next-run` · `rerun` · `setting` · `review` · `info`.

**Releasing a held collection** (`datasync.collection.held`). Working rule 4 stays: a partial run is never shown **as whole**.
The data sync stores every held collection as a release candidate in cfg.GuardRelease (connector `datasync/detailed`, kind
`collection`, key `collection@<UTC time>` -- not a bare date, which pwsh 7's JSON reader would turn into a [datetime]), with a
summary carrying WHAT was incomplete: the producing run's own run-health message (`Get-SIDataRunHealthKql` adds `Detail`;
`Get-SIDataHoldDetail`, internal numbers stripped). An Admin releases it on the Guards page with a required reason
(`guard.collection.release`, audited, attributed; the data sync job is started). The next sync (`Set-SIDataReleasedPlan`) turns
that Hold into Load/Reload ONCE, widening its listing only as far as the released collection needs; after the collection is
'Complete' it is marked in `sidata.CollectionPartial` (reason, released by, when) and the release is applied
(`guard.release.apply`). A released collection whose rows lack ConfigurationId stays refused and its release is closed as
expired. The web app reads the marks once a minute (`IPartialCollections`) and shows a "partial" badge (header notice + picker)
wherever the collection is used. The mark is purged with its collection.

**Acknowledge.** `cfg.GuardAck` (INSERT only): one row per acknowledged event, with the guard key and SHA-256 of its detail; the
grid's source joins the newest matching acknowledgement, so later repeats of exactly the same event read acknowledged too, while a
different detail is a new situation. Acknowledged events are hidden by default (an implicit `Ack = open` filter; `?ack=all`). A
database without cfg.GuardAck uses the same grid with every event open and says so once.

### Data-quality warnings -- a three-run fingerprint, never a block (#577 step 2)
**Why.** Owner 2026-10-11: the real risk is a customer's customising mistake or a KQL change that suddenly returns nothing --
"more of a warning, not a blocker" -- and "it can base it on last 3 runs and compare key numbers", shaped "like anomaly
detection". So these are **warnings**: never a guard event, never a hold, never a mail per check.

**Where the numbers are computed -- ONE point.** The last step of the data sync (`engine/pro-data/_shared/SI-DataQuality.ps1`,
called at the end of `Invoke-SIDataSync.ps1`). The data sync is the Deliver step that runs after every engine that produces
the numbers (the profilers, the CI build in the correlation job, both Risk Analysis runs) and it already holds both seams --
Log Analytics and the Pro database. So the fingerprint *reads what was produced*, once per run, instead of every engine
measuring itself and keeping its own history: the Risk Analysis row-count and column-fill guards keep their history in a
local file per template (lost between container runs) and compare only with the previous run. What is reused from them: the
definition of "filled" (not empty, not blank -- `Get-RAColumnFillSnapshot`), the threshold reports (a report that is one
row only while a count is over a limit -- 0 is a resolved finding, `Get-RAThresholdReportNames`) and the report hand-offs (a
report whose findings moved to a new receiving report is a different population -- `Get-RAReportSuccessorMap`).

| Key number | Read from | Rule (against the median of the last 3 runs) | Re-run from |
|---|---|---|---|
| assets per source (endpoint, identity, azure, public IP) | the newest collection of each `SI_*_Profile_CL`, distinct assets | down 30 % or more | that profiler |
| rows per Risk Analysis report (Summary + Detailed) | the newest collection of each table, rows per report | 0 rows, or down 50 % or more | that Risk Analysis job |
| fill % of RiskFactor_Probability_Detailed, RiskFactor_Consequence_Detailed, tier (CriticalityTier), SQL tag (si_component) | the newest Detailed collection | down 30 points or more | Risk Analysis (detailed) |
| fill % of the active CIs' asset type and owner (si_owner / CMDB owner) | `sidata.Ci` | down 30 points or more | the correlation (CI build) |
| active CIs per tier 0-3 | `sidata.Ci` | moved by 20 % or more of all active CIs, up or down | the pipeline's first step |
| active CIs / CIs not seen any more (to retire) | `sidata.Ci` | down 30 % / up by 20 % of all active CIs | the correlation (CI build) |
| active CIs per asset class (asset type) | `sidata.Ci` | moved by 20 % or more of all active CIs, up or down (so a small class changing by a few assets never warns) | the correlation (CI build) |
| fill % of every catalog field per source that fills it | the current provider records (`sidata.CiRecord`), one pass | down 30 points or more | the step that collects the source |

**The fill per source field is driven by the data model, not by a list.** Which fields are watched = every field of the field
catalog (`data-model/field-catalog.locked.json`) that lives on the provider record (level `record` or `both`) and that a
source's mapping (`data-model/mappings/<source>.locked.json`) fills; the denominator = that source's records of the record
types the mapping names (no record type named = every record of the source). A value = present, not null, not blank, not an
empty list or object (a `false` or a `0` is a value). A field added to a source's mapping is therefore watched from the next
run on with no change here, a field no record carries reads 0 % (never filled is visible, and never warns: the rule is a
DROP), and a source without records is left out. A source that stops filling its context fields is a fill drop like any
other; on the run-health record several fields of one source are ONE line naming the largest.

Fewer than 3 earlier runs (for the run, or for one number that is new) = learning, nothing compared. A count the last run had
that this run did not produce is a **0** (a report that went to zero has no row in Log Analytics at all), carried while it is
not 0 in all of the last 3 runs; a source that could not be **read** is never a 0. One run per Risk Analysis Detailed
collection: a data sync re-run that loaded nothing new adds nothing. Limits: `SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent` (30),
`_ReportDropPercent` (50), `_FillDropPoints` (30), `_TierShiftPercent` (20).

**Likely cause.** The settings changes between the last run WITHOUT a warning and this one (`cfg.ChangeLog`, the settings
database) -- the previous run, unless it warned too: the expected range follows a change only after three runs, so on the
second day of the same anomaly the cause is still the change made before the first. Which setting, who, when -- the ones
whose name concerns the number first (tier / rule words for a tier, the report's own name for a report, the field's or the
source mapping's name for a source field, ...), else every change; none = "the source data itself changed -- or a
collection was incomplete". The changes of the window are stored with the run and linked to the numbers they concern, so
the panel shows each as a link to the audit trail.

**Store (additive).** `sidata.DataQualityRun` (one row per run, the mail), `sidata.DataQualityMetric` (its numbers),
`sidata.DataQualityAnomaly` (the three earlier values, expected, now, change, rule, cause as text, step),
`sidata.DataQualityChange` (the settings changes of the run's window: setting, who, when) and `sidata.DataQualityCause`
(key number -> the changes that concern it) -- guarded CREATEs only. The cause rows are written before the anomalies; a
database without the two cause tables keeps the cause as the text on the anomaly.

**Output.** (1) Operations > **Data quality** (`/Admin/DataQuality`, readers) -- the Data quality view, per run:

- **the verdict at a glance** -- anomaly detected yes / no, how many of the key numbers are outside the range, the largest
  change against the expected range, how many earlier runs the run was compared with;
- **the most significant changes** -- key number, the 3 earlier values, now, the change, a trend line;
- **each warning in full** -- what changed in one sentence; the 3 earlier values, their median and today's; the likely cause
  as the settings changes that concern the number (each a link to the audit trail for a person who may open it), or every
  change of the window when none names the number; what to do in plain words (one text per rule); and **Re-run from here**:
  a button on the warning that queues "the pipeline from the step that produces this number" -- the same request, queue and
  runner start as Re-run from here on Operations > Jobs (one shared piece of code), Admin, asked first, on the audit trail.
  The button stays where it is and the answer is a toast (a plain form post without script answers with the page);
- **every key number of the run**, by group (assets per source, CIs, assets per class, tier distribution, report rows, key
  column fill, field fill per source): now, the 3 runs before, the expected value, the change in the rule's own measure,
  within / outside / no range yet, and a trend over the last 14 runs;
- **the history of runs** (30, 90 or 365) -- picking a run shows that run in every section above.

Empty states say what is true: a database from before the measurements existed, no run yet, no expected range yet (fewer
than 3 earlier runs: the values are shown, nothing is compared), a run that is gone, a run whose numbers were not kept. The
three lists (changes, key numbers, runs) are the shared page table, so the column chooser, each person's layout and the
all-rows exports work there, and the page is listed as a data view. **Speed:** the page reads prepared rows by key -- the
run list (an index end), then the picked run's rows by its run id (primary keys); no document and no JSON at page time. A
run's rows never change once written, so the picked run's detail is kept per data version, and only while it is complete
(as many numbers and anomalies as the run row says). Numbers follow the viewer's number format.

(2) **A mail only when the warnings change** (at most one a day -- see "The mail only when the warnings change" below), shaped like a cloud cost-anomaly alert:
"Data quality alert: an unusual drop (or rise) was detected", one sentence (which run, the expected range from the last 3
runs, please review recent changes), the likely cause, a run summary (anomaly detected yes; the largest delta vs expected),
the "most significant changes" table, what to do (correct the setting, Re-run from here; nothing was blocked) and a Details
button that opens the panel on the run the mail is about -- the MAIL-2 layout and its PDF through `Send-SIMail`, to `SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To`, else the guard
mail's recipients; `SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled` turns it off. (3) One line per anomaly on the data sync's run-health
END record; the verdict is unchanged.

**One warning per source (owner 2026-10-11: "One warning per source").** A source that stops delivering usually drops
many of its fields in the same run. After the comparison, the dropped field fills of ONE source
(`fill.src.<source>.<field>`, two or more) are joined into ONE warning (`Join-SIDataQualitySourceAnomalies`): key
`fill.src.<source>`, rule `source-fill-drop`, label "<source> stopped filling N fields". Its own numbers are the AVERAGE
fill of those fields -- in each of the 3 earlier runs, their median (expected), now, and the change in points -- so it
sorts with the other warnings and the run's largest change still means something. The fields are carried inside it, the
largest drop first, each with its own 3 earlier values, expected value, now and change. One dropped field of a source
stays that field's own warning. Only the WARNING is joined: every field is still measured and stored as a key number of
the run. Where it shows: the stored anomalies (one row in `sidata.DataQualityAnomaly`, the fields in
`sidata.DataQualityAnomalyField` -- guarded CREATE, written before the anomaly; a database without the table keeps the
warning without its list), the panel (one row in "most significant changes", one card with the table of fields, ONE likely
cause -- the source's mapping or any of the fields by name --, one fix, one Re-run from here; each field is still "outside
the range" in the key numbers), the mail's table (the source's row, its fields under it) and run health (one line: the
source, the average, the field that dropped most). The verdict counts key numbers and says how many warnings they are.

**The mail only when the warnings change (owner 2026-10-11: "Only when it changes").** Replaces "every day a number
stays off". After the run is stored, its warnings are compared BY KEY with the warnings of the last run whose mail was
SENT (`Compare-SIDataQualityMailSet`; the last mailed run and its anomaly rows are read from the tables that exist -- no
new column, and a mail that failed is not a mailed run). A source's fields are one key, so a source that drops one field
more is not a change. The outcomes:

| This run against the last mailed run | Mail | Kept on the run (`MailState`) |
|---|---|---|
| a warning is new, or one is gone while others stay | the alert, with a part "Since the last data-quality mail": what is new, what is back within its range | `sent` (or `failed`) |
| no warning now, the last mail had some | ONE "back to normal" mail: which run, what is back, nothing needs doing | `sent` |
| the same warnings | none | `unchanged` |
| no warning now and none mailed (or the last mail was "back to normal") | none | (empty) |
| a change, but a mail went out earlier the same day | none; the next run mails what is different then | `day-limit` |
| the mail is switched off / has no recipients | none | `off` / `no-recipients` |

A warning the last mail had whose numbers could not be READ this run is neither gone nor new (it is carried), so a failed
read never sends "back to normal". A run still learning compares nothing and never mails. The first mail after this change
on an install that mailed per field before compares the one-per-source keys with the old per-field keys, so it goes out
once more. The panel says on the run whether its mail went out and, if not, why -- for `unchanged`: "nothing changed
since the mail of the run of <when>", with a link to that run (the newest mailed run before it, read by the web app) -- and
the history has the same per run. "Back to normal" is the coordinator's reading of "changes"; the owner has not confirmed it.

**Fields that are never filled (owner 2026-10-11: "Hide behind a filter").** A mapping names every field a source CAN
deliver; in one tenant many are never delivered, and their rows read 0 % forever. In "Key numbers of this run" a
field-fill row that reads 0 % in this run AND in every earlier run the page has of it (its trend) is hidden by default.
Next to the group tabs the page says how many there are ("42 fields are never filled") with a link "Show fields that are
never filled" -- an address parameter (`never=true`), no script; with it on the link reads "Hide ...". The group tabs say
shown of total ("3 of 45") while rows are hidden, the exports export what is shown (with the switch on: all), and every
link of the page keeps the switch. Such a field never warns either way (a fill that was never above 0 cannot drop), and a
field that is outside its range is never hidden. Nothing is stored for it: the page decides from the rows it already reads.

### Run transcripts — every run keeps its own log

The heartbeat above says *whether* a run finished. The transcript says *what it did*. Every launcher
wraps its run in `Start-Transcript` via `launcher/_lib/Start-LauncherTranscript.ps1`, and this is **on
by default** — nothing needs enabling.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Path** | `<root>/logs/<engine>_<flavour>[_<simulation>][_<template>]_<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>.log` |
| **Layout** | one `logs/` folder per install (deliberate — easier to grep than a tree), UTC stamp so the folder sorts chronologically |
| **Retention** | 30 days, pruned at the start of each run; override with `$global:SI_LogRetentionDays` |
| **Kill switch** | `$global:SI_DisableTranscript` — both knobs are documented in `config/SecurityInsight.custom.reference.ps1` |

The helper is layout-aware: it resolves `SOLUTIONS/SecurityInsight/logs` in the monorepo and
`<root>/logs` in the flat community layout, so a community install does not end up writing its
transcripts somewhere its operator cannot find them.

#### The container host publishes its transcript to blob storage

A container filesystem is ephemeral, so a log written inside one dies with the replica. The three
container entrypoints — `Start-SIInContainer.ps1` (worker + privilege-tier-classifier branches),
`Start-RiskAnalysisInContainer.ps1` and `Invoke-ShardProducer.ps1` — start a transcript with
`-Flavour container` and hand it to `launcher/_lib/Publish-LauncherTranscript.ps1` at run end, which
uploads it to the staging account under `run-logs/<engine>/<file name>`.

The **dispatch** branches deliberately start no transcript: they hand off to a child `pwsh` that starts
its own, and two transcripts for one run is worse than one. Each leaf branch captures `$LASTEXITCODE`
**before** publishing, because publishing runs commands — without that, a Container Apps Job would
report the publish's exit code rather than the engine's.

Three properties of the publisher, in priority order:

- **It never throws.** Every failure path warns and returns `$null`. Failing a collection run because
  its log could not be uploaded trades the customer's inventory for their audit trail, which is the
  wrong way round.
- **It stops the transcript before reading the file.** `Start-Transcript` buffers, so uploading an open
  transcript ships a file missing exactly the tail an operator wants — the error at the end of a failed
  run.
- **It prunes its own blobs** at `$global:SI_LogRetentionDays` (30), matching local retention. Run logs
  sit **outside** `staging/` on purpose: the staging lifecycle rule is prefix-scoped to `staging/` and
  its 7 days would silently disagree with the 30-day retention everywhere else.

**Known limit, stated rather than hidden:** anything that throws *before* `Connect-AzAccount` succeeds
cannot be published, because there are no credentials to upload with. A container that dies on a missing
environment variable still leaves nothing behind. Everything after that point is covered.

### Monitoring — three layers

Pick the layer that matches your operational posture. Most setups use Layer 1 daily + Layer 2 on production tenants.

#### Layer 1 — CLI: `Show-SIRunHealth.ps1`

> 🔴 **NOT YET SHIPPED — this section describes the intended tool, not one you can run.**
> `Show-SIRunHealth.ps1` does not currently exist in the solution. The **data it reads is real** —
> `SI_RunHealth_CL` is emitted by every asset-profiling and risk-analysis run — so the KQL further
> down this chapter works today and can be run directly in the workspace. Two related gaps to know
> about while this stands: the run-health **DCR is not created by setup** (so the heartbeat has
> nowhere to land until it is provisioned), and heartbeat delivery is deliberately best-effort and
> **swallows its own failures**, which means an absent row does not by itself prove a run failed.
> Use the raw queries below in the meantime.

The day-to-day tool. Reads `SI_RunHealth_CL` and prints three tables: failed replicas, memory warnings, and a planned-vs-completed run summary.

```powershell
# Last 24h, all engines (default)
.\LAUNCHERS\SecurityInsight_AssetProfiling\Show-SIRunHealth.ps1

# Last week, identity engine only
.\Show-SIRunHealth.ps1 -Hours 168 -Engine identity

# Inspect one specific run end-to-end
.\Show-SIRunHealth.ps1 -RunId 20260426T144109Z-identity-7d8c743d

# Tighter memory threshold for 2 GB containers
.\Show-SIRunHealth.ps1 -MemoryWarnMB 1500
```

Output sections:

- **FAILED replicas** — Start with no End. If non-empty, check the Container App Job execution logs for the matching replica's exit reason (OOM kill, timeout).
- **WARNING** — End rows with `PeakWorkingSetMB > MemoryWarnMB` (default 3072 = 75% of a 4 GB Consumption-profile container). These predict the next OOM.
- **RUN SUMMARY** — one line per run: planned `ShardCount` vs `Completed` vs `Missing`, total assets across shards, max peak memory, duration.

Run after every test deploy and once a month per tenant.

#### Layer 2 — Azure Monitor scheduled alert

For tenants you can't manually inspect. Wire one alert per workspace; the alert fires when any replica from the last 6h has no End row.

```bash
az monitor scheduled-query create \
  --name "SI-RunHealth-MissingEnd" \
  --resource-group "$rg" \
  --scopes "$workspaceResourceId" \
  --condition "count > 0" \
  --condition-query "let r = SI_RunHealth_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(6h); r | where Phase == 'Start' | join kind=leftanti (r | where Phase == 'End') on RunId, ShardIndex" \
  --evaluation-frequency 30m --window-size 6h \
  --severity 2 --action "$actionGroupId"
```

Optional companion alert for chronic memory pressure (fires before the OOM):

```bash
az monitor scheduled-query create \
  --name "SI-RunHealth-MemoryPressure" \
  --resource-group "$rg" \
  --scopes "$workspaceResourceId" \
  --condition "count > 3" \
  --condition-query "SI_RunHealth_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) and Phase == 'End' and PeakWorkingSetMB > 3072" \
  --evaluation-frequency 6h --window-size 24h \
  --severity 3 --action "$actionGroupId"
```

Per-tenant config; not deployed by the engine bootstrap.

#### Layer 3 — Workbook tab

Add a section to the existing SecurityInsight Workbook with the same three KQL queries from Layer 1. Visual surface for stakeholders who don't run PowerShell. ~20 minutes of Workbook editing, no engine code change.

### Diagnostic KQL — copy/paste

Use these directly in the LA query blade when triaging a specific incident.

```kql
// Replicas that started but never finished (OOM / killed / infra timeout)
let r = SI_RunHealth_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h);
r | where Phase == 'Start'
| join kind=leftanti (r | where Phase == 'End') on RunId, ShardIndex
| project TimeGenerated, RunId, Engine, ShardIndex, ShardCount, Computer
```

```kql
// Memory pressure — flag at 75% of container limit
SI_RunHealth_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Phase == 'End' and PeakWorkingSetMB > 3072
| project TimeGenerated, RunId, Engine, ShardIndex, AssetCount, PeakWorkingSetMB, DurationSec
| order by PeakWorkingSetMB desc
```

```kql
// Run summary — did all expected shards finish?
let r = SI_RunHealth_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h);
let s = r | where Phase == 'Start' | summarize Started = count(), ShardCount = max(ShardCount) by RunId, Engine;
let e = r | where Phase == 'End' | summarize Completed = count(), Errors = countif(ExitReason == 'error') by RunId, Engine;
s | join kind=leftouter e on RunId, Engine
| extend Missing = ShardCount - coalesce(Completed, 0)
| project RunId, Engine, ShardCount, Completed = coalesce(Completed, 0), Missing, Errors = coalesce(Errors, 0)
| where Missing > 0 or Errors > 0
```

```kql
// Per-shard duration distribution — uneven shards = bad partition function
SI_RunHealth_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) and Phase == 'End' and Engine == 'identity'
| summarize avg(DurationSec), max(DurationSec), avg(AssetCount) by ShardIndex
| order by ShardIndex asc
```

### Right-sizing — when to bump `ParallelismIdentity`

ShardCount is set at bootstrap time per engine via `Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1 -ParallelismIdentity N` (or `-ParallelismEndpoint`, `-ParallelismAzure`). Changing it later requires a redeploy and invalidates the partition map (hash buckets shift).

Use the heartbeat to decide N rather than guessing:

| Signal observed in `SI_RunHealth_CL`           | Action                                                 |
|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| Failed replicas (no End row) > 0               | **Bump ShardCount immediately.** Replica was killed.   |
| `PeakWorkingSetMB > 3072` consistently         | Bump ShardCount at next deploy window.                 |
| `MaxDurationSec > 30 min` for any shard        | Bump ShardCount; wall-clock budget is the constraint.  |
| All shards green, peak <50% of limit           | Current N is fine; consider lowering on next refresh.  |

Rough guidance:

| Tenant size (identities) | Suggested `ParallelismIdentity` |
|---|---|
| ≤ 50,000   | 1   (single-replica scale-up) |
| 50k–200k   | 4–8                           |
| 200k–1M    | 16–32                         |
| > 1M       | 32+ + per-page Graph filter (not yet built — see PREVIEW.md) |

### Other operational signals to watch

Beyond the heartbeat itself, surface these in the Workbook or weekly review:

- **`SI_Identity_Profile_CL`** — row count per `RunId`; sudden drop = upstream Discovery regression.
- **`ExitReason == 'error'` rate** — if > 0% over a week, an engine bug is shipping silent half-runs (the heartbeat fires but the work errored).
- **Cadence skip ratio** — Stage Collect logs `N cadence-skipped`. A first run is 0% skipped, steady state should be 80–95% skipped (only T0 + due-cadence identities re-process). If steady state shows < 50% skipped, fingerprint cache writes are failing — see `Set-SIFingerprintRecord` warnings.
- **EG enrichment rate** — Stage Collect logs `EG-enriched: N`. Should match `[perms] EG identity nodes: M entries indexed by AadObjectId` from Discover. If EG-enriched is 0 but EG nodes > 0, the join key extraction broke (see `Get-SIExposureGraphIdentities` in `IdentityRoleFetcher.ps1`).

### Tenant schema-drift detection (planned)

For the Azure engine: at start of every run, query `ExposureGraphNodes | where NodeLabel startswith "microsoft." | distinct NodeLabel` and diff against the (locked + custom) catalog of known types.

- **Tenant has + catalog has** → run the per-type EG + ARG queries.
- **Tenant has + catalog missing** → log to `schema-discovery-pending/azure/<type>.sample.json` with a real NodePropertiesJson sample for the operator to review and promote into `profiles-custom/azure.schema.custom.json`.
- **Catalog has + tenant doesn't** → skip (query returns 0 rows).

The schema-discovery engine already handles this drift loop for endpoint hunting tables; the same pattern extends to Azure resource types when the locked Azure catalog reaches stable coverage.

## Troubleshooting

### DCE / DCR provisioning failures

LA ingest goes through three Azure resources: the **Log Analytics workspace**, a **Data Collection Endpoint (DCE)**, and one **Data Collection Rule (DCR)** per profile table. The DCR is auto-created/auto-updated on the first ingest of every table by SecurityInsight's REST ingest client (`Update-SILogTableSchema`; before 3.0 the AzLogDcrIngestPS module did this). Four failure modes recur in real tenants.

> **Key invariant** — a new DCR's `location` field is set from the DCE's location, **not** from `$global:SI_Location`. The engine's `SI_Location` global is engine-intent only; once the DCE exists, that DCE's location wins for every DCR pinned to it. Recreating the DCR in a different location is impossible — DCR `location` is immutable post-create.

#### `RequestDisallowedByPolicy` — DCE in wrong region

**Symptom**: `[ERR] Body : RequestDisallowedByPolicy ... target dcr-si-<engine>-profile ... policyDefinition Allowed locations ... targetValue ["global","westeurope"], operator NotIn`. HTTP 403 on the DCR PUT, ingest aborts.

**Root cause**: An Azure Policy assigned at the management-group / subscription scope denies any resource location not in its allowlist. The DCE the engine resolved isn't in that allowlist — so the DCR PUT body that inherits its location is denied.

**Diagnose** (v2.2.42+ logs the picked DCE's location explicitly):
```
DCR pre-create  : SI_Location        = westeurope  (engine intent; NOT used by module for new DCR)
DCR pre-create  : DceLocation        = northeurope  (THIS becomes new DCR location)
DCR pre-create  : LOCATION MISMATCH -- SI_Location='westeurope' but DCE is in 'northeurope'.
```

**Fix**: Delete the DCE and any DCRs pinned to it (their location is immutable), then recreate the DCE in an allowed region:

```powershell
# 1. Confirm the wrong-location DCE
Get-AzDataCollectionEndpoint -ResourceGroupName $global:SI_DceResourceGroup `
                              -Name              $global:SI_DceName |
  Format-List Name, Location, Id

# 2. Drop dependent DCRs (any auto-created dcr-si-*-profile pinned to it)
Get-AzDataCollectionRule -ResourceGroupName $global:SI_DcrResourceGroup |
  Where-Object { $_.Name -like 'dcr-si-*-profile' } |
  Remove-AzDataCollectionRule -Confirm:$false

# 3. Drop and recreate the DCE in the allowed location
Remove-AzDataCollectionEndpoint -ResourceGroupName $global:SI_DceResourceGroup `
                                 -Name              $global:SI_DceName -Confirm:$false
New-AzDataCollectionEndpoint    -ResourceGroupName $global:SI_DceResourceGroup `
                                 -Name              $global:SI_DceName `
                                 -Location          $global:SI_Location `
                                 -NetworkAclsPublicNetworkAccess Enabled

# 4. Re-run any one engine; CheckCreateUpdate will recreate every DCR auto-pinned
#    to the new DCE.
```

#### `LinkedAuthorizationFailed: invalid types 'Array'` — DCE name collision

**Symptom**: `LinkedAuthorizationFailed ... properties.dataCollectionEndpointId has values which are of invalid types 'Array'`. HTTP 4xx on DCR PUT.

**Root cause** (before 3.0, when ingestion went through the AzLogDcrIngestPS module): Two DCEs share `$global:SI_DceName` across subs/RGs (legacy install + new install on the same long-lived tenant). The module did a name-only lookup — `$global:AzDceDetails | Where { $_.name -eq $DceName }` — which returns BOTH records when names collide. `$DceInfo.id` becomes `string[]`, gets serialized as a JSON array, ARM rejects.

**Fix (engine-side, v2.2.41+)**: Engine pre-filters `$global:AzDceDetails` to a single entry by name + RG before the module's name-only lookup runs. Set `$global:SI_DceResourceGroup` in `SecurityInsight.custom.ps1` to disambiguate when the DCE lives in a different RG than the DCRs.

When the guard fires, the engine logs:
```
DCE collision guard: 2 DCEs named '<dce-name>' visible -- pinned to RG '<rg-name>' (/subscriptions/.../<dce-name>)
```

If the wrong DCE is being picked, either:
1. Set `$global:SI_DceResourceGroup` explicitly to the desired RG, or
2. Delete the unwanted duplicate DCE.

#### Wrong `SI_DceName` — silent lookup miss

**Symptom**: `RequestDisallowedByPolicy` (most likely) or generic ARM 400. Often mistaken for the wrong-region case because the policy denial fires on the empty/null location field too.

**Root cause**: `$global:SI_DceName` doesn't match any DCE the SPN can see in ARG. Module's name lookup returns `$null`; `$DceLocation = $null`; DCR PUT body has `location = null`; ARM either rejects or the policy treats null as a disallowed location.

**Diagnose** (v2.2.42+ logs the empty-cache case):
```
DCR pre-create  : DceLocation        = <no DCE in cache>
```
Or: the `DCE collision guard` line is **absent** from the log entirely (no DCEs matched the name, so the guard had nothing to filter).

**Fix**: Verify the actual DCE name in Azure and update `SecurityInsight.custom.ps1`:

```powershell
# List every DCE the SPN can read across the tenant
Get-AzDataCollectionEndpoint | Format-Table Name, ResourceGroupName, Location, Id

# Or scoped to the security-insight RG
Get-AzDataCollectionEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '<rg-name>' |
  Format-Table Name, Location
```

Then in `SecurityInsight.custom.ps1`:
```powershell
$global:SI_DceName          = '<dce-name>'    # match what Azure actually has
$global:SI_DceResourceGroup = '<rg-name>'     # belt-and-suspenders disambiguation
$global:SI_Location         = '<region>'      # documents intent; only used when bootstrap creates a NEW DCE
```

#### `403 OperationFailed -- does not have access to ingest` — RBAC gap on DCR

**Symptom**: DCR was created successfully (`CheckCreateUpdate-TableDcr-Structure` returned clean), then on the first `Post-AzLogAnalyticsLogIngestCustomLogDcrDce-Output` call:
```
HTTP 403 OperationFailed: The authentication token provided does not have access
to ingest data for the data collection rule with immutable Id 'dcr-<32hex>'.
```
Engine retries 3 times with 30s/60s sleeps + cache refresh; all three fail identically. Sink reports `LA=FAIL JSON=OK Excel=OK`.

**Root cause**: SPN is missing the **`Monitoring Metrics Publisher`** role on the DCR (or on a parent scope with propagation still in flight). Two sub-cases:
1. **Bootstrap never granted it** — the setup (the guided install or the unattended setup) was skipped or this DCR was created post-bootstrap by a different engine. Pre-flight catches this.
2. **RG-scope grant exists but hasn't propagated to a freshly-created DCR** — Azure RBAC inheritance can take 5–30 min for newly-created DCRs to become visible to the data plane even though the grant lives at the parent RG. v2.2.42's resource-scope grant in Setup avoids this by granting directly on the DCR (sub-60s propagation).

**Diagnose**: a collection run checks this itself, read-only, once per process, before it collects. When the role
is missing the run log carries ONE line that names it and the command that grants it:
```
access check: SecurityInsight's identity (<objectId>) does not hold Monitoring Metrics Publisher on resource group '<rg-name>' (to send rows to Log Analytics) -- a run assigns no role, so nothing was changed and that step will fail. Someone who may assign roles runs: setup\Grant-SIIdentity.ps1 -PrincipalId <objectId> -SubscriptionId <sub> -WorkspaceResourceId <workspace id> -DcrResourceGroup <rg-name> -AllowSchemaCreate -Apply
```
No line means the role is held (at the resource group or above it, directly or through a group -- any role whose
definition allows the send counts), or the identity may not read its own role assignments (then nothing is said).

**A run never fixes this itself.** It assigns no role and creates no Azure resource -- see
"A collection run assigns no role and creates no resource" under the storage section. The fix is the command in
the line, run by someone who may assign roles.

**Manual fix** (the same grant by hand, when the setup script cannot be used):
```powershell
$spnObjectId = $global:SI_SPN_ObjectId
$dcrId       = (Get-AzDataCollectionRule -ResourceGroupName $global:SI_DcrResourceGroup `
                                          -Name              'dcr-si-identity-profile').Id

# Resource-scope grant -- propagates in <60s vs 5-30 min for RG-scope
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $spnObjectId `
                     -RoleDefinitionName 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' `
                     -Scope              $dcrId

# Belt-and-suspenders: also grant at RG (covers future auto-created DCRs)
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $spnObjectId `
                     -RoleDefinitionName 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' `
                     -Scope "/subscriptions/$($global:SI_AzSubscriptionId)/resourceGroups/$($global:SI_DcrResourceGroup)"

Start-Sleep -Seconds 60   # propagation
```

**Why two roles, not one**: `Monitoring Contributor` lets you read+write monitoring resources (DCEs, DCRs themselves); `Monitoring Metrics Publisher` lets you ingest data INTO a DCR. They're orthogonal — bootstrap needs Contributor (to create the DCR), runtime needs MMP (to send rows to it). Setup grants both at RG scope; v2.2.42 also grants MMP at the DCR resource scope per-DCR.

#### Quick-reference — DCE/DCR location decision table

| Scenario | What governs DCR location |
|---|---|
| First-ever DCE create (via the setup) | `$global:SI_Location` (bootstrap honours it) |
| First-ever DCR create (via engine ingest) | `$DceInfo.location` (whatever location the DCE was created in) |
| Subsequent DCR updates (schema drift) | DCR location is immutable — module sends `location = $DceLocation` again, ARM no-ops the field |
| Recreating DCR in a new location | Impossible without delete + recreate. DCE delete + recreate first if you also want to move the DCE. |

### Engine-level diagnostic signals (cross-reference)

These run-summary log lines double as troubleshooting entry points:

- **Failed replica (Start with no End)** → killed mid-run (OOM / container kill / infra timeout). Bump ShardCount. See heartbeat section.
- **`PeakWorkingSetMB > 3072`** → memory pressure, predicts the next OOM. Bump ShardCount at next deploy window.
- **Cadence skip ratio < 50% in steady state** → fingerprint cache writes failing; check `Set-SIFingerprintRecord` warnings.
- **`EG-enriched: 0` while EG nodes > 0** → ExposureGraph join-key extraction broke; check `Get-SIExposureGraphIdentities` in `IdentityRoleFetcher.ps1`.
- **MDE-discovered devices with empty `Hostname`/`OsPlatform`/`MachineGroup`** → MDE pass-through branch ordering regressed; Stage Collect must hit the `elseif ($a.MDE_DeviceId)` branch before the Entra-device fallback.
