## Operational trust fixes (#904, #911, #913, #917, #918, #919 -- 2026-10-28)

**A part of the data sync that fails is a failure of that part (#904).** Every part the data sync can fail in is in ONE map
(`engine/pro-data/_shared/SI-DataSync.ps1` `SIDataSyncParts`: its result key, its words, its step id). A part that fails keeps
its last complete result and the job completes (owner: "a report fails alone, the job completes"), but it is never only a WARN
line: `Get-SIDataSyncPartFailures` names it with its class, the END record says `PART FAILED <step> (<class>)` and ends
success-partial with FailedStep / FailedStepErrorClass, and each failed part is sent through the failure uplink
(`Send-SITelemetryFailure -Job datasync -Partial`, Job si-datasync, Outcome warning). Azure SQL's size quota (1105 / 40544 /
"reached its size quota") is its own class, `database-full` (product-defect, a ticket: catalogue code si-data-1404), checked
before any SQL or timeout word. The heartbeat's Database field carries `usedMb` / `maxSizeMb` -- the same cheap read as the
Counts' sqlUsedMb / sqlMaxMb (FILEPROPERTY SpaceUsed of the data files, DATABASEPROPERTYEX MaxSizeInBytes), taken from them,
never read twice -- and Warnings raise si-data-1403 at 85 % of the maximum size, before a write fails.

**Two updates never change the install at once; a long step is never a hang (#911).** An updater execution (hourly or update
now) reads its own job's executions after the sign-in and steps aside, with one line and no change, while an EARLIER one still
runs (`Select-SIUpdaterEarlierRunning`; the same second: the lower name goes on; a Running execution past the run limit is a
leftover). A PATCH refused with 409 "an operation is in progress" is waited out -- the resource's provisioningState polled,
bounded at 10 minutes -- and sent again on a fresh read (`Invoke-SIUpdaterPatchWhenFree`). Every call with a token in the update
has a 120 s timeout and 4 attempts and names METHOD + URL when it gives up (`setup/_shared/SI-UpdateRest.ps1`). The lock the
run gate took is registered (`Register-SIUpdaterLockBeat`) and beaten at every updater line and every Step of
`setup/Invoke-SIContainerUpdate.ps1` (at most once a minute, always at a new step). A watch thread
(`setup/_shared/SI-UpdateWatch.ps1`, its own runspace, no SQL) writes `still working: <step> (no log line for N min)` after
20 silent minutes.

**A transient in the runner's lock is nobody's fix (#913).** The lock calls of `New-SIPipelineSqlControl` (acquire, beat,
release, release of a run, read) go through `Invoke-SIPipelineLockCall`: the Azure SQL transients (9001, 40613, 40501, 40197,
49918-49920, 4060, 10928 / 10929, a reset connection, a client timeout) are sent again after 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 s -- each lock
statement names its holder, so a call that lost only its Close is safe to repeat -- then thrown tagged `transient-sql`. The
runner's wake-up that meets it started nothing: one WARN, run health success-partial with class transient-sql, exit 0. The
class has no FixKind: never a fix request, never a red alert.

**Release tooling reads git text as UTF-8; the backlog push refuses what cannot be right (#917).** `setup/_shared/SI-GitText.ps1`
`Invoke-SIGitText` runs git as its own process and decodes its output as UTF-8, whatever the console's code page (a detached
release ran IBM437). `Push-SIBacklog` sends nothing for 0 open items from numbered rows, unreadable status marks, or more than
half of the last pushed count gone (`Test-SIBacklogSnapshotSane`; `-AllowLargeDrop` when a clean-up is real) -- beside
Invardia's own 409 guard. Every open row is sent (Invardia's limit 2,000 / 4 MB); more is refused by the checker, never cut.

**Only a released build reports to the public community uplink (#918).** Every test entry point sets
`SI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` (+ the marker `SI_TEST_GATE=1`) for itself and its children; inside a Pester session the marker
keeps the gate's value from switching off the suites' stubbed senders. `Test-SITelemetryCommunitySendAllowed`: the community
code needs BUILD.json's `release` to be a release label (digits and dots: 3.0.1 or 3.0.0.<build>) -- a dev tree, a dev or rc
label never sends; an identified install's own key is never gated. Applied in the run report, SI's uplink sender and the guards'
default transport; `engine/_shared/AitUplink.ps1` stays the framework's byte-identical copy.

**Release numbers are 3.0.1, 3.0.2 ... (#919, owner 2026-10-28).** `setup/_shared/SI-ReleaseVersion.ps1`: the next patch after
the highest released number of VERSION's major.minor (release-state.json: every ring's Version / PreviousVersion and the
numbers decided before, `assignedVersions`); a feature release (VERSION 3.1.0) starts its own patches; the same commit gets the
same number while it was never released; a number not greater than the highest released one, or of another major, is refused.
The build stamp stays in BUILD.json, the release notes and the support bundle. The package of 3.0.1 carries 3.0.1 in its own VERSION file (`Set-SIReleaseArchiveVersion`, Publish-SIRelease): the updaters installed before #919 accept a release only when it is the archive's VERSION or a <VERSION>.<build> of it. Every compare SI uses is numeric per part with a
missing part 0, so 3.0.1 > 3.0.0.202610272235 everywhere; a code manifest of another MAJOR than the running version is refused
(`Test-SIInvardiaSameMajor`, the major only -- 2.2 is never an upgrade path to 3.0.x). The web app's pill shows the short
version (`InstalledRelease.Short`), the full release and the build date in its tooltip.
## L2 support worker on mgmt1 (#684) — vendor operations, in no customer payload

Invardia's support team (Invardia DESIGN §7 "SUPPORT TEAM"): **L1** = Invardia's support agent (owns the ticket, the only
one who talks to the customer), **L2** = SecurityInsight, **L3** = the owner. Invardia files a *support fix request* for
`securityinsight`; SI's worker fixes it and reports back. It runs **on mgmt1** (owner 2026-10-15: "they run here in
mgmt1 machine as now"), from `ops/support-worker/`.

**The release rule (owner 2026-10-15, replaces the earlier fix classes):** the solution team may fix and release to
**ring 0 + 1** and monitor as part of the release model, then **propose** whether the update is a candidate for ring 2;
the owner judges. *"never can an agent auto approve to ring 2 or 3"*. Classes: `hotfix` (ring 0 + 1, then `fixed` + the
proposal, STOP) and `major` (nothing is built before the owner's decision: a read-only proposal + `needs-owner`).
Anything unclear = major. Until Invardia's `fixClass` is on the request: priority P1-P4 = hotfix, anything else = major.

**Two ways to drive it** (both built): (a) the **poller** — SI's interactive session calls
`Start-SISupportWorker.ps1 -Once -Detach` on a schedule (a /loop); one pass reads Invardia, picks ONE request and
starts (b) in the background, then returns; (b) the **fix run** — `Start-SISupportWorker.ps1 -RequestId <id>`: one
headless `claude -p` in its OWN git worktree (`<worktreeRoot>\si-support-<id8>`, branch `si-v3-support/<id8>`, from
`origin/si-v3`), so the interactive session's tree is never touched. Without `-Once` it loops by itself
(`pollSeconds`, default 300 — mgmt1 is shared by ~3 sessions).

**One request, end to end:**

| Step | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `events_next` (long-poll <= 25 s, `afterId` = the cursor) -> the state (closed / reassigned = ended, re-opened, the owner's choice, the customer's answer); `events_ack` after they are saved | `Invoke-SIWorkerPoll` |
| 2 | `supportfix_list` (open) -> the ONE most urgent request that is not another identity's, not waiting for the owner, not reported, not given up | `Select-SIWorkerNextWork` |
| 3 | `supportfix_claim`, `supportfix_update investigating` (a plain start note), `supportfix_get` -> `runs\<id8>-<time>\request.json` (customer text marked as untrusted DATA) | `Invoke-SIWorkerRequest` |
| 4 | the worktree; the session: hotfix = `Bash` limited to SI's git rules + the quick gate on SI's fixed lane (`gateLane`, default `gate4`) + `Invoke-SIWorkerRelease.ps1 -Ring 0` / `-Ring 1`; major = `Read, Grep, Glob` + writing its report only | `New-SIWorkerClaudeArguments` |
| 5 | the wrapper: the class re-read from Invardia, ring 1 only after ring 0 of the same request, the work committed, `origin/si-v3` in HEAD, push (never forced), fast-forward `si-v3`, then the route that works on mgmt1 today (as `fast-deploy-r1.ps1`): the bootstrap sign-in, ring 0 = `setup\Publish-SIRelease.ps1 -Ref <HEAD> -Build -Ring 0 -Apply` with ring 1's signing config from `release-rings.json` and `-EngineSinceRef <the previous ring 0 commit>` (unknown = `-EngineChanged true -ChangedScopes *`), ring 1 = `-ReleaseOnly -Version <that version> -Ring 1` (the same build moves on); the version recorded in `releases\<id>.json` | `Invoke-SIWorkerRelease.ps1` |
| 6 | `report.json` checked: `released` refused; `fixed` needs ring 1 in the worker's records + the proposal (`candidate { ring2, why }`, it leads the note); `needs-owner` needs 2-4 options; secret-shaped text refuses it -> `supportfix_update` (+ `ticket_finding`) | `Test-SIWorkerReport` |
| 7 | a failed / timed-out run counts a try; after `maxTries` (2) -> `needs-owner` "try again / a person takes it"; the owner's `retry` resets it | `Invoke-SIWorkerRequest`, `Update-SIWorkerStateFromEvents` |

**Ring 2 / 3 can never come from the worker** — five independent stops: the read-only constant `SIWorkerMaxRing` = 1
(no setting; an unknown settings key is refused); the wrapper's `[ValidateRange(0, 1)]` and its own check before any
read, push or release; `Test-SIWorkerRingAllowed`; the session's command lines (only `-Ring 0` and `-Ring 1` exist;
`Release-SI.ps1` / `Publish-SIRelease.ps1` / `git push` are denied); the report check.

**Safety:** `worker.lock` held open (the OS frees it on a crash) = one request at a time; `heartbeat.json` every 30 s;
the hard time limit `timeoutMinutes` (default 120: the process tree is killed); the STOP file; a log line per step in
`<dataFolder>\logs` with secret-shaped text withheld; a major's session that changed its worktree sets the STOP file.
**No secret on disk:** the publisher token stays in memory (`Get-SIWorkerPublisherToken`: mgmt1's bootstrap certificate
-> the Key Vault named in `release-rings.json` -> the publisher's ids by NAME -> its certificate signs the assertion,
exactly as `Publish-SIRelease.ps1`); the session has no MCP server and no token; every file goes through
`Write-SIWorkerFile` (secret-shaped text withheld). The telemetry causes (`GET /api/fixrequests/securityinsight`) are read
and logged only — L1 routes a cause to SI as a support fix request.

**On mgmt1** (machine-local, no secret): `C:\SI-ENVS\_build\support-worker\` = `worker.json` (optional: the defaults of
`ConvertTo-SIWorkerSettings`), `state.json`, `releases\`, `runs\`, `logs\`, `heartbeat.json`, `worker.lock`, `STOP`.
Uses what is already there: SI's publisher certificate + `release-rings.json` + the bootstrap config, git's
credentials, the signed-in Claude Code. **Tests never run on mgmt1** — the session's quick gate runs on the test VM.

**Invardia's MCP, as read in its source (2026-10-15):** `POST https://invardia.com/api/mcp/v1`, JSON-RPC `tools/call`,
the publisher's bearer token (role `Invardia.Publisher.securityinsight`). The SUPPORT fix requests are
`supportfix_list / _get / _claim / _update` (statuses investigating, fixed, released, needs-owner, cannot-reproduce);
`fixrequest_list / _update` are the TELEMETRY causes. The names are kept in ONE table (`$script:SIWorkerTools`).

## Publish layout — what ships vs stays internal

SecurityInsight publishes to its public mirror through the monorepo's shared
`.github/workflows/publish.yml` (flat layout). The workflow mirrors the entire
`SOLUTIONS/SecurityInsight/` tree into the staged public output **except** the internal/runtime
folders and docs listed below. The publish mechanics are shared and already correct — this section
documents the model; do not hand-maintain a divergent list.

### Ships to the public mirror

The customer entrypoints (`Bootstrap-Auth.ps1`, `Bootstrap-Storage.ps1`,
`Bootstrap-ContainerAppJob.ps1`, `Setup-SecurityInsight-Unattended.ps1`, `Get-FingerprintEngine.ps1`,
`VERSION`), `README.md`, `RELEASENOTES.md`, and the engine/runtime trees: `auth/`, `engine/`,
`launcher/` (community + internal-vm flavours), `setup/`, `container/`, `data/`, `tools/`,
`tests/`, `preview/`, `privilege-tier-catalog/`. Plus the customer-facing authority files and
their samples:

- `asset-profiling-schema/*.locked.json` + `*.custom.sample.json`
- `asset-profiling-providers/_manifest.schema.locked.json`, the built-in `entra/` provider, and
  `generic-cmdb/Refresh-CmdbCache.ps1` + `sample/CMDB.csv`
- `asset-profiling-enrichment/**/*.locked.yaml` + `**/*.custom.sample.yaml`
- `risk-analysis-detection/RiskAnalysis_Queries_Locked.yaml`, `risk-analysis.schema.locked.json`,
  `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.sample.json`, `*.exclude.json.sample`
- The canonical public docs: `docs/FEATURES.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md`.
- The bundled shared library (`FUNCTIONS/AutomateITPS*`) is inlined at publish time for community
  customers who don't have the monorepo.

### Community and Pro — one codebase, two payloads

The public mirror carries the **Community** edition. The paid **engines** of SecurityInsight Pro — the
ServiceNow and SQL CMDB connectors, the close-loop and governance mails — live in the same source tree but
in dedicated paths: their engine and launcher folders, their configuration files, their diagnostics and their
tests. Every one of them is listed in `solution.publish.json` `excludePaths` and removed at publish;
the private sync that paying customers use carries everything. The web app (with its MCP server) ships in
both editions as one file set; its paid pages are switched off by the licence.

- **Free code never loads a Pro file.** Anything both editions need lives in `engine/_shared/` — for
  example the Log Analytics publisher that the Defender for Cloud recommendations stage and the
  correlation engine both use. A test fails the build if a file outside the Pro paths names one in
  code, or if a file that declares a Pro gate sits outside them.
- **The licence check stays** inside the Pro payload as a second layer: with no licence, the Pro
  engines print one line and publish nothing, and every free engine runs normally.
- **Licence files.** `LICENSE` is the PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0, verbatim, with a header scoping
  it to the Community edition. `LICENSE-PRO` ships in both copies: part 1 lists the paid web pages, actions
  and services that ship in the Community copy switched off by the licence (proprietary: they may not be
  enabled or their licence check bypassed without a Pro licence), part 2 the Pro paths only the Pro package
  contains.
- **Side by side in one tenant.** A new Community edition install names its tenant-wide directory objects
  apart from a Pro install's: the web app's sign-in application "SecurityInsight Community", the engine's
  application "SecurityInsight Community Engine", the SQL admin group "SecurityInsight Community SQL admins"
  (looked up and created as `grp-si-community-sql-admins`). Setup finds these objects by name, so a shared name
  would have let a Community install reuse -- or rename -- a Pro install's application or admin group. The
  databases keep their names in both editions (`sqldb-si-pro`, `sqldb-si-identity`); the resource group and the
  database server carry the edition (`rg-si-prod-community-ca`, `sql-si-prod-community-ca-<suffix>`).

### The Community edition updater -- in the cloud, on the signed Community channel

A Community container install keeps itself current exactly as Pro does -- the nightly updater job `caj-si-updater` --
but from the **signed Community channel** instead of Invardia's licensed endpoint
(`container/updater/_shared/SI-UpdaterCommunity.ps1`, the client `engine/_shared/SI-CommunityUpdate.ps1`). PIM's
Community edition updates with a `git pull` and a re-run of its deploy; SecurityInsight's has a signed channel, so it
follows the Pro model.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Where releases come from** | Invardia's Community channel, the same route PIM's Community edition reads (owner + Invardia + PIM, 2026-10-28): `GET https://invardia.com/api/updates/securityinsight/community/<ring>`, ANONYMOUS (no install key, no code, no licence), rings 2 and 3 only. 200 = `{ manifest, manifestB64, signature, keyId, downloadUrl }`, an Invardia-signed manifest of the same RS256 family as Pro (kind `community`, `downloadUrl` = the manifest's archive URL); 204 = nothing released to the ring yet; 404 = no such ring. `SI_UPDATER_COMMUNITY_BASE_URL` (https only) points a rehearsal at a test endpoint. |
| **How it checks them** | Before anything is downloaded (`engine/_shared/InvardiaUpdate.verify.ps1`, product-neutral, byte-identical with PIM's, keys embedded): RS256 over the decoded manifest against the update-signing keys embedded in the release (one trust list for both editions); product `securityinsight` and kind `community`; a ring the manifest names is this install's ring; the SAME MAJOR version as the installed one (a new major version is a new installation, never an update); the sequence is not lower than the one applied (no replay); a manual step or a minimum version holds; the link is on the release host. After the download: the signed size and SHA-256, a zip-slip-safe extract, the archive's VERSION is the signed version, and it carries the update client. A first manifest naming an older version than the jobs run is held (forward only). |
| **Ring** | 2 or 3 only (rings 0 and 1 are internal): the ring on the updater job, else the ring recorded for the install (the guided install records 3 unless 2 is chosen), else 3. Anything else is 3, said in the log. |
| **Steps** | The same as Pro, in the same order: the manual-deploy mark, the run gate (never while a pipeline run is going), the database step first (the release's schema and grants), the engine image built in your own registry from the verified archive and the jobs rolled, the web app, the installed record, and the updater's own job last. The size pass and a pending self-update also run when there is no new code. |
| **State** | `cfg.InstallState` `CommunityUpdateState` (applied sequence, version, ring) and the compact `UpdateState` (source `community`) that the Settings page shows. Without the database, the running version is the guard. |
| **Not in the Community edition** | No install key and no claim, no licence request, no template channel (the release's own templates go through the template gate), no update tracking or failure reports to Invardia. |

#### Publishing a Community release (the same scripts as PIM's Community path; documented, NOT run before the owner says so)

1. **Mirror publish.** The shared `.github/workflows/publish.yml` -- never forked, never edited for SI -- is triggered by the
   tag `SecurityInsight-v<x.y.z>` (the short version) and publishes the staged Community copy to the public repository's
   `v3` branch (stable; `v3-preview` for a preview tag), from `solution.publish.json` (`stableBranch` / `previewBranch`,
   `acceptsPR`). The mirror is never edited by hand: the workflow's `last-mirrored-<branch>` guard refuses a public branch
   that carries commits outside the publish path. The public `main` stays frozen at 2.2.460. The public code follows ring 3.
2. **Register** (after the mirror publish): `POST https://invardia.com/api/releases/securityinsight/community`
   `{ version, tag, engineChanged }`, signed in as SecurityInsight's publisher application (app role
   `Invardia.Publisher.securityinsight`, certificate; Key Vault secrets `invardia-publisher-clientid-securityinsight` /
   `invardia-publisher-thumbprint-securityinsight`). Invardia builds the archive URL from the public release itself and hashes
   it -- SI sends no URL and no hash.
3. **Release to the rings** (owner-approved): the ring route for ring 2, then ring 3
   (`POST https://invardia.com/api/releases/securityinsight/community/rings/<2|3> { version, tag }`; `setup/Publish-SICommunityRelease.ps1`).
   Installs on that ring take it with their next nightly update (`GET .../community/<ring>`, above).
4. There is no test registration: the update leg is proven on the real release; the install leg is proven from the staged copy.

**Release-day checklist (the Community edition, owner 2026-10-28)** -- in this order, each only on the owner's word:
- the GitHub repository settings: make `v3` the DEFAULT branch of `KnudsenMorten/SecurityInsight` (a repository setting,
  not a workflow); `main` stays frozen at 2.2.460;
- the shared publish staging writes a `PREVIEW.md` that says `git checkout preview` -- SI's preview branch is `v3-preview`:
  change that shared text (framework, not SI) or accept it for the first release;
- the version is a SHORT x.y.z (the publish tag pattern `<solution>-vX.Y.Z`, #919): tag `SecurityInsight-v<x.y.z>`;
- the mirror publish (step 1), then register (step 2, tag `''`), then ring 2, then ring 3 (step 3) -- each read back;
- the public copy carries no `BUILD.json` and no `SI.Management.sln`: the install's web deploy and the Community updater
  stamp `BUILD.json` themselves (`Initialize-SIBuildInfoFile`); the images build their projects directly.

A copy is the Pro package when it carries a Pro-only file (`setup/_shared/SI-GuidedInstallPro.ps1`,
`engine/_shared/SI-InvardiaUpdate.ps1` or `engine/asset-cmdb/Invoke-SICmdb.ps1`); `LICENSE-PRO` and the `engine/pro-*`
folders ship in both, so they no longer tell the editions apart.

### Stripped at publish (never public)

- **SecurityInsight Pro paths:** everything in `solution.publish.json` `excludePaths` (see above).
- **Internal-only docs:** `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/TESTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the entire
  `internal/` folder (real onboarding playbooks, per-tenant runbooks, customer notes,
  `ENGINE-IDENTITY.md`).
- **Internal launcher flavours:** `launcher.internal-(vm|azure).*` and
  `launcher.internal-*.template.ps1`.
- **Runtime/transient:** `logs/`, `staging/`, `output/` (and `risk-analysis-detection/OUTPUT/`),
  `demo/`, plus `solution.publish.json` and `README.PLAN.md`.

### Never enter the monorepo (gitignored)

Customer-owned files that may carry secrets or tenant-specific overrides are gitignored so they
cannot be committed and therefore cannot leak through publish:

- `config/SecurityInsight.custom.ps1` and every `launcher/*/LauncherConfig.custom.ps1` (may hold
  SPN secrets)
- `asset-profiling-enrichment/**/*.custom.yaml` / `*.custom.yml`
- `asset-profiling-schema/*.custom.json` (excluding `*.sample.`)
- `asset-profiling-providers/**/CMDB.csv` (the real CMDB extract — the `sample/CMDB.csv` ships)
- `risk-analysis-detection/*.exclude.custom.json`, `riskscore_weighted.schema.custom.json`,
  `riskscore.index.custom.csv`, `RiskAnalysis_Queries_Custom.yaml`

`*.custom.sample.*` files are explicitly negated (they ARE documentation and DO ship). The
pre-publish gate (`RepoHygiene` check) fails the build if any customer-only/secret file is tracked.

**Release archives (SecurityInsight Pro).** The archive builder -- `setup/Publish-SIRelease.ps1` (the release sent to
Invardia's update platform; the managed update feed it shared this with is retired) -- packs a commit
with `git archive` and then remove everything the edition must not carry, and prove it is gone, with ONE rule set
(`setup/_shared/SI-ReleasePayload.ps1`, `-Edition Pro` by default, `Community` available):

- **Both editions** -- the public mirror's never-publish rules: top-level `logs`, `OUTPUT`, `staging`, `internal`
  (any case), `demo`, `solution.publish.json`; at any depth a folder named internal / logs / staging / demo / output, a
  file named `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TESTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, an internal-only launcher; and any tracked `*.custom.*`
  that is not a sample or reference (customer files are never shipped).
- **Community** -- plus every `excludePaths` entry of `solution.publish.json` read from the packed commit (the Pro
  code, its configuration, documents and tests).
- **Pro** -- plus `tests/`, `pro-management/tests/`, `analyzer/` and `analyzer-web/` (the deleted SI Analyzer, should an old checkout carry them), the internal release
  kit `release/` and the v3 design documents (`docs/V3-*.md`, `docs/SERVICENOW-INTEGRATION-BRIEF.md`,
  `docs/SERVICENOW-CMDB-SCHEMA.md`).

---

*Real environment values (engine SPN appId, certificate thumbprint, tenant/subscription IDs,
workspace/RG/Key-Vault names) live only under `internal/` — see `internal/ENGINE-IDENTITY.md`,
which is stripped from every public publish.*

### rc12 (2026-10-18): what a failure says, oversized CIs, source-not-present, mail subjects, telemetry on

- **The cause of a failed step is the error that ENDED it (#758).** `Get-SIErrorLines` takes the LAST error block of the
  step's log (from the first line of that block, then the lines after it up to the limit), not the first error-looking
  line. A transcript `PS>TerminatingError(...)` / `>> TerminatingError(...)` marker (PowerShell writes one for an error the
  code CAUGHT) and a `WARNING:` line count only when the log has no other error line. The container's settings decode no
  longer causes such markers: a list of plain words (`[LA,Excel]` -- az.cmd drops the quotes) is read without
  `ConvertFrom-Json`; only real JSON goes through it.
- **A workspace without the IdentityInfo table (#759)** is a fact about the tenant, not a failed read: SEM0100 on
  `IdentityInfo` gives one plain INFO line per run (the empty result is cached, no second query) and the state code
  `source-not-present` (no error text), which the Defender for Identity pull carries (`Set-SIRecordPull -Code`). A table
  that exists and fails is still a warning and a failed read.
- **One CI too large for a Log Analytics post (#760).** Before SI_CI_CL is posted, each FULL row is measured as the post
  measures it (its JSON, gzip-compressed when the post compresses). Over the limit at the post's fill level, the largest
  list or text of that row keeps its first half, measured again after every cut, until it fits -- the CI's id, class,
  name, tier, keys and the row bookkeeping are never cut; `si_truncated` names each field cut and how much was kept. The
  build says it once per CI with both sizes. A row that cannot fit even so is left out of the post and said; the rest of
  the batch is posted. The SQL copy (`sidata.Ci`) always keeps the whole CI. Measured, never a fixed cap.
- **Set-SIMail (#761)** tells the two refusals apart: 401 = Exchange did not accept the sign-in (the token), 403 = the
  account lacks a role. Neither is ever "the mailbox does not exist" (see "Set-SIMail and Exchange Online").
- **Mail subjects never carry an id (#762).** The environment's name is `SIWeb_EnvironmentName`, else `SI_EnvironmentName`,
  else the tenant's name (`SIWeb_TenantName` / `SI_TenantDomain` / `TenantNameOrganization`); a GUID or the install id is
  never a name. With none, the subject has no bracket and the footer says "your SecurityInsight".
- **"More rows than the source" on a COMPLETE report (#763)** is not a report problem: it is never in the run record's
  Reports (Invardia made even an `Action = none` item a fix request). It stays a note (`Get-SIUplinkReportNotes`: report,
  rows, source count) on the run context (`ReportNotes`) and in one line of the run log. A count-more on a report that is
  not complete is a report item as before.
- **Telemetry is on (#764, owner 2026-10-18).** `SI_Telemetry_SetupControls` not set = `all`: the daily setup report
  carries every control; when Invardia refuses it, the same report goes again ONCE with only the framework's minimum list,
  said once per process. `minimum` and `off` stay the customer's choice. `SI_Telemetry_SendHealth` sends by default (as the
  code has since CR2); the texts now say so. No SI code ever wrote either value, so existing installs reach the new
  default without an updater step.
